Dubai. An oasis of technology and lust in the middle of desert. Magnificent buildings in a developed city. But nature is always more ruthless than our ability to oppose. Destroyed by intense sandstorms, a city in ruins. The 33rd Battalion of the American army is sent to town for a rescue and extraction operation of the survivors. And then, they disappear from the map.
You are Captain Martin Walker, leader of an elite team of Delta Force of the Army of the United States of America, leading his fellow Lieutenant Alphanso Adams, heavy gunner and Sergeant John Lugo, sniper. Sent to Dubai after a transmission captured after six months without contact, his mission is to locate, reunite and rescue possible survivors.
Beautiful scenarios, even among ruins. The opulence of Dubai can be seen in the ruins and in few places that remained intact. Even the desert, displays an exotic beauty that brings a melancholy tone to the game.
Spec Ops is not just a shooting game in third person. It is a psychological plot. Every dialogue, every action, every event in this journey shows you more than bullets flying. Dubai is alive. Dubai is at war. And war... war never changes. The horrors of war are not shown as simple digital polygons falling to the ground with AI off. You will really feel them. You will hesitate. You will have anger and and will be thrilled. And maybe you even cry. You'll be confused. Do not stop. Go straight. Reflect, try to understand. Do not come to this game to play. Come to this story to live it. And so, you will not regret it.
Gentlemen, welcome to Dubai.
--
Dubai. Um oásis de tecnologia e luxuria em pleno deserto. Construções magníficas em uma cidade extremamente desenvolvida. Mas a natureza, é sempre mais impiedosa do que nossa capacidade de nos opor. Destruída por intensas tempestades de areia, uma cidade em ruínas. O 33º batalhão do exército americano é enviado a cidade para uma operação de resgate e extração dos sobreviventes. E então, eles desaparecem do mapa.
Você é o Capitão Martin Walker, líder de uma equipe de elite da Força Delta do Exército dos Estados Unidos da América, liderando seus companheiros Tenente Alphanso Adams, artilheiro pesado e Sargento John Lugo, franco-atirador. Enviados a Dubai após uma transmissão ser captada depois de 6 meses sem contato, sua missão é localizar, reunir e resgatar possíveis sobreviventes.
Belos cenários, mesmo entre ruínas. A opulência de Dubai se destaca em traços que podem ser percebidos nas ruínas e em poucos lugares sobreviventes. Mesmo o deserto, exibe uma exótica beleza que traz um tom melancólico ao jogo.
Spec Ops não é apenas um jogo de tiro em terceira pessoa. É uma trama psicológica. Cada diálogo, cada ação, cada acontecimento nesta jornada te mostra mais do que balas voando. Dubai está viva. Dubai está em guerra. E a guerra... a guerra nunca muda. Os horrores da guerra não são mostrados como simples polígonos digitais caindo ao chão com IA desligada. Você realmente irá sentí-los. Você irá hesitar. Você terá raiva e se emocionará. E talvez, você até mesmo chore. Você ficará confuso. Não pare. Siga em frente. Reflita, procure compreender. Não venha a este jogo para jogar. Venha a esta história para vivê-la. E assim, você não irá se arrepender.
Senhores, bem-vindos a Dubai.

Spec Ops: The Line is a third-person shooter with an emphasis on story and tough decisions (which affect how the story plays out/ends).  The storyline sets Spec Ops apart from other shooters; it doesn't glorify war or violence, rather it shows a gruesome side of war not often seen.  I wouldn't go so far as to say this game made me cry or feel depressed, but the mood is definitely dark and macabre at times.
The mechanics and gameplay are much like Gears of War or any other duck and cover third-person shooter.  The AI is fairly good and will present a stiff challenge.  All this being said, the game is very short (the single player missions can be completed in less than 6 hrs).  As far as replay value goes, the only reason to replay the game is to see the different endings/outcomes of your decisions in game.
The bottom line is this game has an interesting story but overall bland mechanics and a very short single player story.  There is no reason to replay this game in my opinion, so I wouldn't recommend buying Spec Ops unless it's on sale (the full $30 price tag is definitely way too much for a game that only takes 6 hrs to complete).

I said I would change my review back if the final product is shiny and it was so I did. I now give this game a solid 10 out of frikken 10. Graphics? Done and Done. Mechanics? Smooth. Everything is there. DX12 is finally fixed. My only complaint is that I am still mad about how they lied about Elusive Targets and I refuse to alter my real life schedule over a video game. We were told different things that weren't delivered. I love escalations though, always have. Look when this game first launghed I was able to forgive bugs. But the bugs extended well into the 3rd episode when I left. THAT is what made me mad. This stuff should of been ironed out. We were told this was an episodic release, which I defended from DAY ONE, but it played out more like a messy Early Access. BUT they got it done. And whatever problems the game had in the past, they had and it's done. Elusive targets aside everything about this game is perfect. The cutscenes look like the best movie I've ever seen. You can't even tell it's animated. Actual gameplay is almost the same. You can tell it's animated but only if you look close. And being able to simply tell the difference between animation and real life isn't a bad thing, in fact this game borders on creepily intesnse graphics. It's only slightly better than the graphics from MGSV which I say are the second best graphics I've ever seen. Keep in mind it took IO a long time to get to this point, but they did it. I notice the game can get a little choppy still, IF you have a bad graphics card. I DONT. But i did notice on some youtube videos, so.. I gotta give it a 10, because they came back from a point where everything really did seem hopeless. Remember this is the follow up after Absolution, a truly terrible experience! This game outshined it, and dare I say it even outshined blood money? The ONLY THING that prevents me from saying "better than blood money" is that blood money was a little longer, had more targets and was more difficult. I still have trouble with the Mississippi River mission and the inbred wedding. Hitman's levels feel easy, BUT it has replayability. So the challenge is totally in your hands which I guess is accurate. It shouldn't be hard to kill people, but it should be hard to do it creatively and such. A few things are missing from blood money like accident mechanics. You can't push someone down the stairs and have it count as an "accident" and the rating system is soul less. I like the newspaper scheme but I can live without it. At least this rating system is competitive and ego crushing. So.. I do like the fact that I can use instinct WHEN I WANT to. Which isn't often. In other words you don't need it to complete a level. I love how they brought back cameras, this time in a digital fashion and on EVERY level. I love the pop culture references. The donald Trump reference had me cracking up! I strongly reccomend playing this game all the way through. Some people diss the story but I dont think they played previous games very much because the story is written the same way the story is always written. Very vague. BUT IT IS THERE. And it DOES answer TONS of questions and there is a HUGE cliff hanger for season 2 which has been confirmed. Anyways, thanks IO. I really wish we could have skipped the summer when things got bad, but you pulled through by November, like you promised so for that I give you credit. And I do think the series made a major comeback. In fact I think you are missing out if you haven't played this game yet. The only thing is I wish there was "advanced mastery" that is to say I wish mastery levels went on to level 40 or 60 instead of just 20, even without rewards, just having the thing on my record would be nice. I feel like some levels I should have a 40, not a 20 know what I mean? A lot of cool stuff you can do is not even listed in the "opportunities" which I think is a good thing. LEaves room for the true Silent Asassins to shine.

DayZ simulates apocalyptic survival fairly well; to name a few aspects of this, you have scarce materials/basic necessities, the weapons available to you are somewhat uncommon and extremely valuable, and the player's character is dynamic, undergoing a lot of change as you run for miles on end in different places. It is very divergent from the original Arma 2: DayZ Mod that more than a million players know and love.
With that said, it's still VERY unpolished, incomplete, and almost underwhelming in some situations. There's not a whole lot of variety; the process of spawning, running, looting, running, taking care of your character, running, fighting and dying is very rinse-and-repeat. That, and the community is select and shrinking as the game continues to disappoint avid DayZ fans over 4+ years of early access development.
As one of the original DayZ Mod players, I am still baffled by the lack of progress that this game has displayed; the mod had progressed much further in far less time than this, and as such, has driven away a pretty dedicated community.
However, I still have hope for this game to cultivate and give rise to something really amazing. With the beta soon to come, and the various implementations the development team has planned out, DayZ still has far more potential than any other survival-based game out there. For this reason only, I still recommend this game.
For the sake of the game, the community, and Bohemia Interactive, I hope that the development team rises to the occasion and breathes life back into DayZ.

After getting the complete version of TM2 during the Steam Winter Fail 2016 (Most of the discounts weren't my cup of tea), I have one thing to say about this game compared to the only other TM game I have played, TM Sunrise.
This game will TEST YOU. It will test you to no end on your precision and how well you can powerslide without sending your car careening into a lampost. One you get it down, you can get that adrenaline rush that the whole of Sonic The Hedgehog wishes it could give you. Getting medals is also a challenge, even with the lower difficulty tracks. I just go for silver medals in single player, because the golds are basically MLG pro (At least they don't quickscope you the moment you get in the lead). The only problem I see with single player is currently, I don't think you can have multiple opponents to race against. Solo is 1v1 the whole way through (As far as I can tell). The physics are still what you'd expect from trackmania: go fast and you'll win, but you might wind up launching yourself off the track at that bump in the road or fly off at the next dip in the road and put yourself into a roll that costs you your silver medal.

Cons:

Overall, I definitely recommend this game.

This was a game I didn't think I wanted, but I'm really glad I gave it a chance.
I was skeptical coming in. The game was developed by a different studio, I had mixed feeling about Chloe in the original, and I didn't think that Rachel Amber could live up to the mystique built around her. I also wondered how a game about choices could make my decisions feel important when I already knew the future. I'm glad I was wrong. The new team did a fantastic job with the game.
The prequel loses all of the more unreaslistic elements of the original like the supernatural powers and the murder mystery, choosing instead to focus in on slice of life. It's a big change, but somehow Before the Storm still manages to maintain much of the tone and feel of the original Life is Strange. I found that I didn't miss the more fantastical elements at all. In some ways, the material was actually more evocative, as it felt closer to life. By the end, I found myself really liking Chloe (and doubling down 6000% on my choice at the end of the original). Rachel Amber was also shockingly not a disappointment. Instead, she felt quite real and reminded me a bit of several people I've met in my life. The events of the original hang over the game, but in a good sort of way, helping to make certain scenes more meaningful.
The biggest critique I have would be that the climax and ending were rushed. I spent most of the final critical conversations confused as to whether it was a dream sequence or reality. There are also some threads that were just left dangling or underdeveloped. I think the last few sequences could do with a little rewrite and maybe some more time.
That being said, I enjoyed the experience and wish it were longer. Would recommend. This was a very nice return to Arcadia Bay.

I really enjoy this little base building & management game. I absolutely love that the development team works to publish regular updates to the game about once per month; each time adding neat new features (it's an alpha!) and working through the known bugs that have been reported and reproducible.
In particular, I love the heat simulation and new room layout mechanism in the most recent update. The former adds a layer of management detail that is complementary to other base needs, while the latter presents a more intuitive and visual way of "painting" the layout of your base than the existing system (you placed entire room tiles with a click). Then they worked to add in color a color picker for the lights, which affects the colonists' moods and plant growth rates. Oh and a brand new scripted mission to play through. So, plenty of new features each month to go along with learning what exactly it is your colonists need to stay alive and form a self-sufficient colony.

Ok, so I'm going to do a review of this game in its current state of 0.54.
Overall, this game isn't bad.
The graphics are ok, especially since it isn't a AAA engine. (The rain kinda is wanked, but that is with most games that are top down) The concept is, in my opinion, one of the best parts of the game and I'd love to see it reach its goal. Making it into the game a few hours, I finally built a lab and was able to start doing research, though it doesn't lead to anything yet. But based on the reserach that I completed and finished, it seems that the goal it to eventually get a tech tree of some sort into the game which would increase the time to "finish" the game and also increase replayability.
So, since this is a great concept and it seems to be on its way, what is the problem? I personaly feel like I don't know if it will ever get to its goal and dream. I've seen so many early access games come and go and never get fully finished. Like I said, the concept is great, but with a UI that needs work, menus that are slightly confusing and an AI that really doesn't seem to know what it is doing, I just don't know. Hopefully I'll get proved wrong.
So, breaking down the issues with the game I'll start with the UI. The UI doesn't provide enough information at a glance. It is slightly cumbersome and it provides so few functions in general. As for the menus I'll just give a few examples; the load and save buttons aren't in the "esc" menu but are buttons in the upper right of your screen... ok, not bad sounding... but they aren't labeled so I lost a two hour base because I hit the "load" and not "save" icon. Another example of the UI needing work is the building menu. To switch between items as of now, one has to press "Q" and "E" a design choice I personally don't get. And that latter brings me into my last point or the AI being wonky. I can get around most of the other issues, but the AI is my biggest gripe right now. I can't tell my colonists what to do by say clicking on them and then clicking on a task I want the to complete. In some cases, this can lead to many deaths. I can set up many tasks, with the first thing I tried to build being a heater, and they'll do other things first, and die from hypothermia. lol. I mean, if I'm freezing to death, I'll build a heater first. But, IDK, maybe they know more than me.
So, in the end I'm going to recommend this game with a caution. Beware of what you are getting. It is, as I said, a great concept and I think that all the negative reviews don't do it quite justice and I want to see this succeed as I miss games like this. However, I think that my fear of it not being finished or what it could be may still be well founded.

*Note: I was a backer for this game*
This latest installment is a bit of a departure from the rest of the series, but is fun nonetheless.  For those of you that are new to the series, this game is made up of 18 well-designed levels (3 levels per world, 6 worlds total).  There are 8 creatures you can transform into to aid in traversal, but some of them are redundant (do we really need 2 forms for flying, and 2 for swimming?  Surely these could have been merged).  Where the level design differs from past games is that they are more linear like you would find in a standard 2-D platformer.  This is a good or bad thing, depending on your preference.
Cons - The game is pretty easy, with up to 10 heart containers to find in the world, buyable armor that you can get very early to cut damage recieved in half, and a bat form that can also be found pretty early that breaks most of the platforming sections after that point (if you really want to cheat).  Bosses can be fun when trying to work out how to damage them, but with lots of health, armor, and recovery items you rarely need to even bother with dodging their attacks.
The story seems to be decently written, and funny at times, but is also unfocused.  Each level is treated like it's own episode, which sounds nice, but also means that things are introduced and quickly discarded.  For example a rival Half-Genie Holly appears after the first level, but disappears after some taunting.  After the next level, she appears in 2 more scenes before she's gone for good.
The game is really short.  My first blind playthrough of this game took about 7 hours to get to 100% completion.  When hunting for trophies on the PS Vita version I finished the main campain in 1 hour 40 minutes (any %) and 3 hours 30 minutes (100%).  More content is on the way as DLC, and it'll be free for me, since I'm a backer, but others will have to pay for it.
Pros - The game is beatiful, with great music.  It is made up of 2-D characters on 3-D background, but at times it hard to tell what's drawn or not.  The style blends very well.  Animations are smooth (though maybe the idle animations can be a bit over-blown sometimes).  I've enjoyed Jake "virt" Kauffman's music since the VGMix days, and this soundtrack is no exception.
The levels are fun when you don't break them with Bat or Harpy form.  Playing with minimal power-ups feels like a closer approximation of the intended experience.  Level and monster designs are good when the skillset is brought more in line with normal 2-D platformers.
Searching for secrets in this game was a lot of fun as well.  The developers put in some interesting puzzles, making re-visiting levels something you actually want to do.
Rotty Tops.
As for a straight "Recommend" or not I'm a bit torn.  I honestly had a lot of fun playing through the game, but at $19.99 USD for what is a 4 - 8 hour game it might not be worth it.  I will click "Recommend" for now, but I would advise that maybe you wait for either a sale or at least for some of the DLC to come out.

Shantae: Half-Genie Hero is a short but very sweet platformer with some nicely integrated Metroidvania elements and interesting character upgrades and skills.
Level design is very good for the most part of the game, the soundtrack features some very nicely remixed versions from some of the previous games and is generally fitting for the fast-paced style of the game.
Character design is especially nice, with some pretty funny and light-hearted dialogues, deceptively cute drawings and brilliant animations. Just seeing the characters bob to the beat of the rhythm is truly heartwarming.
The platforming itself feels good and responsive at all times and integrates the skills the game has to offer nicely.
The difficulty starts off a tad on the challenging side, but actually gets progressively easier as Shantae gets more upgrades, up to the point where she's outright overpowered and some skills that pretty much break the game (talkin' about you, secret-key-bonus. ;P). Thankfully all the upgrades are fully optional and can be switched off in the menu at all times. Some transformations make platforming in some levels a little too easy in my opinion though.
It took me almost 10 hours for 100% completion, but I took it pretty slowly. If you know what you're doing you can certainly beat it much faster. The game does offer a certain replay value, although it might not be enough for everyone to make them want to replay right away.
The only real downside is that, compared to it's predecessor "Shantae and the Pirate's Curse", Half-Genie Hero feels a little more shallow, with less dialogues and a little less of the series' refreshing whacky humor. And even though most of the levels are extremely well designed, I really miss the dungeons of the previous game that had to be beaten at the end of a level.
Still, if you're looking for a light-hearted, nicely paced platformer, I'd say you can't really go wrong here for the ~20€ this game costs. I for my part have had a lot of fun with this and will certainly keep a eye out for possible DLCs or additional content.

This game may just be one of the best single player experiences I have ever had. The story is mind-blowingly amazing, and nothing much comes close, except maybe the story of COD: Black OPS. This game features several choices of morality, which in turn don't affect the gameplay much, but in the end it's how they affect you as a person. This game really makes you feel for the characters and how that in turn reflects on you at the end.
The atmospheric design and levels in this game are truly unique and offer something different to the typical shooter genre. The weapons are varied yet simple, and the shooting mechanics/cover system is simple but great. With the cover system, squad management and varied selection of weapons Spec Ops: The Line keeps the gameplay fresh and interesting, with a complex story that keeps you wanting more.
All in all, I would highly recommend this game to anyone for the story alone, let's just hope you can live with the choices you make...

Lets talk about DayZ, a brilliant survival game with alot more potential. I know, the game is in early access for years and it seems that the progress just doesn´t want to go on. BUT this is a Review about the game.
Is DayZ really that bad? Worst game ever? Is it worth the 30 bucks?
It is worth buying. THIS game is the only kind so far that gives you the feeling of fear, terror, paranoia, success, failure and even happieness. NO other game gets you that nervous if you´re near a Hotspot for Loot. NO other game can generate the adrenalin that you WILL get if you encounter other players. DayZ has a Charm and feeling that no other game has.  If you never played DayZ before, buy it. This game gives you an experience you wont ever forget.
Of course DayZ is far away from being perfect at the moment. It´s still not fluid enough, especially animations.
It just feels that you don´t have 100% control of the character right now. But its forgiveable, belive me.
Some stuff like vehicles are awful because after a time your fps begins to drop and the driving itself is really bad.
For long term players it gets/got boring because of the lack of content. And yes it still has bugs but honestly, I didn´t encountered any bugs for months.
But lets be honest..a bad game doesn´t sell more than 3 million copies. Most people are frustrated and gave the game a bad review because the game didn´t progress fast enough. Or the game just wasn´t for their taste.
People cried over topics like "yeah i was killed on sight from some 13 year old kids".
Its a survival game, if you´re rushing through cities, military bases without caring about your surroundings - it´s your own fault. YOU WILL get shot if you don´t give a damn about your surroundings. One of my  characters "lived" for 3 months straight. If you play with the intend to kill others and get the best gear as soon as possible, you will get killed.
Sure there are people who will kill you if they see you, even if you are not geared. WHY? Because they want to survive and they dont want to give you the opportunity to kill them.
Another important thing i saw in the bad reviews, if the game is really that bad..why you have 50-1500 hours. If a game is bad i quit after 10-15 hours because i want to give the game atleast a chance. But writing a bad review after playing hundreds, thousands of hours? Telling its so bad, its not worth the money and so on. Really? You often Pay 60-70 bucks for a game with a 20 hour story and never touch it again. THESE games are worth the money?
In this game you can spend thousands of hours without getting bored, if you´re open for it. There are Roleplay servers, pvp servers, pve servers, 1st person servers just pick one that suites you the most and make your own storys and experience. LGM Games’ successful debut title, Starpoint Gemini, an RPG tactical sim set in a unique SciFi setting was released in 2010. It was a great learning experience for them and it paved the way for their next game - Starpoint Gemini 2, the sequel. It entered Steam Early Access program in September 2013, and a year later after what most would consider one of the best Early Access communities on Steam, Starpoint Gemini 2 hit the shelves on Steam in Sep 26, 2014.
On a personal note, I was honored to have been with such an amazing community. Both players and the Developers worked together so well that I myself strongly believe it was the best early access game on Steam! I made many friends and I truly enjoyed the journey...
======================================

======================================
Starpoint Gemini 2 is an action space-sim combined with diverse RPG elements. Control various space ships, ranging from small and agile gunships to lumbering, but deadly carriers. Explore, trade, mine asteroids, and research in a star system no longer hindered by loading points. The entire Gemini star system is now one giant area thanks to the implemented streaming technology. Gain experience and upgrade your skills to change the tide of even the fiercest space battles. Complex, but easy-to-use RPG system with skills and perks to customize as you see fit. This also gives great replay value, you can literally spend many many hours just trying different styles...
======================================
I have played EVE online, Elite Dangerous, and lots of other games in the space genre. Out of every space game in my Steam library, this is the one that keeps me coming back for more. Deep, immersive, beautiful. It is the perfect open space sandbox game. To elaborate, yes there is a story campaign mode that will guide you through the lore of the game. It does this via story-missions, in-fact at the start of a new game you can choose to play campaign or free roam(sandbox). A great feature is that even in the campaign you can do the story missions at your own pace. There is a great many of freelance and side missions.
I played the first Starpoint Gemini so I was going into this quite excited, but you don’t have to play the original in order to enjoy this sequel anyway(They made the first one playable with the free DLC Starpoint Gemini 2: Origins). It is a space game all about exploring, mining asteroids, trading, capturing, and flying multiple ships and getting lost in a massive dynamic universe. It is the kind of space game I love to get lost in for long periods of time just roaming through space and immersing myself into the game world. This game certainly provides many ways to do it, such as gearing up a ship to go on a mining run. There is so much to do in this game it can get overwhelming at times. (But in a good way)
When you first launch the game, you will be introduced with tutorial tip screens. These can, of course, be ignored, but I would strongly advise that you read everyone of them. The interface can be quite complex and there is many ways you can customize the ships so no need to go in blind by turning off the Tips!. You want to survive for more than ten minutes in space for your first captain. There is another matter I would like to clear up as well, this game is not EVE Online or Elite: Dangerous. It is a unique tactical space sim with exploration and missions. Many people including the Dev's would say that it is more comparable to Freelancer in all the good ways...
Mastering the ship controls is not that easy at first, because there are a number of ways to view the action. There is the turret view which allows you to swing around the ship so you can track everything around your vessel, the mounted view which puts you just above the ship, and a third person view which puts you just behind the ship. All of them have their own advantages depending on the situation you may be in and half the battle is understanding when to use which view. It takes practice to master this when the combat gets hectic and you need to start switching rapidly between them. As ships have location based shields, being aware of what is attacking (and from where) can be the difference between life and death.
This game really shines at immersing you into the life of a deep space merchant, miner, pirate, or whatever you prefer! There are so many options and the awesome guys at LGM have done a great job at making every path fun and viable. There is a ton of customization to help you really fill the role you choose as well. I personally spent several hours just looking at my options the first time I leveled up. Any hardcore RPG fan will have a ton of fun just building and tweaking their character and ship into their very own ultimate space hero... Or a feared pirate. So just let your imagination run wild.
I mentioned customization earlier and this game has a ton of it. You can hire staff for your ship which affects its performance: For example, you might hire a crew member who increases your propulsion speeds. You have complete control over your equipment load-out and their enhancements. You can even customize the look of your ship to some degree. All of this is generally handled when you anchor yourself to a space station or planet. While docked, in addition you can buy and sell trade goods, read news clips, access a garage which houses your ships, and more. It sounds like a lot to deal with, but between all the tutorials, which are accessible at any time for reference, and the well-designed interface, you’ll have your hands around it in a reasonable amount of time.

Starpoint Gemini 2 is a game for space lovers made by space lovers. This is by far one of the best open space games I played and it will delight you with its gorgeous visuals. There is a true sense of adventure as you discover new areas of the star chart, with opportunity and danger lurking around every corner so you are constantly encouraged to build yourself up in terms of power, wealth, and relationships with the various factions.
LGM and its great team have created an instant classic that will be around for many years....

While I still prefer the more open-ended Metroidvania style of the previous games, especially Risky's Revenge, Half-Genie Hero looks, sounds and plays well enough to be worth a try. It feels like a grab-bag of ideas from Capcom's golden years on the Super Nintendo, especially games like Mega Man X and Demon's Crest, and throughout it all it feels great to play. Hopefully they keep making games with it.  Very nice aesthetic.

It's worth noting that this game is not really a metroidvania, anymore, like previous installments. There are some pros and cons to this format, though. It's much more linear, employing stages rather than a single world for you to explore. I think this helps the player progress through the game more quickly keeping the fun alive rather than feeling like you you're constantly just running around on the map to find things like in previous titles.
The game is gorgeous. It's is colorful, the characters are adorable, the levels are fun to run through, and the music for the game has some really nice arrangements of the main tunes from the franchise. I had doubts, initially, about the style of the game when I first saw it on Kick starter, but it's grown on me and now I really love it. There are lots of transformations -- perhaps too many as some become almost obsolete after getting new ones that replace them -- and open up possibilities for combat and exploration -- and they all looked great, as well. The transformations are pretty easy to utilize and don't really require specific button motions to transform like in the original.
On the flipside, however, the game almost feels like it's not finished. There's a lot of polish to the game overall, but it just feels like it's too short or as if there are stages "missing", if you will. However, this may be remedied with the Risky Boots DLC in the future.
Additionally, one complaint I have about the linear level design is that you have to go back to previous levels many times to get things that you get either later in the stage or in future stages and you can't go backwards inside of a stage. Basically, each stage is split into separate "divisions", where, once you go past one within the stage, you can't go back. If you need to get to an earlier point in the stage -- which is sometimes required because on more than one occasion, you get an item towards the end of a stage that you need for the beginning of a stage for a secret or item to progress further in the game -- you're going to have to go through the entire stage all over again to get to that part of the stage. This made the game feel artificially longer than it was. It almost felt like a weak supplement to the game to lengthen it.
The last problem I had with it was that the characters aren't really developed that much in it. Pirates Curse had a LOT of character development in it. You learned a lot about Risky Boots and almost developed a friendship, almost, with her, by the end of the game. However, in this, it's as if it never happened. She's strictly the villain with seemingly no recollection of the events of the previous game. It's the same way with other characters, as well, like Rotty-Tops, for instance. You grew and learned a lot about her in Pirate's Curse, but in this, you really don't interact with her much. It's like once and that's pretty much it. Even less for Poe and Abner. You basically only say one thing to them at one point in the game and that's more or less the last you see of them. I really wish there had been more character development or some sort of additional focus on the characters than the game gave. It very much felt like a cycle of,
1. Meet one character that needs item to get you to new stage
2. Go to stage to get item
3. Give item to new character
4. Gain access to new stage
5. Next to nothing for interactions with that character for the rest of the game.
and just repeat that for the rest of the game. It just kept the world feeling like it wasn't fully fleshed out when you didn't really interact much with all of the characters you got to know so well in Pirates Curse.
Those are my only big complaints, however, and they're far out-weighed by all of the positives of the game. It's fun, it's colorful, and just a joy to play. Absolutely worth playing.

What made Life is Strange a great game was not it's use of gimmicks, nor it's beautiful art style. It was the way the story unfolded, really making you feel like you WERE the character you played. You made decisions not because it was "how you think the character would feel", you made them because you were practically there with them. This game really makes you connect, and has it's awesome share of plot twists and surprises. I definitely made decisions I regret, but not having the rewind power actually helped my decisions feel more solid, and in the end, I stood by them.
Now of course there are complaints, the voice acting for one became stale and predictable in a few situations. Some dialogue seemed excited for no reason and others seemed too... teenage? It makes sense giving the REBELLIOUS TEEN these kind of lines, and the voice actor specifically nailed those. (For those who weren't aware, the voice actor for this games Chloe Price was not the same as last game) But even so, I found myself rolling my eyes at Chloe more than a few times. Following up dialogue is the new mechanic: Backtalk. I both loved and hated backtalk sequences. Sometimes it felt great, and the lines chloe threw fit perfectly with what I would have said. Other times, it makes absolutely no sense. It's also a bit difficult to feel the emotion on a line of text until you choose it. There have been a couple of time I picked an option just to hear chloe say it with so much anger or other emotions, and it isn't at ALL what I expected the line to unfold as. "Winning" a backtalk also felt weird, like you shouldn't have won. Several of the people you talk to simply have the power and authority to say "No", and yet winning the backtalk still has them skulking like a dog with it's tail between it's legs.

I'd like to preface this review by saying that the game is in Alpha and I'll update the review as things change if I have time.
Ok, so I haven't written a review before but decided to write one for this game. First I'll just list Pros and Cons in order then describe a little about it from my experience thus far,
Pros:
-Neat idea worth expanding on
-Good graphics for an alpha
-Fun*
-Harder sci-fi than some I've played
-Devs work on the game and respond to feedback (Got an answer on the review initially)
Cons:
-Bugs
-More bugs
-Occasionally problematic UI
-Optimization issues
-AI build priorities
-Inability to manually control colonists
So, I'll start with the Pros. First off is the idea, I like it. It is always nice to see older style technology (Like the capsules the colonists land in) in a Sci-fi game instead of the constant use of sleek and streamlined ships and tech. Next up is the graphics, they are actually surprisingly good for an alpha game although I'll admit I've never been much of a snob about graphics. Now on to the "Fun" I mentioned, it is not fun in the sense of a fast-paced action kind of fun. It is more of a challenging fun associated with overcoming the challenges of survival. And finally, the last pro, "Hard" sci-fi. I find hard sci-fi to be more interesting a challenge in a game and that made it just a bit more interesting to me. For example: to get water you have to build a solar still and for food you need to build and maintain a hydroponics area instead of just building a food replicator or the like.
Now on to the Cons. First off let's talk about the bugs, most of the other reviewers say that the dev/devs have focused on features over bugfixing (time will tell if that's true, I've only had the game a few days at time of writing.) I think the dev/devs should absolutely focus on bugfixes first, at least the game breaking ones that is. A good example of this has happened to me several times in a single game where I would call in some additional colonists and they would just stand outside the capsule waiting to die in their suits, that needs to be fixed. Apart from that, there are a few bugs I've encountered like one of my I.M.P. bots just standing in front of a fossil stand that was full holding a fossil and wouldn't dig or another one where my maintenance bots wouldn't go around the local Flora to repair my wind turbines so I had to manually drive them out and around the plants. Now that bugs have been adequately discussed let's move on to the UI. It is hardly there, kind of annoying to get used to, and is a little hard to use for rotating items without placing them. In addition to those, there is no way to save your game during it so you have to hope that it saves it. And, finally, on to the the optimization I mentioned. It freezes while loading it but eventually does get running. It is a minor issue but I did find it frustrating that the game freezes each time I start it even though it'll run well after it loads (with bugs and UI issues of course).
TL;DR: It is definitely worth waiting on. I'll recommend it but with one planet sized caveat: it is buggy and very much an Alpha. In other words, watch the game and buy it when bugs get fixed.
**UPDATE**
I said I'd come and update the review over time, so I will. The bug with colonists getting stuck coming out of their pod is fixed. There are still some problems with AI priorities so far and the game crashes occasionally. For the AI priorities, I can set them to build the basics of a colony (Like heaters, atmosphere generators, and wind turbines) and they will not get around to much of it and die of hypothermia.
One new problem I have with it has emerged though, and it is admittedly a little bit nitpick-y. The problem is that the escape menu has no save option or "quit to main menu" button. I'm assuming it is a save and quit situation, but it is still a little odd that I can't save with how much it crashes for me at present. I'd be fine with a "save and continue" or "save and quit to menu" option or something similar.
I'd still recommend following the game, it is interesting and you don't see too many more "hard sci-fi" styled games like it. I'd recommend buying it if you don't mind it being a little buggy or supporting the devs though.

This is a survival game based on hard sci-fi, so things can be a little "messy". The humans don't have handy mood bars above their heads and machines don't have health bars. You'll have to pay attention to whether your crew are writing dark poetry about setting the repair bots on their fellows to work out if they're going psychotic.
This game goes to great lengths to bring the perils of just existing on a hostile planet to life and the attention to detail can be felt running through all of the interacting systems.
It's been really interesting to watch this game grow through Early Access - update after update have added new systems and fixed bugs, and with a simulation game like this each new system increases the complexity exponentially.
If you want a fast action space fix this is not a game for you (and never will be) but if you want a well thought out simulation of what life could be like on a distant harsh planet then give this your consideration.

I bought this at a significant discount, but still can't justify this being good value for money.  At the time of writing, I'm approximately 80% of the way through the campaign.
Pros
- Decent voice acting.
- Attempts a more mature storyline.
Cons
- Fails at delivering a mature storyline. 'Choices' have little impact so far, and the whole lauded 'grey area' occurs when you're forced to do stupid things. eg See civilians on an overhead cam?  Too bad, level doesn't advance unless you drop a mortar on them.  Try to miss them and target only the enemy?  Whoops, that mortar is magically 10x larger than the last two dozen you fired.
- Don't bother trying to flank, your fireteam magically teleports to your location. No tactical choices at all.
- Don't bother directing your fireteam to attack anything.  They generally can't hit a target in the open when directed by you.  Funnily enough, when left to their own devices, they can actually shoot accurately.
- Blatant corridor shooter with poor level design.  Fairly repetitive and illogical.
- On rails sections sometimes punish you for not firing at that 1 guy out of 5 that almost instakills you for no apparently reason.  His buddies barely scratch you, by the way.
- Gritty story, everyone dies.  Thankfully, that means you don't have to put up with the poor pathfinding, teleporting, and AI cutting into your active line of fire.
Would not recommend, unfortunately.  I like the premise, but it falls flat on its face in the implementation.

So instead, I will explain how to make an ommelette;
Ingredients:
- 2 Large eggs
- Salt and pepper
- Butter
Instructions:
- Crack both eggs into a mixing bowl. Whisk the eggs until completely combined, and season with salt and pepper.
- Place an 8-inch skillet over medium-high heat and melt the butter. Tilt the skillet as the butter melts to evenly coat the bottom. When the butter stops sizzling, the pan is heated and ready.
- Pour the whisked eggs into the skillet. Tilt the pan so the eggs coat the entire bottom.
- After egg mixture begins to set around edges, carefully push the cooked eggs a few times from the side of the skillet towards the center, with a spatula.
- The omelette will finish cooking in 1 to 2 minutes. When it's done, use the spatula to fold one half over another.
- Gently slide the omelette onto a plate, and eat it.

Been playing this game quite extensively and I am very fond of it. Has almost everything you could want from a simulation of a prison management.
You can choose a small or large map so plenty of options, even then if u choose the large map and feel "this is too small" you can research expansions and get even more land and truly get a massive prison going.
It is a lot of the little things for me though. Like you get a boost of income for every hour and day that passes without incident. This truly motivates you to keep check on your prisoner and makes you feel happy seeing this income boost increase like a highscore but with meaning.
All the different backstories for prisoners, their various personalities or attributes, all the needs they have and the challenge to meet them all is very enjoyable. The programs and work you can have running, seeing the effect of also great fun.
While there is already a lot of fun objectives to achieve as you play, I would definitely like to see more of it, because when you start to clear them all up, you find yourself slightly aimless, which is good for some but I would like the chance to fufill more complex or difficult objectives as my prison grows.
Another downside is there are still no gangs in the game to my knowledge, but I believe it may be implemented at some point, which will make me feel there is nothing left besides minor tweeks to make this a dream sim game of its theme.
This is at least to me, one of the best simulation games I have ever played, it really sucks you in, keep you engaged and invested and even offers moral choices. Will you have death row or will you refuse it? Will you offer parole and if so, how much time off?
Not to mention you get a grading system after 10 prisoners have been released, you see the % of chance of committing crime again on each prisoner which gets affected by your choices and what facilities you have. You can decide the amount of punishment on many different things like finding drugs, tools, weapons and even actions like assault or escape attempts.
All the modifiers, stats and how you can alter the 24 hour schedule as you see fit, it has so much creative potential so I would recommend this game, especially now on sale, to anyone who likes simulation management games with a prison theme. You won't find a better game in this theme and in my opinion, one of the best sims of all times.

I myself have been playing since Alpha (September 2013 release) and I have seen SPG2 come along in strides. Below is a basic list of what is in-game and can be done whilst playing. SPG2 brings back many memories of quite a few spaces games I have played since the mid 80's onwards.
Star Point Gemini 2!
DLC - Secrets of Aethera - Adds in new ships, new storyline arc, tweaks and updates to game systems.
Riftways - Oh my, something to experience yourself! - Rollercoaster rides in Space.
Fighter wings for ships with hanger bays are a blast to play with.
70 ships to buy/capture/destroy
Equipment/Weapons that can be modified with enhancements
Customizable ship - Can re-color certain parts of your ship, add decals etc.
Consumables - Shield boosters, damage boosters, repair nanobots, etc
Power ups - Boost your Railgun damage, or Beam weapons etc for a few seconds to turn the tide in battle (Use them wisely though as they have a cool down for re-use)
Ship cloaking (Ships that have cloak devices) - A lot of fun with this one :)
Hero Characters to hunt down and kill for excellent credit reward. (You can kill a few of us Forum members now as Hero Characters! - Thanks to LGM's competition)
Global events - More fun things to do outside of freelance missions etc.
Junk yards - Cruise the junk yard like a junk yard dog looking for some possible cargo and or poor unsuspecting ships that might contain some nice cargo to liberate from them.
Trade your wares in stations and planets that you either bought elsewhere or collected from combat or mining. (Price balancing to still be finalized)
Board and capture ships - Hire troopers and grapple a ship, send in the troops and take over that ship for some extra credits or to take as your own new ship.
Worm Holes appear around the galaxy and can whip you to somewhere else in no time (Be warned you might turn up somewhere "You dont want to be")
AI Security forces scan you ship for contraband and give you an option to dump it or duke it out (Pirates life for me, damn the pollice hehe)
T-drives work as personal T-Gates to quickly jump to other areas very quickly (Same as using T-Gate, but on the spot usage, instead of finding a T-Gate)
Ability to hanger (Personal hanger accessed via stations and planets) upto 5 ships, which you can swap out when needed. Have a freighter parked in your hanger when you want to do those big commodity runs for the big bucks, or some large scale asteroid mining. Drag out your carrier to go out and take on fleets of enemies with your weapons and your fighter wings.
Travel the Galaxy map by normal engine power (I have done this and it takes quite some time - grab a coffee and some food), Power to engines (faster travel speed) or by Fast travel ways (Real fast movement across the galaxy)
Freelance missions, Combat, repair, scan, VIP Courier, Cargo courier the list goes on.
Steam Workshop - Mods are coming along and many more to come as modders get busy!
Did I mention how bloody good the galaxy looks, Nebula's are amazing, Asteroid fields are real special (I like to play a pirate, so I like to hide in the dust clouds of some asteroid fields and wait for passing freighters/mining ships for some easy kills and loots. Junk yards look great, and just a reminder again don't run into them they not hurt hehe :)
Oh and Mod Tools,
Want to add a new ship into game, can do!!
Want to add new sectors into game, Can do!!
Want to add anything virtually into game, can do!!!
Probably the best thing of all about SPG2 is the Dev Team, These people are one of the best I have had the pleasure of enjoying an alpha/beta release with. They are always responding to members posts, questions, technical help, and ideas.
The Dev Team have even taken ideas from members and have put into game those ideas, what more can you ask for in a Dev Team who cares just as much for the player base as their game, that is simply priceless and a quality lacking in many AAA title Dev Teams.
All I can say is, "If you enjoy space gaming, Buy SPG2 today. You wont be disappointed"
And drop by the official forums and say hello as well :)

Shantae: Half-Genie Hero is in no way a bad game. It has much of what made the previous Shantae games great, like its fluid animations, great visuals, silly story and amazing music. The gameplay feels fantastic and responsive aswell. But despite the game's numerous positives, one can't help but feel a little disappointed.
The metroidvania style world building and levels in the previous titles have been cut for "chapters". A chapter consists of several linear stages (go right. for the most part) and side scrollers. There are secrets spread throughout each chapter. Some you can get right away, while others you'll need a certain skill to get to. This forces you to backtrack and revisit chapters, and is a small substitution for the metroidvania styled secrets. This however doesn't make the exploration that enjoyable, as you're forced to run through the stages quite a few times to get everything. There is a dance you can get in the game called "Warp Dance", that lets you skip a previously completed stage. This helps getting to a correct stage faster, if you know there is an unacquired secret there. But you will still always start at the very beginning of a stage, so you'll always have to run through the beginning each time you want to visit the area.
Another minor disappointment is the absence of a few animations that exists in the game's previous titles. Some examples are the various dance animations, a proper dodge animation, and an idle "hurt" animation. Even though they seem minor, and not too important. It all adds up, and more fluid animations helps the atmosphere of the game greatly. However, this doesn't change the fact that the game has quite a few animations already, and of very great quality.
One can't help but feel that the game is missing something when coming from Shantae and the Pirate's Curse. There are many small things that if added, would add that little extra bit of polish and quality, and it would help out the game immensely. There are even concept art within the game that shows that there was so much more planned for the game, but for whatever reason was scrapped. If it is because of the lack of money or time isn't easy to tell, but it could also be because of the promises they have to deliver because of the kickstarter.
These are however minor flaws. Half-Genie hero is very enjoyable for what it offers. The game oozes "Shantae" from the very beginning, and is a treat for every fan of the series. If there is one thing WayForward doesn't get (too) wrong, it's the Shantae titles. And one can tell that they really care about this series.
Here's to a successful Risky dlc campaign, and future Shantae titles, because this series is absolutely splendid.

I honestly don't know how Mad Max got a "Very Positive" overall score. Because IMO, it's one of the worst open world game I've played lately, and I loved most open world games usually. But maybe that's just because I've never seen the Mad Max film, and the game may or may not bee hinging on some of that film hype to get the full enjoyment. TL;DR: Mad Max is an exceedingly mundane open world game, think first assassin's creed minus well formed story, the weapons, and much fewer villains.
As much as like going into details on how much this game fruastrates me, I think the most important thing you need to know is that somewhere between the second stronghold and third stronghold I started playing other games and just couldn't be bothered to get back to Mad Max for a couple weeks, when I finally picked it up I felt less like playing a game and more like doing a chore.
The Sandbox is, well, really sandy, and that's not a compliment, the world could really use some more variation, I know it's the bloody end of the world and water/ food are scarce, so that explains the food and water but does tasteful decoration just magically drop out of a hidden floor board or got eaten up during food shortage? Couldn't the developer decorate the stronghold better? Because honestly, after clearing 16+ stronghold I honestly can't remember any one of them because they all look about the same. (except one where you take the elevator to get back up, and sometimes that's all it takes to distinguish it from other camps).
The enemy in this game is also surprsingly repetitive; most notable on the several camp boss fight, every single one of them fighting in a flaming arena where you dodge a charge attack then combo attack the boss for a few second before dodging again, Arkham Asylum style, every, single, mini-boss fight. I mean seriously Dev, are you guys allergic to quality character designc, personality, or fun?
And then there's the car combat/driving, the absolute worst part of the game, where you're forced to drive around looking at monotone landscape to get from one objective to the next, fighting waves after waves of bad guys you couldn't care less about. Trying to rebuild a car which apparently doesn't even matter to the protagonist, I mean seriously, what's the point of this game!?
If you like open world games then there are tons of much, much, better games I'd recommend over this piece of trash, heck, I think I'd have more enjoyment playing through something like Arkham City or one of the previous Assassin's Creed game again, then I'll ever get from this embarassment.

Rogue legacy is a great "roguelite" game that doesn't desperately try to be something that it isn't.
It doesn't necessarily have as much content and longevity as something like the binding of isaac would have, but what it does have is well made and polished mechanics.   The armor system is well made, supporting fairly many styles of play. The rune system is an interesting and well fleshed out system of secondary perks and abilities which can impact the core gameplay loop quite vastly depending on how you decide to utilise them.
And the gold and level up system is also nicely done, striking a balance between feeling worthwhile and being absolutely necessary.
The descendant system is a nice touch which helps to keep the characters feel fresh, and the traits system adds yet another layer to the gameplay. Some of the traits being helpful, some neutral and some outright bad.
Charon being in the game helps to add some of the "rogue" in to rogue legacy, him not being there would make leveling up and managing your gold very different. And not in a good way in my opinion.
I don't really have anything bad to say about the game, except perhaps the architect. I think removing the ability to lock down the castle would overall profit the game. Although i can see that being somewhat frustrating to a new player. But overall it's probably not a big gripe.
I've beaten rogue legacy tens of times, and grinded to max level and found all armors and runes twice. I guess that tells something about my enjoyment with it.
I guess my summary would be something in the lines of, everything just feels so enjoyable in this game. It never feels like a chore.
And i would definitely recommend it at it's pricepoint. Especially when it's on sale, about 4 dollars or your regional equivalent is a steal for a game like this in my opinion.

REVIEW CONTAINS SPOILERS
I bought this at a significant discount, but still can't justify this being good value for money.  At the time of writing, I'm approximately 80% of the way through the campaign.
Pros
- Decent voice acting.
- Attempts a more mature storyline.
Cons
- Fails at delivering a mature storyline. 'Choices' have little impact so far, and the whole lauded 'grey area' occurs when you're forced to do stupid things. eg See civilians on an overhead cam?  Too bad, level doesn't advance unless you drop a mortar on them.  Try to miss them and target only the enemy?  Whoops, that mortar is magically 10x larger than the last two dozen you fired.
- Don't bother trying to flank, your fireteam magically teleports to your location. No tactical choices at all.
- Don't bother directing your fireteam to attack anything.  They generally can't hit a target in the open when directed by you.  Funnily enough, when left to their own devices, they can actually shoot accurately.
- Blatant corridor shooter with poor level design.  Fairly repetitive and illogical.
- On rails sections sometimes punish you for not firing at that 1 guy out of 5 that almost instakills you for no apparently reason.  His buddies barely scratch you, by the way.
- Gritty story, everyone dies.  Thankfully, that means you don't have to put up with the poor pathfinding, teleporting, and AI cutting into your active line of fire.
Would not recommend, unfortunately.  I like the premise, but it falls flat on its face in the implementation.

There's so much to say about this game. So I'll be descriptive and actually post a thoughtful, in-depth review.
Let me start off by saying that Spec Ops: The Line is an absolute gem. I'd like to say that it's probably the pinnacle of modern shooters in the gaming industry today, although, I won't shun out the other decent shooters that came after this one. Spec Ops: The Line is the result of splicing together fluent game design and a riveting narrative, which blends into a well-thought out, intricate piece of priceless art.
To begin, I'll discuss the story, which was deeply influenced by several various novellas, Joseph Conrad's 'Heart of Darkness' being the most prominent source for influence and inspiration. Spec Ops: The Line sets in Dubai, within the UAE. It is described that Dubai has suffered through the largest sand storm in recorded history, nearly submerging all of Dubai into a pile of rubble and sand. The game's main protagonists are three Delta Force operatives sent on a recon mission into Dubai, the player assuming the role as Captain Martin Walker, the squad leader. Under Walker's command is Sgt. Lugo and Lieutenant Adams, who prove to be an effective, tight knit team. The game does an extremely good job presenting each character's personalities and traits during the many hardships that follow. Each character is unique and displays their own opinions and thoughts on the situations that surround them, and it's up to Walker (the player) to act upon these many decisions. Each decision you make has their own consequences and it will impact upon how the squad looks towards Walker, one way or another. I won't ruin the story for any of you, but I will say that this game will truly make you think afterwards. It does a great job of doing that, believe me. Every scene and every conversation holds it's own weight and it never fails to bore the player. You 'can' skip cutscenes, but I recommend that you don't, as you'll miss out on the nice voice acting and acting the game presents.
Gameplay wise, the player won't have a hard time working out the kinks involved with the cover system, as it's surprisingly easy to maneuver. Beyond that, combat is very fluent for a third person shooter, as the ballistics are almost completely spot on, and for the most part, so is the enemy AI. Commanding your squad in-combat may seem a little difficult to work out at first, but it proves to be extremely effective when picking targets. Enemies *will* swarm you during points, so it's important to stick with your team and to pay attention to their observations on the field. Your squad members will call out units that deviate from your average cannon-fodder, such as shotgun units, snipers, knife bearers, and heavy units. Furthermore, Spec Ops: The Line utilizes not only strategic assault tactics, such as sniping or silently taking out sentries to thin out the numbers of a superior force before an assault, but the game also uses it's superior level design for environmental hazards that the player may use as an advantage over their enemies. There are many other utilities such as the sand storms, the squad's degrading appearance as the game progresses, and the many cinematics and points of interest that make this game truly stand out, making the player's experience with the game one to remember.
The soundtrack... Spec Ops: The Line offers a fantastic soundtrack that truly matches and punctuates the mood of the game itself. From Mogwai and Alice in Chains to the game's own masterfully crafted soundtrack, the game's soundtrack itself never fails to impress and aspires to keep the player entertained during their trek across Dubai. In fact, I still find myself listening to the soundtrack on and off both before and after I played the game.
Whatever you may have heard about this game, it's probably true. It's truly an underrated piece of work and deserves way more praise then it has already recieved. There isn't much that I have to complain about with this game, other than the disappointment I had when I finished the game in one sitting, which took about six hours. I wouldn't say the game offers much in terms of replay value for other than the choices and multiple endings the game has. However, I still found myself playing the game again about a day later, and it was still damn fun. As for other features? I know the game has a multiplayer option that I have yet to try out, which I will get to with a friend of mine when we both have the time.
So to conclude on whether or not you should buy this game? Yes. Hell yes. I bought this game while it was on sale for $5. I can honestly say that it was the best $5 investment that I've ever made. Sale or no sale, this game is worth every cent you put into it. Spec Ops: The Line is a fantastic modern shooter that combines expert game design and a fantastic narrative that is truly a unique experience for every player who touches this game.
Words can't do this game justice. So I'll leave you with this: Buy this game if you want a truly rememberable experience that most videogames these days just can't do.  Also, Walker is voiced by Nolan North, man. Nolan North. Everyone loves Nolan North. So not only will you be buying a stellar videogame, but you'll also be supporting Nolan North's rise to ultimate power. And being me? I usually don't write reviews for games unless they've deeply inspired me on a deeper level.
Cheers, everyone. Happy gaming. :)

Ignored it upon release as I'd wrongly assumed it was another one-sided AMERRCUHHH, KILL THE TERRORISTS, BE A HERO game (the first 30 or so minutes kind of are, to lull you into a false sense of confidence and righteousness) but it quickly turns out to be anything but - throughout, and increasingly so, you'll be questioning whether you're doing more harm than good, and that's putting it lightly. Surprisingly deep and clever. Several references to Heart Of Darkness which it seems to be based on.
Lots can be said about how well it manages it (I ended up writing an essay on the game for uni), but without spoiling anything, you'll feel like a monster by the end. In one small example, there's a part where you're fighting enemies in a shopping mall, with civilians hiding inside. I'd been fighting for roughly 10-15 minutes and hadn't seen a single civilian. An enemy ran down a hallway, and I chased him, ready to shoot back, when a civilian dives out from a gap and ran for cover. Before I had time to think, I shot them, and felt SO bad. It was clear that it was a mistake the game was counting on me to make, and I fell for it.
Downsides: criticises military shooty games while being one (whether that works for or against it is up for debate), fairly unimaginative Gears Of War style cover/shooting mechanics.
Overall: I really recommend anyone gives it a go, if they're into any shooter games, or are just looking for something different within the genre (hard to find, as anyone'll know). BUY IIIIIIT!
(oh, and avoid multiplayer. the devs didn't want it in the game but the publisher got another studio to quickly hash it together, which completely misses/ignores the point of the story.)

4 stars out of 5. It loses that 5th star for a keybinding issue from hell.
I spent the first two days playing this cursing the fact I couldn't skip a cut scene when I restarted and thinking that it was just because it was a really bad console port. Finally got stuck somewhere with a reaaaally long cutscene and went on the internet and discovered that it's a bug instead. Turns out, this is a bug triggered by reassigning the Enter key. Secondly, you can't get away from the bug except by resetting your keybindings to default. Thirdly, this means that playing on the numpad, I can't use the Enter key as my default Reload trigger, which means I keep going into battle with my guns empty.
So yeah, it loses the 5th star for a nasty bug triggered by no one apparently ever testing against people who play from the numpad… Otherwise, I'm having a blast with it. Very Apocalypse Now/Heart of Darkness!

Ingredients:
- 2 Large eggs
- Salt and pepper
- Butter
Instructions:
- Crack both eggs into a mixing bowl. Whisk the eggs until completely combined, and season with salt and pepper.
- Place an 8-inch skillet over medium-high heat and melt the butter. Tilt the skillet as the butter melts to evenly coat the bottom. When the butter stops sizzling, the pan is heated and ready.
- Pour the whisked eggs into the skillet. Tilt the pan so the eggs coat the entire bottom.
- After egg mixture begins to set around edges, carefully push the cooked eggs a few times from the side of the skillet towards the center, with a spatula.

- Gently slide the omelette onto a plate, and eat it.

“What would Chloe do?” was a question I asked myself repeatedly during the three episodes of Life is Strange: Before the Storm, the prequel story set three years prior to 2015’s Life is Strange. Before the Storm puts you in the role of the previous game's protagonist's (Max’s) best friend, back when she was still a sophomore. While playing as Max felt more natural – she was generally more agreeable and hence easier to relate to – Chloe is unlike her in most ways, and her rebellious streak is crucial to not just everything she does, but everything she says too.
Of course, it’s nigh impossible to not let personal biases, prejudices, and experiences influence your choices in dialogue trees. This is an interactive story, after all, one where you get to decide how you want Chloe to behave and how those decisions shape her life.
While most choices are clear cut – a report card at the end of each episode shows what percentage of the community chose what route – the biggest decisions continue to be polarising in Before the Storm, just as they were with Max in Life is Strange, where sacrificing Chloe to save Arcadia Bay or sacrificing Arcadia Bay to save Chloe was split down the middle.
The consequences aren’t as heavy and world-altering as they were in the original. Max’s time-travelling abilities allowed her to reverse events and bring back people from the dead. But now your decisions carry more impact at times, owing to their permanence.
You can still reload from the last checkpoint to try out different scenarios in the short term, but time – and the story – are linear in the long run. Chloe’s “abilities”, if you can even call them that, are simply a by-product of her personality: the Backtalk feature, appearing in dialogue trees now and then, lets you twist people’s words to aggravate and annoy them, in a bid to get them to do what you want. It’s used sparingly throughout Before the Storm, but it develops nicely across the three episodes, giving you more or less room depending on who you’re conversing with.
But the real beauty of the prequel story – penned by American developer Deck Nine, taking over from Paris-based Dontnod, which caused reservations among the fandom before the game’s release at the end of August – is in its writing, be it the emotional depth it affords all its characters (even the supporting cast), the rushed yet touching portrayal of queer teenage romance, as two girls open up about their feelings, or the way it talks about grief over losing a loved one, and exploring how it embeds itself in nearly everything you face.
There were genuine concerns that exploring the origins of Chloe’s reverence of Rachel – who became her best friend in the intervening years Max had moved away to Seattle – could easily backfire, given she was this haloed and mesmerising figure players kept hearing about in Life is Strange. Thankfully, Before the Storm crafts a nuanced, multi-layered depiction of Rachel, one that pulls you in the minute you meet her in the first episode, and progresses in ways that help convince you of the connection between her and Chloe.
And given that you’ve prior knowledge of the tragedy that befell her – the third and final episode of Before the Storm closes with a shot that is bound to evoke heart-breaking memories for anyone who played the original game in full – it makes the moments you spend with the duo all the more important and emotionally-packed, knowing that fate is coming soon for Rachel.
The walk under the street-lights after the play in episode two is a highlight, and it is extended conversations like those, where the characters wallow and inhabit one environment, that enrich Before the Storm. It’s also great to see a game having two powerful female protagonists at its centre, praise which underscores the sad state of video game affairs in 2017.

Equally important, and more affecting, is the honest dialogue and comments on dealing with grief. The death of Chloe’s father is inescapable for the high school dropout, following her like a shadow no matter what she tackles, and the dreamscape sequences in Before the Storm – most of which end in wailing and severe anguish for the protagonist – form the bedrock for understanding her slow descent into caring less and less about the world around her.
She does ultimately start to find peace towards the end of the third episode, accepting that he wasn’t perfect because nobody is, but that doesn’t change the fact he’s still her dad (even though he only exists in her mind). That connects into the story arc of Rachel finding the truth about her parents, who have lied to her to keep her away from any negative influences.
Lying to your loved ones to protect them is another theme for Before the Storm, which ties it into the big final decision you’ve to make as Chloe: will you give Rachel the truth and risk breaking up her family, or shield her from the harshness and bitter nature of truth, in turn keeping her from what she wants? The fact that the player-base has been split evenly on answering that dilemma shows the uniqueness of an interactive game opposed to a TV show, where fans get to see the what-ifs played out, instead of just discussing them in theory.
All this is improved by the game’s defining soundtrack, composed by the British indie folk rock outfit Daughter.  Drums reflected Chloe’s aggressive streak, but it’s also the lyrics that communicate and deepen the tortured nature of the teenager – Burn It Down is a distillation of her feelings – while helping immerse you in the hella-cool fictional world of Arcadia Bay, based in the US state of Oregon.
life is strange before the storm tempest Life is Strange Before the Storm
And between all this misery and heart-break, Before the Storm also manages to squeeze in some much-needed comedy, with Chloe being dragged into a high school performance of Shakespeare’s The Tempest, having helped Rachel win back her leading role from Victoria: Prospera, the original play’s male lead as a female one. The look on Chloe’s face as she realises the horror of having to perform on stage is a delight, and one of the funniest moments the franchise has provided.
Taken all together, the three-episode story of Before the Storm is a meaningful, well-written addition to the Life is Strange canon, that tackles grief, love, and loneliness in noteworthy ways, sheds light on how Chloe became the 19-year-old broken soul, maintains the enigma of Rachel while giving a peek, and even ensures all its side characters are properly serviced. It doesn’t have the scale of the original, but it’s all the better for it.
Life is Strange: Before the Storm is proof that good prequels don’t just extend the atmosphere of what fans loved about its predecessor, but complement one another.

Been playing this game quite extensively and I am very fond of it. Has almost everything you could want from a simulation of a prison management.
You can choose a small or large map so plenty of options, even then if u choose the large map and feel "this is too small" you can research expansions and get even more land and truly get a massive prison going.
It is a lot of the little things for me though. Like you get a boost of income for every hour and day that passes without incident. This truly motivates you to keep check on your prisoner and makes you feel happy seeing this income boost increase like a highscore but with meaning.
All the different backstories for prisoners, their various personalities or attributes, all the needs they have and the challenge to meet them all is very enjoyable. The programs and work you can have running, seeing the effect of also great fun.
While there is already a lot of fun objectives to achieve as you play, I would definitely like to see more of it, because when you start to clear them all up, you find yourself slightly aimless, which is good for some but I would like the chance to fufill more complex or difficult objectives as my prison grows.
Another downside is there are still no gangs in the game to my knowledge, but I believe it may be implemented at some point, which will make me feel there is nothing left besides minor tweeks to make this a dream sim game of its theme.
This is at least to me, one of the best simulation games I have ever played, it really sucks you in, keep you engaged and invested and even offers moral choices. Will you have death row or will you refuse it? Will you offer parole and if so, how much time off?
Not to mention you get a grading system after 10 prisoners have been released, you see the % of chance of committing crime again on each prisoner which gets affected by your choices and what facilities you have. You can decide the amount of punishment on many different things like finding drugs, tools, weapons and even actions like assault or escape attempts.
All the modifiers, stats and how you can alter the 24 hour schedule as you see fit, it has so much creative potential so I would recommend this game, especially now on sale, to anyone who likes simulation management games with a prison theme. You won't find a better game in this theme and in my opinion, one of the best sims of all times.
