The art and music immediately stand out in terms of quality, making for a very enjoyable gaming experience. The controls, level design and gameplay are all highly polished, ensuring that it isn't too punishing for platformer newbies while there are enough secrets and challenges for more serious players to complete. However, like its previous installments, the game suffers from its short length and limited replay value.
Overall, I rate "Shantae: Half-Genie Hero" as one of the best platformers released in 2016. The game is definitely worth full price on its own, but do note that several DLC are already in development to add additional costumes for Shantae and new campaigns where you can play as Risky, Rottytops, Sky and Bolo. I'd recommend keeping an eye out for new game updates this 2017.

Another adorable game by the great folks at Klei.
I'm going to review this game from the perspective of a casual gamer.  Not one steeped in knowledge of chemistry or electrical/plumbing engineering.
Just a regular Joe Casual.
You will fail at this game.  You will fail hard and often.  The first hour of ONI will be the same as your last hour: Frantically running around in a panic while your world goes to hell and falls deeper and deeper into a pit of pee, vomit and polluted water and air.  Your 'dupes' will not be happy.  Many will die.  Those left will wish they were dead.  You will be more stressed than your dupes.
Your dupes will happily chomp away on their lunch while their world is crumbling and there are emergencies to take care of.  You will hate them for it.
One of your dupes will 'binge eat' all your precious food and there will be nothing you can do to stop them.  You will leave them in a mine shaft to starve to death.
Another will vomit non-stop all over your base making everyone sick and foul your water.  Another will destroy everything in his path.
Your 20th base will end in the same pit of despair your first one ended in.  It will just take longer to get there.
But you will load up a new game and try again.  And again.  And again.
You will never win, but you will keep coming back.
Why?  I don't have a clue.  Maybe it's the charm.  You'll certainly love the look and feel of ONI.  Of course it's EA, so we can forgive that it's currently more punishing than fun.
I will recommend ONI because I hold out hope that Klei will add some joy to the game that is currently only suffering.  Beautiful suffering.
UPDATE 10/13/17:  With the 'Oil' update, I have better hopes for ONI, so have at it!

That might be an overstatement since I haven't played every game on steam. Regardless, Rogue Legacy is a fantastic game. It has all the right elements to make a great roguelike and includes personal touches that make it a truly unique game.
- It's different every time you play. Seriously, you pick a new character every time with a class, a spell, and several traits (irritable bowel syndrome hehehe). Additionally, the map is scrambled every time, forcing you to explore the castle over and over again.
- They also include an option to lock down the castle, giving you the option to continue exploring the same map you had before you died. BUT you are slightly punished by doing so (only receive 60% of gold loot). This is a fantastic option because it gives you an advantage at a price. Let's not make things too easy.
- Teleporters (thank you).
- Simple responsive controls.
- Enemies and traps follow specific patterns - learn them!
- The combination of the previous two points makes this game very fair. It is purely skill based. Did you take damage? It was probably your own fault.
- Enjoyable music.
- Different segments of the castle have different themes and enemies.
- Lots of collectables scattered around the castle.
- Option to level up stats and diversify the genepool.
- Different armour, weapon and rune options that you can customize before entering the castle.
- First play through is a challenge (especially the two last bosses, those took me a long time).
- Great replay value.
- You can have up to 3 different profiles at one time (start a new game without overwriting your previous save).
-
- Many enemies are just reskins of older enemies (but they have new abilities and patterns).
- Blob boss is very difficult.
- Attacking downwards to open platforms can be difficult.
- You will die a lot in the beginning - try not to get discouraged.
- Over time you will figure out which kind of character you prefer playing, leaving the other ones almost untouched. Personally I almost never played the mage.
I am fairly certain that you will know whether or not you will like Rogue Legacy based on the trailer. It is exactly as it seems: fun, fast-paced, rewarding and punishing. If the trailer tickles your fancy, I would definitely urge you to get it.

Reading through the reviews you can reach the conclusion this game isn't for everyone. After I first bought it I played for about 30 minutes then quit for a month because of how difficult it was. You're thrown in there with little idea of what to do, so you wander into another room and bam you're dead. You respawn and check out the shop and realize you don't have enough gold for an upgrade, so you go over to Charon who takes your measly amount of gold leaving you at 0 again.
So you're probably wondering why I'm recommending this game and the reason is simple: Because I pushed past it. It took a while but once I began to figure out enemies, and stop dying on the first room the game became a lot of fun. I'm able to kill weak enemies in one hit now, but I still find myself challenged on every room. At 500+ HP on a barbarian king your potential for dying in the first section is pretty much nil, but those enemies will wear you down. Before you know it you're down to 150 HP. You think the game is challenging on the first section wait until you get to the dungeon or the attic, I still find myself getting killed on the first room in those sections. The moral of this game is no matter how hard you work and how good you get you'll always have to work hard to win.
My one gripe about this game is balance issues in the different sections. The first section is good for beginners, the forest is a good step after that, but after the forest it goes from 3/10 difficulty to 10/10 difficulty.
Like I said this game isn't for everyone, but if you're willing to put in time and still get your♥♥♥♥♥kicked than you'll have fun. If not go play undertale you cowards (it's just a prank).

Once again I find myself wishing Steam had an option between Yes and No, but for the moment I'll settle for writing a No review. I got Mad Max for $20 on release and for that price I think I definitely got my money's worth, but at anything over that I really can't recommend it.
If you played Shadow of Mordor or any of the Batman Arkham games, you'll feel right at home with Mad Max's gameplay. Unfortunately melee combat does not feel as fluid or as involved as either of those games and quickly grows boring. Vehicular combat, arguably the peak of the game, also grows stale within the first 10 hours. It mainly involves grinding away at other cars in a battle of attrition, while later in the game your upgraded tools allow you to rip wheels off cars or drivers out behind steering wheels, thus ending the encounter almost as soon as it starts. There is very little variation between fights, and you'll be doing the same thing for most of the game. The gameplay activities are also pretty repetitive, requiring you to grind out boring laundry-list tasks to unlock gear and progress through the story. This would be bearable if you could just skip the side-content and stick to the main story, but you often have to grind to get specific pieces of gear before you can tackle certain missions. It was during one such grind to unlock a new mission that I decided that I'd had enough and called it quits, meaning I never finished the game.
Overall, it's not the worst open-world AAA game out there, just very mediocre. It has pretty visuals, runs like a dream on PC and there are worse ways you could spend your spare time. Just not if it costs more than $20.

To begin with, Spec Ops: The Line is not a typical action shooter. Spec Ops is a game that will indeed shock you in some parts of
the campaign. The developers wanted to show us the other side of the war where everything that you think will be all right, goes wrong and you are the one blamed for that. The campaign takes place in destroyed by storm Dubai where we have the mission to rescue any survivors. The game shows us then a very good perspective of how a such a powerful city as Dubai can be destroyed in days by thirst, hunger and civil war. The campaign then also shows how rest of the world just do not care about other conflicts. The game takes then focus on team-work where you and two other soldiers are going through the city trying to survive. I also felt like the campaign was slowly turning you into a murderer, where you began as a friendly soldier and ended as a killer.                                                                                                                                                              The game itself is very good. The shooting mechanics are great, there is also some stealth gameplay. The game offers a wide list of weapons which is also great. The missions are ´´OK´´designed, so do not expect much. The game offers some decent graphics, but it´s still the gameplay that shows most potential. Spec Ops: The Line offers also a great addition where you have to find several ´´intelligence files´´ so it´s also a great thing for achievement hunters. Unfortunately I haven´t played the multiplayer yet, so I can´t review it.
I personally liked the game. I bought it on Humble Bundle for several dollars and I can´t really say it was not worth it. The campaign after all was great experience in my opinion even though it shocked me in some chapters. The game itself was also good; the AI, weapons, Dubai perspective are definitely its best features.
Overall I would like to say that the game was great and I truly recommend it to anyone to try it out.

Ten years after the release of Spec Ops: Airborne Commando for the PlayStation 2, the franchise reboots with Spec Ops: Line for the current generation of consoles, bringing the classical shooting experience of the 90's to the current generation, changing lots of things to the Spec Ops formula in order to keep up with the current technology and the needs of the market. The story of Spec Ops: The Line follows the Delta Force team formed by Captain Martin Walker, Lieutenant Alphonse Adams and Staff Sergeant John Lugo in their reconnaissance mission in Dubai, after the city was constantly hit by major dust storms in the past six months, killing thousands and leaving those who are still alive in a constant battle for survival. As the city was believed to be abandoned when your team arrived in Dubai, your mission was mainly to confirm the fact that everyone inside the city is dead. As you'll find out from the very first moments of the game, that isn't the case as the 33rd Battalion commanded by Lieutenant Colonel John Konrad made a stop in Dubai on their way back home from Afghanistan. The story is profound and different from what you're used to in modern military shooters, and features multiple moments of tragedy, regret and life changing decisions, keeping you constantly on the edge of what's happening in Dubai and reminding you that lives are at stake. Sometimes the game gives you the opportunity to change how the events will unroll in a situation, making the difference between life and death and also the way your crew will appeal to you. The game does feature four different endings, and even though the decisions you take along the story will impact the way you look upon what happened and what role you played in the entire scheme, they won't affect the ending itself, as you can see all endings by reloading the final chapter. In addition to the amazing story, the game features a multiplayer mode similar to what other games like Uncharted or Call of Duty have already done in the past, but apart from that there isn't much more to it. There are different game modes and maps you can try out, the most unique and entertaining experience probably being provided by the Buried mode, which tasks two teams of four to sabotage the enemy headquarters while defending their own, a great experience enjoyed with a couple of friends or online with all slots filled.
The gameplay is exactly what you would expect from a third person shooter, yet there are a few features that make this experience different from the others. The inventory of weapons is large, including everything from pistols, to SMGs and heavy artillery, and even more the game awards you with achievements for using all of them and killing enemies in unique ways. In addition to those, you have grenades, sticky grenades and flashbangs, which serve as an important tactical maneuver, as you'll often run out of ammo, being forced to use a flashbang to stun your enemies while you make a run to grab another gun or find some extra ammo. One thing that is different in Spec Ops: The Line however, is the fact that you can use the environment to your advantage, from shooting the roof on which an enemy is standing, to exploding barrels and breaking the barrier keeping the sand away from an encampment, there are plenty of ways to use the environment to your advantage and save some ammo. The game features three difficulty levels, plus the FUBAR difficulty level that is unlocked after you've completed the game on the Suicide Mission level of difficulty. Each level of difficulty is nicely optimized depending on your needs for challenge, and combined with the different story outcome, there are lots of reasons the play the game all over again on a higher difficulty level. You are also allowed to give orders to your crew, a feature that will prove quite handy when you're low on ammo or surrounded by groups of enemies that you can't handle by yourself. The enemies are quite diversified, from snipers to shotgunners and heavy armored shooters the game offers enough variety in the terms of combat, while still maintaining the level of realism and logical equipment for those troops in the middle of a desert. On the multiplayer side, the game features many modes, although most of them have the same twists that have been done many times before; in the addition to the classic death match, the game has additional modes such as Rally Point which requires your team to hold the target point for as long as possible, Buried, which serves as a VIP escort mode with a few objectives before getting to that, or Uplink which requires each team to make a rush for the center objective, but only after they've secured their own mini team uplink.
The landscapes of Dubai are simply astonishing, with tall buildings destroyed by the sand, all of it designed by adding the even the smallest detail. The world around you is full of items and equipment, exactly how you would imagine an abandoned luxury city to look like. From the expensive hotels turned upside down by the civilians running for their lives when the storm hit, to the swimming pools filled with sand from the previous storms, everything looks amazing. The visual effects are nice, especially the ones involving sand, dust storms and everything related to that; the lightning effects are awesome and different from a place to another, providing a quality rarely seen in such an area. The characters look okay and detailed enough to actually see the marks left by the combat on the faces of your team from a chapter to another, yet the facial animations could use some improvements.
The sound effects are nice and synchronized with the action on the screen and the quality is standard high definition audio. The soundtrack is okay, yet limited and sometimes unneeded, but it does help you get in the mood for what's coming next, so I'd say it does the job just fine. The voice acting features the legendary Nolan North, known for his great acting in the gaming industry in franchises like Assassin's Creed, Call of Duty and Uncharted, things that made him an obvious choice for the role of Martin Walker. Other roles are played by not so known actors like Christopher Reid in the role of Lieutenant Alphonse Adams or Bruce Boxleitner as Lieutenant Colonel John Konrad, yet they managed to delivered their lines in an outstanding manner, making the entire voice cast for The Line one that gives personality to those characters creating this amazing story around your actions.
There are plenty of reasons to replay the campaign all over again, or at least parts of it as you can choose to play individual chapters after you've completed the game once, plus the achievements are fun to do and trying new things as you progress through the campaign is always a boredom killer. In addition to that you have the multiplayer mode that offers more hours of gameplay depending on how much you're digging it, but don't expect to be a game changer as most of it has been done before in the exact same manner.
This game isn't your typical modern combat shooter, as it doesn't follow the events of any war or your quest to killing an evil treat, instead it focuses on your actions and the way things can change drastically in just a few hours. The game successfully created a great atmosphere and an even better story, making you the center of attention by the moment you arrive in Dubai, as you'll change the entire city with your decisions and dedication to your service.

It's not often I write a negative review, especially of early access games - either it's too soon to tell, or the game is so bad that Jim Sterling will deal with it.  Maia, though, I want to warn people off, for now.
, and it certainly should not have a ticket price of $25.  This is an alpha stage game, with serious, fundamental flaws that need to be worked on before this can be an enjoyable beta experience.
is a colony builder, like
or
.  It takes the
approach of letting you set tasks and build spaces but not directly control the colonists.  With good AI and balanced priorities this works well; without it, you get issues as with Towns.  Maia is somewhere in between: the AI isn't very good, but there is so little going on in the gameworld that it's just about good enough, unless you do something weird.
Graphically I like Maia.  It's got a 1980s styrofoam-and-foil aesthetic, with big-head robots and Space: 1999 jumpsuits.  The graphics are very unpolished, but this game I think qualifies as alpha at this stage, so that will come.
The UI is just so bad.  It is clunky, awkward to use, with unintuitive keybindings, an absence of necessary information in the overlay, no easy way to check what your colonists are doing, and an annoying over-sensitivity to screen scrolling when you're trying to get the obnoxious and imprecise mouse cursor over the icons.  Drawing rooms is a chore, which is an issue when that is pretty much the only thing you can currently do in the game.
It's also very poorly optimised.  Running on min settings, with a mid-range computer in excess of the recommended specs, I get memory crashes, terrible frame rate issues, and periodic freezing as the game tries to calculate something.  I've spent a lot of time on forums trying to find ways to address these issues at my end, with no luck; I'm not the only person with this experience.  A certain level of poor optimisation is to be expected with early access, but not to the degree where it derails your playing.
Development is okay.  I feel like they should be further along than they are at this point.  For over a half a million dollars in funding and a year and a half since the first playable build, it should be further along than this.  I think Maia, Towns, DF9 et al illustrate one central truth about town-management games: they take time to develop.  If you over-promise, you get DF9; if you rush and then run out of hype, you get Folk Tale; if you don't nail the AI, you get Towns.  Dwarf Fortress didn't happen overnight; without having to worry about graphics or platform integration that game took years to get to anything like a quality gaming experience.
And that's principally why I am warning against Maia.  For a well-funded game to be charging $25 for an early access build that isn't optimised, isn't visually polished, doesn't have basic features, lacks solid AI, and is without the diversity of content you need for a game in this genre, that's not a good investment.  I accept that an early access game will be content-light, will have areas needing to be polished, but when a colony-manager after this much work still doesn't have basic UI, AI and optimisation sorted out, they are going to have no chance of adding more content without bringing the game crashing down.
I want this game to succeed, but they don't need more money, and you don't need the current experience of Maia.  Give them until the end of the year, see where they're at then; they will either have fixed these issues by overhauling basically the core of the game, or it will have gone the way of Folk Tale.  Either way you'll have your answer.

Firstly I think I should explain what the game is, its an early access version of a hard sci fi colony sim, very similar in play style to Dungeon Keep. It features I.M.P that are robot versions of imps from Dungeon Keep, they will mine what you select for mining. Your colonists build your rooms and items in them, as well as grow crops, research and all that jazz. Maia is also hard sci fi, the colonists sweat and burn calories when working, the more calories they burn the more food they need to eat. All this is simulated in the game, so you need to get your food correct and it takes time to grow so planning and learning is needed.
Lots of updates to the game since it launched on early access, there is at least 1 sizeable update a month. Its is very stable at the moment, runs very well and no major crashes. Its very much an alive game.
The AI has been improved drastically in the last few updates, they no longer seem to want to die, still a way to go with them, but they are very much do what you think they would at the moment.
The UI is the biggest stumbling block in the game. I kinda like it, but I can understand people that don't. Its very hands off, you know what is going on by seeing it. If a colonist is shivering and you see their breath, then the air is cold. You know the air quality of a room by screens that can be built, there is no overlay or any information readily available to the player.
Also in the construction menu, there are no images, you have to scroll through a list of options with the keyboard, its easy to miss things. I would like a slide out panel that had images and you can select it but you get used to the way of it soon enough.

I'm really enjoying this game. It has some issues, but what game doesn't?
The lack of a tutorial is kind of lame, so you spend the first hour clicking on everything randomly. The game is pretty straight forward once you get the layout figured out.
The visuals are nice, but kind of looks like it was intended for console; having full controller support makes me wonder even more.
The control scheme is very basic, which is nice for time when you just want to lean back and not worry about the keyboard for a while, controlling most basic functions with just the mouse. Its a beer sipping game at times :)
Combat requires both hands lol
Combat is fun, though, dizzying at times from spinning circles around enemies; keeping them on your side for your broadside attacks.
Not only can you destroy pirates, but you can also capture thier ships and add them to your AI driven team/ floatilla.
The game has an RPG style talent tree to make different builds for different styles of play (Think Borderlands skill trees).
Lots of different colors and emblems to pimp your ship and sail out with.
You equip items to your ship like it is your character, like new sails to go faster, armor to protect you from damage, crew to make you better at shooting enemies, etc. All i nall, theres 10-12 items you equip on your ship, then 4 vanity slots for 3 colors and an emblem. The equipable items are typical rarity leveled (White, green, blue, etc.)
I'm only about 5 hours into the game, so I've only seen the ability to buy 4 different ships, though the videos I've watched show way different ships than what I have available, leaving me to safely assume there is more ships as you progress through the "character" levels, and find bigger towns.
The quests the towns provide are fun, but run into the problem of not being varried enough after a few maps: Place a turret here, ferry these people here, buy this stock and make a profit here, and a handful of other pirate elimination/ capture quests. There are lots of random quest drops that add a little flavor into the game, though usually its just bring this scroll you found to this place for a few resources and/or money.
The music is good enough to not be too distracting while playing, where as the sound effects are needed to be turned down for WHAT?! lol jk The sound effects/ ambient sound is great, but a little on the loud side when using headphones.
The worlds you play on are sectioned out by level, so you know where to avoid. Good size maps in each section of the world, leaving you hours of gameplay in each area.
Random pirate attacks on the map you're curently on and have full control over are fun, and keep you on your toes.
I'm almost at 1:1 hours played to Dollars spent, and enjoying it more than I have with some triple A titles that I've spent over $60 on recently, and have almost beaten (storyline) in less that 25 hours...
There is multiplayer and co-op, which I haven't tried out yet.
--TL;DR--
8.5/10 good fun.
There is a possibility of a 9-9.5 if the multiplayer/ co-op is good
All in all, I can say I'm not disappointed with buying this game. Even at its full price of $14.99, I would've bought it; though I caught it on sale for $4.94

What this game is missing from being as great, is a lot more types of Ship Weaponry, Ship types, and just content overall. The main premise of the game is just killing random pirates which ends up being waaaay too repetetive fast due to the lack of changes or abilities your ship gains throughout leveling up. Level 1 to level 50, and youre still just shooting exactly like you was back at the beginning of the game. Speaking of leveling, the currency and XP grind is insanely in-human, asking for 100's of hours grinding on the same brickwall with your brain, its not fun to add a huge grindwall to a game which lacks any content. Is it worth the current price of £11($15)? NO. Far from it, because theres quite literally no depth or content or ship upgrade differences in the game. Its a barebones game.
BUT in the future? MAYBE but work needs to be done here.
This engine is fantastic, the loot system is very well done, all the building blocks are here for an amazing game to be made within it, all it needs is more development, and to be packed with a lot more types of weaponry and enemies.
Windward has HUGE potential, but right now its like an empty sandbox with lack of choice of activity. Its a shame to see a good pirate-combat engine, NOT USED to anywhere near its actual potential.
My Strong Recommendations to the devs:
-1. Go crazy with this game by adding tonnes of weapon types, i dont care if you add tesla coils, flamethrowers, freeze rays or rocket launchers. Go nuts! Basic cannons get old very quickly. Watch how popular this game gets when you do.
-2. Drop the Skill Tree, limiting powers and weapon types to a Skill Tree cripples your games potential by forcing harshe limitations and one-way choices.
-3. XP and Gold are too cruel of a grind in this game, you've got to increase Gold/XP gain significantly. I havent played too much and im already feeling burned out on a game i dont want to feel burned out on.
-4. Allow Guard Towers to be upgraded (possibly into different types of tower aswell), i know this isnt a Moba type game but currently these towers have absolutely no hope of defending anything, ships can regen faster than towers do damage, meaning that they quite literally do ZERO damage.
-5. Add ability for Towns to have a militia which can fight back against invasions (sometimes you may need 2 or 3 ships to overwhelm a town), it's too easy for 1 stray ship to go around stealing towns un-challenged as the rest of the ships fight, its not just cowardly behaviour, but its punishing players who are giving the most effort and rewarding players for not fighting at all.
Show this game some love, i WANT to recommend this game because the potential is there.

Rust... This game is simultaneously one of the best games I've ever played and one of the most egregious examples of the villainy I've ever experienced. The community is both hostile and welcoming. The creators both receptive and stubborn. It's friggin’ fantastic!
Rust is a post-apocalyptic game where survivors pillage for resources. Occasionally you'll find a friend and roam the landscape together working to rebuild civility to a marred world, doing the work of the enlightened. Then, two seconds later, you'll get rolled over by a clan with a superiority complex. Fantastic open world game by Avalanche Studios, made with the license of Mad Max Fury Road (the new one with Tom Hardy).
The game looks great while running at a stable 120fps on max settings. The game sounds fantastic (especially the motors/exhausts and explosions) and has good audio settings (device, speaker type, dynamics).
The vehicular combat is innovative (deeper than RAGE) and fun. Melee combat is Arkham style but a bit harder since you can't automatically parry every direction and the camera is a bit closer, you need to actually press the direction + parry button, which means you shouldn't get surrounded.
Voice artist for main sidekick 'Chumbucket' is amazing, sounds just like the movie.
I wish the game had more vehicular combat, as the regular combat is kinda boring.
Similar to Shadow of Mordor, the wonder wore off after some repetition. I 100% cleared the first area, 80% cleared the second, ~40% cleared the third and don't give a rats♥♥♥♥♥about the fourth.
There are strongholds in each area and you can unlock buildings there which replenish your resources, but unlocking this multiple times is too much of a hassle. I'd rather fast travel to a fully upgraded stronghold and then fast travel back to another one.
It's unfulfilling that most of the income is passive through unlocked camps. The only other big income are Scrapulances (special rare vehicles full of scrap which have to be driven to a stronghold) and scrap pallets during storms. Both of these are unreliable.
The scrap rewards during normal gameplay do not scale. This is ok since scaling rewards would be unrealistic and wouldn't work that well with an open game world. The passive income scales naturally, but this also means that it eclipses all other sources of scrap.
Is this a design weakness or a design strength?
I've played so much that I don't want to pick up every single piece of scrap.
The camps got repetitive, so I stopped doing those. I'm a bit disappointed in the boss fights, they're very simplistic and samey.
I'd rather have had more vehicular boss fights than melee ones.
I'm giving it a thumbs up since it's great during the first third and it's normal for games in this genre to get repetitive after a while. For my taste, these games should be shorter, but there have to be people who like the "extra content".

It's no secret I love the Shantae series, and I've been waiting for this game to come out since I seen the kickstarter page. Now its out and it time to see if it was worth the wait.
Story: Shantae Half-Genie Hero take place after the events of Shantae Pirate's Curse but if you haven't played it don't worry. The game stand on it own.
Shantae is the guardian genie of the town and spend her days solving problems and stopping pirates. After a strange dream followed by a pirate attack, Shantae set off again to save her town.
The story is straight forward. Not as much character development as previous games, but it felt like a good game for new players to jump onto the franchise.
Gameplay: Shantae can jump and hair whip her opponents into submission. As a Genie she can dance and transform into various creatures to gain access to new areas. You can buy upgrades for Shantae hair whip at the item shop and also buy magic spells. The magic spells have always seem to break the game. If you're a completionist  than you're going to upgrade all your magic and with magic that can make you invulnerable, well let just say some bosses become a cake walk. But they give you option in the menu to disable any upgrade if you feel the game is too easy.
Final Comment: Shantae: Half-Genie Hero is a good game for new players to start at, and veterans will be glad to see the return of loved characters. If you like platformers than Shantae: Half-Genie will grant one of your wishes.

I was initially turned off from this game due to the massive amounts of hype it got, but I have to admit it's a brilliant, thoroughly enjoyable game.
The story is simple and episodic in nature, but this isn't necessarily a bad things, as the game is able to focus more on the characters. The characters are easily the best part of this game. I completely fell in love with Sans, Papyrus, Toriel, and Asgore almost immediately. And even the characters that I wasn't completely impressed with at first- such as Alphys and Mettaton- eventually grew on me. I loved the puzzle aspects of the game- not necessarily the puzzles themselves (those are decent, but nothing I haven't seen before) but the process of figuring out how to befriend each and every monster you come across. The soundtrack is absolutely amazing. And no other game has affected me emotionally in the way this game did.
That's not to say the game is perfect. Most of my problems with the game are tiny nitpicks (like the game's obsession with long, dramatic hallways, and sometimes the game gets a little heavy-handed and a bit too meta for my liking), but my biggest issue with this game is the Genocide route. It's completely inferior to the other routes of the game- needlessly repetitive, completely heavy-handed about the point it's trying to make, and since most enemies die in one hit, the combat has zero depth (outside of a couple bosses, which are, admittedly, really cool). And yeah, you could make the argument that the game did that on purpose to make a point, but that's no excuse to purposefully make questionable design choices for the sake of the narrative.
So is it flawless? No. I feel the same way about Undertale as I do Final Fantasy VI- I can see a bunch of problems with it, but the good stuff is just so good, it makes the entire thing worth it. So please, PLEASE don't write this game off due to the obnoxiousness of the fanbase. Like I said, that initially turned me off, but I gave it a go anyway and I'm so glad I did.

I've honestly put enough hours into this game now that I can't really remember how it was starting out. It's definitely been fun, regardless.
The game is definitely best played with friends, otherwise you probably won't have much drive to keep playing past the 10-15 hour mark.
Nothing here but sharks.
Keep in mind that this is definitely designed as a time killer, and as such you'll be repeating *ALOT* of content. Despite that, the game has enough variety in quests and combat to keep you interested.
The best part about this game is you can legitimately play it effectively in a variety of ways. You can take up quests to deliver supplies/people, hunt down and defeat pirate lords, smuggle supplies, build towns/defenses, etc. Everything nets you experience and gold to advance in the game.
If you dont like the idea of combat or questing, you can also become a trader and run around the world(s) buying and selling to get your money and experience.
And if neither of those are for you, you'll still be able to just roam around the world and fight with pirates, factions and other players over control of the worlds regions.
It's loot system is similar to games like diablo, aka, color code loot quality and number statistics. You'll also find items to customize the coloration of your ship, in addition to being able to buy completely new styles of ships once you find their blueprints and save up enough gold.
The combat in the game seemingly simple, and for the most part it is. You'll have to rely on proper positioning and the use of your abilities to win or escape any fights you get into.
You'll definitely find a new appreciation for naval combat after playing this game.
Graphics are definitely where the game is lacking, but it also doesn't need them to be good.
Models: The models are actually well done, for what they are. From the "sloop" to the "clipper", every ship has a unique enough style and quality to it that makes it pleasant to look at, no matter how simple the games graphics are.
Textures: I don't have issues with the textures on the ships, the towns, the towers, water, or anything else... But the ground terrain is definitely lacking. But, since its a game about being a ship captain, that's definitely nothing to worry about. Regardless, you'll notice it from time to time.
Environment: I'm not really sure what to say for this... water? There's water. There's alot of water, everywhere. Sometimes there's an island or a continent. It's nothing that makes you joyous and some of the randomly generated maps will likely make you angry, but that's what you have explosive barrels for... It might be costly, but you'll be able to turn that mountain into another few fathoms of ocean.
Overall, for a time killer game, the graphics are exactly what you'd expect and exactly what they need to be, honestly.
I honestly don't know how to describe the sounds. They have no bass to them, so they never really stand out from eachother... any of them.
The fire barrels crackle like real fire does, cannons sound like cannons, crew members shout when raiding towns or towers... Without any depth to the sound, it's significantly lackluster.
I actually stopped playing with the majority of the sound, dropping it to 20% volume and just listening to my own music in the background. The game doesn't sound bad, it just doesn't really have anything I want to hear... especially for the millionth time.
What they have "works", but it *DEFINITELY* could be improved.
The game has enough content to work towards to keep you going, especially if you're into games that make you grind for really good gear. Regardless, play it in moderation if you want to keep coming back. Finding a few friends to play with helps alot, too.
You'll get significantly more longevity out of this game if you treat it like an android or Iphone app. Otherwise, if you're really into pirates, play all day every day.
I've been looking for a "time-killer" game, something really simple to play that can be mastered with a bit of effort. I've also been looking for something that has some social aspect to it, and this satisfies everything I've wanted.
As far as socializing in it, it's by no means a game you're going to go into and make a ton of new friends everyday, but you'll definitely be able to convince some people you already know to play with you have and fun together.
This is a game in the same style as Mount & Blade, it is what you make it. Don't play it to the "beating a dead horse" point and you'll be having mindless fun for a long time.

Is this a good game? Yes.
Is this a great game? No.
Should you buy this game? Yes.
Pros:
+ For the size of the download this game is beautiful
+ Easy to control and get into right away
+ Trading system not overly complex and easy to use
+ Get 4 or 5 ships to buy right off the bat
+ Starting your own towns is fun and easy
+ Enemy AI is pretty good
+ Lots and lots of area to explore (but broken up)
+ Quests fairly easy to accomplish
+ Easy upgrade system to follow though needs refinement
+ Love the color/pattern sails, hulls, etc - more of thise would be great
Cons (wishlist):
- Friendly AI is terrible - they run into you constantly - stand there and get shot - don't use water cannons effectively,etc
- Enemies get ridiculously powerful as you level up - Captains and newer factions will beat you senseless
- Hard to determine if something is a true upgrade or not
- Repetitive quests (but somehow not that annoying)
- Other human players are fairly scarce - on our server there are generally 3-5 on at any time
- Very simple game - not much depth past the surface
- The game could use a 'simple to learn but complex to master' sort of update
- More elaborate diplomacy would be nice
- More unit customization (though good now) would be nice
- Storyline quests would be excellent
- Land battles would be awesome to take towns
- Establishing a pirate cove would be awesome
Overall a very solid game for the money. Excellent work dev(s)! Ill keep checking back for updates and play it on a somewhat regular basis. Reminds me of games like Pirates! Port Royale, etc.

This game is worth the 20$ I spent.
I'm a Huge fan of the new visuals. Shantae's model is adorable...well all the female characters are adorable both their models and illustrations. It's so clean, crisp, and very colorful. With this new style, details like facial expression are very easy to see on these new models. Every character looks amazing. The characters/items really standout from the background. So it doesn't matter if you are playing this on a teeny tiny screen or your 55" screen in the family room, it's going to look great.
The game ran smoothly.Everything Shantae does looks good. Same goes for enemies. There were some hiccups, not like lag or anything but some blinks of color in spots of the screen. This could be fault with something in the game or something on my end.
The levels were well designed. Many of them seem to be designed for several ways of navigation up until end in the event you miss some transformation or moves hidden along the way. On the topic of transformations. I enjoyed all but one, the one I'd have to say it is nothing more than a joke.
I found the levels to be moderately difficult and some small spots kind of hard. Part of me wishes most was hard but at the same time given the number of times I treked back and forth in levels, I think perhaps moderate is for the best. If you are into time trials be it just finishing as fast as possible, getting all unlocks, or going for 100%(buying all shop items) There levels are large enough that they take a good amount of memorization and creativity to navigate them as quickly/efficiently as possible.
This game also rewards those have keen eyes for finding things in the levels/taking the time to get them. I found the Mermaid level to be my favorite level. Lots of jumps, its really big. Really pretty and cute. Spoiler, don't read unless you played game
The last game's levels were bigger and everything was conencted. There was a lot more exploring. I really liked that bout the last game. I could care less for it all being connected but I really love big levels that can be explored because it really makes you feel like you found stuff rather than it just being inevitable that you'd come across it.
I feel like Shantae's amazing hairproducts overshadowed the offensive spells, fire and electricity a bit. I would wager that if there were no basic atk upgrades that the fire and lightning spells would feel very relevant. In contrast to the shield and pike(swirling DPS) which can be used with your basic atks. Nonetheless its good to have variety. xD I almost never found out what they were because the last game stuff like that were consumables rather than learned abilities lol.
I ended up getting all of the acheivements for this game. I beat it 3 times. 1st playthrough was 7hrs long 100%. The 2nd was 3hrs20min long, 100%, while the 3rd was 2hrs 14min 88%. The game was really enjoyable. I did leave wanting more. i felt that it was a bit short. Honestly I think whether it was a legit 20hr+ game or not, I'd still be left wanting. I'm looking forward to Risky's DLC which gives her, her very own campaign and unique abilities. So I will definitely be playing that whenever it comes out.
Unfortunately I wasn't a backer because it ended by the time I even learned of this game. Seeing some of the other stretch goals really makes me pray this game does well and perhaps does some of them.
Playing as Rottytops, Sky, or Bolo all with their own unique moves sounds amazing. A new chapter (who doesn't love more playable content.) Lastly animated cutscenes that are fully voice....................*drools*
Realistically I hope for the chapter and characters the most.The stretch goals that were not met I'd definitely pay for if they were DLC.
So my only 2 real complaints are these.
1 I already covered, I wish the game was longer.
2 I wish some of the transformations we gained had more time to shine with much larger parts of the levels dedicated to them. Some of them were pretty neglected.
*3 need more Mermaids.
All in all this a great game that I would recommend getting. I hope it does well and that they support it in the future.

Best purchase of 2017. Just finished Episode 3 and I have.. feelings. That's what makes a story-driven game great, doesn't it? And, besides the beautifully drawn characters, the fantastic music and everything we already know from the first Life is Strange game, this game made me value life even more. Value having someone next to you even more.
Technically the game is not perfect. They used Unity engine which has some quirks on non-16:9 screens, or they forgot to animate things here and there, but nothing outstanding. The game is as beautiful as the first one, great voice acting, nice music. And feelings.
The only reason when you should not pick it up is if you're not into story-driven decision-making games. Otherwise get it, you won't regret it. I almost added "Telltale-like" but I realized I should not. In Telltale's otherwise wonderful Walking Dead, you will get a prompt like "John will remember this". 30 seconds later John (or whatever the name might be) is dead by plot. Nice 30 seconds rememberance. Here your decisions actually matter. Here, just deciding the fate of a little bracelet in Episode 2 can determine the outcome in the ending cutscene. You cannot stop destiny from being fulfilled, but you can make someone really happy. You can have someone who truly loves you. You can be the only honest person in someone's life. Or you can join to the club by hoping to spare her from the truth and feel remorse by doing so.
Too much talking. Get this game, free up your night or sit with your SO and play it. One episode each, from start to finish, without looking up anything.

A very lukewarm recommendation as in almost every way, this is a step back from the first game. The story feels rushed in the second half, and the ending is underwhelming. Choices matter about as much as they do in Life is Strange, that is to say not in any significant way outside of a few bonus scenes and the endings. The soundtrack isn't as diverse as before, and the art style tries to mimic the hand-drawn textures of Life is Strange by having everything looking low-quality and blurry. Most disappointing of all is the replacement for the time-travel mechanic, Backtalk, which strips away what little gameplay this franchise had and replaces it with a dialogue mini-game which only felt satisfying in a few very minor conversations.
Still, there were enough moments in the episodes to hold my attention
, and a few sequences were genuinely entertaining and/or impactful. Before the Storm wasn't a story that needed to be told, but it's interesting enough for anyone who enjoyed the first game and fans of story-driven games.

Probably the most compelling story in a video game that I've played.
Spec Ops puts the player through a lot of action sequences typical for modern warfare shooters and then rubs in your face how horrible you are for enjoying it. It was genuinely disconcerting at times to play as a soldier suffering from PTSD who struggles to convince himself (or maybe the player, the game self-consciously breaks the fourth wall at times) that he's a hero and not a monster fighting through his own hell.
I wouldn't call Spec Ops "fun" on any level, but it's a game that really stuck with me. I'd recommend it to anyone looking for more than mindless action or fun adventuring in a video game.

As a passionate gamer for over fifteen years, Spec Ops: The line has some of the most emotionally gripping gameplay I have ever seen. The game starts as any other generic shooter does, you have your proto-typical "small team vs. a big army", with your standard AI classes-the grunts, the guys with knives that run at you, the big heavy guys with machineguns, etc. You think to yourself "So what's the big deal? In no time I'll be mowing through them like a superhero badass." It tricks you into believing it is something totally familiar, then hits you like a cannon shell. While other games have featured "the horrors of war" as a thematic element, this game is one of the few that manages to transcend the boundary from simply affecting the CHARACTER to fully affecting you as a PLAYER. Without spoiling anything, the situations you face during the game will not leave you feeling like a hero. You will not feel invincible. You will not feel the same. By the time the game was over, I felt emotionally distraught. That's the only way I can describe it.
There is, however, one bone I have to pick with this game. The controls are at times unresponsive, and I died numerous times simply because I had difficulty ordering my squad around or performing mission-critical actions. Because, by default, the "take cover" and "sprint" keys are the same, your character will often do the opposite of what you need to do to survive a particularly difficult encounter (run straight towards an enemy instead of hide behind a wall, etc) and attempting take cover near the corner of an object will often see you taking cover on the wrong side, getting you shot in the back. The checkpoint system at times also feels a little inconsistent, sometimes autosaving after every small fight, and sometimes throwing you back to the beginning of a long section of gameplay, creating a few frustrating moments. However, the merits of this game more than compensate for its faults, and honestly, for anyone who's ever played a generic shooter in the history of forever, these are not problems which leave us shocked and totally blindsided, unlike the wonderful story.

This game is very compelling. It's one part Civilization, one part SPAZ, with a dash of Diablo for good measure, all wrapped in a charming Pirates of the Caribbean-esque theme. I don't want to quit playing it, such that my first session was 13+ hours long.
The commissions have the "just... one... more..." that you'd expect from a turn based game (exept that this one is real time), and has manual sailing, including combat, that gives the battles an epic, yet tactical flavour that keeps me spoiling for my next pirate attack. The ship you command even has a number of "slots" that you can upgrade with better items, such as improved hull, better sails, stronger cannons and ammo, and even crew and captain, all of which are randomly acquired Diablo style, by completing commissions, as the spoils of war, or even randomly floating in crates in the sea.
In a nutshell, it's a lot of fun, and I find it very relaxing to play. That said, I do have a few complaints, though minor.
While the ocean graphics are quite nice and detailed, much of the land scenery looks really chunky by comparison. The rocks aren't too bad, but the trees have a decidedly decade-old look.
Sailing into the wind, while realistic, is frustratingly slow. It feels like whenever you need to be somewhere, especially in a hurry, the wind turns against you. Could be my imagination, but it grows tiresome at times.
During instanced missions, you can freely use powderkegs to blast shallows and narrow land bridges asunder, but so far, I have not found a way to do this in the course of normal gameplay. That's unfortunate.
The map view and trading systems could use some quality-of-life polish, to make it easier to see who needs what commodities at a glance. It would also be nice if you could gather rumours about where to go for commodities that you can't get in your local region. It would also be nice to have an idea of what can be found where based on the climate. I know that you'll figure this out with time, but I'd like to see it on the map.
I'd like to see some DLC that adds a little more depth to the trading, diplomacy, and city building aspects of the game. You can already buy off neutral captains to turn them into temporary allies, but it would be nice if it were possible to buy other factions' cities out from under them, and use money and / or diplomacy to bend more trade deals in your favour, like being able to establish a monopoly, or add tarriffs, etc.
There are a ton of shipwrecks dotting the map, and it would be cool if you could salvage them, outside of specific missions that require you to do so.
Pretty minor complaints. This game is good. I recommend it. But it has the potential to be even better, and I'd like to see that happen, even as paid DLC.

This game IS amazing!
Note, I have not played any previous KLEI titles, so I shall base my opinion purely on this game alone.
The artstyle. Man is it gorgeous. I know this is typical of KLEI, however it truly is a very well done and unique artstyle. Fans of Don't Starve I'm sure will not be disappointed.
The gameplay. It's fun, engaging, thought provoking and best of all, challenging! People who love building, strategy and management games will love this gameplay. It's fluid and keeps you on your toes. The nature of the game means you can go from a stable and prosperous situation to completely FUBAR in seconds flat. You really need to think about what you will allocate time and resources to, and think ahead several moves. The resources are all finite, so you will constantly have to be on the lookout for ways to obtain more. Managing your duplicants vitalities is also rewarding and engaging.
The idea. While not completely original, it does have it's own unique twist on things, and is refreshing in our oversaturated gaming marketplace.
The performance. Naturally it's not demanding, and it will run well on almost any system.
The experience. Simply put, incredible. It's great to be able to sit down and relax for a few hours, and just play this game. I find it difficult to become so immersed with a game, however this game pulls me in effortlessly (I have played many an hour offline, do not take my hours as an indication at all). This is one of those games that makes you say: "where did the time go?" when you look at the clock after a session of playing.
Most of my playtime was during the alpha so far, the game does run out of things to do relatively quickly.
Not really a huge complaint, and one I'm sure the devs are working on, but I would like to see more customization options when building, like wall colour etc etc.
That's it!

Post script: Feel free to ask me any questions in the comment section of this, or better, in my comments section on my profile. I shall also update this review as time passes and more content is added.
It has been several months now since I posted my initial review of Oxygen not Included.
Just as expected, the game has continued with it's path of progression in many ways. New fundamental aspects of the duplicants now need to be managed, such as a much more comprehensive disease and health system, wherein unhealthy surroundings will now induce various diseases if the duplicant has a weak immune system.
Item wise things have also progressed. There are now many more ways in which to generate electricity, and more ways in which to use it. The introduction of logic gates is a very progressive step for the game, leading (I hope) to many more complex systems being able to be developed further on. (I say this because at the moment the logic gates have limited application, however there is massive potential here).
The latest update has also added a fast alternative to transport (a tube type system allowing for duplicants to quickly traverse areas, very much needed to allow for more exploration and expansion).
So all is good and dandy? Not quite. There is still very little incentive to expand your colony past it's state of equilibrium (a state reached after not too many hours of play, where your colony is stable and runs itself). There is just nothing else to it, which is fine as this is still very much in beta, however it is important to note, it's very much a self motivation game. The progression of your colony is not really encouraged by the game. I trust fully that more objectives will eventually be added, more rewards for exploration and maybe more of a story?
So, in it's current state (on 16/12/2017), this game still recieves a definite reccomendation from me, as the devs continually update the game and add new mechanics and items to play around with, however I do encourage potential buyers to keep in mind the lack of real objectives and the fact that self motivation is a must. Beyond that, it's a fantastic survival, strategy and management game.

I was initially turned off from this game due to the massive amounts of hype it got, but I have to admit it's a brilliant, thoroughly enjoyable game.
The story is simple and episodic in nature, but this isn't necessarily a bad things, as the game is able to focus more on the characters. The characters are easily the best part of this game. I completely fell in love with Sans, Papyrus, Toriel, and Asgore almost immediately. And even the characters that I wasn't completely impressed with at first- such as Alphys and Mettaton- eventually grew on me. I loved the puzzle aspects of the game- not necessarily the puzzles themselves (those are decent, but nothing I haven't seen before) but the process of figuring out how to befriend each and every monster you come across. The soundtrack is absolutely amazing. And no other game has affected me emotionally in the way this game did.
That's not to say the game is perfect. Most of my problems with the game are tiny nitpicks (like the game's obsession with long, dramatic hallways, and sometimes the game gets a little heavy-handed and a bit too meta for my liking), but my biggest issue with this game is the Genocide route. It's completely inferior to the other routes of the game- needlessly repetitive, completely heavy-handed about the point it's trying to make, and since most enemies die in one hit, the combat has zero depth (outside of a couple bosses, which are, admittedly, really cool). And yeah, you could make the argument that the game did that on purpose to make a point, but that's no excuse to purposefully make questionable design choices for the sake of the narrative.
So is it flawless? No. I feel the same way about Undertale as I do Final Fantasy VI- I can see a bunch of problems with it, but the good stuff is just so good, it makes the entire thing worth it. So please, PLEASE don't write this game off due to the obnoxiousness of the fanbase. Like I said, that initially turned me off, but I gave it a go anyway and I'm so glad I did.

Absolutely loved this game, the soundtrack is amazing and a fun and sometimes challenging platformer, if you are looking for a good old fashion platformer with a twist then this game is for you, a bunch of new features such as *SPOILERS* transformations and magical abilities that keeps the gameplay feeling fresh, even when previous levels have to be scoured through many times over.

If you want to play this game because of the Metroidvania style of the previous games in the series, prepare to be disappointed. But not in a bad way, by any means. This game is something else rather, more of a cross between Megaman X  and old-school Castlevania.
Areas are broken up into fairly linear levels that must be re-played when you unlock more abilities in order to explore various branching paths previously unavailable to you on the first run. However, you're never forced to play any stage from beginning to end more than once, as you can get the ability to warp between all 3 parts of level and also drop out of the level at any time, keeping whatever new items you've grabbed. While it sounds a bit tedious to backtrack, the aforementioned warping plus the added mobility of your new transformation abilities really cut down on the time it takes to backtrack.
The story plays out like a day in the life of Shantae, with all the offbeat humor and cute babes intact from the rest of the series. It's nothing revolutionary, but it makes a lot of shout outs for longtime fans of the series, in addition to serving as a great introduction to the world of sequin land for those who haven't played Shantae before.
Overall, it's a fun game with loads of speedrunning potential. It would be apt to compare it to something like a theme park ride. A rather long wait for an ultimately short experience, but with theming and entertainment so good, I can't help but want to go again sometime later. Speaking of which, I'm looking forward to the upcoming DLC for Risky mode + Sky/Bolo/Rotty mode, which should further add replayability to this joyride of a game.

To all the backers of Shantae: Half-Genie Hero, thank you for all of your support! I would have happily joined you had I known how awesome the Shantae series was, but I came late into the game, and it was only shortly after the campaign ended did I take the time to enjoy Risky's Revenge and The Pirate Curse. Playing those two games, I've come to expect a lot from this series in terms of its artstyle, soundtrack, and gameplay. Needless to say, this game has exceeded some of my expectations while underwhelming others.
Right away you can tell this game is beautifully drawn and the characters are well animated. The colours, the movement, and even the backgrounds are vibrant and beaming of life. I don't usually pay attention to backgrounds, but I can see how much time and attention has gone into them along with the smooth character animations.
Although most of the music is rearranged and redone, the Shantae soundtrack continues to match the levels and the dialogue moods perfectly. None of the new music really stands out as super catchy and memorable, but when they are used for specific moments and levels, it composed well enough to immerse you into the situation.
As much as I love the aesthetics for this game, I feel like the gameplay has taken a stepback. A lot of long times fans come to expect a more Metroidvania kind of structure to the levels and worlds, and for me this more level select method is a better for backtracking. There were times in previous games where I just got lost easily and felt like some stages lost their importance after a while.
Thankfully the levels are all simply structured to have three stages each, along with a few obstacles you can't get past until you earn an animal transformation. I can see they wanted to focus on the use of them along with making the game more accessible to newcomers.
So while the puzzles and extra sections are a ton of fun to figure out in terms of using the right transformations and abilities, I feel like the selection of transformations was overwhelming. There were too many transformations that could have been consolidated into less animals with more abilities as opposed to one animal with one unique ability each. I get excited learning a new ability and this game didn't seem to reward my experience as much as I'd like because you barely ever get to use your new abilities that often except for maybe one or two situations that call for them.
All in all though, I still had a ton of fun with this beautifully designed platformer. I patiently wait for the DLC that is already available for backers *shakes fist* and look forward to more of what WayForward can come up with in the future.
I give this game a solid 7/10. The art, music, and levels are well crafted. Learning and using new abilities felt underwhelming when they were horribly underused, but the game makes up for some of these flaws for having a decent level of difficulty in puzzle solving and its exciting boss battles.
On top of all that, I know that Shantae stories are usually meant to be light hearted and on the Saturday Morning cartoon side, I still can't help but feel like there could have been more to it than what was presented. There were moments where the story could have had some strong themes elaborated on.
But I digress. Gameplay is king in Shantae games and having the story skimped out on is not a huge loss since they're not usually known for their stories alone. All in all a fun and exciting game that is good for its length and what it offers. Replayability is debatable and more geared towards a speed run, but we shall see what gets add for DLC later on!

Spec Ops: The Line is a very difficult game to give a binary "Yes" or "No" reccomendation to. This is mainly because it doesn't provide what many seek from a video game. The gameplay mechanics are average at best, with very few thrills to speak of. It's just not very fun to play.
However that's kind of what makes the game special, as these mechanics inform the story in both compelling and disturbing ways. Spec Ops: The Line is less a video game and more of an interactive art piece, with its main focus being on you, the player. It disects the modern military shooter in a very damning fashion and questions whether we should be feeling catharsis from carrying out acts of violence on our fellow man. It takes a scalpel to our power fantasies and makes you uncomfortable for having them. It's a thought provoking narrative, expertly constructed to deliver gut punch after another and is an experience that will leave you drained and probably much more cynical towards the next installment of "Call Of Duty".

When I first saw the Mad Max movie I immediately wanted to take part in the wasteland that was the Mad Max world. Seeing this game and all the reviews and play throughs I felt like this game would give me the experience I wanted. This game did exactly that. You can get this game for a very cheap price of $10 and for that price, its one of the best games you can get. It was a joy to play and it kept me occupied for a very long time. The game just felt right and when I was done, I felt satisfied. Its a good game to keep you occupied and for $10 you really can't go wrong.
The overall game mechanics are very fine tuned and responsive. The upgrades for your cars actually makes a difference and having the right ones that fit your play style really makes a difference. This isn't a game where you can just slap on all of the best mods on to your car. This game simply just doesn't work like that. There are some situations where you want speed and other times you need a solid tank. With the variety of modifications available, you can achieve all of that and explore and branch out.
The fighting in this game is so so satisfying. Its so easy to fight off hoards of War Boys coming after you and the counters are just a joy to execute. The weapon selection in this game is some what lacking but generally fighting with your two fists are just way more "brolic and manly". The sounds of your fist slamming against a War Boy's jaw never gets old. Later on in the game you can upgrade your fighting skills and pretty much your a walking killing machine. Its one of instances where you want a whole bunch of War Boys to swarm you so you can clobber them.
I felt like the story was decent. In my opinion it tried to fit the persona of the original Mad Max and I think it does a good enough job. Its not phenomenal and at times it gets a little boring but it really picks up at the end. Its really straight forward and quite fast if you have all the upgrades and requirements completed ahead of time. Overall, it was a some what short story line that got right to the point.
When I first ran into a bug, I found out that this game had a history of bugs during their initial release. Those have been addressed by now but it does give you an idea of the bugs in this game. Needless to say, I didn't find any game breaking bugs. Once in a while, your HUD might glitch out, a mission won't show up, an icon won't show up on your world map, etc. A simple restart will fix this but it can get annoying. I didn't run into that many bugs so I won't complain to much on that.
Scrap in this game is the currency and you need a whole lot of it. Scrap is the one thing that keeps the players occupied other then the story. The story doesn't have that many requirements but it becomes increasingly difficult if you don't have the right upgrades. Near the end of the game, scrap becomes easier to obtain due to some "perks" you can get but other then that, the first part was a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ Upgrades aren't cheap either so its gonna be a grind for some. It doesn't take away from the game but it is mildly annoying.
Game is too repetitive and boring. I completed the first area and lost motivation to even continue the game. The combat is a highlight in the game, but overall, there are better games out there.

This game, in terms of gameplay feels like Shadow of Mordor, for the ground fights at least. Unfortunatly the fights aren't really well designed and you often end up just mashig the left mouse button and occasionnally the right one when the game tells you to do so. There is some contextual actions, like shield-bashing, disarming, etc, but those actions are basically just pressing a button at a precise time (with a rather weird time window). The survival system, relying on keeping water to healk you, and fuel for your car, is a good idea but works poorly, because far too permissive.
Now, about the car, which is a main part of the gameplay, well, it's not bad, but not good either, the car does not feel really good, but car battles are something quite fun, if a little boring in the end. The customization, sadly, is pretty poor and consist of just upgrading each part of your car without having real choice to do, and it just seem too artificial. It's even worse for max, where the only possible choice is levlling up each items he wear, to just make them better (using scrap, kek). And the customization via levels feels really poorly designed.
The story isn't really crazy, and suffers from some lazyness in some character designs, which are poor (hello top dogs recolors) or not developed enough. The main feminine char is really cliché and her story with max is telegraphed as♥♥♥♥♥ (The two others you can meet aren't that bad, tho).
Where the game really stands out, for me, is that the world around you is quite well thought and graphically really nice (in terms of art), There is really some beautiful views, and tons of good screenshot to make for sure. The camps you have to destroy in order to progress and the stonghold you can rest in are not bad, but sometimes (especially for camps), feels just like a lazy attempt to create a maze, while some others are pretty well thought.
Overall :
Pros :
-Good World Design
-Car Battles
-Beautiful Areas
-Some background to discover thoughout the game about the world.
-Technically Working. (Yes I'm looking at you, XCOM 2)
-Explosions.
Cons :
-Car Driving could have been better
-Sound Design (really boring in the end)
-Upgrade System (no real choice)
-Survival System (not evry deep)
Meh :
-Fighting System
-Story

Rust... This game is simultaneously one of the best games I've ever played and one of the most egregious examples of the villainy I've ever experienced. The community is both hostile and welcoming. The creators both receptive and stubborn. It's friggin’ fantastic!
Rust is a post-apocalyptic game where survivors pillage for resources. Occasionally you'll find a friend and roam the landscape together working to rebuild civility to a marred world, doing the work of the enlightened. Then, two seconds later, you'll get rolled over by a clan with a superiority complex. Meanwhile, a solo player has been farming for days, has managed to twig raid into the clan's main loot room and blow up the whole works. It's chaos and order, dancing as one in the fires of a beautiful hell.
So, if you want to murder nakeds for no reason of a 300+ server, this is the game for you. If you want to grind alone on a dead server with no mods to be seen, this is the game for you. It is a social experiment gone array, Stanford Prison to epic proportions. Glorious and tragic.

At level 50 and above, the pirates start spawning in great numbers, versus the 4 allies that spawn, 5 minutes intervals between them.

There's almost no distinction between the factions other then the colors of their sails, which you can change anyways with sail and hull paint. Going against the 2 higher level factions is LITERALLY unfair, they have special bonuses such as 10% more damage, speed, and armor.
The land is nice, but a bit buggy, sometimes you can get stuck on it and fly backwards 10 miles with no control, the towers they provide are way too weak, until you get to the max level of them.
Enemy AI have almost 100% accuracy with barrels and such, while my own allies can't hit me with a water barrel 10 feet away.
The first couple of levels are fun, when you have to trade and quest to get started. At about 15 you're forced to do instances because the land is too high of a level for you, at about level 25 it's consant grinding and farming.
The Syndicate's required reputation of 1000 is far to hard to get, especially when you only have a 100% difficulty. Each quest only gives about 10 reputation each, and they take 2 minutes each. The last faction is also the most ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t system I can think about. Level 150 and you're allowed to spawn allies near you, and give others rewards, making firefights against other players unfair.
The game not very popular either, the highest ranking server has about 60 people on it, the others are lucky to have 15.

Shantae: Half-Genie Hero is the fourth Shantae game in the series, and is a pretty good game overall.
The minute I started playing this, I was instantly blown away by the amazing graphics and catchy soundtrack the game had to offer. Unlike previous Shantae games, almost all the songs in the sountrack are not remixed and are completely new (one of them being Burning Town). The characters are humorous and lovable, just as usual.
In terms of gameplay, Half Genie Hero is a very fun and enjoyable experience. The platforming and quests aren't very difficult. The game itself isn't very difficult either; at most, something in a boss battle catches you off guard but when you try again it's simple. The game is very linear, and there are no dungeons or labyrinths unlike previous Shantae games. Despite these differences, the game is still extremely fun to play and I see it as WayForward trying a new, fresh approach to making a Shantae game. Half-Genie Hero still has its fair share of backtracking to collect secret items, though.
The only complaint I have about this game is the amount of content. It feels a bit short. The game also has a weaker plot structure compared to the other games. My first playthrough of the game, collecting everything, took me approximately eight hours. There are always the achievements, though, and you'll probably have to play the game some more if you want them all. The game is good, though, so no trouble. Also, additional downloadable content for Half-Genie Hero is scheduled to come out soon. It looks really interesting and will add more things to do in the game.
Overall, I would definitely recommend Half-Genie Hero to anyone who likes Shantae, platformers, or anyone who just wants to play a well-made game. The game has a bit of an arcade feel to it, kind of like Mega Man, and is very entertaining and simple to just pick up and play. While the game may seem short, extensions will be released in the near future. The game is definitely worth playing (especially multiple times) and I suggest picking it up and experiencing it yourself, too.
