This may seem like a long review but I adore this game and cant stop playing it. I find the jokes hilarious, even after hearing them multiple times. I highly recommend this game to everyone.
Borderlands 2 is a first person shooter that gets harder with more friends playing alongside you in a world called Pandora. I play as Axton the Commando and Salvador the Gunzerker in my solo games. Axton's action skill is a sabre turret that I use to draw fire away from myself so I can be on the offensive while dodging the damage. Salvador has the action skill Gunzerking that allows him to use two guns at once to riddle the enemies with bullets. I have a Maya the Siren and Zer0 the Assassin characters for multiplayer playing with my friends. My version of Maya is a healer uses her action skill of Phaselock, suspends enemies in midair, to revive teammates from afar through a certain skill in one of the class trees for leveling skills. The Zer0 I play applies marks to the enemies, while in his action skill of Deception, so that all damage has more power. Everyone has his or her own play styles, so you get to choose what perks you want to use. The developers have cast two downloadable content (DLC) characters that give six new class trees to play, Gaige the Mechromancer and Krieg the Psycho. Gaige has the action skill called Deathtrap, a robot bodyguard that she can summon to fight beside her. Krieg is a psycho with a Rampage skill with massive melee damage. My Krieg is a tank that takes damage then evolves to a badass psycho and retaliates with monstrous damage. I have two friends that play as Maya the Siren: one that uses her skill to brainwash of the enemies to fight for us so that we don’t have to, and the second that uses her as an elemental damager (damage over time). Everyone has their own way to play each class. The characters are not dependent on any one-weapon category either so an Assassin (Zer0) can use a shotgun just as well as everyone else.
I have some high level characters that I’m still going through again to find the best weapons; the more levels that you gain the better the loot becomes, with 17 Million guns in the main game, you will always be looking for the best guns for your playing style. There are six types of weapons, however every manufacturer adds their own properties to each gun, for example Torgue weapons will always deal explosive damage, Tediore weapons have the fastest reload speed, Dahl burst fires while zoomed, and Vladof has high fire rates. The most powerful damage gun isn’t always the best fit for every situation, there are some weapons that have elemental effect guns that some enemies without having to fire as many bullets as the standard damage guns. Elemental guns have one of five additives, fire, shock, corrosive, explosive or slag. Fire, shock and corrosive are more effective against flesh, shields, and armor respectively. Slag weapons will double the damage of any non-slag weapon, unless the player is in Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode DLC, in which the damage is tripled! Just because of the distinctiveness of elemental weapons, it does not create a less challenging aspect. There are some exceptional weapons that will spawn occasionally and have some unique abilities. An example is the Swordsplosion, a Shotgun from Mr. Torgue’s Campaign of Carnage DLC, which fires a sword that explodes instead of a bullet.
The Developers have added four main DLC story lines that are beautiful expansions to the game. Captain Scarlett and her Pirates Booty will add a swashbuckling story where you travel in a new hoverboat vehicle across the desert to find the compass pieces that will lead you to Captain Blades Treasure. Mr. Torgue’s Campaign of Carnage is all about being the ultimate badass in the sheer butchery of all who rank above you in a competition to find the champion of Pandora. Sir Hammerlocks Big Game Hunt will have you search for exotic animals (that haven’t been introduced until this DLC) while you take down native tribes, Professor Nakayama, and his twisted creations. Tiny Tina’s Assault on Dragons Keep, my favorite DLC, has a Dungeons and Dragons twist titled Bunkers and Badasses where you be trying to save the princess while fighting against the Handsome Sorcerer and his Orc minions.  It includes mythical creatures that will give you new battles with a very unique feel compared to the main game and other DLCs. Beware, Tiny Tina’s Assault on Dragons Keep occurs at the end of the main story line and reveals spoilers; I do recommend finishing the main story before starting this DLC. Ultimate Vault Hunter Pack will allow the player to play a new advanced mode rightly named Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode. Enemies will level up with the players and have the ability to regenerate health to enhance the difficulty. To battle these upgrades, players are given the ability to gain 11 more levels and slagging enemies will cause more damage. Ultimate Vault Hunter Pack 2 will allow the player to gain an extra 11 levels and battle more challenges on Digistruct Peak. Digistruct Peak is a special area where all enemies will appear through digital construction machines. When players have reached level 72, they will be given the option of developing 8 Overpower Levels on Digistruct Peak to gain the highest level of play. Another section of the game’s vast DLC content is Headhunter, DLC maps that are a short story with a boss. Bloody Harvest is a Halloween themed adventure, Wattle Gobbler has a Thanksgiving theme, and Mercenary Day is a Christmas type escapade. Wedding Day Massacre brings a Romeo & Juliet story to life with the bride and groom as Goliaths (one type of enemy in the game). Son of Crawmerax is an island vacation where Hammerlock gets kidnapped.
I highly recommend buying this game, the four main DLC map, the two Ultimate Vault Hunter Packs and the two DLC characters. The cel-shaded style may be a turn off for those that are looking for the highest detail games but I like how it uses the style and made a superb game.

Disclaimer: Was given a streamkey for the game. This has no effect on my judgement of the game
So i was given a key for the game through keymailer and decided to check it out. And honestly i was really surprised. and Pleasantly! The game is extremely solid in execution and the art is crisp yet simple. I am a sucker for smaller games that i can play in short breaks and this is one of them.
Gameplay: The game is a Turn Based Strategy game where you use 4 heroes to try and get to the end. You pick 4 out of 8 classes to use. The game field is a 3x7 grid where your heroes are placed 1 in the back and 3 in front. When you are in the fight enemies spawn and move/attack every round and when it is your turn you attack by switching position with two of your heroes. This means you always move around the heroes and you have to look a turn ahead. I had a few times where im like "This is the perfect position" and then i had to move them. This is enhanced by the fact that every hero is either melee or range and that some heroes can attack through enemies. What really makes every hero special is that when you pull a hero from the back into the front they use a unique ability. Ranging from healing to damaging all enemies. The gameplay loop is set up with you starting with few heroes. then you go into battles that gets progressively harder. As soon as even a single heroes die you lose (unless you have items to prevent it) and the round is over. depending on how well you did you are rewarded with Miftril which can be spent to upgrade heroes and then you go again. There is also a quest system and a skill system. So go in. get as far as you can. get stronger. go back in. Its really compelling and quite satisfying. The downside is that i am not sure how much there is to keep you playing after you have upgraded everything and beaten the game on normal and nightmare and hell. This will however take several hours and I am not quite sure how challenging or welldone the two additional difficulties are
TL;DR
Pros:
-Simple yet crisp graphics
-Can be played in short bursts
-Has an interesting game loop
Cons:
-Quite heavily based around an upgrade based gameplay loop which is finite.
To see it in action you can watch my first stream of it

A bit of an adventure game ala prince of persia, with pits you need to jump and ropes you need to zip-line mixed with a bit of gearhead simulation, fortress building (or more, improving. Max scours the wasteland looking for scrap and interesting pieces that can be combined into improvements for your car, for max himself, or for the various fortresses that shelters him while adventuring in the region.
Building and improving on a new wagon that will carry Max across the Silent Wasteland, you run into warlords, bands of villains, interesting exotic locations, and you find hidden caches of scrap and ammo. Water is essencial since it replentishes your hitpoints, so you learn to keep your canteen full at all times.
Your hunchbacked sidekick Chumbucket keeps your car repaired and delivers one-liners when need be. He also acts as a spotter, warning you of warboys and buzzards and other dangers.
And sand storms. Big, red flashing sand storms that will impale you with electricity if don't find shelter or drive like hell.
I was afraid the game would anonymize the villains too much. The warboys in the movie were all given personalities and names and you could see them several times thoughout the heated action scenes. In a sense, you "witnessed" all of them go either under the wheel of a tractor or explode as they sacrificed themselves.
In this game, the warboys are mindless cretins that only need to be pummeled down. The more important npcs however have personalities, decent voice-actors and wonderful scripts.
The fighting mechanics is easy to get a hang of, and the incremental build-up of "rage" in a fight that makes you ever more powerful for every successive hit you land, gives you a feeling of being really bloody good at what you're doing and a proper badass.

Yes, it's popular. Yes, it's kind of fun. Yet its physics are disapppointingly despondent towards drifting and have a numbing feeling in general. The cars are also programmed to be mortal enemies towards any wall, making it impossible to recover your race after a single mistake or botched turn. The game seems to be geared towards racing AI that always knows the right line to take. This makes playing the game agitating, tedious, and stressful. Also, there is an extremely annoying and obvious lack of any learning curve at all, as if the game expects you to be a pro-TrackMania player with hundreds of hours logged as soon as you start playing. This once again points to the idea that the game is designed for computers. The basic level editor allows the choice of, quite literally, less than 10 pieces and seems to be designed for toddlers. This is in stark contrast to the advanced level editor, which gives absolutely no direction as to how to use its nonsensical pre-race footage editing tools and seems to expect you to compute shadows every time you edit a map, a process that can take 10+ minutes with all the computations forgotten by the file even after you save the map. There is also no option for car-on-car collision, allowing them to pathetically phase through one another. The game also requires intimate router port forwarding knowledge in order to use several customization functions, which is something I spent all day trying to figure out. Generally the ports are forwarded by the .exe install file instead. Moreover, there is no boost, very few graphics and audio options, and a completely stupid currency system. This is only a portion of the things I have a problem with, but I'll spare the rest. In short, this game is great for people who love experiencing repeated failure, but a dismal waste to all others.

Pros:
-Decent graphics, certainly not knock-your-socks-off detailed, but pleasing enough.
-Combat is simple, but still manages to be exciting, thanks to the active abilities.
-A handful of ships based on real ships from the Age of Sail, such as Schooners or Brigs. (Look them up on Wikipedia if you aren't sure what they are)
-Plenty of fun with friends.
-Aside from combat, you can also choose to do trades or quests, both of which are alternative sources of gold/xp.
-Towns can level up, which affects the quantity/quality of items for sale, and the maximum price of equipment sold to them.
-You can choose one of 3 self-explanatory roles: Offense, Defense or Support.
Cons:
-Combat is by far the best source of XP, and Trading is the best source of gold (from my experience). Questing is rather lackluster unless you can get quests for sinking pirates, or delivering items to a town you were stopping at anyway for a trade.
-The game can be somewhat grindy at various points, whether that be saving up for the next ship you want, or getting enough XP to level up again.
-The game is quite multiplayer oriented; soloing is perfectly viable until about region level 39, after which the difficulty ramps up immensely as you start seeing only elite pirates (pirate captains or above), making it hard to play without others to back you up/provide extra dps.
-Good loot can be hard to come by if you're not doing group instances.
-The randomly generated region maps can have a few... issues, ranging from spawn points in the middle of land (causing you to die if you don't fast travel away in time), or creating walls of terrain that block your progress.
Other things of note:
-Healing your friends involves throwing barrels of water at them.
-NPC ships have amusing dialogue for various circumstances, including the aforementioned water barrels.
-Pirate speak translator. Yarr!
All in all, not a bad game, but not a good game either, unless you have friends to play with, or can stand playing with strangers on a server.
Overall, I give it an 8/10 if you have friends/play on a server, or a 5/10 if you don't.

Not much else to say.  Despite there being much more "hardcore-esq" gaming mechincs for those that want it, Euro Truck Simulator 2 is one of those games that can easily sit in anyone's Steam library, and not bring about any regrets of it's presence being there.
It's apparently as deep, or as shallow as you'd like it.
The ability to add your mp3 collection into it's radio is the absolute clincher/testamet to how casual and carefree this game is at it's core, if you'd like it that way.
I'm playing it on a Mac, and it's nothing spectaculr in graphics, but have everything maxed out, and it's hanging well above "console 30 fps performance" with zero dips.  At medium settings the fps goes into 80-100+ fps territory.
MacBook Pro (Retina, 15-inch, Mid 2014)
2.8 GHz Intel Core i7
16 GB 1600 MHz DDR3
NVIDIA GeForce GT 750M 2048 MB
1 TB Flash Storage
OS X 10.10.3
So yeah, it's an excellent Mac port. from my experience.
The only caveat I'd warn of; is that you definitely need a mouse with a customizable button to toggle DPI settings (mouse sensitivity) to make this game as casual as it can truly be, IMO.  On my Logitech G700s mouse, anything above 250 DPI results in over-steering... but anything less than 1600 DPI results in broken mouse camera panning. So, being able to switch between those two DPI spectrums on the fly makes this game a casual breeze.
I'd almost recommend this game at full price... but it is found on sale at severely discounted prices on a fairly regular basis.  I got my keys from MacGameStore at around $12 for the base game with Scandinavia DLC bundled.
You probably need/want this game in your Steam library, it truly fills a specific need/void, you know you do!  It's just a matter of how much you are willing to pay to get it now, or wait for that sale that comes pretty often these days...

This game was given to me by a colleague who had a spare copy. I put the game aside due to the general consensus that the game was ‘okay’, however when I did get round to booting up the game - I didn’t play anything else until I finished it! And I don’t get to finish many games…
The main story
a bit meh. The narrative has clearly been written to fit in with the game mechanics (you need to upgrade your car a bunch and you need a buddy riding along with you), though it does get a bit better towards the end.
The side quests are nice because they have a level of narrative, don’t take too long and there aren’t so many of them that they detract from the main story.
Post-apocalypse themes are always cool. The Mad Max setting is no Fallout. It is very brutal. There is death, violation, drugs and not to mention insane amounts of violence. I’m almost afraid to say I prefer this level of seriousness that almost everyone in this world wants to kill you purely for the fun of it.
Combat is truly where the game shines. There are two types; on foot and in car.
Ground combat is just like the Batman games but super bloody and delightfully violent. It follows the action mechanic formula of punching and parrying, with weapons and unlockable skills thrown into the mix. Max has a gun, but true to the world, ammo is scarce so I found myself very rarely using it (much more fun to save for use in car combat).
The car combat mechanics are awesome. The nature of it, though unscripted, comes across as highly cinematic, detailed skirmishes. Intercepting convoys is extremely fun, there’s nothing like scouting out a dust trail from atop a plateau with your ‘long lookers’, getting into your vehicle and T-boning the target car, shooting raiders off your bonnet in the process. Very fun.
Max and his car are the player’s main focus. Levelling up Max unlocks Max upgrades such as armor and skills. This system is very well done; rather than gathering experience points, you level up by completing challenges (blow up 50 barrels, do a 10-hit combo, etc.). Completing quests and eliminating threats unlocks car upgrades. There are many different combinations, the most expensive upgrades aren’t always the best to use. Sometimes the weaker upgrades are a better choice - they may have less mass, which allows for faster acceleration, for example.
The game is beautiful. From far away landmarks, right the way down to sand trails and dust clouds, the level of detail is impressive. There’s even a feature to freeze time and capture screenshots and videos. No loading screens interrupt traversing the huge open world.
I’ve touched on the parts of this game that spoke out to me the most. If you are a fan of open-world action games, post-apocalyptic themes or good o’ violence ‘n explosions, then I highly suggest buying this. Some patience with the first introductory part is required until the game opens up and becomes much more fun. The game is NOT a survival game, Max is a very capable individual, though a bit simple and predictable - he fights like a total badass.

Yes, it's popular. Yes, it's kind of fun. Yet its physics are disapppointingly despondent towards drifting and have a numbing feeling in general. The cars are also programmed to be mortal enemies towards any wall, making it impossible to recover your race after a single mistake or botched turn. The game seems to be geared towards racing AI that always knows the right line to take. This makes playing the game agitating, tedious, and stressful. Also, there is an extremely annoying and obvious lack of any learning curve at all, as if the game expects you to be a pro-TrackMania player with hundreds of hours logged as soon as you start playing. This once again points to the idea that the game is designed for computers. The basic level editor allows the choice of, quite literally, less than 10 pieces and seems to be designed for toddlers. This is in stark contrast to the advanced level editor, which gives absolutely no direction as to how to use its nonsensical pre-race footage editing tools and seems to expect you to compute shadows every time you edit a map, a process that can take 10+ minutes with all the computations forgotten by the file even after you save the map. There is also no option for car-on-car collision, allowing them to pathetically phase through one another. The game also requires intimate router port forwarding knowledge in order to use several customization functions, which is something I spent all day trying to figure out. Generally the ports are forwarded by the .exe install file instead. Moreover, there is no boost, very few graphics and audio options, and a completely stupid currency system. This is only a portion of the things I have a problem with, but I'll spare the rest. In short, this game is great for people who love experiencing repeated failure, but a dismal waste to all others.

This game IMHO is a jewel that deserves to be discovered. At 122mb in size, it packs a lot. Good graphics, nice ambiant sounds and funny NPCs comment when you meet them on your travels.
The gameplay is easy to understand and after an hour of play time, you know all that there is to know. Deliver cargo or passengers you pick up at different cities for small rewards. Capture enemy towns or sink pirate ships for higher rewards and loot.
I wouldn't recommend playing this game only in single player mode because the allied NPCs artificial intelligence isn't that great. On several occasions I was trying to conquer a map while the allied NPCs remained near already conquered towns, ignoring the pirate owned cities. For the lower level maps it wasn't much an issue but above level 30 it becomes quite an issue and makes conquering a full map long and tedious.
That being said... the multiplayer portion of the game has also some issues. If you join a largely populated server then you will be faced with maps that have been already conquered long ago, leaving you to do small quests until you can catch up. Sure there are instances you can join or create but most of the time, if you are starting your life as a captain you'll end up dead quite quickly. Still, playing in multiplayer will have you raise in levels way more quickly.
I beleive that playing with a few friends on a private multiplayer game is the way to go, that's where this game trully shines. You will be able to generate maps at will that will suit your needs. You will have the number of ships to plan and develop strategies to capture enemy towns. That's how the game was meant to be played according to the devs.
There are plenty of upgrades and ships you can aquire as you level up which adds to the long term gameplay. Some people may say that there is also some balancing issues to the skills at higher levels but I think not , the game is harder as you get more used to it, which makes sense.
In conclusion, I have to give a "tip of the hat" to the devs that made this game. I don't remember having one single bug while playing so far and again... at 122mb of data only, it's obvious they did a great job coding this game.
I would give this game a perfect score of 10/10 if the allied NPCs Ai's was a bit more polished.

Citizens of Dunwall, please accept my apologies. I was a hop, skip and a slide away from the Lord Regent's chamber when this seriously compelling lorry sim sped into my life. Suddenly, stealthy vengeance seems far less important than ensuring a load of new JCBs gets to Bratislava on time.
Euro Truck Simulator 2 is that rare thing, a strong sim tethered to a strong game. Where other vehicle-obsessed devs seem to take player motivation for granted, Czech studio SCS understand that a pleasingly modelled steed needs a pleasingly modelled environment to shine.
On this occasion that environment is a swathe of Europe stretching from Plymouth in the west to Wroclaw in the east, from Aberdeen in the north to Milan in the South. The tangle of motorways and major roads is stylised and condensed, but feels massive. After a splendid week of non-stop trucking the stats screen tells me I've still only seen 50% of it.
There's satisfaction in exploring new routes, seeing new golden been-there-done-that squiggles appearing on the in-game map, but it tends to be the promise of cold, hard cash that gets you out of bed in the morning. Like Farming Simulator, ETS2 has a simple yet resonant economic sandbox at its centre.
Euro Truck Simulator 2 review Adding streams to the radio list is harder than it should be.
You start as a low-skilled, truckless lorry jockey, forced to take work from established haulage companies. Slowly (or rapidly if you go to a bank) you amass the funds to buy your first rig and rent your first yard. Then the fun really begins. Contract perusing, truck pimping, skill upgrading, driver hiring... this is Eddie Stobart: The Game in all but name.
Spending 90 minutes ferrying a tank of propane from Sheffield to Prague could (should?) be tedious. The fact that it isn't is largely down to good-if-not-quite-OMSI-standard physics, and varied road layouts and scenery. Periods of smooth, almost soporific motorway motoring nestle between passages of edgier wheelwork. One minute you're cruising along contemplating the sunset over the central reservation, the next you're on a rain-lashed country road at night, waiting for the right moment to pass a painfully slow pantechnicon. Tiredness can't kill in ETS2, but it can leave you jack-knifed in a ditch, feeling awful with a substantial repair bill to pay.
The only time when the game itself loses concentration is when attempting to evoke certain regions and sounds. The further you get from central Europe the less convincing the landscapes become. No one seems to have told SCS's countryside crafters that rural Britain features long green things called hedges. Cities are often depicted with the shortest of visual shorthand – a few warehouses, the odd landmark if you're lucky. Don't expect to see a favourite local roundabout, slip-road, or speed camera in this highly-recommended HGV-driver RPG.

Pros:
- Soundtrack: Really sets the atmosphere well. I liked it so much I listen to it on the bus or during spare time.
- Cinematography: The game uses a lot of imagery and symbolism and it combines it the great camerawork and soundtrack to create a really good cinematic experience.
Cons:
- Poor Writing: I love the intention the writers had, I really do. But they executed it poorly.
- Bad Voice Acting: Rachel is the only one that's good. Chloe's new voice actor is just absolute garbage. Everyone else just sounds bland and emotionless.
- Bugs: Every single episode had an odd thing where everyone's dialogue would cut early once in a while and it would mess up the flow of the conversation, and sometimes I would miss some important details.
I don't think the game is terrible. At the same time, there are too many flaws for me to mark it as a good game. The first game had the same problem with poor writing, and I hoped this prequel would fix some of the plot holes it had. While it mostly did, it mostly left me unsatisfied because of how messy it all is. There is a much better way of telling a story about friendship and there is a much better way of telling a story about what a broken teenage life can be.

Spec Ops: The Line Review
-------
Story: 9.5/10
Among the sea of silent protagonists and countless shooters, there lies one that can actually tell a story. Even though it is incredibly disturbing at times, it really showcases just how awful war can be. Post Traumatic Stress Disorder is the primary reason why soliders get taken off of the battefield. Something like PTSD can only be understood if you have it yourself, which is why it (among other mental illnesses) are rarely taken seriously; especially once an affected solider returns home. Playing through Spec Ops: The Line shows you what it takes to break a battle-hardened warrior, leaving him completely raving mad in a journey that goes from bad to worse. The story of The Line is definitely the forefront reason to play this game, giving you an overlook on all the things you never really hear about in war. Regardless of its' fiction, the message is raw truth: war is hell.
-------
Gameplay: 7/10
The gameplay for Spec Ops: The Line is decent. It's much better when you actually take the time to observe your surroundings and strategize your attacks instead of rushing in, guns blazing. The game also plays better on higher difficulties, as you must be exceptionally careful in practically every combat setting in order to overcome your enemies. There is always a way out that is rather obvious in most situations, although, and sometimes the game gives away the challenge. Enemy AI is wonky to say the least. Most of the time they are ruthless and smart and can screw up your day, but sometimes they just stick to some cover and wait for you to come kill them. Movement is very shaky too. Sometimes you wanna slide to some cover, but you end up just sprinting past it, which can earn you a frustrating death. Since it's a third-person shooter, I admire the fluidity of combat that this game offers, but it does not always execute.
-------
Graphics: 8.5/10
The graphics are good...there's no doubt about it. This game has beautiful scenic shots and gorgeous sand storm visuals, as well as spot on interpretation of the architectural beauty that is Dubai (even though it's also ravaged by sand and war). Some of the lighting is confusing though, especially in combat situations. You can tell that the goal was to use the weather and lighting elements to affect combat, which is both a good thing and a bad thing. The frequent sand storms are brilliant and are incredibly unique even though they are seen in other games. They really tie into feeling choked and helpless when you've got 20 bad guys on you and you can't do anything other than just hide behind a cracking wall of a beached yacht, waiting for the storm to subside so you can take your shots. That's awesome. But the lighting can really screw you up because they try to do the HD light glare thing on your screen, but it can be a bit much at times, forcing you to move around until you can get clear shots. It's simply annoying gameplay due to the graphics. This only happens a few times, and the lighting is usually done very well to accentuate set pieces and events that are pretty good.
-------
Overall: 8/10
Spec Ops: The Line has an amazing storyline and generic but satisfying gameplay. It is a definite 9/10. The game also does a good job of making you feel like♥♥♥♥♥♥

This is the most ♥♥♥♥ed up game I have ever played. Is that a good thing? Absolutely, Spec Ops The Line has extremly deep character development that takes you through the horrors of war. Now I'am personally a huge CoD & Battlefield fan, but this takes the cake. Every choice is just plain bad, do you let someone that may be beneficial in your team survival live or allow a group of civilians die. Throughout the game you will find each character in your squad becoming increasingly spiteful towards each other. They all have their ideas on the decisions you made. In the beginning your character look like they have clean uniforms no injuries, but by the end each character has looked as if they had stepped into hell and barely survived. The story is just original with America not being the good guy finding the terrorist, but instead you actually fight and kill many American troops. The character take no side, they fight to survive because in war that is the key element is survival.

Beautiful art direction, awesome soundtrack, cute girls and tight platforming, Shantae has it all!
Fans who have played the other games in the series may notice that this game in particular takes a step back a bit from the backtracking, and instead focuses more on transformation abilities and platforming abilities.
Nevertheless, this game is yet another fantastic entry in the Shantae series, and an even better one to start with if you want to dive into the series.

This game is in plenty ways amazing and dissapointing in others. It's a very beautiful platformer that feels just as good or better than previous Shantae games and also has some great level design that focuses more on linear megaman-style levels than those games more open Metroidvania or Zelda influences, and then lets that new focus down by adding unnecessary filler. I'm going to be comparing this game to the previous modern Shantae games quite a bit in this assessment, they are games that are pretty dear to me as far as modern-but-classic style platformers. Pirates Curse particularly I hold in very high regard, it's definitely the highest point where the series correctly iterated on the prequel and knocked it out of the park with the new skills. 1/2 Hero doesn't quite hit that mark.
Just to be clear, the core levels are all great and a pleasure to play. The upbeat music (I really don't like the lyrical version of the main theme, but everything else is great) and flow of the game works exceedingly well when you are jumping and hair whipping enemies. That first time you finish a level and a boss feels great...but after you do that there's this middle time when you meander around doing fetch quests for various NPCs. If these quests were optional they would be much easier to stomach, but their quirky weirdness don't make up for the fact that it's clearly game padding. Instead of filling the game with interesting side stuff to collect, most of it is all there to progress the main story. These levels are not really made for exploration either, and there is no map to assist you for finding the hidden stuff. It's mostly just reading NPC dialog to figure out where you need to go out of the levels you've already been, going there to get the necessary plot item. It seems like this game is trying to have it's tight platformer levels and is adding metroid elements to extend it, rather than building them into the game naturally. It doesn't really work too well, the game would only be about 4 hours with just the levels, but I would definitely prefer that to all of the filler.
Tied into the monotony of the between-levels is that most of the transformations just aren't very fun to use. The Monkey might be my favorite, but it is criminally underused because many of the later game transformations make it redundant. A lot of the transformations accomplish *almost* the same thing, Crab lets you sink underwater, Mermaid lets you swim. Sometimes you need to be a crab to fit underneath tight spots but there would be no way to know that by just looking at a body of water. When this happens you would have to jump out of the water, go back to the land area, dance to the right transformation and dive back in. This kind of thing sounds trivial, but it's just one of the many quirks that annoy me about the transformations. The entire idea of pausing the game and dancing just to have access to a traversal element seems unnecessary. The game doesn't even use all of the buttons on a ps4 pad, they could have let you bind transformations to individual buttons. If you compare this to the sleek implementations of Shantae's abilities in Pirate's Curse it definitely falls flat. Add to the fact that the charge, triplejump, saber, pistol, and Hat were all just way more fun to use in that game and integrated into the main game more often instead of being used just for item collection. Some of the transformations in this game are used for literally one item and never again, while some of the powerups you get for Shantae's different forms like the Spider Venom or Mouse bite seem never used at all.
Another issue I have with the game is the plot, or rather the lack of one. The dialog keeps that Shantae charm found in the previous games, Shantae herself remains a good protag with the right amount of snark. It is however tonally all over the place compared to Pirate's Curse. This series has never been about the amazing writing or anything, but at least Pirate's Curse had a solid goal and a tone that remained consistent. 1/2 Genie Hero drops the ball on this, most of the stuff that happens is silly for silliness sake and there is hardly an end goal to speak of. There are times when I really appreciate the weirdness of this game and the character interactions, but it also uses that weirdness to feed into those mandatory fetch quests I was talking about earlier which is unfortunate. None of the chapters really have much to do with each other, they don't build towards anything by the end. I think the desire for this to be THE Shantae game to bring the series on modern hardware, as well as the expectations associated with a kickstarter game encouraged Wayforward to find a way to cram every Shantae villian into this game to its detriment.
So what does work? Why am I recommending it? I would like to emphasis I really enjoyed playing this game a lot especially when I was playing through each of its 6 levels for the first time. As far as Shantae herself goes minus abilities this game might be the best feeling one yet. The levels are all utterly fantastic in that special linear megaman way. Hair whipping feels great and I hum the music obessively in my day to day life. Every level is an incredibly varied and unforgettable platformer experience that mostly makes up for all of those shortcomings I listed. I am able to look past those annoyances and confidently say I love this game and you should definitely play it, just temper your expectations a bit regarding everything else. I honestly can't wait for a more Pirate's Curse style game to come out with this engine they have crafted, it would be truly incredible.

A decent platformer, but with it has its faults
I was a huge fan of the previous game in the series, and I was very excited to play this, unfortunately some things feel like a step backwards rather than forwards. There, however, are a lot of things to love here: The art is fantastic, and is easily one of the best looking platformers you can play on PC.
The music, as composed by the great Jake Kaufman (Shovel Knight/Mighty Switch Force)  is generally top notch, although a few tracks (such as the last two parts of the game) I found very underwhelming.
The levels are extremely fun the first time through, they all have fun gimmicks to them that make them stand out among the others, but you will be doing a ton of backtracking to find items, which can feel like a chore, and make the levels feel very small after a while, I know it was done to lengthen the game, but it spreads too thin, and I'd have preferred a 3-4 hour game that stayed fresh than a 7-8 hour game where you constantly comb through the same areas.
The boss fights are hit and miss, not horrible for a platform game (a genre not generally known for good bosses, outside of megaman and metroid) but not as challenging or charming as they were in Pirate's curse.
The biggest positive of the game by far is the transformations, there are tons of forms Shantae aquires and they all have fun and unique properties that change up the game a lot, and they all look dang cute.
I give this game a soft reccomendation, but hope there will be more that feels in line with Pirate's Curse in the upcoming Risky Boots campaign, as it was left feeling pretty dry at the end.
Still, one of the better platformers on steam, and for 20 dollars it's not a bad way to kill a few hours.

Shantae: Half-Genie Hero is a game that wastes my time and jerks me around. I have beaten this game to 100% and this is my review:
-Good music, which will get repetitive as you replay levels over and over.
-Pretty good visuals.
-Poorly thought out level design
-Terrible controls for several different Shantae transformations.
-Monkey Island style wacky nonsensical solutions to puzzles that make no sense.
-Awful check point system that makes you replay entire levels/the worst part of a level over and over.
-Forces you to constantly replay levels over and over as you unlock new powers which, in the end, does not feel satisfying but instead wastes your time.
-Boring boss battles.
-Terrible memeatic writing that is forced sounding and fan service feeling in general
-Has kick starter ‘backer-exclusive’ content that cannot be bought at all by anyone who didn’t get in early on the kick starter. This is anti-consumerism no matter how you try to spin it. This basically says to people who wanted to wait for a finished product and reviews, “your money is worth less to us than those who backed it”.
-Very little bang for your buck. I frustratingly played through this game in 8 hours, it is designed to be beaten in 4 hours. This is a 20 dollar game.
Details of this filth:
I have invented a new term just for this game, which upon reflection can be applied to a lot of bad games.
This term is called, “Monkey Island solutions” what is a, Monkey Island solution you ask? It is when a game, not just point-n-click adventure games, ask you to perform a series of complicated tasks to do a simple objective but also in which none of the steps nor end result makes sense and cannot be deduced naturally. Some other people in the video game realm might call this, “rub the fish on everything” syndrome.
Here is an example from this very game: you must get the power, as a mermaid, to shoot bubbles. How do you do this? Well, one of the villagers tells you that only “elder” sea creatures know this power! Well look at that, in town suddenly is the Grandma Blobfish (which earlier you had to find two tickets for her grandkids to go see a magic carpet ride via killing gator enemies with magic you must grind money for to unlock until they drop “gator stakes” to give to too villains for a ticket and that was only HALF of that quest).
Ahem, the example:
"We're gonna need you to get this blobfish a new hat so she can sing you a song and give you the mermaid shooting ability but to do that you must get the hat from a WACKY CHARACTER GUY that tells you to find ANOTHER WACKY CHARACTER GUY but to do that you first need to unlock the Mermaid form (several step subquest), combo into Harpy unlock (several step subquest), and figure out this cryptic clue that actually makes no sense (subquest to get clue)"
Do you see how this is a problem, how it is unfun to deal with and why guides are so popular for games today? This game is entirely like this, the whole game.
Let’s mention some gameplay; there is a point in this game in which you must control Shantae through a SPIKE MAZE using the WORST CONTROLLING form in the game, the Harpy. The harpy controls like a flappy bird clone but you can move forwards and backwards. She does not stop in midair, she always slightly moves forward which is a problem when this is happening:
See these two blocks? They are rotating around each other, and before them there are a series of three columns that block the entire way from ceiling to floor (the floor also kills you) and you must step in between the middle set of these spike walls as it opens to wait for the next to open; all doing this mind you
so you must constantly tap jump to flap while wiggling back and forth to not die in a space less than an 8th of your screen for a character that takes up 90% of said space you are safe. This section alone is so disgustingly made, so poorly thought out I almost quit the game right then and there;
Oh right, for good measure they take you back to the start of the level if you die so ya know, have fun backtracking through the level to get up to the point you died, only to then die again on the very next trap you have no idea is coming.
The examples I give above are not single instances, but throughout the entire game. This whole game is a huge mess of poorly thought out choices, obscure and often offensive puzzles, poor controls for multiple transformation forms, and a absolutely terrible check point system that will make you want to quit.
Backer exclusive content is anti-consumerism in pure form.
Well fear not, for I shall explain; you see by offering 'backer-exclusive" content the game devs are tempting you in parting with your money before a finished product is made. They are offering you promises for cash, this is anti-consumer.
Pro-consumer is waiting for a finished, final product. If you are offered a chance to wait for a product, to see if you would like it and to experience reviews then you are in the clear and so are the devs. Backer-exclusives can be grouped in with other scummy practices devs/publishers often use. Here is an example:
"If you buy this game now, you will get access to X thing! No one else will get access to X thing because they bought it AFTER the game was released." Can you name that anti-consumer practice? That's right, preorder bonuses! Buy now, get product later! Secure money now for nothing, offer a game that might be as good we promise ;). Sound familiar? In the above sentence replace "after the game is released" with "after the game is funded". Nice.
A quick question to people that will come shilling in because of the bottom of this review: please riddle me this, how did games get made before kick starter?
How did a game get produced without the backing of a publisher, triple A or otherwise? How did indie games come into this world without the hand holding of kick starter? Through the blood, sweet, and tears of game devs everywhere. Cave story came to exist and became an excellent game as it was done by a man in his spare time.

Whether it be a reboot, soft reboot, sequel or soft robot rabbit, Shantae is back in town.  Everything is familiar for fans of the series, maybe a little too much so in some respects, and if you're unfamiliar to the series and looking for a light metroidvania-esque platforming game that isn't too hard, you'll enjoy this.
The world is bright and colourful and the 3d background visuals are a pleasant departure from the standard 2d pixel art.  The soundtrack is pretty solid, as usual for the series.  Controls are mostly smooth, some jumps didn't feel quite as responsive as I'd like but good on the whole.  Though, Relic usage for animal transformations could be more seamless in game. On the topic of Relics, there are far too many transformations and not enough puzzles using them.  A few of the transformation upgrades only get used once or not at all.  There may have been plans to use these upgrades that never made it into the game, but it still feels like there's unnecessary clutter and it's disappointing to have useless abilities.  A lot of the magic you can buy from the store also isn't as useful as in past series.
Plotline is disappointing.  Just... disappointing.  It's like the events of the previous game were completely forgotten.  Whilst I do enjoy seeing familiar faces like Sky, Bolo, Rotty and Mimic again, too many of the minor antagonists were reused from previous games in shallow ways and the culmination of the plot just felt very half-baked.  That being said, there is some witty banter and some enjoyable dialogue.  And some nice 'plot' as usual.
The level design is decent and there are some interesting concepts and designs, though the execution isn't entirely there.  Bosses... eh.  I think the game misses not having any dungeons whatsoever, though, and the difficulty curve is pretty nonexistent.  I've no major issue with the backtracking elements to the game, but I do think that the game spoonfeeds a little too much with regards to some of the hidden items.  The hinting system is pretty inelegant as well.
Overall, enjoyable.  Bit of a step back from Pirate's Curse - WayForward may not be living up to their name - but a nice few hours romping around anyway.

Brutal open world complete-a-thon with a short but intriguing story.
----
The world has become chaos. Chaos such that it reminds you of the true meaning of the word. Max, a loner and a survivalist, has lost everything and drifts aimlessly through the wastes in his iconic V8 Interceptor, until a wrench is thrown into the works in the form of the sadistic, god-like Scrotus Scabrous and his vast hordes of devoted cult followers. Max is left destitute and without his car - his lifeline - is forced to start over.
Through his jouney in this game he encounters many different kinds of people - most little more than savage beasts, but some allies too. Maybe friends even. Companions. Does Max dare to hope for more than just survival?
----
Despite the game essentially being a big open world completion-fest of travelling from place to place and repeating the same activities, I played it to near enough 100% completion - which I wouldn't normally bother to do. There always comes a point in these games where you look at the icons filling the map and think "wow, I really can't be arsed with this", blitz through the remaining story and never look back. There's something about this one though that dragged me in. Max is wrath incarnate, and roaming from place to place cleansing the land felt somehow appropriate. Like Max's purpose, his unfortunate fate, becomes your own.
In terms of setting, the game plays it's bleak, insane apocalypse very well. When I first began playing I was somewhat taken aback by the levels of brutality - and it's everywhere, in every pore of the game. When Max takes damage, he bleeds and bruises and his visual wounding takes time to heal. Even the V6 and later V8 engines scream and roar at you incessantly. The whole thing is incredibly visceral. But as you continue to play, it becomes such a regularity that it's almost mundane. Business as usual. The madness becomes you.
Anyway, in terms of reviewing the video game, it has it's problems of course. It's terribly repetitive and the actual story content makes for a very tiny portion of the total package. Nonetheless, I enjoyed it (if that's the right word) and I recommend it heartily.

However after about 10 hours of gameplay you realise that is all that the game offers. Its really rinse & repeat after that with just a few new tricks up your sleeve with your car.

I was skepticle at first about this game. I'm not a huge fan of the Mad Max franchise, but got this game in a bundle. Graphics, voice acting, music, brawling, car mechanics (for the most part), scenery, map size, and minor details are top notch. It feels like the Arkham and Shadows of Mordor games, but I think benefitted from lower expectations that those beloved IPs.
Complaints - there is no real sense of urgency on the part of the protaganist or the antagonist. For instance, you have this terrifying enemy who controls the world with an iron fist, but even as you rip his empire down he doesn't seem to take notice. As I futzed around taking camp after camp, he never once put a bounty on my head or tried to stymie my progress. He just let me do it. So I would say that the story telling and lack of push back is a problem. For example, you tear down a tower or a camp, you should get a wanted rating like GTA.
Another complaint - post completion the game is deserted. After you reduce the enemies numbers, nothing really seems to spawn at all. For completionist, this is very frustrating, because many of the tasks required for 100% require more enemies. Again, after your complete the game and leave a power vacuum, no-body else comes to power and you are just left on your own. Boring.
Other than that the game is great and should be purchased.

Trackmania 2: Stadium WAS the definitive way to play the game.
Was.
On May 9th, 2017 the game updated to a newer version of... well, everything. The login system changed, many of the graphics were changed, and other elements of the game were changed arbitrarily. I have spent nearly an hour just trying to play Trackmania 2 at all, but the game claimed my account didn't exist anymore and wouldn't let me reset my password.
This is a problem, because even though Trackmania 2 downloaded a nearly 100mb patch, I had to log in to ManiaPlanet in order to download another 700mb of data. Otherwise, even if I tried to play in Offline mode without logging in, this new updated version of ManiaPlanet wouldn't have the necessary game data to even launch Trackmania 2 at all.
After deciphering their broken password reset system and logging in, I found that the updated Trackmania 2 had erased all of my medals and ranks. This is because the new Trackmania 2 changed how vehicle physics work, so all of the old ranking data was invalid. This also breaks tons of custom tracks made over the last 3-5 years, which are the lifeblood of a game like this.
Ubisoft and Nadeo have essentially decided to arbitrarily reset everything about Trackmania 2 without warning or any way to go back to the old game. For users just starting out from this point forward it's not going to be a big deal, but for a Trackmania veteran like me, an update like this is devastating.
What a disaster.

Guards - fantasy turn-based strategy game, where we manage the team of 4 heroes and fight hordes of monsters.
Gameplay is rather simple - you pick 4 out of 8 basic heroes and start battle with monsters. Heroes have different stats and abilties, so you should choose them carefully, because every time your hero dies you have to start over again. In battle you need to switch heroes in order them to take turn and attack foes. There are 3 front and 1 back places in hero formation and when you move hero back he start regenerating health. If you move hero from back to front he uses his ultimate ability (for example healer restores life of teammates, archer shoots valley of arrows to every enemy and so on). You can upgrade heroes by several means - permanently upgrade them by rune stones before adventure, upgrade their stats (only for the current adventure) between missions by gold and use potions in battles to gain some short advantage.
The game is smple, but very addictive. The battles difficulty is rather hard and you really have to use your head to think over your next turn. I liked the game and recommend it to anyone who likes fantasy turn-based strategies or just wants to have a nice evening with a good game.

I have played almost 200 hours, and am still ridiculously addicted to this game. Graphics are top-notch, controls, physics, AI vehicles - it all feels like you are really out there on the European roads driving your rig. I also got the Scandinavia expansion, and ...wow...the landscapes up there are mindblowing. Of course the fact I'm playing this on a 44" screen just makes it even more awe-inspiring! Highly recommend this, if you love aesthetics and gorgeous landscapes and very, very realistic driving games. And of course, if you love trucks then you will love this game. Tons of cargo to haul, tons of different trucks from lots of different manufacturers to choose from, lots of upgrades, lots of customization options for your rig. And the expansions (if you get any) and DLC just add to them. In the beginning, when you start out and can't afford your own truck and have to take loads as a driver for someone else - not a lot of $$, not a lot of options - even then it is fun getting into it and starting your "career." and they make it so you can dive in pretty quick by going to a bank and borrowing enough $ to buy your own truck. Then - watch the game expand! Easily make enough $$ choosing the right loads with good pay after that to pay back the loan fast, and of course you can choose which skills to train in each time you level (which happens swiftly in the beginning as you log those miles). - Long Distance loads, Eco-Driving (conserving fuel), High Value Cargo, Fragile Cargo, Just-In-Time Loads, etc. Every skill you train in just adds to your per-mile $$ rate, and the number and variety of the loads you can haul.
Can't recommend this game enough. NO complaints, no bugs that I have discovered after 185 hours on the road, endless replayability (if you love truck driving in Europe that is). You can even expand your Garage to 3 or 5 slots, buy more trucks, and hire other drivers to drive for you (they find their own loads and drive automatically and level up over time with no input or worry from you), earning you even more residual income, while you drive on your own. And you can open up more and more garages and hire more and more drivers over time if you choose to.
It's actually a guilty pleasure of mine to log in, get behind the wheel, and just cruise the highways of Europe for hours on end. The sights and landscapes are gorgeous, and you really feel like you're driving a big rig hauling a 25 ton trailer. Can't see myself getting tired of this game for a long, long time. Why are you reading this, and not buying the game? Get hauling!

This is a 2-D platformer that succeeds in bringing in some Metroidvania elements, to a certain extent.
Pros:
- Self-aware humor.
- Good level design.
- Colorful graphics and vivid animations.
- Lots of power-ups and transformations to play with.
- Soundtrack is catchy and memorable (for the most part).
- Doesn't overstay its welcome (around 7-7:30 hours, which is perfect for this type of game).
Cons:
- No map to see which places you've already explored in a specific level.
- Way too much backtracking.

- Last stage has a rather big difficulty spike with poor checkpoint placement.
- Last boss fight is painfully slow and annoying,
Overall, the game is bigger than the sum of its parts. I did enjoy it and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a good platformer with some solid exploration elements.
It's a shame the last stage and boss weren't so good as it left me with a bitter taste, though.

Pretty much the first Shantae game I ever completed and for good reason. This game involves a lot of backtracking, which is the reason I guess fans are disappoint. As a person who usually hates backtracking more than any other video game mechanic, I have to say this is the one of the few games that did it right.
Gameplay:
Pros-
As I tried to imply, I barely know much about Shantae or the gameplay so overall how I can describe this game as the love-child of the Paper Mario series and Donkey Kong Country. As I said, a 'lot' of the game revolves around backtracking, yet it honestly didn't feel at all like a chore. It flows well for this type of game as levels feel brand new or updated once you acquire more power ups and dances. My fear when I purchased this is that the animal dances were going to be used as gimmicks for obstacles and puzzles, but there are several situations where you can get through a level more efficiently than base Shantae.
Cons-
This game goes from delightfully challenging(while annoying on a few parts) to being way too easy. You'll get multiple hearts and food to keep them full forever later in the game, despite the x9 limit for each food. Combining her hair whip with the spike balls/scimitar magic could pretty much smash virtually every enemy away with ease. In fact, magic is immensely unbalanced in this game. You could literally just only purchase the weapon summoning and barrier magic then still beat the game with ease. The difficulty jump and lack of checkpoints can get annoying at times, if you fall off or run into a spike then 2-3 minutes of platforming is basically gone.
Story:
How can I describe it? It basically feels like a Saturday morning cartoon. I don't mean that in a negative or positive way. The dialogue feels witty and the characters keep the liveliness of the game going. Even though I found it funny, I actually felt characters taking catastrophic events to lightly to be rather museless about. The main characters seemed a bit cookie cutter, but they were solid through and through. Even though it was mostly Shantae doing the work, you enjoyed the moral support you was giving from your friends. It's hard to go too deep into it without spoiling. The town NPCs felt like characters in the beginning, but then they reverted into mere hint givers. Overall, I did find it awesome how a simple anti-monster Beacon turned into genie corrupting war machine.
Music:
Overall it was enjoyable to play through the game, but it didn't feel memorable aside from maybe the slide theme. Although, I can't get over Shantae dancing to the town theme.
Overall:
I give it a 7.5/10. Despite a lot of my nit-pickings(and a couple more I didn't mention without spoiling), there was nothing in this game that was game breaking. The platforming by itself is... decent. What saves the game is the versatile abilities and how you can use them to get through puzzles along with faster methods to defeat enemies. It also could've been 'much' longer, yet seeing how this is a Kickstarter game it's understand they had to use the funds they were given in such a little time.

Brutal open world complete-a-thon with a short but intriguing story.
----
The world has become chaos. Chaos such that it reminds you of the true meaning of the word. Max, a loner and a survivalist, has lost everything and drifts aimlessly through the wastes in his iconic V8 Interceptor, until a wrench is thrown into the works in the form of the sadistic, god-like Scrotus Scabrous and his vast hordes of devoted cult followers. Max is left destitute and without his car - his lifeline - is forced to start over.
Through his jouney in this game he encounters many different kinds of people - most little more than savage beasts, but some allies too. Maybe friends even. Companions. Does Max dare to hope for more than just survival?
----
Despite the game essentially being a big open world completion-fest of travelling from place to place and repeating the same activities, I played it to near enough 100% completion - which I wouldn't normally bother to do. There always comes a point in these games where you look at the icons filling the map and think "wow, I really can't be arsed with this", blitz through the remaining story and never look back. There's something about this one though that dragged me in. Max is wrath incarnate, and roaming from place to place cleansing the land felt somehow appropriate. Like Max's purpose, his unfortunate fate, becomes your own.
In terms of setting, the game plays it's bleak, insane apocalypse very well. When I first began playing I was somewhat taken aback by the levels of brutality - and it's everywhere, in every pore of the game. When Max takes damage, he bleeds and bruises and his visual wounding takes time to heal. Even the V6 and later V8 engines scream and roar at you incessantly. The whole thing is incredibly visceral. But as you continue to play, it becomes such a regularity that it's almost mundane. Business as usual. The madness becomes you.
Anyway, in terms of reviewing the video game, it has it's problems of course. It's terribly repetitive and the actual story content makes for a very tiny portion of the total package. Nonetheless, I enjoyed it (if that's the right word) and I recommend it heartily.

This game was all-around a dissapointing experience. The first issue I had was the awful gunplay. If I wasn't aware of the fact the game was supposed to have an amazing story, I probably would've deleted the game on the spot. And the story wasn't incredible either. They literally give you an illusion of choice, since number one your character is insane and half of what he sees isn't there, and two it doesn't matter in the end, because no matter what you do, Lugo and Adams die, you get to the tower, and you get a whopping three different endings to pick from. Quick sidenote, Lugo's death irritated me. The period when Lugo is actually hung and the time you reach him is probably close to five seconds, and it only takes you another two seconds to free him, yet he dies. Back to my main point. You get three endings, which are:
1. Kill yourself, basically the worst ending and a huge cliffhanger
2. Get rescued by soldiers and go home, still a bad ending since your character will obviously never recover
3. Kill the soldiers who try to rescue you and basically let your insanity fully take you over as you head back into Dubai to presumably die (hopefully), and it's still a bad ending and probably the most moral-questioning one.
I also feel like the whole Walker and Conrad relationship is basically the Mason and Reznov of third person shooters. One appears to the other constantly, both talk to eachother, hero gets questionable looks, and in the end discovers it was all in his head. And that's probably my final issue. Since Conrad wasn't behind this, it was obviously the radio man, who was controlling the 33rd. And yet even though there were obvious signs (in the eyes of Lugo and Adams) that Walker was imagining things, they went along even after they killed the culprit, resulting in guaranteed death for your comrades and a bad ending for you.
So there you have it.
Spectacular Story.

This is a really fun and addictive racing game where you will find yourself travelling at ridiculously high speeds, over jumps, around loops and drifting around corners. The single player mode provides a challenge and you will want to keep improving your times to move up the leaderboards, but the game really shines in multiplayer. Races can be tense and very exciting and final results will often be decided on just milliseconds. The tracks and other content produced by Nadeo are good enough, but the many customisation options bring so much more to the game. The level editor in particular is mostly simple to use and there are many good tracks provided by the community that add a lot of variety and will keep you interested in the game for a long time. The other TrackMania games are very good as well, but the track features and excellent car handling that form the Stadium environment make this game come highly recommended.

Rogue Legacy is a roguelike (duh), bullethell, platformer, where you explore a randomly generated castle collecting gold in order to get better abilities. The biggest draw to this game for me was the fact that everything you earn is passed down to a new heir each time you die. Every heir has their own unique traits, classes, and spells at their disposal. The traits are sometimes helpful like perma-roided which gives you more knockback and drwarfism which makes you tiny and able to reach secret areas of the castle. Other traits however can be silly like colorblindness, nearsightedness, and vertigo, which flips the whole world upside down and reverses the controls. All in all definitely worthwhile if you can get it on sale. I give Rogue Legacy an 8/10

Everybody's favorite Half-Genie Hero is back and Ret-2-Go! She's dancing her way through the danger with a variety of forms, spells, and items--but does it hold up compared to the former entries?
Mostly, yes. Let's start off with some pros.
PROS:
*The new art design is absolutely gorgeous, with painstaking attention paid to both the animation fidelity and character design. Sequin Land and its people have never looked so good.
*Core gameplay is still superb: jump, whip your hair back and forth, and dodge what you can as you make your way through levels and discover hidden secrets with the help of any shapeshifting forms you happen to pick up along the way (and after). If you've played a Shantae game before? You'll feel right at home.
*As always, the soundtrack is a joy to listen to. Nothing more to say on that--the music is great!
*If you're a fan of the usual dialogue found in a Shantae game--wacky, weird, and sometimes a little 4th Wall-Breaking with a veritable drenching of saccharine Feel Good Vibes--then you're in for a treat. It's not gonna make you think on the existential crisis that plagues us all, but hey, it'll warm your heart and probably get you to crack a smile. Just as good, right?
But, no game is perfect. So let's look at some cons.
CONS:
*While the backtracking you'd come to expect from Shantae, or any Metroidvania for that matter, is still present? It feels cut down, streamlined, and less rewarding than before. While you'll amass over a dozen new forms that get your hips shaking, most of them are rarely used for more than bit puzzles--and then they're never really needed again. Mermaid, Monkey, and Harpy eventually become your main forms, and the rest are kind of left hanging.
*While the dialogue remains as endearing as ever, the main storyline itself feels somewhat disconnected from the actual theme it's trying to convey. There are also elements that're introduced, but addressed in a manner that feels lacking--looking at you, Holly.
*While the UI itself is very comfortable, the menu screen suffers from some clutter issues that were a minor irritation. Items you wouldn't think to use again--like the previous ranks of your damage upgrades--are kept in the inventory as toggles, so you can weaken yourself by choice. Still, that's a case of "Your Mileage May Vary." I could see somebody using those toggles as self-inflicted "hard mode" conditions.
*It's not long. I clocked in at around seven hours to complete the main campaign, though there's the additional Hero mode to tackle for fun--you get to start a new game with all of your main forms.
Shante: Half-Genie Hero isn't -better- than the previous games, but despite some minor gripes and irritations, I find it still holds up rather well to former iterations of the series. There's also the point that DLC will be introduced at a later date which may shake up some of my points. If it does? I'll revise my review to accommodate.
Still, if you're looking for a simple "buy it or not" deal? Go ahead and buy it. It's good, simple fun that's worth the price of admission.

I was skepticle at first about this game. I'm not a huge fan of the Mad Max franchise, but got this game in a bundle. Graphics, voice acting, music, brawling, car mechanics (for the most part), scenery, map size, and minor details are top notch. It feels like the Arkham and Shadows of Mordor games, but I think benefitted from lower expectations that those beloved IPs.
Complaints - there is no real sense of urgency on the part of the protaganist or the antagonist. For instance, you have this terrifying enemy who controls the world with an iron fist, but even as you rip his empire down he doesn't seem to take notice. As I futzed around taking camp after camp, he never once put a bounty on my head or tried to stymie my progress. He just let me do it. So I would say that the story telling and lack of push back is a problem. For example, you tear down a tower or a camp, you should get a wanted rating like GTA.
Another complaint - post completion the game is deserted. After you reduce the enemies numbers, nothing really seems to spawn at all. For completionist, this is very frustrating, because many of the tasks required for 100% require more enemies. Again, after your complete the game and leave a power vacuum, no-body else comes to power and you are just left on your own. Boring.
Other than that the game is great and should be purchased.

Lost in the Wasteland "The Game" Inspired by the movie "Mad Max: Fury Road" and the other Mad Max movies... that's how  i call this game, wich in my opinion begins as game "inspired by" a movie, but ends up creating a world of its own. A world that when it doesn't try to justify it's existence with a main story it is great and alive, full of dust/sand/sun, good main characters, absolutely great secondary characters, much more cars that you can ever want to see (full of crazy designs) and lots, lots of scrap... (and that's just the beginning)
Mad Max is the second great game that i've played based on a movie, the first one being Alien Isolation. Of course these are two very different games, and Mad Max is by all means NOT perfect, but it is good, very good in fact.
The first thing to say about Mad Max before making any ideas, is that you won't play this game because of the main story, and by main story i don't mean the world , the characters and the "context" of the game, wich are great, and totally developed, in fact they are really good, better than most games out there... but the main story and by that i mean the main narrative, or the thing that tries to justify all that is happening in the game... well  it was pretty bad, it was mainly and excuse to introduce all the games elements.
But from the first moment you land your foot (literally) on the game world, you see the first sites of this world, you begin to meet the characters and start doing different tasks and you see all the detail and care that went into creating each landscape, each region or zone of this game and it is by far the best depiction of a wasteland that i ever saw.  It's not only about the technical quality of the graphics, of course that is great and is the first thing you notice, but besides that, there is a design and artistic quality to the lands of mad max (the outback!) that is missing from many games today.
The thing is, that, when you are doing the main missions, you meet of course many great characters, and you go to the main levels wich are great and big, and it is amazing (not the story itself) but....then you have all the secondary levels, and secondary missions, and even more: the scavenging sites...this are not main levels, not secondary even, just optionals things to do, and there are more than a hundred to look for in the map(191!), some of them are big, most of them are small, but all of them have some kind of story to tell, the story of the people that lives in this wasteland, sometimes even the story before all the world became a desert, and it is in moments like this, when you are outside the main story and just wandering the wasteland with you car, and the sun and the dust in your face that the game really comes alive on it's own and it shows you what it does best.
So, graphics are great, but the sound its a thing of it's own too. Starting with the voice actors, they are all great and well acted, main and secondary characters. Max has a great australian accent, wich in some ways makes the game even more close to the original movie. The music for the game is great, a great introduction track but many "desolate world" tracks when you are exploring the wasteland that helps you feel lost and alone, but also are quiet and even peacefull....of course that's the opposite of what happens when you enter a death race, or chase a convoy, wich are very high energy tracks, similar to what you hear in the movie fury road.
Speaking of convoys, chasing convoys is one thing you do many times in the game, and it is one the most exciting things and great moments of this game (specially when you start upgrading your car and building it's destructive capacities).
This game is 50/50. By that i mean, racing, riding your car / exploring on foot, fighting. Both are great, and you could even make it more fighting than racing if you want to (unless you want to complete all the optionals objectives).
The game has an upgrade system, both for max and the car. There are tons of things to upgrade, and sometimes you have to choose what thing to upgrade in order to reflect your gameplay stile (not all upgrades are better than the last one, sometimes they do different things and you have to choose, wich is great). Of course in the end you can try all upgrades if you want.
There is an absurdely big amount of cars to try besides your own (And it's upgrades). Because you can own every car that is featured in game (enemy cars) and different versions of yours.
I'm doing this review after playing the main missions, the secondary missions, fully upgrading max and still playing some more days all the other things that are left to do in game. And i still have a long way to go to achieve everything. This could be repetitive if you don't like it, but if like me you like to wonder in the wasteland and explore it you will enjoy it a lot. In fact it's more fun than it's main story to tell you the truth.
The game is not perfect, but alltough the main story is not good, it does tell a story, trough its world, it's setting and the history of it's characters.
The gameplay is great, diverse and really fun and it what's make this game so great along with the wasteland.
