My first impressions of the game: Wow, this is a great rogue-like! The randomized heroes are funny and diverse. Just like Spelunky, every run teaches you something about the game. I love the fact that you may upgrade your character between runs, so there's a sense of progress.
My impression now: Sadly, after a while, Rogue Legacy is mostly a grinding game. You'll do runs knowing you won't discover anything new, only destroying everything on your way to get money to spend on upgrades. Furthermore, it's always the same rooms, just in a different order. It is not properly procedurally-generated like Spelunky. It may take 15 hours at most to see everything this game has to offer, and even before that, you get a huge feeling of redundancy. Oh, and the randomization of heroes becomes extremely annoying: you always get to choose between three random characters, but you will sometimes have to choose between three unbearable heroes (for example, one with a useless class, one that makes your screen goes upside-down, and one that greatly increases knockback from enemy attacks). Great, one wasted run.
It is an addictive game, but playing it is not quality time. Stay away from it.

Ah Rogue Legacy, from the looks of it you would think it would be a pretty straight-forward platformer with enemies to kill and bosses to fight. Then they throw in the element of RNG where everytime you die, you are given three random heroes each with a trait sometimes good and some GOD AWFUL. Seems ok enough only that everytime you die you lose your money and go right back into the dungeon that also changes each time you go in. So some runs you'll get lucky getting the right class and decent dungeon that you can survive without getting completely futt-bucked by every trap, enemy, and whatever else they throw at you.
So should I get this game is probably the question you're asking yourself. I'll ask you this; do you like hitting your head on a wall so much until you actually start making a a crack in it? Then that's the exact metaphor this game offers. It's very grindy no question about that and you will get frusturated especially if platforming is not your forte but if you're a gaming masochist that likes failing over and over and over and OVER again until you actually succeed, then that feeling of getting through and over-coming a challenge through all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t will give you the euphoria you're looking for. If platforming, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t RNG, and getting angry so often that you want to kick a baby over a field goal post, then don't get this game at all.
Overall I give it a 7.5/10

I whole heartedly recommend this game.  At the time of review I have 210 hrs of game time in.  Far behind in my library at #2 is Kerbal Space Program with 105.  This game is perfectly paced, completely open to infinite designs and has so much depth I can easily see hitting 500hrs.  After the latest update (alpha 31) this game is packed with content and the workshop offers massive expansion and awesome mods (Imperial architect being my current fav.  Star wars prison!).
Pros:
As big as you wanna be!  Want to make a small 25 person prison  that runs efficiently and makes money with minimum security bluecollar criminals?  Go ahead!  Want to make a 500 person Max security only iron curtain that can hold and control intensely volatile and psychotic madmen?  Sure can!
Well designed!  The UI and indicators for things like prison heat, tech tree, controlling and managing intake and regime of the inmates and hiring and firing staff, as well as prison programs is easy to understand and impliment.  I've played plenty of games that after opening them up and fiddling with for 20 minutes I can hardly make heads or tails of the UI or it has infinitely frusturating menus to navigate or item info to memorize.  Not so with PA.
Entertaining!  Set up phone taps and learn a prisoner has set up a time for someone to throw booze over the wall into the garbage area?  Watch them toddle over into the area and as they head back inside stop them and counter their contraband!  Initiate shakedowns to find inmates who have dummys in their beds and are digging tunnels!  The excitement of unearthing a tunnel they have been digging for days that NEARLY reached the outside but was thwarted is always satisfying.  Recruit confidential informants to reveal persons who have knives, needles, poison SHOTGUNS in their cells.  Use sniffer dogs to inspect incoming food and items to ensure they are poison and piano wire free.  The combinations and implications are endless.
No two prisons are ever the same!  One prison may be full of raging alcoholics, another may be a mix of volatile angry inmates and ex law enforcment or snitches that must be contained and seperated or death ensues!  My last prison had 3 legendary prisoners, each capable of disarming and killing guards in a single punch. Citizens of Dunwall, please accept my apologies. I was a hop, skip and a slide away from the Lord Regent's chamber when this seriously compelling lorry sim sped into my life. Suddenly, stealthy vengeance seems far less important than ensuring a load of new JCBs gets to Bratislava on time.
Euro Truck Simulator 2 is that rare thing, a strong sim tethered to a strong game. Where other vehicle-obsessed devs seem to take player motivation for granted, Czech studio SCS understand that a pleasingly modelled steed needs a pleasingly modelled environment to shine.
On this occasion that environment is a swathe of Europe stretching from Plymouth in the west to Wroclaw in the east, from Aberdeen in the north to Milan in the South. The tangle of motorways and major roads is stylised and condensed, but feels massive. After a splendid week of non-stop trucking the stats screen tells me I've still only seen 50% of it.
There's satisfaction in exploring new routes, seeing new golden been-there-done-that squiggles appearing on the in-game map, but it tends to be the promise of cold, hard cash that gets you out of bed in the morning. Like Farming Simulator, ETS2 has a simple yet resonant economic sandbox at its centre.
Euro Truck Simulator 2 review Adding streams to the radio list is harder than it should be.
You start as a low-skilled, truckless lorry jockey, forced to take work from established haulage companies. Slowly (or rapidly if you go to a bank) you amass the funds to buy your first rig and rent your first yard. Then the fun really begins. Contract perusing, truck pimping, skill upgrading, driver hiring... this is Eddie Stobart: The Game in all but name.
Spending 90 minutes ferrying a tank of propane from Sheffield to Prague could (should?) be tedious. The fact that it isn't is largely down to good-if-not-quite-OMSI-standard physics, and varied road layouts and scenery. Periods of smooth, almost soporific motorway motoring nestle between passages of edgier wheelwork. One minute you're cruising along contemplating the sunset over the central reservation, the next you're on a rain-lashed country road at night, waiting for the right moment to pass a painfully slow pantechnicon. Tiredness can't kill in ETS2, but it can leave you jack-knifed in a ditch, feeling awful with a substantial repair bill to pay.
The only time when the game itself loses concentration is when attempting to evoke certain regions and sounds. The further you get from central Europe the less convincing the landscapes become. No one seems to have told SCS's countryside crafters that rural Britain features long green things called hedges. Cities are often depicted with the shortest of visual shorthand – a few warehouses, the odd landmark if you're lucky. Don't expect to see a favourite local roundabout, slip-road, or speed camera in this highly-recommended HGV-driver RPG.

Do not buy this. I regret Maia more than any other useless, unplayable purchase in the dark history of Early Access. Maia is absolutely beneath what's acceptable to release as an EA game. It does not even meet the minimum bar of quality for paid alphas.
As of this updated review, you're still paying for an extremely limited demo sandbox where you can place objects and watch animations happen. The setting can't decide whether it wants to be a realistic simulator (vital statistics on each colonist, food/water/atmosphere required for survival) or a complete joke (giant fuzzy extraterrestrial life).
User interface design is not good, and it's difficult to tell what each control does. The current main controls for Maia are a series of badly documented hotkeys. One of the only good new features: you can skip the tutorial now.
But if you take one thing away from this review: the bugs are
bad. I've experienced sudden framerate slowdowns on both Mac and PC, as well as crashes-to-desktop for no discernable reason. The colonist and robot AI will get stuck in walls or stand next to piles of rubble on no notice. There appears to be very little QA before each release, and minimal progress in fixing the crash bugs since I wrote my last review in 2013 December.
Summer 2015 Update: It still sucks. I'm not even going to sugar-coat this. It crashes and freezes even more than it did last year, and there's still no resource management or objectives to speak of. They literally just added more framerate-drop-inducing wildlife.
Maia isn't worth paying for and probably never will be. I used to think something good might come of it eventually, but after more than a year and a half I've lost all hope.
Summer 2016 Update: Still pretty unstable. They finally made time to fix a few bugs.

While it falls short of previous Shantae-games, it's still quite the fun game and there's currently more to come (I believe there's a Risky Boots addition coming along). The art style alone makes the game worth the money. Game play is responsive and fluid, no major hiccups and as is usual you're able to chose your upgrades freely (magic or pure damage). The game is quite short though, beware.
It's way easier to navigate than earlier games and there's more places to save your game - so if you haven't played any Shantae-games earlier this could be a good place to start. Though you will probably miss out on some of the jokes that's been carried since the very beginning.
The only real negatives about this game is the lack of dungeons. Those were fun in previous titles. But since this whole game is built on instanced content and each level is a form of a dungeon which you'll need to do several times in order to unlock more and more of it - it's my favourite metroidvania-style-type of game series.
Casual playthrough: 7h~ est.
100% playthrough: 8h~est.
100% steam achievements: 11h~ est.

Before I begin, I will let you know that I have played both Risky's Revenge and the Pirates Curse (both prequels). And Although I don't recommend this game, YOU SHOULD GO PLAY SHANTAE AND THE PIRATES CURSE! (which is a great game).
First impressions about this game.
The graphics are amazing (much more so than predecessors) and music is fantastic. And as usual, the gameplay is exceedingly smooth and controls respond very well. The dances are pretty cool and the story also leans more on the comical side compared to most games leaving a lighthearted feeling.
Despite my glowing remarks above, I have 3 large issues with the game.
Content: The length of time required to beat the game and get full completion is ridiculously short, ~5-7 hours for the average gamer.
Story/Character Development: This is also related to the content. The story is pretty weak and honestly if you remove playing the actual levels, I could tell the entire story of the game to completion with like 2 sentences. Connected to this is character development. This game in no way makes anyone really care about any of the characters! Not even Shantae! If I hadn't played both the prequels, I would have no idea why Shantae was a half-genie and why she cared about the genie realm, or what her relation to Risky was! And then the supporting characters, rotty-tops/brothers + sky + bolo/grandpa: the game really does a disservice to how these people relate to shantae as from this game alone you could barely even tell that they were friends and not just some random townfolk A, B, C.
Difficulty: This is yet another problem. Going through the levels are like a walk in the park (even so for non gamers) and the bosses while looking cool, are extremely dissapointing. All of the bosses patterns are extremely easy and they are honestly so weak that as long as you decide to use a potion (which you shouldn't really ever need), you can completely face-tank never dodge any of the bosses attacks and still smash them! Also the 4 skills which have always been a shantae staple are pretty much never needed. The fireball->flamethrower and lightning cloud are excessively weak and useless it pretty much every scenario. The pikeball/scimitar aren't really necessary but are usefull for clearing out monsters/bosses faster. And then the bubble is really good enough to make you invicible to some bosses (not counting the 3rd upgrade which is literally invincibility). And the magic power these things use is almost negligible for the time you need to activate it.
Aside from ease in monsters and bosses, getting 100% completion and finding all the "secrets" is so simple that I don't even need to put any thought to find every single item! While it wasn't extremely hard in the Pirates curse at least I had to go revisit some areas just to search every nook and cranny for the special tinkerbells. In Half-genie hero, all the secrets are pretty much just lying in front of you waiting for you to get the right power to unlock it.
Overall, the game is lovely but is waaaay too easy with a laughably simple and short plot that does not make you care for it in any way. I was really looking forward to this game but it really dissapointed me on many levels, even as a Shantae fan. Although I don't regret buying the game because I was a fan of the Shantae series (and this is probably the last game I'm guessing), I can't really recommend this unless this game is under $10. However, if you haven't picked up any Shantae games before I recommend you try out Shantae and the Pirates Curse. That game is way more polished than this one and doesn't really have any of these big issues that I listed for this entry here.

First of all, this is not exactly a game,  but rather a interactive video, you follow the plot with clicks, where you can make choices of-course that have different outcomes, but in the end we all know how this is going to end. There is no challenge, you can't die in this 'game' unlike the original LiS. There is no trial and error, where, if failed, you must restart from the checkpoint. You just simply follow the objectives on the screen, even if you choose wrong, you can still continue and choose another option till you get it right. The chapters themselves are quite short compared to the first game, the first episode doesn't reveal anything important, except for the origin of Chloe's famous quote 'hella'. The only good part of it was the D&D part. The stretched out cutscenes make it feel longer than it actually is. Voice actors are different - okay, there were some strikes and protests or whatever, but come on, Chloe Price without Ashly Burch voice is not Chloe Price. Developers could just delay the game a bit longer. As much as I love LiS this is one of the unnecessary games. The key element of the first game was the 'rewind' ability which made the game unique. In this game all you get is the 'talk back' ability. I understand that Chloe can't have the same ability as Max, especially if it takes 3 years before the events of the first game, otherwise it could conflict with events established in the first game that take place later (duh), but it just proves my point. The game doesn't provide the same amount of emotions the first game did. LiS had moments that actually made me very sad or even nearly cry. LiS: BtS didn't really make me feel sad, but whether that's a good thing or bad thing - you be the judge. And it takes place 3 years before LiS right? Well, every single character (maybe expect for Chloe) in the game looks exactly the same, not even slighlty younger - 16-19 is not 40-43. so there should be some distinctive differences. I'm not hating the game, I'm just pointing out the elements that bother me. There are many good things about this game though. The game atmophere is great. Graphics and music keep the style of the original LiS game. There are many nods and references to LiS and Max. The BtS story is interesting, but quite short. It took me less than a day to complete all 3 episodes. But it's cheap. And you can also change your outfit that could actually affect some people' reactions. If you are a real fan of Life Is Strange then you will enjoy it, just don't expect it to be as stunning, plot-twisting and unexpected as the first game.

I last left a review / played this game about 3 years ago. I had many issues with the game then. This time around, the same applied. Still having issues with features of the game working.
Here is a list of things I had trouble with during my 4 hour playthrough (which is also up on my Twitch/YT Gaming/Hitbox/Beam profiles):
- Colonists move incredibly slow and thus, progressing through a game is excrutiatingly slow.
- Placing items/rooms is difficult. I had mined out the rocks between my initial default space and the empty space nearby and I hit a bug in which, I couldn't place any type of room in the given empty space.
- During the first mission I had to repeatedly find a new place to setup the microwave transmitter. The transparent showing of the object would be green, assuming to me it was a good position to place the transmitter, but then when placed that ghost object would be red.
- Double clicking to prioritize jobs works some of the time I feel. I had the transmitter, some atmos gens and meat trolleys prioritized, but they were not taken care of in time and I failed the mission or my colonists died.
- I would like to see smarter AI...If I have my storage room setup with atmos gen and a small heater...I'd kinda expect them to hang out in there most of the time instead of venturing into other parts of the base to then die from cold exposure or asphyxiation.
- I had 2 or 3 crash to desktops as well during my 4 hour playthrough.
After trying out this game again, I still cannot recommend anyone to pick this up. I'm sure that Simon is the only one developing this game and it has got to be tough, but I am no happier playing now than I was 3 years ago. There have been improvements for sure since my last playthrough, but from alpha 0.1 (or w/e it was when I first played 3 years ago) to Alpha 0,58 there are still issues that I saw 3 years ago not addressed.

I can see where the game is going from this. I like what I see.
One thing to keep in mind is that this game is in alpha. Now I know a lot of people go, "Oh I'm a software developer, I know what alpha is! This isn't it!" Those people are dumb and probably liars because, hey, this is the internet. So from a completely normal, non-developer girl: This game is in alpha. It's obviously in alpha. It is not feature complete. There is very little in the way of UI and things people expect to be there (like cancelling orders for objects) are not there.
But the concept is there. You can see things working. You can ooh and aah at the pretty graphics because they do look really freaking nice. One thing you can't do is play much. You can't save. Why? It's in alpha. Alphas are not feature complete. They lack many things we've grown used to and honestly take for granted in games. The developer isn't lying to you. They aren't tricking you. They're being very honest that the game is very deep in development. It says that right there on the tin.
So if you don't want to see and experience a slice of game development, if you can wait and be patient, or if you hate bugs and incomplete UI... Then don't invest in this right now. If you can't wait, if you like to see a game grow and change, or if you want to help with development then do invest in it.
So I'll say it again: I like what I see here. I can't wait for more. I mean, cats in bee suits? Come on. That's gold right there.

A charming expedition through the pirate-infested waters of the Caribbean -- or the Norse fjords -- depending on where you sail.
You start with a ship, and choose where to go and what to do in classic, to use buzzwords, "open world" "procedurally-generated" style.  Trade, quest, explore, or fight in pve or pvp battles.   Search ruins, pickup loot.   Level up, but better ships and equipment.   Diablo on the high seas.
Pros:
+ A physics engine that resembles real sailing, adding fun tactical possibilities.
+ Polished UI, especially for an indy title.
+ Great graphics and sound.   Very ambient and relaxing.
+ A semi-MMO.  You can play in single player or on a LAN, but the best fun is joining a big server full of factions engaged in a tug-of-war.  Optional PvP.
+ Helpful trading system so you know what's in demand and where.
+ Nice customization options so you "own" your ship visually, and all without annoying micropayments.
Cons (minor).
+ Documentation a little light.  It's unclear how you unlock abilities.  Learning how to do the more advanced gameplay takes a little time.
+ Ship customization is OK, but ship selection is fairly linear from what I've seen.
A great buy for $10-$15, and solid entertainment when played in a group.

Before I begin, I will let you know that I have played both Risky's Revenge and the Pirates Curse (both prequels). And Although I don't recommend this game, YOU SHOULD GO PLAY SHANTAE AND THE PIRATES CURSE! (which is a great game).
First impressions about this game.
The graphics are amazing (much more so than predecessors) and music is fantastic. And as usual, the gameplay is exceedingly smooth and controls respond very well. The dances are pretty cool and the story also leans more on the comical side compared to most games leaving a lighthearted feeling.
Despite my glowing remarks above, I have 3 large issues with the game.
Content: The length of time required to beat the game and get full completion is ridiculously short, ~5-7 hours for the average gamer.
Story/Character Development: This is also related to the content. The story is pretty weak and honestly if you remove playing the actual levels, I could tell the entire story of the game to completion with like 2 sentences. Connected to this is character development. This game in no way makes anyone really care about any of the characters! Not even Shantae! If I hadn't played both the prequels, I would have no idea why Shantae was a half-genie and why she cared about the genie realm, or what her relation to Risky was! And then the supporting characters, rotty-tops/brothers + sky + bolo/grandpa: the game really does a disservice to how these people relate to shantae as from this game alone you could barely even tell that they were friends and not just some random townfolk A, B, C.
Difficulty: This is yet another problem. Going through the levels are like a walk in the park (even so for non gamers) and the bosses while looking cool, are extremely dissapointing. All of the bosses patterns are extremely easy and they are honestly so weak that as long as you decide to use a potion (which you shouldn't really ever need), you can completely face-tank never dodge any of the bosses attacks and still smash them! Also the 4 skills which have always been a shantae staple are pretty much never needed. The fireball->flamethrower and lightning cloud are excessively weak and useless it pretty much every scenario. The pikeball/scimitar aren't really necessary but are usefull for clearing out monsters/bosses faster. And then the bubble is really good enough to make you invicible to some bosses (not counting the 3rd upgrade which is literally invincibility). And the magic power these things use is almost negligible for the time you need to activate it.
Aside from ease in monsters and bosses, getting 100% completion and finding all the "secrets" is so simple that I don't even need to put any thought to find every single item! While it wasn't extremely hard in the Pirates curse at least I had to go revisit some areas just to search every nook and cranny for the special tinkerbells. In Half-genie hero, all the secrets are pretty much just lying in front of you waiting for you to get the right power to unlock it.
Overall, the game is lovely but is waaaay too easy with a laughably simple and short plot that does not make you care for it in any way. I was really looking forward to this game but it really dissapointed me on many levels, even as a Shantae fan. Although I don't regret buying the game because I was a fan of the Shantae series (and this is probably the last game I'm guessing), I can't really recommend this unless this game is under $10. However, if you haven't picked up any Shantae games before I recommend you try out Shantae and the Pirates Curse. That game is way more polished than this one and doesn't really have any of these big issues that I listed for this entry here.

Beautiful animations and gorgeous designs, this is definitely one of the prettiest 2.5D sidescrollers I've seen in a while. Visually, this game, is so vibrant and joyous to watch, it simply leaves you feeling good.
The music is also nice and simple, having a sort of retro feel to it without the exclussive use of 8-bit samples. It feels very Early-Sonic-ish at some points, wich is high praise considering that the early Sonic games had nice, catchy and energetic tunes for each level to give emphasis to the rapid action.
The game controls very much like most 2D platformers, the controls are fast and responsive and after only a few minutes they will feel like second nature. This game also adds a bit of variety with transformations, meaning that as you progress through the game you will gain the ability to transform into a variety of cratures with different abilities, but I won't spoil too much about that. This mechanic adds to the value of each level, as when you return to them with your new transformation abilities, after you played for a while, you will be able to explore more areas that you couldn't before.
Now, the game in total is not all that long, in fact if you are really into it and don't do much of exploring around each level, you could easily get to the end in the same day you downloaded it. As mentioned before, bacause of the transformations, you will have to do a lot of backtracking, which it can get tedious if you are not into this sort of thing, but discovering little secrets in each level can feel so rewarding at times.
Overall, it's a pleasant little game that I highly recomend to people who want a nice platforming expireince, amazing visuals and simple story that doesn't take forever to finish. It just makes me wonder; if the team had a bigger budget (the game was crowd-funded) and maybe more time, what more could have they accomplished.

I backed this game on kickstarter and have no regrets. The gameplay is fast-paced and highly enjoyable. The main mechanic, transforming, is very well executed and a pleasure to use. This is definitely one of those games that makes you feel powerful, jumping around and whipping things to death with hair attacks and shifting smoothly between whatever forms you need for the task at hand. I played with an XBox 360 USB controller and had no issues whatsoever. You can even rebind the buttons if you want, something not every game offers.
The game has a cute but fairly light story, which is honestly perfect for it. It is enough to keep you moving without bogging you down or getting in the way of the main feature, which is the excellent gameplay. Pretty much my only issue with the game is one I knew I'd have going in. I do find the female outfits and character designs a bit silly/fanservicey (personal preference here, not an attack). That said, they don't really exploit that in gross ways like some titles do. Something I read on TVTropes seems pretty true, describing the style as 'sexy but not sexualized'.
The only exception I found was the first playthrough of the second level Mermaid Factory. I found that level seriously squicky in a variety of ways.
Thankfully all the disturbing elements are gone when you come back later. And to be fair this series has always had some squicky elements to its humor.
I am generally pretty sensitive to this sort of thing, so if you aren't this may not bother you at all. If you are very sensitve, then, be aware. I still definitely reccommend the game, which I feel has a great deal of heart and is well worth it. I have already beat both normal and hero mode, and am looking forward to the extra content that will eventually be released.
EDIT: Something I forgot to mention was the soundtrack, which I found highly enjoyable and perfectly suited to the rhythm of the gameplay. It's all instrumental with the exception of the theme song, 'Dance Through the Danger', which plays during the first run of the first level as well as during the ending credits. That song... well, let's just say that three days after playing it was still getting stuck in my head. xD

This game is pretty ridiculous. It's like the company asked a bunch of 4th graders to come up with ideas for a racing game, and this is the result. Wall rides, loops, huge jumps, crazy speed. It's awesome.
That being said, the skill cap is infinitely high. Yes, it's massively fun to go on a server and smash through a bunch of new tracks, crashing all over the place and hitting walls like they owe you money. And it's worth mentioning that since the multiplayer is almost exclusively user-created levels, there are tens of thousands of maps to play. But once you settle in to a server and have learned the maps, then it becomes a wonderfully technical game about shaving off bits of time where you can.
A notable game mechanic, for those unaware, is that in time attack mode (probably the most popular game type, that and Rounds) you can reset to the beginning of the track (or the last checkpoint) at any time. This is a bit of departure from many other racing games. You'll just have a set amount of time (usually 5 to 7 minutes), to get a single best run possible. This makes it so that you never have to waste time finishing a run when you've already messed up, you can just reset and start fresh immediately. Makes for a much more efficient practice regimen, and resulting rate of improvement.
There are three environments within TrackMania 2 (Stadium, Valley, Canyon), but within each environment is an abundance of variety in itself. Since this review is Stadium, I'll focus on that briefly:
-Track materials: Pavement, Dirt, Grass, Water
-Game Modes: Time Attack, Rounds. Probably others, but rarely used. RPG, I suppose.
-Track Types: FullSpeed (because braking is for losers), Tech (because fullspeed is for neanderthals), Dirt (because you are full of self-loathing), Speedtech (Because you're a well-balanced individual with many friends and a winning smile).
Seriously, the infinite permutations of tracks alone makes this game worth it.
The End

While everyting about it feels simple, easy to understand, from the controls to the rules they are also hard to master. You will get better and some rides will feel amazing. I'm not a fan of racing games but this one had me addicted. I don't play all the time but I always enjoy when I race on TM² Stadium. And as some famous anonymous guy said once: "Time you enjoy wasting isn't wasted".
If you are trying to decide if that's a game for you, get it already (TM² Stadium) and give it a try. The production value is well worth the price.

Rogue Legacy is a roguelike platformer that combines elements of games like Castlevania, Dark Souls and various roguelike titles, as such it is a pretty harsh game with a steep learning curve. If platforming and a fair challenge are your thing then I can't recommend this game enough.
The premise involves some dude who does a thing that I won't spoil regardless of how early it happens, said event will be explained throughout the game via the diary entry rooms. Anyway, after completing the tutorial you take the reins of a knight with underwhelming combat strength and set off to explore a randomized castle. Unless you have godlike natural talent then you will most likely die fairly early on, this is where the game's most interesting mechanic comes into play, leveling.
As you progress through each room you will slay monsters and destroy furniture which will reward you with gold, meat and mana potions. Gold is almost useless within the walls of the castle outside of the minigame rooms and is primarily only useful upon your death. You see, once the cold embrace of death takes you, your gold is then inherited by your decendants. They can then use the gold to build up your family manor.
Each upgrade to the manor will increase the stats of each decendant born after the upgrade is purchased. Early on you'll be more focused on purchasing several NPCs used to upgrade your gear or locking the current castle layout for the next heir. But afterward you will want to start buying upgrades to your stats, I for one usually ignore mana and go straight for attach, health and crit rate/damage.
Sometimes you will even find a treasure chest which may contain runes and blueprints. These are useful when you die as you can give them to NPCs in order to forge new armour and equip new runes. Armour being self explanatory lets look at runes, runes are extremely useful in a variety of situations and you can equip one into each armour slot and your weapon slot on top of your equipment. Some runes allow for extra jumps, a dash ability, movement speed and several other mobility boosts. Others affect the castle more than you, for example there's one that boosts how much gold you recieve but at the cost of making the enemies stronger.
There are tons of mechanics to discover and master and the game rewards skill. One of my most memorable gaming moments came from this game when I unlocked the achievement for beating it with less than x amount of deaths. I was on my last life fighting the last boss and he killed me, or so I thought. My character went into the death animation and got back up whereupon I slew the boss. It was such a huge rush as if I failed I would have had to reset my save.
TL;DR
Rogue Legacy is hard but fair, if you like Metroidvania style games with a bit of challenge, go for it. If not, maybe give it a miss until a sale and give it a go.

Man how to be concise about a series that technically spans 8 episodes?  Here we go...
In short: It's good.
It's unlikely to convert those whom weren't crazy about the original, but fans can feel safe to jump on this.
Similar to the original Life is Strange, this 3-part series is far from perfect.  Some newer characters don't get much of a chance to develop, so it's pretty hard to empathize with some of their decisions in the plot.  The climax of the 3rd episode will likely divide a number of people.  The build-up is great, but, uh, let's just say it's bizzarely over in a matter of seconds.   Another episode would have gave some time for more development (but I'm biased because I really liked the middle portions of the original series).  With more time Rachel's character might have had more of a chance to be more than just a reactionary character and the overarching plot probably could have been smoothed out.
But you know what? It doesn't really matter.  Before the Storm rallied against my initial skepticism and captures a lot of original's charm.  Deck Nine is able to similarly weave school life into the larger narrative, which balances the darker aspects of the story.  The inhabitants of Arcadia Bay and Blackwell Academy are back and are still quirky and fun.
The dynamic between Chloe and Rachel is great, satisfying a curiosity I never knew I had about their backstory.  In fact I feel the cameos from the majority of the original cast were well used.  Your view of them might change in some instances, especially through the lens of Chloe rather than Max.  It may take a little time to get used to the different tone for Chloe, but it works in the end.  Gone is the ability to manipulate time, but I think that was for the better, making the narrative more cohesive.  The supernatural parts this time around are more for the narrative effect and they work well.
However the biggest thing I feel that these episodes do is put a unique spin to Chloe's narrative.   It achieves some closure for both Chloe and Rachel, something we couldn't have gotten through Max's perspective.  Some may argue that they wished for more explicit development leading to the events of the first game, but I think that would make this game difficult to stand as its own entity.  Let the girls have their own story, Max will be piecing together the in-betweens soon enough.
Who was the bigger figure in Chloe's life? Max or Rachel? Thanks to Before the Storm the answer is much more complicated that it was before.

Much like the first game, you really think about every decision you make. But as Chloe, you can't rewind time to undo your mistaskes so you end up spending more time thinking about what you will say. I barely noticed the game engine change from Unreal Engine to the Unity engine as well and Deck Nine kept the art style and game mechanics very close to the first game which is a plus. The story personally felt a bit short as it was only 3 "in game" days. Many things did happen in the game for technically being a prologue. It's great to see mostly all the characters from the original game in a younger form and revisiting places. But if you haven't played the first game yet, I'd highly suggest to play the main game first before moving on to Before the Storm.
TLDR: 2x decision making, Good engine port, story is a bit short, play the first game
playing Before the Storm.
In conclusion, it's
worth a play; and your money.

Trackmania 2 Stadium is a casual arcade racing game,like the Trackmania 1 series before it,it has a massive online following of players and modders,online leaderboards for country and region and an unlimited amount of tracks to race on,Trackmania 2 series is more of an updated version of the original game with a new graphics and sound engine,a more streamlined interface geared towards simplified ingame downloadable content and trying to combine the other expansions of the trackmania series together.
The old Trackmania games could be purchased as several different themes,sunshine,nations,united and forever,these were separate games with the same racing only set in different locals and racing car types,like F1 rally,exotic.There are also a few other versions on the game that combined everything together as one purchase called united nations.The original is old,it's pricing structure and layout was a mess but the game was very good in it's own right however it would never be recommended over the Trackmania 2 series these days.
Trackmania 2,so for the new updated game,it has now been split into three games,Stadium,Canyon and Valley -F1-STOCK-RALLY each of these games have their own locale and racing style,each of these games are superb in their own way and now these three games are tied together with the new menu system.The gameplay is very arcade,these games use for example the rally theme in a very loose sense to make up the look and sound of the game but overall,all three games are of the Trackmania style of gameplay,a gameplay all on it's own.
Gameplay consists of racing without racing !,you racing on the games tracks or the user created tracks that can resemble something from FZero or Micromachines or Hotwheels,you race simply for the race record and you race against your own and everyone else's ghost car,when you play online you are also racing against online players ghost cars,they are playing in real time but you can't crash into them as there is no collision,if there were collision then the game would simply not work as you can be racing along side as many as 400 other players at the same time of any given track !
This is a very casual pick up and play,have fun and turn off again game but it's also a very skillful game,also a very exciting game that looks and sounds great to boot,it doesn't matter what version of the game you buy,stadium canyon and valley all offer the same level of skill and fun.
So I would recommend everyone play this game,it's the PC racing game that everyone should own a copy of,I will break down the differences of each of the three games in preference as my opinion below.
Trackmania Stadium -You can't go wrong with stadium as it's the base game,the original and the best and has a f1 style car,and roads and track set similar to something like hot wheels and fzero,good traction on the road see's your car doing loop the loops and crazy wallrides,a very fast game and the number one choice over the other two.
Trackmania Canyon -The weakest of the three but it's really really fun,as good as the others but just not the best,however there is a certain amount of skill involved with canyon that pushes it further than vally and stadium,handling is similar to ridge racer making for very fast laptimes and the official trackmania contest finalists play canyon over the other two,i can understand why !
Trackmania Valley - the best looking of the three as it's engine was tweaked as the locale has more going on,more detail and simply just amazing looking ! Valley is the middle ground of the TM games,it feels more like stadium with more traction on the road,but ultra fast like canyon but doesn't offer anything really different apart from being an all round great game,however there are some other things about valley that do stand out and that's in it's level track design,the editor has a little more scope for making day and night time tracks,forrest tracks and underground tracks that can have you driving through mountains,i would say it's the middle ground and having all the of the best features of the two before it you would think it's the best of the bunch but it just isn't ! not a thing wrong with it but it still can't beat stadium.
I would always recommend Stadium as the starting game,it's the cheapest of the three and the core game is there,the other two are just as good but I would say Stadium is the best of the three,with stadium you do not even need to ever play the other two games,the other two are for those who can't get enough of the Trackmania series and it's also good to change out every now and then for something s bit different to race on.
CONS
The game like soo many others are not without problems,many bugs have already been sorted but I found the Trackmania series in particular to have some very backwards design ideas/flaws,for the most part this game and it's expansions will run 60fps+ on the very high graphical settings,some settings still slow it down like motionblur but thankfully you can turn all details from off,low,med,high,the vsync options are not very well explained as there are six options for vsync as well as triple buffering and first time users won't know the correct/best setup,I will say now that you should use vsync,also use every third frame (not constant frame) and also use triple buffer and this should give you a proper 60fps,water shader detail for medium pc's should be med or low,and motion blur would be recommended as off,there are many other options in the start up menu and you should take the time in setting these up,resolution is very important in this game,i found that lower resolutions are fine but you really miss the graphical details so I would recommend you aim for 1080,full frame rate with vsync options and then turn up other details to see what you can get away with.
Other problems with the game are the lack of support,this game is made by a French company and the forums and users are mostly EU users,there's not as many users from the uk and usa on the forums,that doesn't mean there are not many users from uk and usa playing the game,just means we try to avoid the unhelpful forums as I found I didn't get anywhere when asking for help.
The game's layout,the way the game works can be quite strange as well,you earn points for scoring high,these points are called Planets ? your planets are displayed in the top bar when you are in the main menu,these Planets are then used to buy online user created content,you earn a little planets each day that you play as well,another thing that seems backward to me is the apparent new menu system that combines everything together (it doesn't actually work) after all the time this game has been out it still is broken but since an update a month ago it is now working outside of steam but the steam version is still unworking,this means that if you own two or more of the trackmania games,you need to exit out the game and start then other one up from steam ( not a big deal really)
Overall this game is amazing,be prepared to spend some time on the game,take your time and mess about in the menus and try to get used to the way the Trackmania system works,playing the game for the first time gave me the feeling of (wtf have I just bought ?) it took me a while to understand the games charm,I was expecting far too much from the game and when I couldn't really GET the concept of the game along with the many problems I faced in trying to find out what Planets are and why my planets would disappear without buying content or sometimes I would buy content and lose my planets but not receive my item,I found it very hard in finding the answers on google or the mania forums,little things like this can really put you off a strange game and concept like this one,but give it a go and you will find it hard not to fall in love with this game,it's a classic reborn and in my opinion one of the best hardcore/arcade racers you can get !

Disclaimer: I backed the kickstarter (sort of). To be more accurate, I gave a paypal donation that counted towards backing the game well after the campaign had been successfully funded. I'd just finished Pirate's Curse and was excited to see how they'd treat the franchise going forward. Well, you see that red thumb in the corner so I've got some explaining to do.
Let's start things off by saying that my actual feelings towards this game lie somewhere in the middle, however, steam only has a binary "good or bad" system for rating games. Given what I have to say though, I'm sad to say I'm going to have to give this a thumbs down. The game leaves a great first impression but the deeper you get in the more you can see the cracks in its structure.
Let's start off with the positives. The music is fantastic, Jake Kaufman continues to be one of my favorite game music composers and I'm delighted to enjoy the soundtrack to most games he's worked on. The upgrade from pixel art to drawn sprites is absolutely wonderful. The future looks great assuming they stick with this art style, the game looks fantastic. The controls are nice and responsive and the basic gameplay has a good feel to it. While my issues with the genie transformations, that have followed me as I've played through all four games in the series, aren't entirely solved in this game they're much quicker to access, especially with the metronome, which I consider a must have item. There's a couple fun ideas for settings and it's neat to see how the tech of this world is advancing in each installment.
Unfortunately, good music and visuals do not alone for a good game make, now we're in the negatives. The game only has a small handful of levels that feel shorter and shorter the more you have to scour over every inch of them to find more collectables to progress the story. That's the biggest problem with the game, it's spread incredibly thin over a very small and tightly packed space. I loved my first run through each level, the first time through mermaid falls is my personal highlight of this game. The second run through, it was neat to see how little elements had changed. However, by the time I'd finally gotten everything there was to pick up I was pretty much sick of every area. Well, aside from the first and the fifth one which are both, comparatively, tiny levels with little to do.
The linear "level" structure really went against what I've become familiar with in this series. While the map design is nowhere near as bad as Risky's Revenge, (Which, as it stands, is my least favorite entry in this franchise by a wide margin.) it's definitely a huge step back from Pirate's Curse. They went from open maps to screen to screen "levels" packed with things you are required to get but can't until you get more transformations. Aside from that, the biggest problem with them is how they're checkpointed, which is really only an issue because of any of the instant death traps that are in the later environments. The game isn't really all that hard but instant death spikes/lasers isn't how you remedy that. (Side Note: Games don't have to be "hard" to be good.) At best, it's a nuisance, but at worst it's a complete waste of time. Some genie transformations are usefully only for one or two manditory uses to collect an item but outside of that are completely pointless when put up against the other transformations you get (spider). Any points I can get into beyond this get more into the territory of nitpicking so I'll spare you that.
If I were to give you a recommendation it'd be for what is, in my opinion, the best of this series and perhaps the only 5/5 worthy one on the list. I'd highly encourage you to check out Shantae and the Pirate's Curse. It goes above and beyond all 3 of the games it sits alongside. Funnily enough, it's the only game where Shantae doesn't have her genie powers (animal transformations) and I think it plays like a dream because using your abilities flows better with the controls. There's no stopping to turn into a less powerful, less interesting form. Instead you flow smoothly through actions. Be careful though since there might, unfortunately, be some odd issues with the PC port of Pirate's curse based on my browse of the community page.
Edit: 12/30/2016 This review was made with the base version of the game in mind. In the event that any of the added characters/campaigns be paid DLC I feel my review will not need to be adjusted to reflect content sold separately of the original product. There's no guarantee that I'll think to return to the game by the time additional content is added. Any willing to "take up the mantle" are free to do so in my absence.
Author's note: If you enjoy the game, great, more power to you. I'm honestly happy that you have a thing to be happy with. You don't have to agree with me, in fact, I don't expect you to. I just felt compelled to put this together by the time I'd finished with the game. I don't often share my opinions in writing like this but I felt like I had a case to make even though it was going against the tide. Hope your day treats you well.

This game is a mixed bag. On one hand, it is rather enjoyable to sail around and decimate pirates in a glorified colonial-era motif. The combat is simple to grasp and the upgrade tree really forces the player to make choices on equipment rather than paying X gold for a reskinned version of your current arrangement. The rendering is smooth and the battles are frequent enough to keep one interested, which is important because the worlds will bleed together. However, that package comes with a rather grind-heavy level system (even for an RPG, the mechanics scream tedious fetch quests). The singleplayer falls flat, and that remains the biggest disappointment for people who don't want to venture into multi-player maps. I can't say the game is bad, far from it. But I can't recommend it at full price either.
I suppose the best analogy I can think of is the first Assassin's Creed game: beautiful interface, pseudo-historic setting that doesn't worry about the banal details, exciting concept, but the whisps of exploration fun are drowned out by obvious campaign lengthening quests.

Every year, as soon as the cold weather sets in, my hands become dry and flaky. With flu and cold season in full swing, I turn to excess hand washing, which always strips the moisture from my skin. To slough off dead skin cells and restore moisture, I make a batch of exfoliating sea salt hand scrub and keep it by my kitchen sink to enjoy all winter long.
Though it's perfectly acceptable to keep this scrub to yourself, it also makes a great gift to give around the holidays. It's remarkably easy to throw together, so as long as you have all (three) of the ingredients on hand, you can whip up a quick batch. It's a thoughtful, customizable alternative to store-bought gifts, and ensures you'll never show up empty-handed to a party or dinner again.
What You Need
Supplies
1 cup coarse sea salt
1/2 cup liquid coconut oil
5 to 7 drops grapefruit essential oil
Equipment
Dry measuring cups
10-ounce glass container (I used a Weck canning jar)
Fork
Instructions
Grab your supplies. You'll need 1 cup coarse sea salt, 1/2 cup liquid coconut oil, 5 to 7 drops of grapefruit essential oil, and a 10-ounce glass container.
Add the salt. Pour 1 cup of salt into the empty glass container.
Add the oil. Pour 1/2 cup of coconut oil over the salt.
Add essential oil. Add 5 to 7 drops of grapefruit essential oil to mixture.
Stir the mixture. Stir all ingredients until well combined.
Seal and gift. Seal the jar and affix a label or gift tag to the top.
Recipe Notes
Use scrub sparingly — about once or twice a week — by spooning a small amount into your hands, gently rubbing it in, rinsing it off with warm water, and drying your hands thoroughly.
I tried (and failed) to wrap both ribbon and twine around this jar. (It was so slippery!) To save your sanity, just affix a label, tag, or bow to the top of the jar.

I have close to 800 hours on this game, and truth be told it was money very well spent at the time. Today, I would not recommend anyone buying this game because you have missed "the train". The train is what Dayz was back in 2014-2015, easily pulling player peaks of 20.000ish players, with averages pulling at 10,000 players. Dayz was the thing, everyone didn't play it but everyone heard about it. As of this moment, Dayz is pulling barely 2,000 players in average and the peak in December is a 'whooping' 4,800 players. Ever since the q2-q3 of 2015 this game has steadily drained in playerbase, and the reason of that drain is why I cannot recommend this game to anyone of you anymore. Do note that during 2014-2015 this game was a complete bugfest (still is) and yet it pulled massive numbers. It had crap performance; Most players wouldn't even hit 35-40FPS in larger cities: Yet it had such insane coverage and love within the gaming community. Today (2017) this game does not have the same performance issues, a lot of bugs have been fixed; But the games' numbers are in the tank; Ask yourself why before you buy this game.
Dayz firefights are unparallelled, they are better than any game out there can offer. Firefights will always get your adrenaline pumping, you will always be stressed out and you will always be completely swallowed by them. Massive shoot-outs between several groups slugging it out inside the airfield, realistic gun sounds, bullets flying left and right crackling as you run to cover; Simply amazing. The simplicity, elegance of the game, and yet firefights between groups can become extremely messy and impossibly hard to control ones nerves. It is a beatiful combination that is very hard to explain, and that is what has drawn everyone to play Dayz. Dayz will offer you beatiful landscapes and ability to choose what you want to do; PvE, PvP, banditry, friendliness. All you need to do is to find yourself a server and make it your home.
However, the issue with Dayz lies within its inability to create new content. During 2014-2015 there were patches montly, every time a new patch dropped it was new guns, new changes or new clothes - It didn't have to be huge updates. What those updates/patches did was to freshen up Dayz. Because ultimately content is what makes 99% of gamers to stick to their game.
Since late 2015 till 2017 these patches have at best 4 months in-between, or at worst you could be waiting 180 days for one single patch. And these blow some fresh air into Dayz, but in a month; Maybe two the content becomes repetitive. This is why Dayz has been losing players for so long, and for such a large portion of their playerbase. There are simply no new guns inserted into the game, and when it happens once every year or so; They are exclusively spawned in "helicopter spawns" (helicopter crash-sites that spawn once (of 100+ possible sites) every few hours; Which means you'll likely not find that new gun in the next 40-50 hours of gameplay.
2015 this game was supposed to hit Beta, 2016 this game was supposed to hit Beta, 2017 this game was supposed to hit Beta, 2018 this game will hit Beta. This game has been in Alpha (Yes ALPA) since 2014; How long do you think it will take for Dayz to go from Beta to full release?
The developers aren't lazy, they aren't incompetent; They are likely very hard working, But they made a huge mistake. They did not press on with their hype-train. They should had kept pumping out new content in small portions monthly to keep this game fresh, while having a secondary team to work on their engine (in a slower pace). They believed they could re-build an engine from the bottom up and release it quickly, instead patches and content creation disappeared and this game turned into a rinse and repeat. Lack of new content games can work, CS:GO is a great example. CS:GO doesn't get that much new content, but that is because CS:GO is a competitive game where the ultimate goal is to become the best. In Dayz it is to survive, and to survive and keep coming back you need new things to keep you entertained.
Your first 10-70 hours of gameplay will be awesome, you'll love it for its quirks and hilarity; But you'll grow tired of doing the same, with the same over and over. This game is stale, nothing is happening at all.
Instead you should wait. Go look up the steam charts for Dayz, months before 0.60 patch dropped this game was barren with no players left; 0.60 comes out and it peaks at 20,000 like it did back in 2014. After 0.60, no major content has come and as such the game fizzled out. The playerbase is there, it's just that no one wants to play the game until there is new content and as such, you should wait until Beta/full release hits before you buy this game.

"WARNING: THIS GAME IS EARLY ACCESS ALPHA. PLEASE DO NOT PURCHASE IT UNLESS YOU WANT TO ACTIVELY SUPPORT DEVELOPMENT OF THE GAME AND ARE PREPARED TO HANDLE WITH SERIOUS ISSUES AND POSSIBLE INTERRUPTIONS OF GAME " This is one of multiple warnings you get for Dayz by the devs. Yes, the development is slow. Yes the game has huge issues, it is a highly problematic game. It is however, not a bad game. People complain about all the bugs well maybe that's because unlike battlefield games, this wasn't funded by a billion dollar studio. And unlike battlefield this game has some of the most complicated mechanics out there, Dayz isn't a perfect game but it is definitely one of the most expansive ones. I've seen no games that take survival to the extreme like dayz does. so yes, it comes with bugs. Now that we have that out of the way let's begin with the pros and cons of this game.
Pros:
-You can do pretty much everything you want. Every item you find can be used for some kind of interraction. find food? force feed it. Find a needle? find pure alcohol? find an orange? use the needle to poison the orange and give it to an unsuspecting victim.
-It's highly realistic.
-It's graphics look awesome.
-The developers keep working on it and use community feedback.
-Experimental servers so that most gamebreaking bugs are rooted out before you even get to see them in stable branch.
-The community has it's quirks but those quirks are what makes the community so great.
Cons:
- Yes, it's buggy but to me finding a bug that is truly gamebreaking is about as rare as finding a VSS with a full mag and 2 ammo boxes. (Rare AF)
- There's a lot of hackers, it's a shame but it's just how it is. Doesn't make the game bad though. because even AAA titles have hackers and often on the same level as dayz.
-Development takes a while (At the same time a pro because atleast the game's eventual full release will be properly polished.)
-It has a tendency to crash occasionally however the x64 bit server if you're running a x64 OS pretty much nullifies this to make it a rarity.
Overall, dayz is a highly controversial game, some love it some don't. I don't recommend it to the person who wants to have everything handed to him and just not have to put any effort into anything. However if you like a challenge, a serious challenge I recommend checking out, maybe wait until it hits BETA but otherwise, I am sure if you like a challenge you will like the game.

This may seem like a long review but I adore this game and cant stop playing it. I find the jokes hilarious, even after hearing them multiple times. I highly recommend this game to everyone.
Borderlands 2 is a first person shooter that gets harder with more friends playing alongside you in a world called Pandora. I play as Axton the Commando and Salvador the Gunzerker in my solo games. Axton's action skill is a sabre turret that I use to draw fire away from myself so I can be on the offensive while dodging the damage. Salvador has the action skill Gunzerking that allows him to use two guns at once to riddle the enemies with bullets. I have a Maya the Siren and Zer0 the Assassin characters for multiplayer playing with my friends. My version of Maya is a healer uses her action skill of Phaselock, suspends enemies in midair, to revive teammates from afar through a certain skill in one of the class trees for leveling skills. The Zer0 I play applies marks to the enemies, while in his action skill of Deception, so that all damage has more power. Everyone has his or her own play styles, so you get to choose what perks you want to use. The developers have cast two downloadable content (DLC) characters that give six new class trees to play, Gaige the Mechromancer and Krieg the Psycho. Gaige has the action skill called Deathtrap, a robot bodyguard that she can summon to fight beside her. Krieg is a psycho with a Rampage skill with massive melee damage. My Krieg is a tank that takes damage then evolves to a badass psycho and retaliates with monstrous damage. I have two friends that play as Maya the Siren: one that uses her skill to brainwash of the enemies to fight for us so that we don’t have to, and the second that uses her as an elemental damager (damage over time). Everyone has their own way to play each class. The characters are not dependent on any one-weapon category either so an Assassin (Zer0) can use a shotgun just as well as everyone else.
I have some high level characters that I’m still going through again to find the best weapons; the more levels that you gain the better the loot becomes, with 17 Million guns in the main game, you will always be looking for the best guns for your playing style. There are six types of weapons, however every manufacturer adds their own properties to each gun, for example Torgue weapons will always deal explosive damage, Tediore weapons have the fastest reload speed, Dahl burst fires while zoomed, and Vladof has high fire rates. The most powerful damage gun isn’t always the best fit for every situation, there are some weapons that have elemental effect guns that some enemies without having to fire as many bullets as the standard damage guns. Elemental guns have one of five additives, fire, shock, corrosive, explosive or slag. Fire, shock and corrosive are more effective against flesh, shields, and armor respectively. Slag weapons will double the damage of any non-slag weapon, unless the player is in Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode DLC, in which the damage is tripled! Just because of the distinctiveness of elemental weapons, it does not create a less challenging aspect. There are some exceptional weapons that will spawn occasionally and have some unique abilities. An example is the Swordsplosion, a Shotgun from Mr. Torgue’s Campaign of Carnage DLC, which fires a sword that explodes instead of a bullet.
The Developers have added four main DLC story lines that are beautiful expansions to the game. Captain Scarlett and her Pirates Booty will add a swashbuckling story where you travel in a new hoverboat vehicle across the desert to find the compass pieces that will lead you to Captain Blades Treasure. Mr. Torgue’s Campaign of Carnage is all about being the ultimate badass in the sheer butchery of all who rank above you in a competition to find the champion of Pandora. Sir Hammerlocks Big Game Hunt will have you search for exotic animals (that haven’t been introduced until this DLC) while you take down native tribes, Professor Nakayama, and his twisted creations. Tiny Tina’s Assault on Dragons Keep, my favorite DLC, has a Dungeons and Dragons twist titled Bunkers and Badasses where you be trying to save the princess while fighting against the Handsome Sorcerer and his Orc minions.  It includes mythical creatures that will give you new battles with a very unique feel compared to the main game and other DLCs. Beware, Tiny Tina’s Assault on Dragons Keep occurs at the end of the main story line and reveals spoilers; I do recommend finishing the main story before starting this DLC. Ultimate Vault Hunter Pack will allow the player to play a new advanced mode rightly named Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode. Enemies will level up with the players and have the ability to regenerate health to enhance the difficulty. To battle these upgrades, players are given the ability to gain 11 more levels and slagging enemies will cause more damage. Ultimate Vault Hunter Pack 2 will allow the player to gain an extra 11 levels and battle more challenges on Digistruct Peak. Digistruct Peak is a special area where all enemies will appear through digital construction machines. When players have reached level 72, they will be given the option of developing 8 Overpower Levels on Digistruct Peak to gain the highest level of play. Another section of the game’s vast DLC content is Headhunter, DLC maps that are a short story with a boss. Bloody Harvest is a Halloween themed adventure, Wattle Gobbler has a Thanksgiving theme, and Mercenary Day is a Christmas type escapade. Wedding Day Massacre brings a Romeo & Juliet story to life with the bride and groom as Goliaths (one type of enemy in the game). Son of Crawmerax is an island vacation where Hammerlock gets kidnapped.
I highly recommend buying this game, the four main DLC map, the two Ultimate Vault Hunter Packs and the two DLC characters. The cel-shaded style may be a turn off for those that are looking for the highest detail games but I like how it uses the style and made a superb game.

5 reasons I love this game:
1. It is simple, yet addicting. You could just play a quick run for 10 minutes or you can play for hours on end to earn upgrades and try and make more progress in the castle.
2. You will always have more milestones to reach. When you're starting out, struggling to defeat enemies, and have no mastery of the controls you will be motivated just to have runs that contribute anything to your game. Whatever money you make is lost if you don't spend it, and everytime you buy an upgrade, the cost of all the upgrades available slightly increases.
You're motivation is just to improve, however you can. Strive for runs where you get just far enough to afford something that can make your situation a bit easier. As you start to acquire upgrades and get used to the controls, you find you can make more money, but you also need to earn more to keep upgrading your characters. Then you may get far enough to fight the area boss, but you will probably get decimated by them. So you're goal is to fight them more, to learn their patterns and try to defeat them.
Then you finally defeat the boss, but you have 3 other areas to explore, which means going deeper in the castle to fight tougher enemies and surviving enough to challenge 3 more bosses, who will also demand a similar learning curve and challenge you to reach them while earning upgrades to increase your chances. This excellent pacing makes it so the game is constantly rewarding.
3. The game has a lot of variety thanks to the randomized layouts, traits, character classes, and rune/weapon unlocks. It's really fun to experiment with different classes and test out new gear and runes. There are also a large variety of enemies with various patterns to keep you on your toes.
4. This game has a nice metrovanian art style and a good soundtrack as well. I especially like Ponce de Leon's theme.
5. Unlimited New Game +'s. Nuff said.

Gang Beasts is a very unique breed of fighting game. Rather than executing fireballs or memorizing 127 hit combos, you’re flailing around wildly hoping to knock somebody unconscious and toss them aside, all while dressed up in your dinosaur onesie. The physics-based combat consists primarily of punching with your left or right fist, kicking, and headbutting.
That said, it’s a hilarious game. Part of what makes it shine are the different levels you can fight in. Levels include a ferris wheel, two suspended scaffolds, on top of a blimp, or in a subway. On each level there’s always some interesting ways to kill your enemies, so watch out because they’ll be coming after you to throw you into the path of an oncoming train or to break the wires holding your scaffold in the air so you plummet to your doom.
Having played this with some friends locally, it can get downright hilarious when there’s a lot of different things going on at once, or when people start ganging up on somebody else. The online component works, but it’s still very much in beta, it seems. I experienced a few glitches where a round would end and it wouldn’t proceed to either the next round or the next map. Eventually I had to quit the game altogether and join a different server manually because quick joining a server put me right back in same one.
As with any fighting game, do yourself a favor and play this one with a controller. The keyboard controls feel weird. I played the game with a wired X Box One controller and didn’t have any issues with it. With the punches being on the left and right bumpers, my hand was cramping up after a while, but that didn’t bother me.
All in all, Gang Beasts is a lot of fun, but there’s a lot to learn. It’s easy to pick up and just start wailing on somebody, but to really excel at it you need to do some internet searches for more advanced tactics. I ended up watching some videos on YouTube and learned some things that I couldn’t find explained anywhere. An in-game tutorial (basic and advanced combat) really would be a very welcome addition to the game.
Now get in there, punch some people in the head, and throw them from the top of an 18-wheeler driving down the highway.

Maia is basically one of many atempts to juice up an old concept. Throughout teh years many games about colony survival hit the games market and only a couple gained a place in our memories. e.g. Outpost, Space Colony, Startopia. But, most of those games are lost in the vast endless space of cybernet.
So, how able is Maia in obtaining a place amongst our memory?
At this point, it's a buy and forget game. Not because of the way it looks, it's probably one the best looking colony survival games out there, but because of the way it tries to create an atmosphere.
I don't know exactly why, but something is missing.. The feeling of survival. Why should I build s**t if I don't care. Why should I research things if I don't see the point in doing so.
This is probably because of the lack of any solid plot and future goal that keeps me interested.
Yea, sure, my goal is to survive. Yea, whatever, I'm playing a game, I want some glittering prices along the way and some motivation to do some crazy things. I'm playing a game to escape the dull side of reality, so please, don't show me my daily struggle.
In other words, we need a good Visual Novel style content / plot / story. We need interesting characters and social dillema's.
If Maia is able to provide us with those things in the near future, well, in that case we might have ourselves a winner.
But, as long as it stays the way it is (Bugs not taken into account) it's a dull experience.
My final verdict, which might sound strange, is "Yes"not bad, actually pretty good, because it shows good potential.
On the other hand, I won't hesitate to put out a huge "NO" if the developers don't change the "Living" part of the game. The social interaction, story and story driven motivation.

Windward is very entertaining. You sail around countless regions, plundering towns and converting them to your allegience. Once you drive off all the pirates, you're free to sail around, performing quests and gathering gold. Every so often you'll find some lost cargo floating around that's yours for the taking. Just as with any enemy though, the pirates will eventually return and you get the taste of battle once again.
Quests you can do are numerous in quantity, always being replenished by each town. You can ferry passengers to neighboring towns, drop off/pick up supplies, take a few drunken townsmen on a sightseeing trip, hunt down rogue pirates, convert pirates to fly your banner, etc. The amount of quests available are too many to list.
The sailing controls arent perfect, but they're very well done. You actually feel as if you're sailing around, subject to the laws of physics as in real life. The game does this by adding an inertia factor with turning and stopping, and other ways that must be experienced first hand.
There is a working market with upgrades and materials for sale. Work towards advancing to the largest ship available and customize your ship to fit your needs. You can change your ship's color, sails, emblem, hull, etc. When you first start off the game, you're also able to choose your allegience which comes with unique perks.
All in all, windward is a great sandbox game with a lot to do. You can create many worlds of various sizes and explore all the regions available in them. Singleplayer is fun, multiplayer is great, and the combination of visuals and music makes for a relaxing time.

Full disclosure: I backed the game way back in 2013 and may be a little biased.
I was really worried that Shantae: HGH is going to be another Mighty No. 9. I reminded myself that WayForward is a company with a good service list, but to err is human, right? Well, It has been out for 3 days now and I'm glad to say that it's not Mighty No. 9. In fact, HGH kinda blows the Kickstarter failure out of the water. HGH is a neat experience of a great colorful and vivid artstyle, amazing music and comfortable gameplay. The gameplay is your typical metroidvania: scattered over the levels are areas that are reachable only by performing a certain dance that transforms Shantae into a spider, a crab, a mermaid and et cetera. You could seperate the transformations into two groups: group 1 is made for platforming and group 2 is made strictly for puzzles (at least I have never personally found a platforming use for the mouse transformation). You're going to spend most of the game travelling back-and-forth, collecting hidden items with newfound transformations.
This is when you get to the cons of the game. The transformations are, long term, pointless gimmicks. The mouse transformation is used around 5 times all over the game, while some of the other ones (mermaid, for example) come in too late to be a viable alternative to the one you got earlier (crab transformation). There's also no point to use them to combat enemies. In the end, you're going to use transformations to discover the occasional blocked off area, transform back to original Shantae because she's stronger, faster and more versatile, and then go on. By the way, as I've said, that's all you're gonna do for the majority of the game. I didn't really find that too bad because I'd be doing it anyway, but the fact that you're basically forced to repeatedly go through the levels to find hidden stuff makes it easier to 100% the game. And if you 100% the game too early, you get an eight hours long playtime. Now, I think that's quite normal for an indie platformer (for example, Shovel Knight takes about 8 hours to beat it too), but some people may disagree - that's quite alright, though WayForward has new characters for the game in the works. Maybe that will make the game longer?
Basically, as a summary: Shantae: HGH was a very good experience, however it's only two real flaws are the most important ones: the transformation gimmick that dies off as the game progresses and the length.
