Shantae: Half-Genie Hero has a lot of charm and I love the stylization. I really like how you can transform into different animals to get through obstacles from being a monkey climbing walls, to a harpy that can flap flap flap. Its a Average platformer at best, as the game has a lot of backtracking and how the difficulty scale goes from very easy to a super hard, flappy bird like final level. I think that kind of killed the fun for me, (especially that final level.)
The game is under 10 hours, even finding all the secrets. I think they could have put a few more levels to help the difficulty scale, maybe make them progressivly harder.

Caution: While my end result is that I do recommend the game, I do not heavily recommend it like I would with snap-buy titles.
I've enjoyed Shantae throughout the years. Pirate's Curse is, to me, the best game of the series and sadly, Half-Genie Hero does not surpass that game's level. It has too many flaws for that.
For one, the past games had a sense of exploration. Big worlds which you'd discover all kinds of new things in when going through them later on, metroidvania style. Half-Genie Hero...tries to have that, but the worlds are just so tiny. There's a feeling that there should be more, but there simply isn't.
The end-game also has a very strong "Collect 10 Bear Asses" feel to it. Just padding to make the game last a bit longer for those who want to get the proper ending. While it is a tradition for Shantae games to do something like that, it never felt as obvious as it does here.
Then there's the various forms you can take. Some just feel a bit tacked on, like the Spider form which you need only for one little thing, and is never needed again except for an achievement. The Crab form also feels redundant with the Mermaid form around, with only a very few small things ensuring you must use it.
Finally, the game is on the short side. 7.5 hours for 100% completion without actually rushing through the game...it's not horribly short, but I had hoped for longer.
Having said that, these aren't huge problems. The gameplay itself is smooth as ever, perhaps even smoother than before. The flow of most of the game is perfect, the enemies are nice and varied, the level design itself, while small, is very well done, so gameplay wise there's nothing really wrong with the game.
The graphics are also top notch. A lot of work has gone into the animation and it shows, the game looks fabulous. The music also helps, the ever-present ear worms keep up a great tone.
Finally, the absurd and hilarious conversations are, as ever, another highlight of the game. It does refer it's predecessors a fair bit which might be annoying if this is your first Shantae, but even for those people there's plenty of good humor to go around.
All in all, I think that this game's biggest problem is the existence of Pirate's Curse. That game set a very high bar that Half-Genie Hero falls just short of. I definitely do not regret the purchase, I had just hoped for a bit more after the kickstarter and the various postponings. The game is technically very well done, it just lacks that bit of punch.

But seriously though this is a great game. A charming artstyle with beautiful and bright HD graphics, fun level design, and tight platforming controls make this a must-buy for any fan of the 2D platforming genre. The mechanics of your genie powers, the great music, and Shantae's cheery personality itself makes this an amazing game in my opinion. If you like the idea of playing a head-strong, spunky girl who transforms into animals as she saves the day, then this is the game for you.
This is more of a Megaman style of platforming than a Metroidvania, this means the levels are going to feel alot more linear at first. The real exploration comes from after you get your animal abilities, where the extra means of movement allow you to explore the untouched nooks and crannies  of the levels you previously cleared.
The cons I can think of are:
backtracking to find every item in every stage may get repetitive. However this is entirely optional unless you either want to do the little bit of extra work to get the good ending or just 100% complete the game.
This game is also probably the easiest game in the Shantae series. Shop items might as well be given to you with how cheap they are, barely any real threats in terms of enemies, and thinking creatively will sometimes let you use your animal transformations to completely bypass entire sections of the game.
Edit:
The new introduction of hardcore ups the difficulty on a grand scale. More enemies, different enemy placement, more damage, and new boss attacks make for a much more exhilerating experience.
However.
Even with its faults, I stil llove the game. It is an excellent edition to the series and a pretty good step forward.
Personally I loved the story, but heads up, its episodic like a Saturday morning cartoon. *SPOILERS* There is no Big Evil threatening to destroy the entire planet that requires an epic adventure. Instead Shantae has to deal with a bunch of smaller threats and go on smaller adventures one at a time. It's less of "This is one of the most important days in this character's life" and more of a "This the stuff this young lady has to deal with sometimes."
Using internet guides at the late part of the game, I was able to 100% the main default story within a total of about 7 hours. Its a short game, but it was fun enough that I'm going to be revisiting this story plenty more times.
I also need to mention that there is going to be alot of DLC coming out in the future of writing this review. Costume swaps for Shantae, and extra story modes where you play as some of the side characters are all underway. As a fan of the series, I am very excited to see some of the other characters get some time in the spotlight.

The best waifu.
But seriously though this is a great game. A charming artstyle with beautiful and bright HD graphics, fun level design, and tight platforming controls make this a must-buy for any fan of the 2D platforming genre. The mechanics of your genie powers, the great music, and Shantae's cheery personality itself makes this an amazing game in my opinion. If you like the idea of playing a head-strong, spunky girl who transforms into animals as she saves the day, then this is the game for you.
This is more of a Megaman style of platforming than a Metroidvania, this means the levels are going to feel alot more linear at first. The real exploration comes from after you get your animal abilities, where the extra means of movement allow you to explore the untouched nooks and crannies  of the levels you previously cleared.
The cons I can think of are:
backtracking to find every item in every stage may get repetitive. However this is entirely optional unless you either want to do the little bit of extra work to get the good ending or just 100% complete the game.
This game is also probably the easiest game in the Shantae series. Shop items might as well be given to you with how cheap they are, barely any real threats in terms of enemies, and thinking creatively will sometimes let you use your animal transformations to completely bypass entire sections of the game.
Edit:
The new introduction of hardcore ups the difficulty on a grand scale. More enemies, different enemy placement, more damage, and new boss attacks make for a much more exhilerating experience.
However.
Even with its faults, I stil llove the game. It is an excellent edition to the series and a pretty good step forward.
Personally I loved the story, but heads up, its episodic like a Saturday morning cartoon. *SPOILERS* There is no Big Evil threatening to destroy the entire planet that requires an epic adventure. Instead Shantae has to deal with a bunch of smaller threats and go on smaller adventures one at a time. It's less of "This is one of the most important days in this character's life" and more of a "This the stuff this young lady has to deal with sometimes."
Using internet guides at the late part of the game, I was able to 100% the main default story within a total of about 7 hours. Its a short game, but it was fun enough that I'm going to be revisiting this story plenty more times.
I also need to mention that there is going to be alot of DLC coming out in the future of writing this review. Costume swaps for Shantae, and extra story modes where you play as some of the side characters are all underway. As a fan of the series, I am very excited to see some of the other characters get some time in the spotlight.

This is a solid game, with plenty of charm and great gameplay.  I love hearing the intro song for the first stage, and there's so many little tidbits to make this game extra nice.  I'd say it has that "Nintendo Polish"... like you know when something's added into a game that's not nessessary but adds positive spice to the presentation and emmersion of the world? The dance transformations are back and they're great, with little time used to transform to different animals and objects for all your platforming/spell needs.  And I think the best part is the fact when you get an item like the Max Attract (third tier item) you can switch them off and go into every stage with as little equipment as you'd want, giving you a little challenge should you wish it.  It's wonderful to have that as an option, especially if folks want to challenge one another to beat the game with certain aspects. (hint hint Mr. Dragonrider Completionist ;D )
As for completing the game, achievements and all, it's very doable.  So long as you've got a good memory for all item locations and a good place to farm the cash, and with the bonus Hero Mode when you beat the game once, you'll have a fun time. For those who want a quick review with little explanation for ratings. The TL:DR is just below.
1 - Worst I've seen,  5 - Around most games in this genre,  10 - best I've ever seen
Graphics 8/10
Game Play 9/10
Replay Value 7/10
Multiplayer Aspect 9/10
Progression System 8/10
If you hate micromanaging every little thing, then this game is the game for you. Otherwise if you're looking for the ability to manage crew and other ships with great detail then you'll have to look somewhere else. Unless the Dev has plans for adding permanent fleets to the game. I would certainly enjoy having control of a fleet.
The TL:DR stop here. Now for a break down.
Graphics 8/10
Pros: This game has beautiful graphics, you'll never feel like you're staring at some ugly mess of low resolution textures. Nice vibrant colors and wonderful water. The world feels very much alive. the game doesn't feel dated like most games you'll see today or in this genre.

Cons:The downside is the limitation of a zooming, so you can't really see your ship up close. Best thing is a spy glass which will only let you zoom out farther to see around you further away, an upgrade that I would recommend everyone getting.
Game Play 9/10
Pros: I rated this really high, although I could have rated it lower. I gave it a 9/10 because it works. Everything just works and the flow of the fights are all seamless. You can end up in a tangled mess with 4 pirates and skillfully maneuver you way to victory. This is of course challenging if you're not very good at tactics. I have friend who can't even handle one pirate let alone 4.  Some fights you win, some fights you don't. Pick your fights wisely, no one will shame you for running away to survive and fight another day.
You can die, die, die, die and always get back up with out any major loss. I would recommend not dying as I believe it can negatively impact your stats temporarily. Not 100% sure, but it makes sense to have some sort of repercussion.
Cons: There's no crew on crew fights, or captain vs captain sword play. It would really break the intended game play and  I always hated having to restock on crew after every battle in the other games, but those types of fights were always fun as well and helped to immerse you into the pirates life.
Replay Value 7/10
Pros: You can play as 4 other factions and experience the world semi-differently. There are multiple ways the world can be constructed so the maps will never be the same. The loot drops keep it ever so different and your luck plays a big role on the kinds of drops you get.
Cons: The game is a big grind fest and to do it once kind of puts off wanting to do it again. If I was leveling up at about twice the rate I am now it would be a whole lot better for the progression.
Multiplayer Aspect 9/10
Pros: You can have tons of people in your game, not sure what the limit is. Everyone has their own loot drops HUGE PLUS!  You can trade all aspects of your ship's items with other players. The sky is the limit *wink wink* The multiplayer in this game is fully functional and
Cons: You can't join instances without being first invited even if you're friends with that person. Maybe Dev can add an option to allow others to freely join your instance or to lock it to invite only? There's no option to auto follow friends or allies, would make afking easier so at least your ship isn't idling around being useless if you have to leave for a moment. It would be something I'd love to see added to the game.
Progression System 8/10
Pros: The progression system is nice, the talent points you earn from leveling give nice bonuses depending on what you pick. You can eventually max out the tree from what it looks like so you won't be missing any skills. You have a nice variation of abilities that accomplish different goals. I would like to see more passives in respect to leveling towns and such.
Cons: The skills do no differ a lot from other nations. They are pretty much the same with respect to your primary cannon skill varying by faction or whatever you decide.
Overall Score 8/10
I highly recommend this game to everyone. It's very fun and you'll spend a lot of time especially with friends playing the instances and capturing towns. For a real challenge put the slider to 200%, the pirates are a real threat at this difficulty, but the rewards are real.  You can always change the difficulty of the game on start so you'll never be locked in a specific setting.  For a $15 game you're getting your money's worth. This is a good game to make friends on. Even though it doesn't have a lot of content or substance (although that might change in later updates), it always draws you back in with the promise of having fun with friends or family. It's also really silly and fun to watch. That may not sound like a lot to some people, but that's enough for me. I will warn you though, this game is best played with a console controller and not a keyboard. If you can find a way to make the keyboard work though, then go ahead and use that instead.
Now for some criticisms for the game in it's 0.5.6 Beta form as of May 9th 2017.
-On the subway map, people can simply stand on the side of the tracks and will be knocked back into the arena by the train
-On the truck levels, I really don't like how the only way to avoid being hit by the signs is to lie down on the front of the truck, or go in the storage area.
-Again on the truck level, lying down on the front of the truck often leads to the sign pushing a person into the truck (and I wouldn't be surprised if people did this on purpose in order to win). Getting stuck isn't unique to the trucks level, but it is the most often I've seen in happen on, and I think getting stuck on the map in general needs to be fixed. Also, maybe it shouldn't be allowed to get in the storage area of the truck with the poor and uncontrolable camera, as you can't see yourself most of the time.
-This is just my opinion, but I really liked the lives system better than the wins system. I'd rather have it so that the person who survives is the winner, not the person who won the most rounds. This is because it makes rounds last way too long, with everyone in the game getting two wins before someone can finally win. This is especially true when the game is full of people who kill themselves while holding you and making the round a draw.
-As you can probably tell by that last criticism, I don't want each game/level/map to last too long, so I believe that a timer that ends the game when it's taking too long should happen in a shorter amount of time after the game starts. You'd be surprised by how many people in this game don't do anything and wait for the other person to die, thereby making the game take longer than it has to.
-One of the trench coat options for the costumes actually affects that players chances of beating others and winning. The coat is very flappy and heavy, making it hard to pick them up and throw them over the ropes or kick them under the ropes in the Ring level. I don't know if this was done on purpose but this trench coat seems to be the only costume choice that affects the actual gameplay. I think having costumes do that is a great idea though.
-I'm perplexed by the fact that you only seem to allow one map in the "wave" gamemode. What happened to that building roof map in earlier versions? And why did you replace it with the grinder level of all of them?
-On the map with the fans (I think it's called "vent"), I really don't like how people can stand on the fan blades without dying, that shouldn't be possible, and I don't even think it was in earlier versions.
-And finally, the act of going unconscience seems very inconsistent. It feels like certain people just head-butt me unconscience easier than others, and sometimes I head-butt people unconscience even though it seems like the opponent put in the same amount of effort. The amount of time you stay unconscience too is very unpredictable. Sometimes it's a second until you wake up, sometimes it's six. And I understand that the more you head-butt, the liklier you are to go unconscience, but even with that knowledge it doesn't seem to affect certain people. What I especially don't like is when I get knocked unconscience with a head-butt immediately after waking up. It's the same frustration I get with spawn killing. That is especially a problem in the wave gamemode.
Things I wanna see:
-More maps on the wave gamemode
-More maps in general
-Costumes having effect on the gameplay or getting rid of that trench coat I mentioned
-More gamemodes

Rating: 8/10
Overview: Open World RPG
Similar Games: Batman Arkham city/Knight, Shadow of Mordor,
The Good
+ The wasteland is beautiful yet deadly, it feels massive and empty yet there is plenty of things to do. Driving over sand dunes while the sun sets, exploring desolate locations,races, liberating camps, story and side missions etc. The first time you experience a massive sand/thunder storm is pretty amazing, you can either seek shelter and wait for it to pass to try to survive it and collect massive rewards. Things like that only re-enforce the perception that the wasteland is tough to survive in. The wasteland is a great example of how good art direction and design can take a seemingly boring environment and turn it into something special.
+ Scavenging locations and liberating camps throughout the wasteland allows you to collect scrap which can then be used to upgrade your character or your vehicle the magnum opus
+ Lots of different challenges to complete, completing challenges grants you special tokens which can then be used to further upgrade your character.
+ Car combat is a big component of the game and destroying vehicles feels very satisfying. You can destroy enemy vehicles in a variety of ways.
+ Chumbucket, your loveable yet strange hunchback sidekick. The most interesting and fun character in the game.
+ Incredibly well optimized, plenty of graphical options
+ Lots of side quests, collectables, missions, races etc that are varied and provide a nice distraction from the main quest.
+ Great soundtrack and sound effects.
The Average:
The combat is a shallow version of Rocksteady's Batman games. There isn't enough gameplay mechanics or depth tied to the combat so the majority of the time you are only punching or parrying attacks with the occasional dodge. Even when you upgrade your combat skills, it doesn't feel like much has changed. Parrying an attack isn't instant so many times you will be in the middle of an attack only to be punched/charged from behind. This is further aggravated by the camera angle which is zoomed in to close to the character making it hard to see where all the enemies are.
The story is decent but nothing really special either, it doesn't stand out but it gets the job done.
The game is fairly easy especially if you are accustomed to the combat system. I never found the game to be challenging.
Some annoying  glitches, nothing game breaking but every once in a while an enemy will disappear through the floor, characters getting stuck etc.
If you want to do many of the optional quests, it can start to feel repetitive....like most open world games.
The Bad:
Boss battles are all the same which is a shame because there is so much potential here.
Conclusion:
A fun game that is great if played in short sessions. If you love a collect-a-thon, then you will truly love this game. The good news is you can skip many of the optional stuff and stick to the main story and still have a good time.

For a little foundation as to my experience with the Hunter, I started playing the subscription based game as long as 8 years ago.  I did not play it consistently, but amassed a large amount of hours off and on over a long period of time.  When I saw they had made a standalone, non-subscription based game I was pretty excited.
Call of the Wild is a fantastic spiritual successor to the original the Hunter and offers a similarly satisfying, as well as frustrating, experience.  Call of the Wild offers a little bit more on the RPG elemnts of the game, allowing you to level up skills and perks along various trees, with two different "classes" for skill points and 4 different perk trees for the various weapons.  The game currently offers 4 different weapon types with Shotguns, Rifles, Handguns, and Bow-and-Arrow being represented.  Three different hunting reserves offer a diverse range of weather, and biomes, as well as a decent number of different species of animals to hunt.  Gone are the licenses required to hunt different species and this is a welcome addition.
The gameplay is quite similar to the original the Hunter.  There are different animal calls and tracks to follow as well as being able to place bait, luers, and make calls of your own.  As you level up your skills and perks your ability to used these various mechanics will increase along with the items effectiveness.  There two different skill trees accentuate the stalker and camper methods by increasing your ability to follow tracks or plant luers/make calls respectively.  This allows you to progress down a path no matter how you prefer to play the game.
It can be frustrating following animals.  Sometimes it feels like they are impossible to catch up to, or will never stop running.  I recommend going slow.  Animals will often loop back towards you after being startled and running away.  This includes when they have been shot.  Patience almost always outweights charging through in this game.  You might feel like Jeff Goldbloom in Jurassic Park, "Are there any animals to hunt in this hunting simulator", but more often than not the animals are plentiful.  I'd recommend traveling around and finding hot-spots with bountiful game.  Areas with branching paths around water are a great place to start.
Also, the preserves are massive for how slow you move.  Not having the ATV is a hinderance if you plan to spend any amount of time playing the game.  I'd recommend buying the ATV DLC, even though they definitely should have included buyable ATV's in the game.

Shantae: Half Genie Hero is the 4th installment of  developer WayForward's Shantae series and the first to be funded by the fans via Kickstarter. Despite being overlooked and criminally under funded when compared to the likes of the now long forgotten Mighty No 9, Wayforward has once again have shown their true talents as a game developer.
HGH is the first Shantae game that's in full HD.  It's also a more linear adventure, although there are secrets and hidden areas to find and discover. There are a total of 6 levels. Each broken into 3 to 4 stages each with a boss waiting at the end of each level. In this new adventure Shantae has more transformations at her disposal that totals up to 12 forms she can use. The animations and the overall look of HGH is possibly the best visualls WayForward has brought to the table with the series. The soundtrack has once again hit another home run thanks to series composer Jake Kaufman and also credit to Shantae's voice actress Christina Vee for lending her talented voice in main theme.
Pros:
-Beautiful visuals that match with the equally vibrating soundtrack
-Shantae's arsinal and transformations is the most varied in the series yet
-Each of the 6 levels do well to make use and compliment the way the transfomations are used in certain situations
-Gameplay is simple, but does offer some complexity
-The 6 levels are varied and offer plenty of action platforming that doesnt get dull
Con:
-Short playthough that could be completed around 6+ hours on a blind run
-4 of the transformations are forgeteble and are hardly used
-Certain pickup items can make Shantae go extremely OP
-Difficulty is easiest entry out of the entire series
Verdict: Despite the game's shortcommings, this is still one of the better Shantae titles released being behind The Pirate's Curse. It doesn't change the formula too much, but rather it gives it a bigger, HD paint-job. This is an easy buy, but may want to wait for a sale and/or DLC to come out for additional content.

Excellent game! The graphics are awesome, with very fluid animations, and the gameplay is great and fun. Unfortunately, the gameplay and mechanics have been simplified a bit (it is more platformer and less metroidvania than previous Shantae games, there are no puzzles or dungeons, and it is much more linear than the previous games). The game has few but long levels, and I think the duration of the game is similar to the previous games; there is a lot of backtracking, but this does not make the game repetitive since you are getting new magic powers all the time, which allow to explore new areas. This is a must-have for all who enjoyed the previous Shantae games.

This game is very cute and has a lot of love poured into it, but suffers immensely from a very bumpy difficulty curve. The developers seem to be either unable or unwilling to create levels that are anywhere between easy and hard.
Most of the easy levels feature platforming and enemies, but with little or no consequence for failing the platforming - and enemies can be easily dispatched, ignored, or avoided most of the time. I never once died to any of the enemies, including the bosses, and I imagine most other players will be able to say the same thing.
However, some of the levels are completely different, and feature very few enemies, and often difficult or finicky platforming, with the consequence of missing a jump being an instakill, which sends you back to the last checkpoint. Unfortunately, there are very few of these, so falling into a pit can send you back quite a distance.
The final zone is where this all culminates into one huge mess. The levels leading up to the final boss consist mostly of screens that are almost literally Flappy Bird, with instant kills lining every wall. Getting through those screens took me significantly longer than beating the final boss itself, and after that I was dropped in an auto-run level that was even more difficult, and took me even longer to complete. I didn't feel a sense of accomplishment by the time I was done; just frustration.
Bottom line: Watch a playthrough instead. The difficulty of the levels spikes too much for me to call this a good game, which sucks, because there's a lot of great work put into just about everything else.

It's not easy making a game where choices mathers when you ultimatly know where everyone is going to end. Since you cannot alter what is going to take place in LIS, you end up choosing little to nothing creating small inconsistancies along the way.
That being said, It does not mean this is a boring game. The story is still good. The gameplay is more or less the same ( minus the time rewind thing). You just have to have the right expectations coming in and take the game for what it is.

Life is Strange: Before the Storm is definitely worth playing if you loved the original, just don’t expect it to be as good in all areas. It expands and enhances the universe, offering great insights into the mind of Chloe Price in addition to more back-story. Its dialogue and characters are strong; Rachel Amber is crucial, as her alluring friendship with Chloe is the proverbial glue, even if the emotional threads are not quite as powerful. Unfortunately the secondary elements prevent it from always walking hand-in-hand with the 2015 release. Player choice is unsatisfactory because circumstances happen regardless of what the choices indicate. The adventure puzzles and Backtalk challenges are flimsy. Even the ending is anticlimactic. But when put together, both the original game and Before the Storm become better experiences, and isn't that the mark of a good friendship?

Windward is a bit more straightforward than I anticipated from the description, but it's still fun enough and on a big enough scale that I've gotten dozens of hours of enjoyment from it. Start with a simple ship, by fighting and quests improve your equipment and skills, and help your faction wrest control of the map from the pirates or other factions. Powering up and slowly taking over a map really scratches an itch of mine.
Quests are pretty basic--you're either delivering things to one or more places, or fighting pirate ships. Taking over new squares of the map from pirates are where I found the real fun, but also some frustration--I can totally understand other reviewers who trash the solo game for this. As a solo player, it sometimes feels like you're the only sensible player in a 5v5 game of idiots. You might find yourself trying to single-handedly fight off the pirates being spawned from their single remaining town while your allies are dicking around in safe territory. Or even if you vastly outpower the enemy need to reconquer towns multiple times because the tower-based defenses aren't great and you can't count on allied ships to defend sensibly. It is possible to hire your allies to either stay with you or go to a destination of your choice, but this control is pretty limited.
However, fighting off the pirates is enough fun that I don't really mind the protracted battles--it's one of the best ways to get new equipment and experience, anyway.

You played CoD campaigns because they are fun? Heck yeah, they are.
You were♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥because the campaigns never last for more than 4-5 hours? Damn, we're soul brothers!
And now you stumble upon this game, and you think about buying it for about 5 bucks? DO IT.
What CoD campaigns made fun, this game makes it intense. The story is superb, I♥♥♥♥♥♥you not. It's a bit futuristic: Dubai is covered in sand, since a gigantic sandstorm got there and still rages on. A platoon of the US Army has been sent there to help civilians get out of this sandy hell-hole, but communication has been interrupted ever since they went in. Now you and your two SEAL buddies are sent in to find out what happened. But sure enough, what you find is way more than you bargained for.
Now, what is really intriguing about this game is its style. The game system itself is fun enough, but nothing new; you can duck behind cover, shoot from it, you throw grenades, yadda yadda. The mechanics are pretty much the same as e.g. CoDs. BUT, and this is the funny point, you get to choose. From time to time, you as the leader of your little pack will have to make a (often-times) moral decision and live with its consequences. And this is when the game overcomes CoD and becomse pure awesomeness.
Because no, the game won't have a different ending based on your decisions. No, there are no NPCs around you who could react to you differently based on what you did. Instead, you keep pushing towards your goal, remembering what you did, thinking about it, being reminded of it from time to time, and more and more you ask yourself:
Did I do the right thing?
And you go down into a moral dilemma. Of course you did the right thing, there was no other option. But wait, THERE WAS. No CoD ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t à la "Do this, do that, and of course we are the good guys, what we do we have to do, and lets not think about it." YOU have chosen the path you go, and you have to live with it. YOU are the guy responsible for YOUR actions, and YOU will have to look at what that caused. YOU will see the bodies of innocent and people who just were in the wrong place at the wrong time, that is, being where YOU are.
So, is this a war-game shooter? Hell yeah, it is. But unlike CoD, you won't emerge from it as the sparkling war hero who did everything right just as his commanding superior told him to.
No, my friend. You are alone out there. Your decisions. Your responsibility. Your faults.
Welcome to Dubai.
War is hell.

I'm not gonna go too deep into this game because it's pretty obvious as to what it is by looking at it but I can say it is an excellent platformer from WayForward that has some metroidvania elements. The game is hud based, and you can revisit previous levels in order to collect items needed to progress. So, what you are looking at is a game that's part traditional run left to right platformer, and part collectathon. You will get various powers and upgrades as you progress through the game not unlike a Metroid or Castlevania title. You'll have a scene with characters in a hub town, go to a level and make it through, then likely have to find something you couldnt get before to progress to the next level by revisiting previous levels. The good news is that you won't be playing the exact same things over again as levels do have some changes as you go through them again but it's mostly the same. If I have any major negatives it may be the nature of having to revist old levels over again though it didn't bother me too much, and that it's fairly short, taking about 7 hours for me on my first run to collect everything and beat the game.

Before the Storm portrays itself as the polar opposite of its sequel, the main game. Instead of playing the role of Max trying to combat bullying and change fate, this time, you're playing the role of her delinquent best friend Chloe who is trying to cope with the death of her father as she reluctantly goes through high school.
The game takes a very comedic approach, and if you take it at face value, it is very enjoyable. The game hasn't lost any of its beauty. Employing the same dialogue decision making as the main game, the only real difference in this one is that Chloe lacks Max's ability to reverse time. You can only make decisions based on your best judgement and how you want a relationship to develop. There are no second chances.
The game is simpler than before since you're just following along. This time, instead of trial-and-error by reversing choices, you occasionally have the ability to persuade someone through a simple mini-game. The change of developers initially put me off since I feared the game may change too much. However, after I started the game, I found that virtually nothing has changed. The game still looks and feels the same. Great work, Deck Nine.
Chloe is absolutely hilarious. Your enjoyment of the game pretty much boils down to watching her be a smartass to people. Chloe develops based on how much of a delinquent you want her to be, or whether you want her to be good instead. It's a breath of fresh air from the detective story that the main game had, since there's no right or wrong answer to a question. Only whatever you think is best.
The main game actually reveals quite a bit about all the characters, so if you've already beaten it, your decisions in the prequel will be heavily influenced since you already know how each person is like. If you haven't played the main game yet, playing this prequel first might not be a bad idea since all three episodes are released now. I think this way is more enjoyable instead, since it merges with the main game smoothly.
My only real con about this game is the lack of a vsync option, the screen tearing is outrageous!
I rate this game 8/10 ^^

Pros

Immersion
The lore and storylines
Cons
Random animal AI problems (not a huge con)

Overview:
The game has a ton of potential. However, at this point it feels like an alpha or beta version that was pushed to release too early. There are only a few different types of animals to hunt and only like 5-6 guns to upgrade to. The game just feels like the devs left stuff out for future DLC. Sure, the graphics and atmospheric elements are nice. But the fact that the game feels like a walking simulator is a problem. There are no incentives in the game. You literally walk around, find a target and kill it. Then you can see the stats from your kill and the animal once. Once you accept the kill you can never see any of those stats again. Why?
Here is my opinion on how the game could be better.
Since this game takes place on hunting reserves I feel like the devs should have added in lodges, or central hubs, where there are npc's that sell you gear, ammo, guns, etc. It would be a place that you could meet and hang out with your friends. In the lodge you could have the heads of animals mounted on walls that either the single player, or other players have killed, so people can see them. You could even place full sized 'stuffed' versions of the best kills from players in the game. In the cabins scattered around the map, maybe you could place trophies from animals that you have killed within them for viewing.
There should be some form of interaction with the environment within the game. By this I mean, being able to chop wood and start a fire, creating traps from smalls bushes and trees to catch small game, buying tree stands and hunting from above, or even FISHING. It would be really cool if you could buy a boat and cruise the lakes fishing as well. (Not to mention the fact that they have added ATV's in the game that you pay money for and you cannot drive over a small bush. In real life ATVs would have no problem doing this, but in the game you hit a half inch in diameter tree and it's like you hit a brick wall. There is no destructability in the game and that's a problem.)
An interesting mechanic could be to section off portions of the map so that players are limited to zones based on their level. It would not feel limiting as the maps are gigantic, but it would give the player something to work towards instead of just running around and killing things randomly. The bigger game (animals) would be located within these zones. There needs to be some incentive within the game for people to progress towards, or else you wont retain players.
There is so much potential that this game could have that it just isnt living up to. I have a bunch of other ideas; I could go on forever, but I'll spare you.
---Long story short, the graphics and atmosphere are beautiful, but the gameplay get repetitive quickly and there is no incentive to keep playing after the first ten hours. For being such a large open world game, it feels very barren and devoid of life and energy.

So this game's been out since September 2012, and still has utterly gamebreaking bugs, mostly centred around the most core game concepts. Things that haven't been fixed since it's initial Alpha release include:
Doors failing to "exist", or becoming part of a wall once built and failing to function as doors.
Areas of the prison becoming "unsafe" during a fight, and then staying that way permanently, causing dozens of staff to become stuck trying to leave the area and going back and forth. The only solution is to wall off the area and everyone inside, and forget about it. I've noticed on several occasions this unsafe area seems to "spread", until the entire prison is unsafe, and the entire corrupted save file has to be deleted.
Prisoners becoming stuck inside objects, while i've never observed this happening to staff, it results in prisoners becoming impossible to search, and therefore a "Shakedown" cannot ever be completed. As this is required to progress past certain Grants or conditions, the game is essentially unprogressable at this point.
These are just the most glaring issues still in effect, nearly 3 years on, but not an exclusive list. Please keep in mind that this is a VERY unstable game, crashes are to be EXPECTED, game file corruptions common, expect to have to uninstall and reinstall this game CONSTANTLY to overcome certain access errors. Keep these in mind before deciding to spend money on this game.
UPDATED: October 6th 2015.
I can now confirm that none of the issues above have been addressed in the V1.0 release.
In addition I have discovered a few new issues:
Invincible inmates. They are impossible to suppress. I hired 20 guards, all beating the same guy for more than a day. He killed every single one of them. So I brought in Riot Police. Same issue. I kept going. He was immune to Tazers, Shotguns, Guard Dogs, and 20 people simultaneously beating the crap out of him.
The Deployment screen lags. After a section of a prison is completed, it can take up to half an hour real-life (not in-game) time before the game recognizes that area as complete, and therefore you can now deploy guards there, or create routes.
Doors losing their functionality. Occasionally a door will simply stop opening. Manually clicking it and clicking "force to stay open" does nothing. The only way around it is to have an engineer remove the door altogether. This seems to happen to Staff Doors (green doors) most commonly, but that could simply be due to their usage in my prisons.
When building a building of any size greater than 100x100, or when employing any more than 300 Engineers on a single project, the engine is simply incapable of handling it, and the game really shows how limited it is. Engineers will follow seemingly random paths. There is no rhyme or reason. Progress is painfully slow. The bigger a building gets, the more exponentially long it will take to finish. Instead of working from one corner outwards, from one side across, Engineers will randomly complete tasks, sometimes spending more than 10 minutes (real life time not in game) to go from storage/deliveries, to complete a single task, to go back to storage/deliveries. Half of your engineers will simply not work on the project, and will scurry about the deliveries/storage/garbage rooms doing absolutely nothing. It took more than 8 hours (real life time) on the fastest game speed for a force of 1000 (one thousand) engineers to build a building which was 250x250 tiles big. The engine/AI is quite simply not designed for any project that big. You will never be able to foesibly build a Prison of any scale beyond say 800 prisoners at the most. The game simply can't Simulate a Prison bigger than that without the engine completely coming apart.
When creating more than ~800 Cells (Cell rooms) at once, even if the rooms are all pre-prepared, the game is incapable of processing that many requests at once. As a result, out of 1200 Cells, about 400 of them were left with errors claiming that they were not fully encircled by walls/indoors. No matter what was done, what was changed, even when those rooms were completely demolished and re-built, that prison was no longer capable of having any more cells built. Another issue, it seems, when trying to create a Prison of any decent size.
These may have existed prior to the Version 1.0 update, but I have only now discovered them when attempting to create a larger prison.
***
In summary: Do not buy this game. It's barely playable.
This game is NOT a good example of what the Unity engine is capable of. Please don't let it taint your view of Unity, which is a great engine. What this developer has done with it is not Unity's fault.
If you want to make a dinky little 200 person "Prison", this game will (almost) work. If you're looking for anything bigger than that, look elsewhere. That seems to be about the limit for this game's shoddy design.
10/10 would recommend it.

Mad Max is the first game inspired by the hit post-apocalyptic franchise of the same name.  An open-world, action, adventure, with some RPG elements, it really isn't that "unique" of a game to be completely honest.  There is no dialog trees, and no branching storyline.  The combat is very Batman: Arkham-like, but the saving grace, the identifying feature of the game, if you will, is the importance of the car.  If you know anything of the Mad Max universe, you know that Max drives an Interceptor, named the "Black-on-Black."
Let's just say, in this game, you aren't driving that car for some reason, and instead you build your own machine from the scrap, up.  You can customize the color, engine, weapons, suspension, tires, boost, etc... to your liking, per your completion of some aspects of the game.  You can also customize Max himself.  Outfits, hair style, shotgun, gloves, fighting abilities, etc...
The story itself, I think, does so well because it is not a copy of one of the already-told Mad Max universe stories, it makes a completely new story (as far as I'm aware).  The story isn't phenomenal, or ground-breaking, but it is good.  There are a few moments that genuinely squeezed some emotion from me as a player, which proves that the game is successful in getting you invested in the characters and the story if you try and let it (this will only work if this source material is your cup of tea).
The gameplay is pretty good and refined (BTW devs, what's with never telling the player there is a damn JUMP BUTTON? on an Xbox controller it's LB).  The combat system is just as good as Batman: Arkham or the standard Assassin's Creed combat system.  The graphics are pretty good, nothing groundbreaking, but good.
The world size is enourmous, one of the better parts of the game.  The map size essentially requires the use of the car you build, this is part of what makes the car so successful as such an integral part of the story.  There are plenty of locations to loot (too many, honestly), mini-bosses to defeat, locations to discover and expore and strongholds to upgrade.
All-in-all, the game is good for those interested.  If you aren't into Post-apocalyptic settings, you won't like it.  If you aren't into that combat style, lots of driving, big worlds, linear stories, or any combination of those, then I can't guarantee you'll like the game, but otherwise, I would most certainly recommend the experience.

Depending on what you are looking for, Mad Max will bore you to tears or entertain you for 50+ hours.  The game blends popular elements from other games into a post-apocalyptic open world with a focus on driving.  Fans of Assassins Creed, Shadow of Mordor and the Batman Arkham games will feel instantly at home.
You have the Batman combat, but surprisingly more brutal and less "smooth", which I think works pretty well as you aren't a superhero!  You have an enormous map, which is probably the biggest I've seen in a game like this.  Finally, you have an abundance of collectibles and that satisfactory feeling when you completely clear an area  and have it marked as 100%.  The game certainly is repetitive, but fans of collectibles and upgrading will enjoy this game and that part of the game appealed to me more than the lacklustre story on offer.
What makes Max Max stand out from the open world crowd is the use of the "Magnum Opus", a car that you will do battle in, upgrade and race over the entire course of the game.  There's plenty of choice when it comes to upgrading weapons, making the car faster, getting the armour upgraded and adjusting the parts for the task at hand.  I enjoyed this part of the game immensely and I don't even enjoy driving games.
A slightly boring story and repetitive gameplay will turn a lot of people off, but the game does shine when it comes to its driving mechanics and how it gives you so much to collect and explore in its enormous map.  Graphics aren't the most important thing, but I have to say that the game is gorgeous and managed to make a game that is mostly sand look breathtaking at times.  I highly recommend this game to people who like the games I have mentioned and perhaps those who were intrigued by the driving sections in Rage.

Shantae is one of my favorite game series of all time. While other reviews will talk about the great level design, the (occasionally) amusing writing, the phenomenal music (thanks to Jake Kaufman). I'd like to talk about the thing I truly love about the shantae series (excluding the original).
The game engine in these games is flawless. The greatest crime I feel a platformer can commit in my opinion is have a poor engine. If I ever feel like missing a jump is the game's fault, or some BS pixel perfect jump requirements, then it is a bad platformer.
This is never the case in Shantae. Shantae always lands from every jump exactly the way I expect based on the buttons I pressed. If I miss a jump, it is clear and obvious what I did wrong. I timed it wrong for the moving platform, I misjudged the arc, an enemy attack threw me off. I never fight the controls, and I never yell at the screen "OH THATS BULL, I MADE THAT JUMP". Hard sections feel challenging, not frustrating.
That right there, the silky smooth controls and rock solid engine, are the best part of this game and its predecessors (except the original, lets not talk about the original....)
UPDATE:
Now that I'm less starry eyed from just finishing the game. I'll give my honest opinion to long time fans of Shantae. The biggest difference in this game is the style of level design. Its less metroidvania, more mega man. This isn't a bad thing, its just different. Levels are less about being labyrinths, and more about combining enemy placement and platforming to create a challenge. To those that prefer the labyrinth style designs, Shantae and the Pirate's Curse remains your best bet. To those that prefer stuff like Mega Man X, this game is perfect. To those that like both, like me, both games are awesome.

Half-Genie hero is the fourth installment in the Shantae series, and each entry manages to impress in new ways. Half-Genie Hero's visuals are its most impressive feature, from the artwork to the animation, its all very good. I liked this game a lot, but I think it does have a few minor shortcomings.
+++ Visuals, they're great. The character portraits are nice, the models and sprites fit the style well, and the animations accentuate character personalities
+++ Soundtrack, it's very good, each area has a unique track that sets the mood well
++ Level Design, the levels are nicely designed, each new ability that is unlocked makes them easier to traverse in some way, as well as unlocking new areas in previous levels, new enemies appear in previous levels after clearing them as well
+ Gameplay, transformations add a fresh take on the playstyle of Pirate's Curse, but transforming back and forth between them can sometimes feel tedious
- Length, as a metroidvania game, short lengths are to be expected and replay value is where play time comes from. However, in comparison to Pirate's Curse I found this game to be shorter without much justification gameplay-wise
-- Difficulty, Half-Genie Hero is an easy game. The ability to toggle upgrades helps to add an artifical challenge should it be desired, but for a casual player the base game is hardly challenging, especially compared to Pirate's Curse
Overall, Half-Genie hero is an excellent game. I never felt frustrated with it, and that made it a fun experience. Even though it was an easy game, the effort WayForward put into creating and polishing this title was evident. With more content coming next year and a 10% discount on the game, I wholly recommend giving Shantae: Half-Genie Hero your consideration.

So this game's been out since September 2012, and still has utterly gamebreaking bugs, mostly centred around the most core game concepts. Things that haven't been fixed since it's initial Alpha release include:
Doors failing to "exist", or becoming part of a wall once built and failing to function as doors.
Areas of the prison becoming "unsafe" during a fight, and then staying that way permanently, causing dozens of staff to become stuck trying to leave the area and going back and forth. The only solution is to wall off the area and everyone inside, and forget about it. I've noticed on several occasions this unsafe area seems to "spread", until the entire prison is unsafe, and the entire corrupted save file has to be deleted.
Prisoners becoming stuck inside objects, while i've never observed this happening to staff, it results in prisoners becoming impossible to search, and therefore a "Shakedown" cannot ever be completed. As this is required to progress past certain Grants or conditions, the game is essentially unprogressable at this point.
These are just the most glaring issues still in effect, nearly 3 years on, but not an exclusive list. Please keep in mind that this is a VERY unstable game, crashes are to be EXPECTED, game file corruptions common, expect to have to uninstall and reinstall this game CONSTANTLY to overcome certain access errors. Keep these in mind before deciding to spend money on this game.
UPDATED: October 6th 2015.
I can now confirm that none of the issues above have been addressed in the V1.0 release.
In addition I have discovered a few new issues:
Invincible inmates. They are impossible to suppress. I hired 20 guards, all beating the same guy for more than a day. He killed every single one of them. So I brought in Riot Police. Same issue. I kept going. He was immune to Tazers, Shotguns, Guard Dogs, and 20 people simultaneously beating the crap out of him.
The Deployment screen lags. After a section of a prison is completed, it can take up to half an hour real-life (not in-game) time before the game recognizes that area as complete, and therefore you can now deploy guards there, or create routes.
Doors losing their functionality. Occasionally a door will simply stop opening. Manually clicking it and clicking "force to stay open" does nothing. The only way around it is to have an engineer remove the door altogether. This seems to happen to Staff Doors (green doors) most commonly, but that could simply be due to their usage in my prisons.
When building a building of any size greater than 100x100, or when employing any more than 300 Engineers on a single project, the engine is simply incapable of handling it, and the game really shows how limited it is. Engineers will follow seemingly random paths. There is no rhyme or reason. Progress is painfully slow. The bigger a building gets, the more exponentially long it will take to finish. Instead of working from one corner outwards, from one side across, Engineers will randomly complete tasks, sometimes spending more than 10 minutes (real life time not in game) to go from storage/deliveries, to complete a single task, to go back to storage/deliveries. Half of your engineers will simply not work on the project, and will scurry about the deliveries/storage/garbage rooms doing absolutely nothing. It took more than 8 hours (real life time) on the fastest game speed for a force of 1000 (one thousand) engineers to build a building which was 250x250 tiles big. The engine/AI is quite simply not designed for any project that big. You will never be able to foesibly build a Prison of any scale beyond say 800 prisoners at the most. The game simply can't Simulate a Prison bigger than that without the engine completely coming apart.
When creating more than ~800 Cells (Cell rooms) at once, even if the rooms are all pre-prepared, the game is incapable of processing that many requests at once. As a result, out of 1200 Cells, about 400 of them were left with errors claiming that they were not fully encircled by walls/indoors. No matter what was done, what was changed, even when those rooms were completely demolished and re-built, that prison was no longer capable of having any more cells built. Another issue, it seems, when trying to create a Prison of any decent size.
These may have existed prior to the Version 1.0 update, but I have only now discovered them when attempting to create a larger prison.
***
In summary: Do not buy this game. It's barely playable.
This game is NOT a good example of what the Unity engine is capable of. Please don't let it taint your view of Unity, which is a great engine. What this developer has done with it is not Unity's fault.
If you want to make a dinky little 200 person "Prison", this game will (almost) work. If you're looking for anything bigger than that, look elsewhere. That seems to be about the limit for this game's shoddy design.
10/10 would recommend it.

is a delightful medieval-themed action platformer with adorable art and a few unique twists.
Its masterstroke is how the permadeath and rogue-like mechanics are wrapped in a tale of heirloom and magic castle with ever-shifting walls. Each death does indeed end your run, but then you get to continue as one of your descendants, able to spend all the gold earned by your unfortunate ancestor on equipment, runes and the expansion of the family's manor, which is basically a gigantic tree of permanent upgrades that will help subsequent playthroughs.
Any boost will be very welcome, as you start off very weak. Working your way through the randomly generated castle and its three surrounding areas will be a painful journey at first, but it will get more and more rewarding and satisfying as you crawl further and further with each run. You might even be so fortunate as to end up slaying one of the four bosses, whose spirits seal off a mysterious room!
The second stroke of genius is the way your descendant's abilities are defined not only by their class (barbarian, mage, paladin, etc.) but also a gazillion of unique traits, which might provide benefits or be hugely detrimental. Your chosen hero might have A.D.H.D. and gain a speed boost, while also being near-sighted making everything far away blurry. His/her hypochondriasis may well result in hilariously exaggerated reactions to any damage taken, not to mention a number of purely cosmetic or anecdotical traits such as baldness or same-sex attraction. You only get a choice between three random heirs on every playthrough, meaning you'll likely end up having to work and compromise with most of these characteristics at one point or another.
With all these twists that keep every playthrough refreshing as well as the sense of progress and accomplishing things in the bigger perspective of your heirloom as a whole,
is as charming as it is oddly addictive. Although the final few achievements may require a bit of grinding, it also has a bit in store for the hardcore gamers with five vicious secret bosses and the option to advance into ever-harder "New Game +" modes everytime you complete the game. I'd say it's worth at least a good 40 hours if you want to accomplish everything, and you'll more than likely keep playing the occasional run after that just for the hell of it.

A hack'n'slash game where the hacking and slashing is cannon fire and launching barrels of explosives/fire/old stinky fish toward enemy ships.  Call it an ARPG (heavy on the Action, light on the RPG), and toss some (light) tower defense and (very light) RTS elements in to the mix for good measure.
Create your own custom map and factions or have the game make a random one. Manually set the challenge levels (level requirement) of each region in the map - tedious but also important if you want to, say, make a giant spiral map that goes from level 0-330 or higher (default is 0-39).
Pick a faction (*combat*/questing/trading/exploration) and set sail. Unlock more ships, better cannons, captain and crew. Level up and spend talent points unlocking new abilities and specializing in defense, offense, or support.
The combat is where the game really shines, and it's deeper than surface appearances.
Early on, pirates are rather easy to take out. In the higher challenge level regions you can no longer simply trade cannon fire. You will need to get better at staying in their 'blind spot' where they can't return fire. You will need to clear out enemy towers - which will quickly turn a winning battle into a losing one. Hire friendly nearby ships and send them off to create a distraction and buy you enough time to capture a town.
You can use guerilla hit and run tactics with a small, fast, high-damage 'Corvette' that can sail through smaller openings and shallower water. You may want to drop anchor in a huge tanky 'Ship of the Line' and soak up damage so your friendly ships can attack safely. You may choose to support your fleet by sailing a 'Galleon' and tossing out barrels of water that put out fires and heal your allies. Or maybe you want to try out the <secret> end-game unlockable ship that can be good at both damage and support but is extremely squishy.
However you decide to approach a new pirate-controlled region, it's some good fun and can be quite a challenge. To counter the 'too many pirates spawning' when trying to get the final town in a region - they cease respawning if you or one of your towers are in firing range of their harbor. Use explosives to dredge out a new canal to the town. They'll never see it coming. Fun times with moddable terrain once you find a construction kit.
The game is not for everyone. It can be frustrating at times. And it can feel a bit grindy and repetitive on the questing/trading side of things. But this can also be a tranquil relaxing time to de-stress from all your pirate murdering.
The majority of my play time is in single-player, but as with most any game, it only gets better when you play with friends (and sometimes strangers too).

Mad Max is the first game inspired by the hit post-apocalyptic franchise of the same name.  An open-world, action, adventure, with some RPG elements, it really isn't that "unique" of a game to be completely honest.  There is no dialog trees, and no branching storyline.  The combat is very Batman: Arkham-like, but the saving grace, the identifying feature of the game, if you will, is the importance of the car.  If you know anything of the Mad Max universe, you know that Max drives an Interceptor, named the "Black-on-Black."
Let's just say, in this game, you aren't driving that car for some reason, and instead you build your own machine from the scrap, up.  You can customize the color, engine, weapons, suspension, tires, boost, etc... to your liking, per your completion of some aspects of the game.  You can also customize Max himself.  Outfits, hair style, shotgun, gloves, fighting abilities, etc...
The story itself, I think, does so well because it is not a copy of one of the already-told Mad Max universe stories, it makes a completely new story (as far as I'm aware).  The story isn't phenomenal, or ground-breaking, but it is good.  There are a few moments that genuinely squeezed some emotion from me as a player, which proves that the game is successful in getting you invested in the characters and the story if you try and let it (this will only work if this source material is your cup of tea).
The gameplay is pretty good and refined (BTW devs, what's with never telling the player there is a damn JUMP BUTTON? on an Xbox controller it's LB).  The combat system is just as good as Batman: Arkham or the standard Assassin's Creed combat system.  The graphics are pretty good, nothing groundbreaking, but good.
The world size is enourmous, one of the better parts of the game.  The map size essentially requires the use of the car you build, this is part of what makes the car so successful as such an integral part of the story.  There are plenty of locations to loot (too many, honestly), mini-bosses to defeat, locations to discover and expore and strongholds to upgrade.
All-in-all, the game is good for those interested.  If you aren't into Post-apocalyptic settings, you won't like it.  If you aren't into that combat style, lots of driving, big worlds, linear stories, or any combination of those, then I can't guarantee you'll like the game, but otherwise, I would most certainly recommend the experience.

Super short summary: Mad max is far cry 3 on a desert with a ♥♥♥♥ing cliché storyline.
That is the main game I will use to compare mad max with because they really share a lot. But mad max also borrowed tons of gameplay mechanics from other games, in fact the game doesn’t have a single ♥♥♥♥ing unique mechanic. The devs only included tried and tested mechanics from other games like Batman (melee combat) but without batman’s intensive amount of tools/gadgets making the combat very shallow. Ubisoft’s Assassins’ creed and far cry 3’s watchtower replaced by a hot air balloon to view legends on the map. Repetitive encounters in ubisoft open world games replaced with scavenging locations where most of them you only need to get 1-4 actions/scrap to finish which are pretty meaningless since you’ll be overflowing with scrap anyways.

Let me start off by saying I have never been hunting in real life. I have also never played a hunting game before. I mainly play shooters and RPG's. Playing this game has been a real breath of fresh air (no pun intended). It is so different from other games where you are constanly being bombarded with killing something or someone every second of gameplay. With this game you might go 30 minutes or more without seeing anything and when you finally do see something you might scare it off if you are not carefu, then you have to track the animal again until you find it. But when you finally get the kill with an amazing shot from a long distance, it is the most satisfying feeling I have felt in a long time while playing a video game.
I was skeptical I would like it since I am not a very patient person and i was not to keen on the idea of just walking around for half an hour with no action. Do not let that discourage you since you will be so busy sneaking around, listening, and looking for animals you will not notice the time. I definitely believe this game is worth the money.
Now I do have a problem with this game, not the actual gameplay but the way essential items are locked behind DLC. To use ATV's you have to buy the DLC and to use tent fast travel you have to buy the DLC. The DLC's are not expensive at 4 dollars each, but these features should have been included in the game. I wish instead of making essential features like this locked behind DLC they would instead sell cosmetics for the ATV's, tents, cabins, guns, etc.

theHunter: Call of the Wild is a large and vast landscape full of opportunity, that is sure to scratch your hunting game itch. I don’t think I need to go into great detail about the concept of this game, if you’re familiar with other hunting simulators, then this is better than those.
I’ve enjoyed my time theHunter, and I’m more excited for all the updates and additions they’re adding to the game that will set it over the top. This is the best hunting simulator out at the moment. It has missions, side quests, goals, and with all its future additions it may be hard to beat, but it’s not without its flaws.
——————————————————————————
I have spent more time walking than actually hunting, and I know this is a simulator, but the animals scare way too easily. I don’t know if the game expects me to low crawl anytime I’m on the trail of a deer, but no one even does that in real life. The sound meter sensitivity needs to be adjusted, so that I can actually properly sight a deer. Walking is apparently the equivalent of firing off cannons that alert all near by animals.
The game is on consoles now, and full controller support for the PC should be a thing. It’s frustrating that when I need to place a waypoint, track a mission, or fast travel I have to hop off the couch and get to my keyboard to do so.
I’ve shot a moose 6 times with a rifle and it kept on trotting like it was just barely wounded. Even though I was using a lower caliber rifle, after six shots from it, the moose should have went down or eventually bled out.
I’ve encountered a few typical bugs with animal behavior and tracking, but are guaranteed to be patched. Other than that, the game is really fun.
——————————————————————————
With all those cons though, the game is still engaging and does get easier the further you grind your way through levels. Better lures and weapons make hunting less of a struggle once you start unlocking things, and level up your skills and perks. The starting stages of the game are a grind though, but if you’re patient and stay persistent, the game becomes quite satisfying and more enjoyable.

With the Season (not counting the Bonus Farewell episode) conluded I figured it's time to write my review for the next lineup game in the LiS series.
This is a prequel to the First LiS game. Taking place 3 years before. You play as Chloe Price. A massive fan favorite character from the First Season who was Max's best friend. The Game takes you through 3 fairly lenghy episodes (about 2-3 hrs each) showing what Life was like for Chloe before the First Season. Before the Storm takes place 2 years after her father died and Max left for Seattle. In this game, this is where you watch as Chloe meets Rachel Amber. A name that should be familiar to you if you played the first game, as she was described as the most popular girl in Arcadia Bay and Max's replacement to be Chloe's Best friend. The story will take you through how they met, and how their Friendship grows.
Right off the bat I will say That Decknine did a outstanding job. The Writing (to me personally) is alot better than the First Season. The Chemistry Between Chloe and Rachel is so hella great. At first I was skeptical about this game when it was announced because I didn't really care for Rachel (you never really meet her in S1, you just hear rumors and stories) but man did I through out all doubts after Episode 1.
While Season 1 was great, it is true it had alot of cringy stuff in the writing. There's still certainly some cringy things said in the writing of this game, but it's alot less obvious and even at some points purposefully done which helps the script (i.e. Chloe trying to hit on Rachel).
There are no time travel mechanics in this game like S1 (no suprise since Max as we know so far is the only one who can do this ability). But the game does introduce a cool "Back Talk" system. Chloe being her rebelious self can back talk to certain characters in a conversation to get what she wants. This starts up a little mini game in which characters will say something and you have to use what they just said against them. If you mess up though the other character gets a point. Whoever gets to the center first with the most points (you as chloe or the character your having the back talk with) they'll win the conversation. The rest of the game mechanics are the same from S1. Talking to people. Choosing what to say. Investigating objects. Looking around, finding easter eggs, etc...
Ashly Burch was unable to return to voice Chloe for the 3 episodes (she did come back for The Farewell episode) but the new voice actor for Chloe starts to grow on you after a while. Some other characters go through some different voice actors (probably due to either the voice strike that was going on, or scheduling, or budget) but they don't do a horrible job so you should be able to deal with it.
The Soundtrack once again is Outstanding. They even got the band Daughter to bring some of their songs to the game and even compose some new ones for the game itself. Give it a listen, it's really good. The Music as many describe, brings so much more emotion to the game and is like one of the most essential things to this game.
Now because this is a prequel it is true, your choices don't have the biggest impact as none of it is ever brought up in S1.
But to me, that doesn't mean the Choices aren't hella hard to decide or impactful to you the player. There were some choices i was so conflicted with (I was trying to play as closely as possible to how I think Chloe would react to the situation herself) That had me sitting there for minutes trying to decide.
Overall this was a great game to help tie over us LiS fans who are waiting for Season 2. In many aspects I think I like this Season more than S1. Chloe is definitley one of my favorte video game characters of all time, so getting to see part of her journey in becoming the character she is in S1 is enjoyable. Rachel and Chloe's relationship is almost, if not, just as great to watch as Max and Chloe's.
Episode 3 does kinda disappoint as I was hoping to see more events that lead up to S1 appear closer to the end of the episode. But Episode 2 just might be my favorite LiS episode ever.
If you enjoyed Season 1 of Life is Strange and enjoyed Chloe as a character and want to see more of her (and can get over there not being any time travel) Then this is a must play for you.

As many people name COD one of the worst franchises out there in the gaming world today, I am NOT 12 and actually enjoy COD. What I mean is that I love playing the Black Ops series although, I am not a big fan of the Modern Warefare series because I just don't exactly like the weapons choices that the developers chose and quick scoping is a very VERY overpowered way to kill people, but that's a different story. What makes me love Black Ops 2 & 1 so much is because it includes 3 ways to play (yes Modern Warefare has the same thing, but hostiles and special ops really aren't fun...) which is zombies, multiplayer, and campaign. I really do like the campaign in both of the Black Ops series because of it's fun and very destructive weaopns and very memorable characters. One of my favourite aspects of Black Ops II is the fact that Treyarch connected the story between Black Ops 1 and Black Ops 2, basically leaving off from where it ended. Sort of like how MD3 left off from MD2 except Black Ops just sort of dwells on things that weren't so clear in Black Ops 1 (i.e. explaining how Woods DIDN'T die from that explosion in BO 1). The multiplayer functions very well as far as COD multiplayer. I really do enjoy the maps that it has to offer, and the DLC maps are also very fun to play on as well. The ranking system is very diverse and takes awhile to level up (depending on how much you play the game). Even when you do level up, you get rewarded with very nice choices of weaponry, backgrounds for your player card, and emblems. Zombies is even better (in my opinion) than it's pretesessor; Black Ops 1. Zombies in BO2 offers a bit more as far as playing style while holding it's normal zombie wave survival. In this installment of zombies, things change as zombies sort of has a story line now (Origins I'm looking at you) and new game modes such as grief, survival, tranzit, and turned, compared to just your normal wave survival featured in Black Ops 1. One very noticible thing that players realize when they first start zombies is that there are 4 new characters (I'm not going to list them because you can find them out yourself) and that the zombies eyes are no longer orange, but a very nice shade of blue. I find this appealing to me because blue is my favourite colour. And overall players noticed that zombies has a better resolution and the graphical settings have been bumped up quite some. Things render very quickly also, which provides better looking elements in the game (this goes for campaign, and multiplayer). I also quickly found out that the more graphical one (BO2) ran faster and better than the very bad looking ungraphical game (BO1) which I have yet to find out more about (most likely something in better optimizing for PCs). Overall I very much do enjoy this game, it seems to never get old and even when you are sick and tired of multiplayer, there is always something new to try. Now for the negative side of things; oh goodie... 1. I do still recieve quite some bits of lag in multiplayer which doesn't help much at all 2. I believe this game is way too overpriced. Have you seen COD Ghosts? The gold edition is the same price as the normal version of BO2! It's absolutely unbelieveable! 3. I wish that if you had bought it on Xbox or PSN, you could sync it to your PC and download all the DLC, and maby the entire videogame for free. Although they aren't going to do that because Treyarch is a money ♥♥♥♥♥ and don't give 2 ♥♥♥♥s about their customers -_-. 4. I find campaign REDICULOUSLY buggy, sometimes I can't even load the game up because it goes to a black screen and just sits there, doing absolutely nothing. The campaign crashes A THOUSANDFOLD as well. The main reason why it doens't matter much to me is because I have already finished the entire campaign on my Xbox. That was mainly everything you should expect from this installment of COD. I do really recommend it to COD fans, or people looking for a nice shooter for PC, although I do recommend you have deep pockets and have a nice gaming PC. Mine is basically a low teir gaming PC, which is why I experience problems with this, if you have a very powerful computer, you should have NO problems getting this thing to run smoothly. 8.5/10.
