I just wish hunting in real life was this easy ( well not really...would lose the fun then ) but over all just a great job.
Everyone complaining about the movement speeds...well all I can say is I know I am getting old but you just can't move as fast in real life as you do in this game so just enjoy the walk and the graphics they put together for us...it really is worth taking your time to enjoy it...and really...unlimited run time...I want to see anyone do that in real life. I personally think that is just fine the way it is...just enjoy the game and all it offers and quit trying to rush through everything.
Now for the paid DLC"s...well I always love the screams about this topic...first off...look at the Hunter Primal as an example of what they do for a game where the money stops after the initial cost...great potential but sucks since the just abandoned it half finished.This game is far better than both their other games. The positives of this game far exceed the few negatives I have been able to find in it.

The vehicle driving and combat is impressively polished, but the ground combat is mostly just button-mashing, with the same combat system as from the Batman: Arkham series. The side quests seems to have large impacts on character and vehicle skills, and unlike other open world games there are no follow quests (at least so far). Completion of side quests gives the player "scrap" which can in turn be used to upgrade the player's vehicle which has many customization options. 100% completing enemy strongholds has not been too difficult thus far, and is a rewarding experience. This is definitely one of my top 10 open-world games and I would recommend this to fans of the series, new fans of "Fury Road," and anyone who wants a good, self-contained, open-world adventure.

The concept is really well done, and definitely has it's humor to it. One of the quirks your hero can have is IBS, which just makes them fart occasionally. It does nothing else. People can have really silly names, and it's just generally a lighthearted game.

The bosses are also well designed, and enjoyable to fight. Even the super hard versions of the bosses, although they are really damn hard.
This game does have NG+, but I really didn't play it too much, so I can't comment on it.
For $15, I'd thoroughly recommend this game to someone who wants an rpg-ish roguelike game.

I haven't been a big fan of shooters. BL and I think Call of Juarez were the last couple I've played. Also, "on rails" games (which this is) aren't my favorite. But, at a friend's suggestion, I picked this up during a sale.
The mechanics are a bit clunky for the controls, but you do get team-based commands and the overall action is pretty well laid out. It takes some getting used to as far as how the combat scenes will take place. If you're looking for an amazing combat system, I'd say look elsewhere. But it is decent, and playable.
I've seen other reviews talk about choices you make in this game, but let's be clear, 100% clear, you don't really get a choice on most things, and the choices you do get are pretty minor (in the grand scheme of things). So don't expect arcing story paths, fifteen playthroughs, and multiple ways to solve things. The "choices" are made for you - and yes, while it's between "terrible" and "reprehensible", there is no way to "make a call" - you're forced into the decision to continue the game.
Now, I'll go onto why someone should buy this game: The story.
Yes, it's on rails.
Yes, your choices are pretty light.
But I can safely say that if you can play this game without a single twinge of conscience, without feeling (not just thinking the words) "that's messed up - truly messed up", and if you don't learn at least a little bit you didn't know about the horrors of war, either you've been through it (and I feel truly sorry for you), or you're a sociopath.
I don't get disturbed and almost never moved by video games. I immerse myself in thier worlds, but I don't get emotionally involved. This one did a pretty good job of breaking that streak. I was... disturbed by the content. War isn't glorious, no one is a hero when stuff goes down and gets real, and certainly in this day and age, not everything is what it seems - "good" and "bad" are pretty subjective.
Even knowing about this, and expecting some pretty labrynthine plot once the CIA showed up and stuff wasn't making sense, this game took me by surprise.
And you know what?
That's fracking rare in this day and age.
So even with some mediocre mechanics, buy this game. Play it. And, should you feel no twinge of upset, remorse or empathy, you might just be a sociopath.

The only criticism I have is that the singleplayer-campaign is rather short for an AAA title. I needed roughly 9 hours and was not rushing through the levels. I did not play multiplayer or coop. Altogether I recommend that game to every serious actionplayer - do you feel like a hero yet?

Windward gives you the chance to explore,trade and fight in a randomly generated world: whether you're doing it with friends,random people or alone the result is a very fun albeit quite simple game.
-Windward manages to get the "just one more quest/trade/fight" concept right, it can easily get pretty addictive and take quite alot of your time while you try to gather more money, get some equipment or capture a city
-simple graphics,but with a good overall style
-four factions to choose from,the bonuses they get arn't game-changing but are good enough to provide some flavour to them,also two more factions you can unlock during gameplay
-good amount of ships to choose from
-countless different equipment choices of different rarity,you also get a decent amount of ship customization (hull/sails/emblem colour and type of emblem)
-several skill sets to choose from,you can also mix and match from them. There's also three different specializations you can put points into.
-decent amount of servers and good playerbase for those wanting to try multiplayer, sadly the EU server selection is limited though
-overall sound design is very simple, even a bit barren perhaps, music is also nothing to write home about
-can get grindy, especially when you're trying to improve a faction's reputation or leveling a city
-pvp is generally unbalanced,the player with the better ship usually wins easily, same goes for equipment, this can lead to a good amount of griefing on pvp servers/ contested zones
-pirate spawn rate can get annoying very fast, freeing a region when every ship you sink respawns in less than a minute and often comes straight back to you gets aggravating. This can be solved by coming back with a better ship but,again,it means you'll be in for a possibly long grind. Grouping will make things easier ofc.
-game progression is unbalanced towards instances, where you can easily sink pirates for a good amount of money/exp/loot: in contrast trading/questing progression feels way slower reward-wise (even though a recent patch improved money/exp rewards at least). This also means you'd enter a server and find that most people are just playing instances, leaving the sandbox world feeling barren.
-NPC AI is pretty stupid overall, they wont react when they're in a collision course, they often get in your way and, during fights, do not maneuver well and might get stuck on land

Overall Windward has its share of flaws and, generally speaking, is a pretty simple game when you look at how combat and trading works: despite this it's still a very fun game though. It can provide a relaxing experience and some pretty frantic fights especially when going against other players (provided you're of similar level to ensure a fair fight).
If you're looking for a well crafted sandbox game that isn't too complex then this game will provide a good amount of game time before you can consider your adventure "complete", just be mindful of its limits and whether they might affect your overall enjoyment.

A simple, seafaring game. You never leave the ship, if you're a graphics junkie this probably isn't your bag (the graphics are simple, but effective, much like the rest of the game), and if you want tons of action right out of the gate, this game takes a little bit to build up.
That said, I've got about 30 hours into it at the time of this review.
This game offers a meditative experience, and once you get a feel for how you want to play it, it becomes much more fun. I'm playing as a military faction (red), so I've been pretty much trying to wipe piracy off the map... before I join the pirates and take it all back (I've got my black flag stored and I'm just waiting until the map is all mine). It's been fun as I take towns away from opposing forces and run missions to grow them in size. I'm currently the proud owner of a frigate, and I'm getting curb-stomped by hordes of pirates in what I assume is a man-of-war on the upper levels. This game also doesn't like to just give you tons of money, so you're going to need to plan your next ship upgrade with some questing and/or exploration. I'm finding just grabbing floating debris, and sinking ships (mostly to collect their floating debris) is pretty rewarding, but the game mentions if you're a shrewd trader, you can earn faster.
It's kind of RPG-esque as you try to upgrade your fighting style (or exploring style, or merchant style) of your ship. My ship is taking on much more powerful vessels with tons more HP simply because I've learned what strategies work for me (that said, the game seems to be punishing you for daring to take on tougher maps later if you haven't grown enough). It doesn't dial back the difficulty (unless you want to dial it back, I left it at default settings), and you're going to end up turning tail and bailing out for calmer seas and better upgrades.
ADD: If you're wondering what an "epic item" is in the achievements, I found a dive-helmet that allows you to pull "treasure" (usually just gun power, wood and stone) from the bottom (it was in a level 21 part of the map).

As someone who backed this game way back when, I gotta say what we got on hand (so far) definitely made the 3 year wait worth it ~
Much like Pirate's Curse it controls like a dream, and the soundtrack is top notch Kaufman as always. The addition of fully-drawn graphics especially help this game shine, especially during Boss Fights and occasional set-piece like sliding through the Mermaid Falls or escaping certain death in Tassel Town's Tower.
Transforming into certain animals has been retooled from the first two games, and this time for the better. It's great to be able to switch between forms on the fly rather than having to perform a brief dancing mini-game or waiting for Shantae to make a specific dance. Only downside is that I felt some transformations are better than others (the Spider Form is borderline useless. ;;), though thankfully there's more good ones than lame ones.
The overall playthrough did feel pretty short, with only 6 levels (some of which you need to do some backtracking for the sake of plot), but it's not that much shorter than say the entirety of Pirate's Curse. On top of that this is only taking Shantae's Campaign into account, so the matter of game length is currently negligible at best. Really looking forward to when they bring about the Risky Boots and the other Campaigns starring Shantae's friends.
Overall this is a very tightly made package, and is worth the investment! Check it out if you get the chance (preferably once there's more DLC available ~). :)

DISCLAIMER: I am a backer of this title and paid $55.
A project started 4 years ago has come to fruition and I'll be honest, it easily makes my personal game of the year. Playing similar to previous titles like Ducktales Remastered, A Boy and his Blob, and various other titles by the company it shows that Wayforward has not lost it's touch with making platformers. Bright, cheerful and a difficulty that ranges from easy to difficult without being a cackewalk or mind-numbingly difficult. Often compared to Mighty No. 9, Wayforward delivered on something that Comcept failed to do so: a relatively smooth game that has very intuitive gameplay mechanics and stages that put the mind to work as much as the fingers. The bosses, while really large (HUGE in some cases) all have a very capable strategy to beat. To add, while there are cases of a large number of enemies, I never felt at any point where I was forced to take a hit, making untouchable runs a fun challenge. To add, as with most Wayforward titles there is a game clock so speedrunners are going to have fun optimizing this game. The music and voices are superb as always with variations of Jake Kaufman (Wayforwards cheif Maestro) and Cristina Vee's (the voice actor for Shantae amongst others and the lead singer) "Dance Through the Danger" interspecced throughout amid an incredible selection of other music.
As good as the game is, it is not perfect however. There are two nagging issues. The dances are not as dynamic as the tools from Pirate's curse though the mechanic has been improved from previous iterations, utilizing a radial menu system instead of button presses or timing cues. However there are three panels of four icons that cycle automatically, slowing down the gameplay. This can be sped up with a store purchase but that also has the drawback of accidentally picking the wrong dance. Second, like Ducktales Remastered the game is laid out in a stage format as opposed to a single world format like the original game or Risky's Revenge and each stage has a LOt of stuff to collect, often requiring special hidden dances and abilities. This necessitates a LOT of backtracking in the stages, in some cases being required to progress. Personally, not a huge issue but it can frustrate players. Both of these issues are relatively minor and only impact the game in marginal ways.
Overall, another fantastic game from an incredible team who have the support of their fans. People on the fence waiting to know whether it will be any good or not can rest easy knowing that Wayforward can still deliver a fun game with a mix of fast paced gameplay, humorous characters and story, and a bright, colorful world.

Gotta get that right off the bat: I'm one of 18.500+ backers that made this game possible and I'm happy how it turned out.
You play as Shantae, a half-genie and sole protector of Scuttle Town, ready to defend it against any threat. She uses her long, purple hair as a weapon, alongside few offensive and defensive spells. Her magical heritage allow her to perform a variety of belly dances that transform her into various forms, each with different uses. For example, she can turn into a crab and a mermaid, but only her crustacean form can snap through tangled vines, while as a water nymph she can swim properly and attack with bubbles.
Even though it is a part of a series, you absolutely don't need to play any other Shantae game. All characters from previous installments (plus few new faces) make a return and are properly reintroduced. Plot is once again silly with tongue-in-cheek, self-aware humor sprinkled all over. There are six levels in total, but as you unlock new abilities you can replay them to find numerous hidden collectibles and secrets.
This time WayForward went for HD graphics instead of pixel art I dare say it turned out pretty well. All character models are hand drawn, big, colorful and wonderfully animated. They mesh really well with lush, detailed backgrounds.
Not everything is shiny though. Sometimes a tool tip or two would be helpful. For example, it took me half of my play through to realize that you can jump directly down through some platforms. There are also few frustrating sections that simply require player to memorize sequences of obstacles by trial and error. That wouldn't be much of a problem if it weren't for inconsistent checkpoints. Thankfully you can obtain a special dance to skip sections of a previously completed levels. Levels that try their hardest to hide that they are way too short and  you will be revisiting them many times even if you don't want to get 100% of items. Story is also noticeably weaker compared to previous Pirate's Curse, where Shantae, Risky and each side-character had a story arc.
Finishing the game took me around 7 hours and unlocked new game plus mode. There is at least one planned free DLC (for backers) with (supposedly) brand new story. There might be more content coming along the way based on stretch goals, which may or may not turn it into best Shantae game to date.
A solid entry in the series, slightly below Pirate's Curse. Recommended.

(Note: Shantae Half-Genie Hero was a Kickstarter-funded game, and this reviewer backed it at the $12 level.)
Shantae Half-Genie Hero is an exploratory platformer made by developer Wayforward Technologies, and it's absolutely fantastic. As the titular half-genie, Shantae, you run all around the world of Sequin Land, alternating between finding machine parts for your uncle and solving various crises that might pop up. Instead of an interconnected sidescrolling world map with towns and dungeons like previous games in the series, Half-Genie Hero opts to give you a handful of large stages, each divided into sub-areas and each filled with hidden permanent upgrades and/or new mobility options. On your first visits to these stages, you'll only be able to grab a few items. As you unlock new powers, however, you gain the ability to explore new parts of the levels and gain even more abilities and powerups to help you through the game.
Shantae's main attack is whipping her hair, but you also have the ability to transform into different animals. These vary in usage, and they'll be often used to get to the aforementioned new areas. From a wall-climbing monkey to a sea-swimming mermaid to a high-flying harpy, the powers are welcome and interesting to use... although some are situational. You can also purchase magic spells for more offensive/defensive capability, and these are helpful items to grab as well. The game looks and sounds amazing, with HD art assets for all the characters and 3D rendered platforms to jump and climb over. Its soundtrack by Jake Kaufman is especially catchy, and you'll have the hooks of more than a few stage tracks in your head. Helpful, since you'll be revisiting them a lot.
There are only one or two flaws with the game, and one is far less a transgression than the other. Some of the upgrades hardly change anything, and feel like filler. Attacks for forms you'll hardly use unless you're messing around, or powers used exactly once in a single area to gain another hidden item. In addition, things peak before the climax; the final two stages offer almost no hidden treasures to be found whatsoever. It's as if the game runs out of momentum before the end, and speaking of that we must discuss the penultimate boss. The fights before and after it are relatively engaging and straightforward, but in this middle fight you can only deal damage when the boss uses one of three attacks. The problem is that it spams the other two over and over again, turning what should be a three-minute fight into an agonizingly slow-paced slog where you're just waiting around, dodging the same two easily-dodged attacks over and over again and waiting for the game to decide to give you a chance to deal damage. It's unfortunate and really deflates the climax of an otherwise great game.
At $16 USD you're looking at a five to six-hour experience, if you go for 100% item completion. That would be a bit short for the price, but there's an unlocked "Hero Mode" that lets you play the game over with most of your endgame transformations, and fly through it for kicks in half the time. Other playable modes are forthcoming, so I feel confident in saying the asking price is a worthy investment and giving this the thumbs-up. If you're a fan of the "retro" style of platformers, or love exploratory games like Demon's Crest or Odallus The Dark Call, this will absolutely be your jam.

Great level design, very tight controls, and wonderful music are the best ways to describe this game.  Every level feels fresh and unique, and the game very heavily (almost to a fault) promotes revisiting old areas with new abilities to discover secrets and items.  There are a few bugs here and there, but nothing that harmed the experience.  My only gripes with the game is that there aren't enough areas to explore (5 in total), and the lack of overall challenge in the game.  I said that the areas are fun to explore, but they are considerably less fun the umpteenth time an npc sends you out looking for an item.  Many items can be achieved prior to an npc asking for them however, and those looking for the shortest completion time will be challenged to find the quickest way to collect everything.  Enemies do very little damage and falling down pits does even less.  Additionally, the game hands you upgrades in the form of "Relics", which grant secondary abilities to your transformations, magic attacks that draw power from a mana bar, or passive abilities.  One such relic, obtained by gathering 10 keys hidden throughout the game that unlock concept art in the town hall, gives you an endless mana pool to draw on.  This is very easily abusable with the magic powers you acquire over the course of the game, including a shield that makes you invisible.  By collecting this one relic, you essentially activate god mode and can't be damaged at all.  You are able to turn the upgrades on and off at any time, which I found very welcome trying to give myself a bit more of a challenge, but even without them you'll very rarely see the game over screen.  The game also relies on manual saves where an autosave system would serve so much better.  For instance, going to the map screen mid-level calls a save screen, and upon selecting any other area on the map calls ANOTHER save screen.  The game is also rather short (I achieved 100% completion in about 7 hours according to the in-game timer), so I would mostly recommend this game to completionists or those looking to speed run.  Overall, this is a fantastic game marred by just a few disappointments.  As of the writing of this review, I have only finished the standard game mode with 100% completion with an early copy provided by backing the kickstarter campaign, so the bugs I mentioned earlier will probably be ironed out by the time the game fully launches.
PROS:
-Great sound design/OST
-Fun and diverse levels
-Incredibly tight controls
-Great for speedrunning
CONS:
-A little too much backtracking
-Lacking in overall number of areas
-Some minor oversights (such as the save system)
I give Shantae: Half Genie Hero a 9/10.
So far it's the platformer game i have had the most fun in!

Once again imbued with her magic powers, Shantae has access to a record-breaking twelve transformations. Each form bears a unique function that allows you to further unravel a level on subsequent playthroughs.

There's plenty of fresh, risque content to pique your interest. Several new, cute enemies are bound to catch your eye. It's refreshing to see fantasy mainstays like ghosts and slimes portrayed as cute, sultry ladies. Newcomers and familiar faces both are given a fresh look as the entire game is now beautifully rendered and animated in cel-shaded art, an upgrade from those classic pixels.

The storyline remains as lighthearted and humorous as ever. Progressing the story once again hinges upon catering to fetch quests and revisiting old levels with new powers. Levels are now incredibly linear, complete with a level select screen ala Megaman.  A tremendous amount of effort has been put into developing the bosses, these are by far the most developed in the series.

Unfortunately I must temper my praise for this game by pointing out a few fundamental, glaring flaws.

Several transformations and their upgrades go nearly or entirely unused. Most forms can't attack by default, and those that can be upgraded to strike are not viable compared to Shantae's regular form. This game should have focused on four main transformations, consolidating their abilities (Mermaid and crab have too much overlap) and giving them decent attacks. Majora's Mask did it better. In Pirate's Curse you had access to every upgrade at the press of a single button. The final gauntlet was complex, requiring all of your abilities in conjunction with one another. In here you have sections of gameplay sharply divided between each transformation with no interplay.

I love going back to a level with new powers to find new items. Here I ended up repeating the same levels four or more times, well beyond being able to enjoy my revisits. You can 100% the game in under 3 hours, but your first time without a guide may take you up to six. Since the levels are entirely linear, the game world feels less interconnected and more sterile. Unlocking new transformations no longer fills me with any sense of wonder partially since there are so many and also since they're not punctuated by deeply buried, ancient shrines. There are no dungeons, and the penultimate level is painfully brief.

Amazing art direction coupled with Jake Kaufman's musical prowess make for a winning combination. Half Genie Hero is another wonderful installment, but doesn't hit the same high notes as Pirate's Curse.

Disclosure:
I backed this game during it's crowdfunding campaign. Upon launching the game offers a 64bit DX11 version, this is the one I played.
Shantae returns to once again do battle with her arch nemisis Risky boots and save Scuttle Town from certain doom.
Graphics:
This time out the pixel styled graphics from the previous games make way for new hand drawn sprites and 3D rendered environments (think Duck Takes Remastered). The game looks beautiful with high quality assests used throughout also teamed with the high quality animations the series has had in the past. The game also runs at a locked 60fps. However the graphics options are lacking, offering only resolution changes and AA options of off, on or dynamic.
Controls:
Controls are nice and responsive, press a button and the action is immidiate I was unable to detect any input lag or delay during my playthrough. The game supports both keyboard and mouse and controller configurations. However the game is best played on a controller and also gives out Xbox One button prompts. The default keyboard controls are a little odd with movement on the arrow keys, but are fully rebindable in the optins menu. The options menu is fully mouse driver as is the inventory screen, but the level select and save promps are not which is a little odd.
Gameplay:
The game plays out in the same way as the other Shantae games. Scuttle Town acts as the main hub world for the game offering a shop, access to the games art gallery (with unlockable concept and fan art), a save point and a selection of npc's to talk to who offer game hints or side quests to undertake. Heading into Sky's Hatchery allows Shantae to access the world map where the games levels are represented as desitnations that are unlocked using maps Shantae uncovers along her journey.
The levels themselves consist of two platforming areas followed by a boss battle, however subsiquent visits to a level once completed does not have the boss battle and there is no way I have found yet to replaying bosses without starting a new game. The game does offer three save slots so new games can be played without fear of data loss.
As with previous games in the series, Shantae unlocks transformations and abilities which allow her to further explore each of the levels and uncover more secrets each time through. It is the upgrades that are bring up the first negative of the game which is difficulty. The game is more on the easier side than previous installments if you go for all of the upgrades, especially health. Max health gives Shantae 14 hits before she is defeated and the game is quite generous regarding healing items as well. But these health items are optional and the game can be played through to the end with the starting 2 hit points if desired.
Sound/Music:
The sound in this game is great. Nice high quality sound effects are used throughout and some dialogue is even voice acted at times, although this is limited to Shantae and Risky Boots. Shantae even has voice lines for her magic spells.
The music is also fantastic in this game, with personal notable tracks for me being the music for Mermaid Falls, the boss theme and of course the rocking main theme of the game Dance Through the Danger.
Overall:
I would thoroughly recommend this game as a purchase for those who are into platforming games or those who want a fun (all be it quite short, but replayable) experience. My first playthrough took me 7 1/2 hours to complete, with a 98% completion rating. There are unlockables such as gallery art and a Hero mode which opens up after completing the story once. Not sure what Hero mode is at the time of writing.

This game is a load of fun. I think this is my favorite type of Roguelike game. Doing well enough in a run will get you more money, thus allowing you to buy more classes or upgrades for your characters. Everyone run is different. Before you start a run, you get to choose an adventurer. The adventurers you get to choose from are all random, so you could have a really bad pool to pick from sometimes. Other times, it'll be great.
The concept is really well done, and definitely has it's humor to it. One of the quirks your hero can have is IBS, which just makes them fart occasionally. It does nothing else. People can have really silly names, and it's just generally a lighthearted game.
It's also addictive as hell. It's really easy to set goals in the game, It's really easy to just keep playing. Just one more. Just one more. 3 hours later, you bought that health upgrade, but you probably should have gone to sleep 4 hours ago. I say 4 hours, because it's 4 in the morning, and you meant to go to sleep at 12.
The bosses are also well designed, and enjoyable to fight. Even the super hard versions of the bosses, although they are really damn hard.
This game does have NG+, but I really didn't play it too much, so I can't comment on it.
For $15, I'd thoroughly recommend this game to someone who wants an rpg-ish roguelike game.

This is generally a good game, there are some bugs none of them are gamebreaking though.
However there are a number of aspects where the game could be improved to keep it interesting for much longer. Currently the game is too easy.
- Animal populations should be adjusted, for example:
brown bear and black bear are far too common.
roe deer and white tail on the other hand seem too rare
reindeer herds should be much larger but less frequent
lynxes are also too numerous
- Boar are way too aggressive and strong. Yes they do sometimes charge but probably more like 1 in a 100 times in real
life. They pretty much never charge after a shot has been fired.
- Fur should be a trophy type for all species.
- Callers are way too effective and also way too expensive in relation to rifles
- Cost of items is generally out of proportion a 338 rifle is not almost twice as expensive as a 7mm
- Rifles: for some weird reason the smaller cal rifles (.223,.243,.270) are modern rifles while the larger caliber rifles are
vintage models. More modern rifles should be added to more closely reflect what hunters use in real life.
- Weather cycles should be longer, I'd like to see bad weather lasting several days in a row and vice versa. Weather
should also affect hunting. Noise wise and in regards to animals being more or less active.
- There should be a sandbox mode and a separate progression/career mode. Sandbox should have everything unlocked and
free to play around with full customization of world parameters (weather, day length, spawn rates, etc.) Career mode
should be what the game is now.
- Allow an unlimited number of saves to exist at the same time
- On a map like Hirschfelden which is obviously located in a populated area there should be road traffic, farming etc. going
on.
- Huntermate should be improved, higher res map and scaleable map.
- Maps are of low quality, they need to be improved and brought up to real life standards.

Pros:
-Amazing immersive environments. Some of the best I've seen in any game.
-Realistic acting and looking animals. Hunting them is a challenge.
-Large maps with varied optional side missions.
Cons:
-Too many things need to be unlocked through gameplay. Why do I need to level up in order to sight my rifle in or retrieve shot arrows? It's like they were so stuck with the micro-transaction model from the original game, that they had to include it even when using fake in-game money.
-Lacks a stamina bar. Battling the elements with proper clothing, shelter, and making fires would make the game more engaging.
-Could use some more content, like more small-game and firearms. Squirrels and rabbits exist on the maps, but you can't harvest them.
-Some of the animal calls don't sound right. I've been around whitetail deer a lot and their warning calls don't sound like truck horns.
Overall, this is a fantastic game and one of the best modern hunting experiences out there. You'll stop walking all of the time to snap a picture, it looks and feels that good.

I'm a Kickstarter backer and am a big fan of the Shantae series.
There's three things Wayforward excells at in each Shantae game. Animation, Music, and Writing.
It's literally the best i've seen throughout the games yet, i'm not only gushing over the transition into 2.5D but am also liking the cartoonish character portraits.  The small image bobs gives a sense of liveliness and brings across the way each character is feeling quite adequately.  It's her first HD adventure and and HGH (Half-Genie Hero) fully captures the visual look of a Shantae game.
Jake Kaufman (who has composed each Shantae soundtrack) is the "Audio guy" yet again and has done yet another great job.  You can listen to remixes of older Shantae music and fully original tracks as well, my favorites being the title screen music and Neo Burning Town.
Wayforward yet again gives you their classic tongue-and-cheek style of writing so you can enjoy both the plot and all of the silly jokes that go along with it with one of my favorite quotes being: "Blast it All. That airship cost billions of crowd-funded dollars!"
The major gripe I have with the game currently is the content, it's somewhat of a short game and you'll find yourself finishing it with 100% in about 6-9 hours, Risky's Revenge is a shorter game but the story for HGH leaves more to be desired with the only other option available being the speedrun achievements).  Also two of the transformations only really have one-time uses and are under-powered in comparison to the others.  Granted the other transformations are very useful and gives shantae both tools for tackling a stage and a different means of attacking various enemies.
However, they plan on adding THREE seperate playable costumes for Shantae (similar to the Dancer costume in Risky's Revenge) and plan on adding FOUR additional campaigns for Risky Boots, Rottytops, Bolo, and Sky which should solve the game's launch-date content issue.
If you want to get a full-enjoyment out of HGH, I recommend you play through Risky's Revenge and Pirates Curse beforehand since it'll increase your enjoyment for HGH.  Regardless, this is a good starting point if you're thinking about getting into the series since it does a good job capturing the feel and gameplay of a Shantae game.
I hope you enjoy!  I sure did!!

Worth it. Sure it took 3 years for this kickstarter game to come out, but I can say I got my money's worth for backing this game...and the game only just has the FIRST of FIVE playable characters so far with the rest coming up soon!
Wayforward's best traits are simple yet enteraining gameplay & amazing animation, and both are on full display in Shantae: Half-Genie Hero. They really took what they learned from Ducktales Remastered and refined it into some of the best use of 2D Sprite and Vector animation in a videogame to date. All the characters are drawn by hand this way, no cop-out use 3D-Model characters like in Rayman Legends and many other similar 2.5D games. 3D is only used for the colorful levels and backgrounds, but even you can hardly tell half the time by how well painted and textured they are that the characters feel right at home in the game.
The game itself is probably the easiest to get into of the Shantae series; keeping the mainstay of the series' gameplay, but reducing the amount of backtracking of its metroidvania roots for a wider audience, though a little bit does remain, especially  when trying to get the optional upgrades and 100% completion. I would say that Pirate's Curse is a bigger and more epic adventure entry in the series then this game. However throughout the development of this game I felt like Wayforward were trying to make a more accessable game for the Shantae series, as the first three games are all tied together in their overarching story, making playing only one of the games a bit confusing if you didn't know the plot of the previous ones. Half Genie Hero is its own self contained story so there is no need to play the other games, which can be troublesome for many people as the first game for the Gameboy Advance is a bit arcadic; Risky's Revenge though still enjoyable is a tad flawed with bits of its gameplay, and Pirate's Curse relies on the player knowing the story up until that point in the series.
Currently as of the day before release, none of the DLC has been implemented yet, but once everything is set in it should be avaliable. The only DLC that may take a while is the other playable characters as Wayforward plans to release them one at a time as the three stretchgoal characters Bolo, Sky, and Rottytops aren't quite ready if I remember one of their previous development logs. But the backer level DLC and Risky Boots character story should be coming in soon hopefully.
That said, there are a couple minor shortcomings I am a bit disappointed about. Nothing that impacts my enjoyment of the game, but just a couple nitpicks I have:
1) Once you beat the boss of some levels, if you return to a place you have beaten before, the background is fill with a glooming fog, obscuring the wonderful and charming backgrounds of the levels. It's a shame that such nice looking levels become muddied up by the choice to put up a fog in some of these levels once they are beaten.
2) This one bugs be more then the other: Shantae only has one dancing animation for all her transformations and magic dances. Reguardless of which transformation you choose, she currently only has the hip-shaking dance and the finishing pose for all 14 of her dances. In previous games she had various dancing moves for each one; most notable was the first game where each dance was unique to the transformation or magic; then in Risky's Revenge she only had three dances, but each one was different for the animal she transformed into though the final pose was the same one for all three. FInally is Pirate's Curse, which granted do to plot didn't have transformation dances, but using the lamp item did give two different animations, one of which was a all new belly dancing animation. It wasn't necessary for the gameplay or plot, but it was a nice little touch to her character. However here in this game there are 14 dances, but they all use the same one.
It could easily be fixed by tweaking the animations a bit. Here's how the dancing works to get an idea. You press the "Dance" button to bring up the dancing menu. Soft music and a steady beat starts playing and Shantae dances to it in rhythm. The menu shows the first 4 dance slots for 2 beats then for the next 2 beats it switches to the second set of 4 dances, then 2 beats for the third set, then it cycles back to the first four, making 12 slots for dances total. Risky's Revenge had a similar concept with the dances where holding down the dance button would cycle through the three dances in that game and releasing it activated the transformation she was performing.
The issue of Shantae having only one dance and one finishing pose could be fixed of each of the 2 beats she did a different dance move for each set of dances, then finally once the dance is selected she does a finishing pose that represents the transformation she turns into.
However, regardless of the minor shortcomings that may get fixed, Shantae: Half-Genie Hero is a success in my book. Sure this kickstarter isn't the groundbreaker or epic adventure Shovel Knight is; but it is FAR from the disaster Mighty No. 9 was. This game isn't meant to be grand, but rather a fun, charming adventure with likeable and often funnily-bizzard characters you know from Wayforward. So if you enjoyed Wayforward's previous games or want to start getting into their games; Half-Genie Hero is a full time winner, and will get even better as the stretchgoal content is released.

Full disclosure: I am a Kickstarter backer of this game.
The Shantae series has been a consistent provider of well-crafted platform adventures since the original was released on the Game Boy Color, with each game adding new refinements to a proven formula. This latest release continues the trend with updated abilities and a combination of hand-drawn and 3D graphics.
As mentioned, this game doesn't deviate much from previous Shantae games - though this isn't a bad thing. Bad guys are up to bad things in Sequin Land, and it's Shantae's job to collect what she needs to stop them. Fans of the series will be on familiar territory, and metroidvania fans will find a lot to like. The characters are endearing and memorable, and the plot would fit nicely in a well-written Saturday morning cartoon.
Of course, an important element in any game of this type is the quality of the puzzles and secrets. This game has well-crafted ones just difficult enough to make you want to finish them, without being overly frustrating. I was able to clear 96% of the game without a guide, and the items I had to really work for can be passed over if you just want to play through without finding every little secret. The boss fights are mostly of the "action puzzle" variety as well. At times, the method for beating them wasn't immediately clear, but it didn't require much work to figure it out, and the fights themselves were still challenging.
As for the shift in art style, I am in favor of it. As much as I appreciate well-done sprite graphics (and I do), the hand-drawn characters really suit this series, and it goes well with the cartoony atmosphere. Speaking of, I enjoyed the dialogue as well, with well-written humor that managed to be sharp without resorting to being too crude.
All in all, I think adventure fans will enjoy this game if they've never tried the series before, and returning Shantae fans will be well satisfied. Shantae is securing her position among gaming greats.

While this game is a bit shorter than the series' previous outings (though the addition of in-development add-on content at a later date will likely change that), the gameplay, animation, sound and visual design are all utterly fantastic.
The game sports pop-in voice overs at select points in the otherwise (and more often than not hilarious) message box based dialogue, that the developers at WayForward used to great effect to enhance the charm of the game. There is also a bevy of usually well-hidden items to collect throughout the levels that will require copious backtracking to acquire all of- several of which, as with past entries in the series, will result in encounters with some of the game's highly amusing NPC characters.
The soundtrack to the game is also completely fantastic. Composed by WayForward go-to composer, the masterful Jake 'Virt' Kaufman, the entirety of the game's score is nothing short of pure ear candy. Every stage, cinematic, screen and else all exude top-quality music that earns the games' track list the highest of marks.
The game controls extremely well with tight responsiveness to input, and features native controller support for those that want a more classic gaming experience.
The series' signature transformations are triggered by pressing a key/button to enter dance mode, at which point any currently available transformations can be selected via a wheel that will appear on screen, which switches pages in time with the beat.
In addition, usable items such as those used to restore health are accessed via the game's item menu, which features a simple and efficient design with scrollable lists and fields rather than relying on spreading items and features across multiple pages.
The game is entirely a side-scrolling single-depth platformer, as with (for the most part) all previous Shantae installments.
There are a few spontaneous and sudden upswings in difficulty at select points throughout the game, though most players will find that in some cases these troubles are merely caused by a lack of clarity as to the intended objective at hand, rather than that of a spontaneous rise in the actual challenge of the gameplay. In most cases, these unfortunate but minor hurdles can be overcome quickly once the solution is discovered, resulting in a speedy resolution and a return to the game's usual play.
In addition to the previously mentioned (as of this writing) pending additional gameplay content, the game also boasts a new game+ feature which allows you to replay the story after beating the game once with all of your main transformations unlocked from the start of the game, perfect for speed running purposes.
Featuring a clean blend of high-quality hand-drawn character sprites, specific world elements, enemies, items, etc., and typical 3D environments, the game's '2.5D' graphics presentation are refreshing and striking. The combination of vivid color palettes and layered animations make the game stand out noticeably and beautifully. Even in spite of combinations of multiple entities, particle effects, and more on screen at many points throughout the game, it maintains a consistent run speed that should function fairly well even on less than impressive machines (I played the game on a relatively underpowered laptop, and suffered no lag or frame loss the entire game).
Overall, Shantae: ½ Genie Hero is a stellar addition to an already extremely consistently quality franchise that will likely go down, and unsurprisingly so, as the greatest installment in the series yet. While a tad underwhelming in length, the entirety of the rest of what's on offer is fantastic. If you like classic platforming games, striking visual presentation, and constant comedic banter, then you're sure to come away from this one thoroughly satisfied.

I have put a lot, and I mean A LOT of time into this game, I've been playing it for over a year so I think I've got enough knowledge about this game to finally review/talk it.
First, I would like to say that I have not spent a single penny on this game, not because I don't want to support it, but because I'm still a student with no job, so this will all be how it goes from a £0 experience.
Now, this game is really fun, it has 3 a side street basketball where you play with people online, you can choose one of 8 positions (5 main ones plus 3 special positions which makes the game a lot more fun) I have dabbled in each class, the best for me being a Short Forward and a Swing Man.
It has a lot of skills in the game, each class getting a different set depending on their role, but also allowing them to extend what they can do, for example, my main SF is also really good at passing and assisting like a Point Guard. You unlock these as you level up your separate characters, skills do not transfer between characters so every time you make a new one it will be like starting over again. Something else that doesn't go between characters is your inventory (Unless it's a character coupon) so everything you get with a character can't be used with another, which is really good as you can't make a new character but give them clothes or cards that a level 50 (Max level) character would use.
What does go between characters is points and money (Points being things you get after a game and money being what you buy with real money) so you may be able to buy a skill (which use regular points) as soon as you unlock it instead of having to wait for you to get more money. What also is between characters would be sponsors (Being exp, points and VIP) which gives you a boost in what you get after a match. You can get these by either buying them or getting them dropped through one of the many events that take place.
The main downside to this game is that I live in England but my friend who I play with lives in America, meaning that if we decide to play together, one of us will have to sacrifice some ping to go to the other server, luckily the account goes between severs so I can play in Europe server with my characters while not playing with my friend and level them up.
All in all, this game is really fun and I recommend it to anyone that wants a basketball game to play with friends but doesn’t have a lot of money, but you can always spend money if you want. You can always win if you are good enough, so just practice and have fun!

Don't let this game's generic gameplay fool you. It may seem like your typical 3rd-person, over-the-shoulder, pop-out-of-cover, military shooter (I even told myself that when I first heard of the game), but it's much more than that. In fact, many argue that its gameplay is just a means to further add to the game’s storytelling which is the core of this game. You will question what you do and the choices you make.
There is no black and white here. You’re in for a moral ride. If you get it, don’t spoil the story for yourself, otherwise you won’t get the full impact of the story (you’ll probably just be wasting your money at that point).
The game is not long; I think I clocked in about 7 hours on the campaign, maybe less. The gameplay is not bad but it may seem a bit repetitive as it doesn’t vary much from what you get from the start. So if you’re willing to put up with that to get at a good story I highly recommend this title.
Though I would still advise to pick it up during a sale, it’s hard to enjoy a 7 hour story when you pay $30 for it. The cheaper you pay the more you can sit back and enjoy the game for its qualities rather than being♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥at it for its faults.

Let's get some things out of the way first: the "innovative" ways of altering the environment are gimmicks. The shooter elements don't have the tightest controls. The actual gameplay is good but nothing amazing.
Now that I've gotten that out of the way, the story, is absolutely UNBELIEVABLE. This game will make you do things and then make you hate yourself for doing them. It will relate to real life in ways unseen. It's a deliberate and biting criticism on the happy-go-lucky glorification of war that seems to happen in many other modern military shooter campaigns (hell, several elements in the game struck me as a "screw you!" to Modern Warfare 2's campaign, to be frank). It's powerful, it's emotional, it will leave you in shock, and you will learn to hate yourself by the end.
I highly recommend it.

This game is a prequel to the original Life is Strange game. I highly recommend you play this first before you start the original Life is Strange game.
The game features Chloe who you play as throughout the 3 episodes, giving you a greater depth of Chloe's life, her relationships, her hidden motives, etc.
STORY: 8.5/10
The storyline showed so much that wasn't in the original game, gives you a huge insight if you were to know who Rachel was before playing the original game. The character relationships in this game is the big impact that really keeps everyone wanting to keep playing/watching. Problem for me was that from playing the original game first, you already know what happens so the prequel is just lining you up for this, as you feel like your decisions won't impact much at all. This is one reason why I'd highly recommend you play the prequel first. Showing the conflicts and difficulties Chloe had throughout her life really makes you feel for her, this shows that the writer really did well in making the audience feel this way.
SOUNDTRACK: 10/10
I think most people would agree how amazing the life is strange soundtrack is. The tracks used for each scene were perfect in making the player feel the emotions of Chloe herself or whatever character was being portrayed in that scene. People undermine soundtracks in games, but do not realize how much of an effect this actually has on a scene. Try muting music within the game and see how you feel playing through it. No emotion whatsoever.
VOICE ACTING: 9/10
A new voice actor was brought in to replace Chloe's previous actor. I feel as though this VA really fitted the role of Chloe a lot better than the previous one in the original Life is Strange. Although this could be marked as pro as there is a 3 year time lapse between Before the Storm and the original game, therefore Chloe's emotions, her personality, etc change throughout those 3 years, thus affecting how her voice is portrayed after the 3 years.
OVERALL RATING: 9/10
After finishing the final episode of this game, I honestly felt broken after getting to know these characters and now finally it's finished, if there is a sequel to the game I feel as though it won't be the same without certrain characters (Don't want to spoil). The story isn't a masterpiece but it really attracted the player to feel the emotions that a particular character was feeling, this is not a trait you will see in many games, this shows a great game. This game builds a strong base for Chloe's character going into the next game and really helps you get to know more about Chloe and Rachel's relationship.
An amazing roller coaster of emotions. Lives up to, and possibly exceeds the original Life is Strange.

If you're looking for a brand new style of gameplay, or some game that changes the way you think about gaming as a concept or a medium: this isn't it. Much like the original Life is Strange, Before the Storm relies on a somewhat more natural extension of the Telltale episodic games, where the story is placed first, with gameplay falling somewhere near the bottom of the list of priorities. However, the clever idea to have the 'permanent' choices be reversible presented in the original is missing here, as is the actual presence of time-messer-upper Max Caulfield. Instead, the fan favorite Chloe Price is given to the player, and, much like her behavior in the original, there is no fixing of mistakes in this game. If you truly want to fix a problem, you're gonna have to deal with immediate consequences, followed by using your point-and-click adventure abilities, if the option is offered at all. The only truly unique thing about playing as Chloe in terms of gameplay is the Backtalk ability, which puts the focus on being in the moment to the limit. Outside of all this context, this game is a phenominal story, complete with likeable characters, intriguing plot, and (mostly) believable setting. While not Ashly Burch, Rhianna DeVries still brings forth the character of Chloe without fault, bringing the badass punk rocker rebel who also plays Dungeons and Dragons to life. The other characters, specifically Steph, Nathan, David, Frank, among many others I dare not spoil, are also fantastic, both in voice and model. Outside of a couple awkward animations, the characters are human as can be, with strengths and faults and so on. My only issue with some of the characters is their sometimes archetypal behavior, such as the Warren Graham of this game, Eliot, or the return of the all-seeing groundskeeper, Samuel. Most of these are made up for in the game's plot, where its sometimes necessary to have these styles of character, despite the unstable behavior of the plot itself. Every single bit of information that Chloe, and by extension, the player, gains spins the characters in a new light. Of course there are the standard end-of-episode twists that are mostly there to keep episode-only buyers invested in the next one, but within each episode as well, the player has difficulty keeping track of who is an ally and who is an enemy. I personally found myself classifying and reclassifying characters after conversations or even just lines, which is great for a story about angsty teenagers and their misadventures. The setting is one that I generally have no qualms about; only near the end of the LiS games is there any sort of shark jumping, and I'd compare it more to a ten year old's bike ramp to an actual issue regarding believability. The atmosphere of Blackwell Academy, the Price Household, the mill during the concert sequence that begins the first episode, all do great to ensnare the player in the location, specifically in the moment, much like the oft inebriated Chloe Price would likely be. There were moments where I needed to be reminded of issues outside of the ones taking place in the current room, because otherwise I wouldn't have considered them at all. While this game is incredibly great in story, characters, settings, and a specific few character models (Chloe, Rachel, James, the rest are relatively hit or miss), there are a few issues. For one, as said before, there's not much to gameplay. Even in the original, or some of the Telltale games I have played, there's at least some variety, or at least some quicktime events. Before the Storm knows this, however, and, much like it's main character, it doesn't give a f*ck. The game is here less as a game, and more as an example of how choices made in the moment change things going forward, presented in a dramatic version of reality. Outside of gameplay, there were a couple of model issues in my playthrough, which, while distracting, didn't ruin the game or its message(s). And, again, there were some character choices that I thought felt either forced or not generally believeable. However, despite these flaws, Life is Strange: Before the Storm takes the player by the hand, much like Rachel Amber or Chloe Price in the original, and presents them with a story that is equally as beautiful as it is heartbreaking. It'll be a sad day when the Farewell bonus episode drops, because it means saying goodbye to the characters that I've come to know as friends. If you want a game with gameplay, look elsewhere. If you want to see how much a person can change the world around them, welcome to Aracadia Bay. 4.25/5

As i mentioned in my general overview of the game, there is enough gameplay and enjoyment to be had if playing with others, to go into more detail let us look at what you can actually do as a group:
As a group you're able to take over territory for the faction you chose to join, (so long as your faction has territory already adjacent to the area you're trying to take control of that is), and the more people you have in your group the easier this becomes, the pirates in Windward are merciless they won't often just have one or two ships, there will be many a time when you'll be trying to take over pirate territory to expand your factions control, only to have to face many pirates (from my experience 5 - 7) all at the same time and some of those pirates will probably be captains in the tougher areas of the server you're playing on and eventually you'll reach lords and dread lords which will happily chew you up and spit you out if you're not ready for them. this is why you need a group because no matter what ship you're in, unless you've gone defence for your specialisation  or are some what over leveled for the zone you're in, taking out a pirate zone solo is neigh impossible.
Trading isn't necessarily a group activity if all i was to base this section on was the trading quests you receive from towns ("drop cargo of at..."), no instead if we look at levelling up a town or increasing a towns rank you do this by either, "A" quests for that town being completed or "B" from finding and selling materials the town needs to the town, a group effort in this scenario makes the task a little easier as the goods a town requires increases for each level so having help here is greatly appreciated as it saves one person a lot of work.
not something I've spent much time doing (as doing so requires you to wear a black flag which unfortunately that makes you hostile to everything other than pirates), but from what I've heard PvP is all well and good until high levels decide to enter low level areas with black flags and wreck the newer players, now while i know that's what the white flag is for i don't think you start off with a white flag i think you have to find it just like you have to find the black flag (which to my knowledge drops from pirates, but i'm unaware as to what drops the white flag or how it is obtained).
solo gameplay is possible but in comparison to playing with a friend or a group of people it is considerably slower and in some cases (such as expanding territories), much harder.
these are my thoughts on the game and if anything changes i'll modify my review.

TrackMania Stadium is a solid high-speed multiplayer racing game that puts you against the clock with other players across the world simultaneously.
TrackMania is a game about precision. If you are looking for a racing game with crashes and power-ups, this is not for you. TMS has a large surplus of maps with various difficulties. Almost every track involve a very large amount of skill to pull of fast times. TMS has a single-player mode and it's pretty basic. You competing against yourself to get bronze, silver or gold medals. The single-player is here to enhance your ability to do better on courses and to make you even better at the game. The money is well spent when you play multiplayer.
There are a ton of servers that are up across the world. All ranging from U.S. to Germany to Japan. I was amazed by how the servers ran, even with over 50 people. Obviously, this was needed as this type of game relies on time based racing.
It's exhilerating to go at a such high speed and making perfect turns as you barely beat the opponent who is ahead of you. You actually feel like you are going extremely fast and it makes the game challenging and pretty addicting at certain times. The graphics in TMS aren't amazing compared to TrackMania Valley, but they get the job done as well as the audio.
The controls aren't totally perfect, but they're responsive enough to give you a chance of making some really good times.
I'm not that great at the game, but these last 7 hours have improved me as a player and I can only learn from the professionals around me.
PROS:
+High Speed Time Trials
+Great Amount of Tracks
+Solid Controls
+Good Community with a large surplus of servers
+Decent Price
+Excellent Frame-rate with very rare connection issues
+Skill Based
CONS:
-Can get tedious on occasion
While I only have one con, that bullet is very important. I rarely find myself playing TMS for more than an hour on any given time which isn't that great of a thing. Although, TMS is a solid game nonetheless.

Trackmania's uniquely in-depth track creator and rule-of-cool physics could have added up to a great game, but the community has utterly killed it.
I was sold by the demo servers. The tracks were interesting and varied, the atmosphere was one of friendly competition, and even if you lost you still had fun trying to beat your own time. So you buy the game, open the server list and pick the first one that isn't plain black text.
And then it all comes tumbling down.
Half the screen is filled with needless leaderboards, ugly buttons that don't do anything and other pointless bells and whistles. The other half of the screen is a horrifically complex track you'll be lucky to beat even once. Most of the time they're so horrifically cluttered that you need to drive off the track and let a replay show you the path, and that still won't help because the map is 60 seconds of madness and you only have 5 minutes to beat it.
If this were the game the demo claimed it would be, I would wholeheartedly recommend it. But if you're a newcomer to the series who likes the demo version, just keep playing it instead of wasting your money on a game that's been mutated in a demonic, unforgiving shell of its former self.

You will make a tight, high-speed turn, followed by a jump, fly across an enourmous gulf, land, do a loop, and then crash into a finish line. Or miss, but eventually you will succeed.
And then there is the extraordinarily powerful (AND easy to use!!) level editor, which has led to large community of excellent user created tracks and multiplayer servers.
It's fun to make Europeans angry when you beat them.

In short, if you you're a Trackmania veteran, you don’t need this. If you're new to Trackmania you can play essentially the same game for free, so go and play Nations and see what all the fuss is about.

The best CoD so far.
Customizable loadouts in singleplayer, such as weapons and weapon attachments, camo, gadgets, all that. You can choose between BO1 weapons or BO2 weapons in the campaign too. Story is meh, good ol' "America is the good guy, some crazy russian/middle-eastern guy is the crazy bad guy who wants to kill everyone in the world" and of course the bad guy knows exactly what you're gonna do and when you're gonna do it.
Multiplayer is where it's at for me. The multiplayer is absolutley GREAT. There's lots of different weapons that are actually pretty balanced, there's not really any dominant weapons (although there are of course weapons that are really easy to use and that are good in alot of situations but it's a casual game I don't mind). I think pretty much every weapon in the game has it's own strengths, especially since they keep balancing the weapons.
If you prestige in this game, you keep all your titles, your weapon levels, all that. The only thing that actually resets is your level and of course the things you've unlocked to use in create a class, would be kinda ridiculous to start with everything unlocked. Then, after you've prestiged, you have a choice of unlocking any one thing in create a class that you want to, and you also have a choice of resetting your stats, getting a new class slot and something else I forgot.
You can also prestige weapons. You don't lose your weapon camos if you do this, only your weapon level (weapon level unlocks attachments) and the camo unlocks are really cool and unique, sometimes hard so you have to work for them. Example: Art of War is getting 150 kills with no attachments, stuff like that. You have to get X amount of kills until you get to the "harder" camo unlocks which I think is great. To get gold you have to get all the camos for the weapon (you can also put camo and unlock camos on your knife), and there's even a diamond camo to get if you can unlock gold for every single weapon in a category. Doing that rewards you with a golden camo on all weapons in that category.
The best thing is probably the create-a-class system as you get 10 points to spend however you want, litteraly. You can even go without any weapons and just your knife but have lots of perks or lots of grenades and stuff.
This is without a doubt my favourite CoD.

The Steam achievements are fantastic, and the looting aspect of the game definitely appeals to those who love rogue games and dungeon crawlers. Any connoisseur of platformers should also give this a try.

It's hard to judge this game as a standalone, because as a standalone game I really do think it is an amazing game. However, as it is part of the series, I was really disappointed in the cutscene simulator this game has become. Episode 1 uses it in decent and quite logical ways, a lot of them being optional(like the tabletop game) without making it feel like you're just looking at a cutscene. But episode 2 shows instantly that its not a game anymore, just a movie you can change the dialogue of. Which is fine on its own, but the world of life is strange is one you feel like you need to explore a little.
!!!!!(Spoilers for LiS1)!!!!! Like back in the diner as Max to get the keys from Frank you could decide how long you needed to walk around and talk to people to get your objective, but you could also get a lot of interesting information in general. When you had to collect items at the junkyard, you could explore Chloe's world a bit more if you wanted to.
!!!!!(Spoilers for this game ahead)!!!!!
Now here, even though it is hella fun to smash things in the junkyard, we know from Max's story that the junkyard meant a lot to both Rachel and Chloe. This story was supposed to show that, but I guess I missed out on that. I get that with altering time you can add a lot of puzzles to fix while being able to retry them when they fail, but it feels like they cared way more for story telling than actual gameplay. There were definitely amazing things, like the story on its own, the backtalking and some very unexpected events like Rachel getting stabbed. But that doesnt make up for the lazy decision to make nearly everything a cutscene. If you compare both games to each other, only the cutscenes, I am pretty sure Before the Storm has about 8 hours of cutscene of the average 9 hour playthrough. If they just added a bit more exploration or the options to skip texts of the texts you have already been through. I get that Max used her time altering abilities to do so, but why not let Chloe use snarky remarks to speed up the conversation? Why not use the junkyard more often as a place? Why make everything a cutscene? And most importantly: why make a choice based game if you clearly dont know what to do with the smaller choices? This game felt like it was rushed and published to keep a decent schedule, but I would have been willing to wait 1 more year for the final episode to make sure the cutscenes were less present. Before Chloe speaks with Sera, she arrives at the area she started this story in. An amazing time to explore what was once a partyplace, but now a burned down shack. But no, you can only comment on the couch Frank sat on and the random bong on the counter. The rest? Cutscenes.

This is one of those reviews where I really wish there was a "meh" option.
- You will like this game if you are an avid hunter who wants to experience the slow, long, dreadfully boring experience that is crawling after a deer while proning not over, but through rocks and trees like a 4 dimensional being with no legs.
- You will not like this game if you want the stability, progression, and fun of a game in the $30 range.
- I shot a deer in the head and it ran away. I tracked the blood and found it walking around, so I shot it in the vital organs. It ran away again. I tracked the blood and found it walking around, so I shot it in the neck, It ran away. I tracked the blood and the deer I shot in the neck turned out to be a different deer. I found the trail of the original deer, and it was just bleeding profusely while hanging out walking around in circles. I shot it again, it ran away, and I uninstalled and refunded the game.
- There's a weird help system that is this kind sounding guy who is on the phone(?) with you the entire time. You'll find a bear track, and he'll be like "Oh hey, we got bears out here. They can be dangerous but they usually notice you before you notice them." At one point I started looking around for a little drone or something that enabled this creep to follow me around the forest telling me what bears are.
- The leveling up system seems pointless and forced. If you're going to put XP and special abilities into a hunting game, it shouldn't try to be a realistic hunting game. This might be the first game where I realized I had skill points and didn't even care enough to spend them.
- I guess this is the best hunting game on Steam, which is kind of like being the best baseball game on Xbox One. There's a couple to choose from, and the other ones probably won't even run.
So if you REALLY want a hunting game, this is your best bet. I'd have kept the game if it was $9.99 or less. As a gaming experience I've had much more fun hunting in Far Cry 3/4 or Red Dead Redemption.
Oh and the ATV DLC is dumb, although a vital feature. It should absolutely be part of the base game.

Pros
-Absolutely breath taking game. Those screenshots that you see on the store page? The game actually looks like that. It blows my mind every time I play this game just because it is so gorgeous.
-The sound design. Oh god the sound design is amazing. It sounds exactly as a forest should, as quiet as it is when there's little around, the scampering of small creatures in the brush, the whoosh of the wind through the trees, the crackling of bark, the calls of birds, the leaves falling down and nestling on the ground. It's amazing.
-The hunting. Hunting in this game is as easy or as hard, as fast or as slow, as in depth or as simple as you want it to be. While this might be a con for some, playing the game slow, hard, and in depth will be rewarding and net you high quality trophies, and playing in the opposite fasion will get you kills, but not on the better quality animals.
-It's not thehunter classic. Everything in this game you can get and use without paying money, save the ATVs and tents. You do not have to pay a monthly subscription, and you can hunt any of the animals in the game no matter what.
-The maps are gigantic. While discovering every area might be a chore because of this, the amazingly huge maps of this game are truly an achievement. Every area looks as beautiful as the screenshots, and there is so much of it that you could play this game for months and not find everything.
Cons
-It is a thehunter game and is not classic. Because of this it suffers the same problems as primal did. Lack of content, low support from the developers, and here's a new one- content hidden behind pay walls. The good thing though, you only have to pay once for the items on the dlc page and the ATV at least is infinitely replenishable.

The absolute best multiplayer racing game ever created. My favorite and the most popular game mode, time attack, is the best implementation of multiplayer racing I've ever seen. This game is just like Trackmania United but with more players, upgraded graphics, and a nicer interface. There are thousands of maps made by players. Ladder points also put an objective to the game which lets players want to keep playing to rank up. Lots of different map types too, including tech, fullspeed, speed tech, dirt, nascar, etc. You can make this game as competitive as you want -- whether you're after that dedi 1 or just to beat your pb, it's fun for every player. In the beginning, some maps may be hard to finish. You'll be crashing into walls, trying to just finish. That can be fun, but with a bit of practice you can really have fun trying to finish first on a server or beat records. Driving mechanics are wonderful, and the loops and crazy transitions in fullspeed make it a ridiculous arcade style game with endless enjoyment. A great community of people too. Everyone is willing to help you out if you need it and, for example, if you get a good time on a map, people will say "nt" (Nice time). From shredding your time down to the best it can be in the limited time the map runs for, to trying to rank up in your region, Trackmania Stadium (and all the other Trackmania games for that matter) is a wonderful game and worth every penny.

The best CoD so far.
Customizable loadouts in singleplayer, such as weapons and weapon attachments, camo, gadgets, all that. You can choose between BO1 weapons or BO2 weapons in the campaign too. Story is meh, good ol' "America is the good guy, some crazy russian/middle-eastern guy is the crazy bad guy who wants to kill everyone in the world" and of course the bad guy knows exactly what you're gonna do and when you're gonna do it.
Multiplayer is where it's at for me. The multiplayer is absolutley GREAT. There's lots of different weapons that are actually pretty balanced, there's not really any dominant weapons (although there are of course weapons that are really easy to use and that are good in alot of situations but it's a casual game I don't mind). I think pretty much every weapon in the game has it's own strengths, especially since they keep balancing the weapons.
If you prestige in this game, you keep all your titles, your weapon levels, all that. The only thing that actually resets is your level and of course the things you've unlocked to use in create a class, would be kinda ridiculous to start with everything unlocked. Then, after you've prestiged, you have a choice of unlocking any one thing in create a class that you want to, and you also have a choice of resetting your stats, getting a new class slot and something else I forgot.
You can also prestige weapons. You don't lose your weapon camos if you do this, only your weapon level (weapon level unlocks attachments) and the camo unlocks are really cool and unique, sometimes hard so you have to work for them. Example: Art of War is getting 150 kills with no attachments, stuff like that. You have to get X amount of kills until you get to the "harder" camo unlocks which I think is great. To get gold you have to get all the camos for the weapon (you can also put camo and unlock camos on your knife), and there's even a diamond camo to get if you can unlock gold for every single weapon in a category. Doing that rewards you with a golden camo on all weapons in that category.
The best thing is probably the create-a-class system as you get 10 points to spend however you want, litteraly. You can even go without any weapons and just your knife but have lots of perks or lots of grenades and stuff.
This is without a doubt my favourite CoD.
