I have had my eye on Mad Max for a while now but was hesitant to buy it due to being let down on many occasions with big budget games. I managed to get a good deal on the game and started it up with mediocre expectations. It surpassed those.
It is a great game to play, even if for a short period of time. You know that itch you get to play GTA or Saints Row for half and hour just to drive around, explore and kill random folk? Well, I got it with this too.
The combat system is akin to the modern Batman games and Assassins Creed. You can attack by pressing the X button, hold it for longer to do a strong attack and you can counter enemies with a well times press of the Y button. As you progress through the game you are able to learn abilities to instantly kill some enemies. I found it fun hitting some combos on a dude, turning to another and blowing him away with a shotgun and then countering someone else to then German suplex him. It's feels like it has some good weight behind it.
Being a Mad Max game, the driving had to be great... and they succeeded! It's so much fun to drive around the world exploring and seeing how your car upgrades affect your vehicle and play style. The vehicular combat leaves a lot to be desired though as the camera never seems to want to play nice, the lock-on system can be temperamental and can also just downright not work on occasion. It leaves a bit of frustration but is easily glossed over.
Overall I would recommend it, even at full price. I got 38 hours from it and I may even play more as similar to games like Fallout, it let's you carry on playing after you beat the story. It's a gorgeous, fun to play game with a few frustrations here and there but we;; worth your time and money.

Quoting "Just Good PC Games" (because it's easy and it's true):
"With an enthralling story, great combat, and even better driving mechanics, Mad Max proves to be a solid game for newcomers and hardcore fans alike."
After 30 hours I feel like I've done nearly everything in the game.
I've played through the story (which is very well done in the end, you get the "Mad Max"-series end but you can continue with your own story), I've taken down all the camps, I've upgraded all the Strongholds, I've finished all the side missions.
For $10 I have to recommend this game for anyone who loves getting lost in a Single Player game (with great driving, an awesome world and interesting characters) that's just fun to play.
Tips for new players to the game:
* Figure out all the keyboard shortcuts; X on foot (in a camp!) and C while driving are two important ones.
* I'd recommend doing the blue missions (side missions) before continuing with the main story line (green missions)
* Don't forget to go see Griffa every once in a while

It took me around 14 hours to complete my first playthrough, and I've seen others complete it in just 8. I found that a lot of people that took less time to complete the game were not as satisfied and even confused at times by the events taking place.
From my experience it was the little things that really brought the story to life. The little details that add so much depth, but can be completely missed if you don't take the time to look for them. If you don't have the patience to explore everywhere, talk to everyone, and read all of chloe's journal you are going to miss out. There are some details that are un important and others that may completely change your perspective on things.
If you are not a fan of slow paced story driven games, you won't get as much enjoyment from it as others.
Personally, I could relate to the characters, loved the depth, details, and the nods to the original. (I highly recommend replaying the original to really see all the connections).
The Life is Strange series has one of my favorite stories of all time. I can't wait to see what new stories they come up with next.

First I just want to explain the "have not yet played the game much" part that might show up over this review. I have played through this entire game on the xbox 360 several times, so this review is legitimate. I have experienced this game to its fullest and am therefore qualified to review it. I have only played it for the short time now so that I could see how well it ran on my computer compared to the Xbox 360. It runs very smoothly. I was using an Xbox controller and it was responsive but I am nto sure that it would as good with the keyboard and mouse as I have not yet tried it. Now, let us get on with the review.
You are Captain Martin Walker, with your team you are being sent on a rescue mission where things end up going south really fast. It seems like everything is just spiraling down to very dark matters very quickly where you end up having to kill the people you came to save.
If you are looking for a game like the COD or Battlefield series, this is not what you are looking for. The creators of this game knew that they did not have the budget for such a production so they therefore worked more on the games story and mechanics which was truly worth it. On the surface this game seems like a generic 3'rd person shooter. The gameplay mostly consists of lining up headshots on your enemies to preserve ammunition, which in the long run on its own would be boring. What they do right is putting out branching paths, without specifically telling you that you have choices to choose from. I'm going to try to explain one of these as spoiler free as possible, but I will put the notice *SPOILER* in case you want to know none of the things happening in the game before playing it. (Skip to the next paragraph from here if that is the case). There is a part of the game where you are surrounded by civilians who seem to be quite agressive. you can not move on if you do not choose to fire your weapon. On the first playthrough, I shot at the crowd. Making them run away in horror. On my second playthrough I thought that I might be able to scare them off if I just shot into the air, and I was delighted to find out that it worked, but the game has a lot of these.
As I played the game for a while I started to realize that I started to dislike myself more and more while playing it. When the loading screens were loading, it said some things in the place where there are usually hints in games that resonated within me. An example being "How many people have you killed today?" It seemed as the game was directly talking to me, not the character I was playing in the game. It made me think for a while, why was I doing what I was doing? I of course justified it to myself, saying that I had to do those things, if not I could not progress with the game, but I was yet not satisfied with my reasoning. It was clear for me that it was a bad excuse as I just felt uneasy while playing the game, which became abundantly clear in the end of the game (Which I will not at all spoil for you, but I will say that it has all to do with why we play games. If you read this review before you complete the game, just remember that the last level is directly speaking to you, the player). You actually end up regretting the things you have done.
When you first meet your character, your mind will probably go to the place of "Oh, here we go again. A very clichè, testosterone filled Soldier with problems, who cares*, but after a while you will maybe dislike your character. The fact that I didn't like my main character might be something that made me enjoy the game more(I have heard different things, this is only my experience with the character, while others have said that they started to sympathize with him.)
All in all, it was one of my favorite games of 2012. If the things I've written in this review(my first review) captures your interest, I would tell you to get the game. I do not want you to get into the game with the wrong idèa, so I felt like putting out my thoughts on this one. Remember, this is my own experiences with the game. All have their own thoughts about this. I am just glad I was able to share mine.

Spec Ops: The Line, is most certainly, without a doubt, THE hidden gem of 2012. Here's why:
Gameplay: 6.5/10 - This is probably the weakest part of this game. However, it was still enjoyable enough to keep me occupied during the whole single-player campaign. This game is a cover-based third-person shooter. While there are some neat little gimmicks here and there, Spec Ops doesn't really do much to innovate, and stands as basically being an average shooter when it comes to the core mechanics. You will move from cover to cover, shooting blankly, or pushing yourself out and aiming, using your fairly average assortment of modern-military shooter weapons.
You also have two squad members that you can direct to either attack enemies or to paralyze them. This is rather useful, and the A.I. is fairly decent and can actually help you out quite a bit when you're in a pickle. Another thing to mention would have to be using the environment to kill your enemies. However, this is nothing too special and just looks pretty for show.
Now, if you're expecting a non-linear experience from Spec Ops: The Line, then you should look elsewhere. Spec Ops: The Line is an extremely linear game, in which you will go through corridor after corridor of enemy encounters as the story and character progression grows. There are collectibles to find in the game, but are fairly easy to find for the most part, and won't lead you off the beaten trail.
Spec Ops: The Line also has the cinematic setpieces you would expect from modern-military shooters, but they actually compliment the story for the most part.

When it comes to multiplayer, it really should just be avoided. It's nothing special and may even ruin the atmosphere of the game itself for you.
Presentation: 9.0/10 - Spec Ops: The Line isn't exactly set in the most original place when it comes to modern-military shooters (Dubai), but the art-style is fantastic and compliments the game's overall atmosphere greatly. Everything is very bright and colorful, as the lighting and particle effects are excellent. The whole city of Dubai feels very surreal and liely, though the whole game is extremely dark in tone. This actually creates a rather disturbing and disjointed feeling throughout the entire game, which is great. When it comes to textures, there's nothing really special here. The game looks average, with character models especially having seemingly low resolution textures.
Cutscenes are decent, except for the pre-rendered ones, which are locked at thirty frames per second, and don't even look much better than the ones that aren't. However, many cutscenes are very emotional and well voice-acted, just as the rest of the game.
What I do have to mention is that anti-aliasing does not work for the most part, which is a shame.
When it comes to music, Spec Ops did something different than hiring an orchestra. Instead, the developers rigged all of Dubai with massive speakers that play classic rock songs during gunfights that creates an oddly disturbing feeling throughout the whole thing. Other than that, it's mostly low base chords, but it still sounds great.
Plot: 9.5/10 - Spec Ops: The Line is a game about how gruelling war truly is and what it does to you. The game has great character development and pacing, along with some truly emotionally crushing moments. The endings are all fantastic, as they all lead up to a more subtly devesating conclusion.
While all this is great, what may turn people off is the length of the single-player campaign. I beat it in about four and a half hours on normal difficulty. It would seem the average range for game completion for people is 4-7 hours. While these are not good statistics, I fell like the game ended itself when it needed to, and didn't just keep adding filler content.
Overall: 8.5/10 - Great.
Spec Ops: The Line doesn't innovate on gameplay, but it makes up for it with an outstanding story and beautiful world.

For any fan of simulators, driving games, or both, Euro Truck Simulator 2 is everything you want. It has all the breadth a good simulator should have: Realistic controls in the trucks, banking and loans to build your business, buying and managing trucks with employed drivers. But at the same time, everything is simple and user friendly in a way that allows you to enjoy the game and not get bogged down feeling like you are working more than you are playing. At the end of the day, you're trucking along open roads, winding through beautifully rendered European roadways making money to build your business. After putting a bit of time into game, you hire more and more drivers and soon find you have enough income to really build your business and feel like you've accomplished something!
Aside from the fun of the game, especially for people who like driving games, there is something very theraputic about it. Once you get used to it, you find you can almost meditate, losing yourself in thought as you drive peacefully on your route. You can play your own custom MP3's and radio stations, either listening to some good music while you drive or listening to podcasts. I like to listen to news while I drive, which is actually kind of productive.
The core game is praseworthy enough, but I also want to point out that the developers are incredibly dedicated to the fanbase, constantly making updates to improve the game. For example: I was always happy with the look of the game, but a few months ago the atmospheric day/night sky was updated, making late evening and early morning skies more breathtaking than you ever thought the damn sky in a trucking game could be.
Altogether, I WHOLEHEARTEDLY recommend this game. If it sounds like something you'd be interested in, it's worth every penny. If you don't think it sounds very appealing, I think it's at least worth a try when it's on sale. You might be surprised how fun, relaxing and enjoyable virtual trucking can be!

I have had my eye on Mad Max for a while now but was hesitant to buy it due to being let down on many occasions with big budget games. I managed to get a good deal on the game and started it up with mediocre expectations. It surpassed those.
It is a great game to play, even if for a short period of time. You know that itch you get to play GTA or Saints Row for half and hour just to drive around, explore and kill random folk? Well, I got it with this too.
The combat system is akin to the modern Batman games and Assassins Creed. You can attack by pressing the X button, hold it for longer to do a strong attack and you can counter enemies with a well times press of the Y button. As you progress through the game you are able to learn abilities to instantly kill some enemies. I found it fun hitting some combos on a dude, turning to another and blowing him away with a shotgun and then countering someone else to then German suplex him. It's feels like it has some good weight behind it.
Being a Mad Max game, the driving had to be great... and they succeeded! It's so much fun to drive around the world exploring and seeing how your car upgrades affect your vehicle and play style. The vehicular combat leaves a lot to be desired though as the camera never seems to want to play nice, the lock-on system can be temperamental and can also just downright not work on occasion. It leaves a bit of frustration but is easily glossed over.
Overall I would recommend it, even at full price. I got 38 hours from it and I may even play more as similar to games like Fallout, it let's you carry on playing after you beat the story. It's a gorgeous, fun to play game with a few frustrations here and there but we;; worth your time and money.

After 30 hours I feel like I've done nearly everything in the game.
I've played through the story (which is very well done in the end, you get the "Mad Max"-series end but you can continue with your own story), I've taken down all the camps, I've upgraded all the Strongholds, I've finished all the side missions.
For $10 I have to recommend this game for anyone who loves getting lost in a Single Player game (with great driving, an awesome world and interesting characters) that's just fun to play.
Tips for new players to the game:
* Figure out all the keyboard shortcuts; X on foot (in a camp!) and C while driving are two important ones.
* I'd recommend doing the blue missions (side missions) before continuing with the main story line (green missions)
* Don't forget to go see Griffa every once in a while

Good:
+Open desert world
+Mad Max inspired all the way
+Optimized like ♥♥♥♥ yeah
Bad:
-Deja vu
-Late game car combat difficulty
-Missions
-Missions: I have never cared so little about the story for a game I've spent over 20 hours playing. It really only seems to exist as an excuse to move you from zone to zone. Several missions, including one that forces you to do every activity in a zone, serve only to impede your ability to aquire upgrades. Too many missions or activities require you to slow your momentum or return to an early zone and thereby suffer outright boredom if you want to complete this game.
-Late game car combat difficulty: I like the vehicle handling. It reminds me of the Mad Max muscle cars and the indie movie Bellflower (inspired somewhat by Mad Max). What I don't like is the way that car armor is used late game to remove the most enjoyable part of the car combat (the grapple gun) and the way the AI can outperform you or get random speedboosts in cars without nitro. It's something that can be learned to deal with, but it's just not fun.
-Dejay vu: The huge game world is split up into zones that feature the same tasks in every zone. The developers did a great job adding random touches of personality here and there. However, it's far too easy to experience moments of "didn't I just do this?"
+Optimized like ♥♥♥♥ yeah: Even on my old GTX 750 this game runs surprisingly well. There are occasional stutters at Low with resolution 1920x1080 but that's about it.
+Mad Max inspired all the way: Mad Max as a character isn't very interesting. However, this game is arguably more about exploring his world then exploring him, and from that perspective the game does really well. The cars, the combat, the guns, even the stupid hot-air balloons feel like they belong (the hot-air balloons are stretching it a bit, though).
+Open desert world: I am a huge fan of post-apocalypse wastelands, and the open world for this game is on par with Fallout and STALKER. Actually, between Fallout 3 and Mad Max, I'd say Mad Max wins both in terms of world building and personality. My hours were spent driving everywhere and trying to see everything, because there is always something new when you least expect it.

Trackmania is the most fun I've ever had playing a game in a LAN environment. It is multiplayer time trials. Everybody is racing at the same time, for the best time. Canyon also includes nicer-looking cars which show damage when you hit things. Valley, which I have not yet played, features more off-road driving. All games have the capabilities to create your own tracks or download pre-made tracks from the Internet.
I recommend starting with Trackmania 2: Stadium as it is the cheapest and most popular environment. Trackmania Nations Forever is free on Steam if you want to try out the original.

This is my first looks review of Windward after 5 hours of playtime (in one day i might add), which already gives the game a good merit as it's hooked me into it already. TL:DR at the bottom.
Windward is a sea trading/combat/questing game which sets you the task of completing quests and exploring sea sectors whilst battling off pirates who want to take over the towns in the said sectors. It provides a nice ranking system with different factions and paths to take when upgrading your ship. The combat can get very intense and the travelling gives you a tranquil break from blowing up Captain Blackbeard and his pirate cronies.
The art style is simplistic yet very appealing, with great water effects which give you nice waves and added gems like schools of fish and great cloud effects (which is good as whats the point of nice graphics in a sailing game if you neglect the water effects).
The combat is also simplistic yet very enjoyably and engaging. Your cannons are set to autofire whenever you get into range and angle of a pirate ship and gives you control over using your special combat abilities.
The questing aspect of the game mainly involves either sailing across the map to deliver cargo or passengers (which is somehow very serene and calming) or taking out pirates and capturing their towns.
Windward is a very engaging and fun game, which can also provide relaxing scenarios as well as intense combat. The art style is very appealing and is never a strain on the eyes. However, the game can seem repetitive for some people. I can imagine a lot of players hitting a wall in which they just lose interest in the game at some point. However, until you get to that point the game is very nice to play and gives the player a rewarding and comfortable feeling whilst playing. At a small price (less than £10 when I brought it) Windward is well worth your money no matter what types of games you enjoy.
Sail across the map, stop in town, get quest.
Sail to other town to complete quest.
Oooh, pirates! *engage in intense combat and feel rewarded to see ships blow up and sink*.
Hire two faction ships which are highly more advanced than yours and take over pirate town.
Complete another quest from another town.
Repeat.
5 hours later, Jeeez, is that the time?! Wow.
10/10 would waste an evening sailing again. Great game.

Foremost I would say that Windward is a relaxing and fun game. There is no great penalty on dying and you can easily ramp up the difficulty to push yourself without losing out. You can happily sit in a friendly region and use a very simple quest and trading system to get some gold and just while away a few hours; or what I consider to be the more fun part is to set out capturing new regions.
Combat turns out to be both complex and very simple. Point the side of your ship towards the enemy and your ship automatically shoots at them, but the tricky part is then not having them shoot back at the same time or fighting / running away from multiple enemy ships.
Windward is essentially very simple and can be repetitive, yet it is beautiful, engaging and well worth buying.

This game sucks, but the story does not. It's full of glitches and bugs that destroy some of the enjoyment, for example I have died countless times on FUBAR difficulty level (which is equivalent to very hard in other games), for no reason at all because the character won’t move up or down the stairs or some magical-non-exciting-invisible-wall stops a perfect headshot, or there is a sticky corner so your character stops while you try to maneuver your way to safety. There are also few poor level design decisions made so it depends on luck and not skill do you make it or not during some cut-scene-boss-fight-circle-jerk-parade or not. However even if the controls do suck and are unresponsive, playability is zero from time to time and enemies can take 3 to 8 headshots sometimes before they die. There are however some very good and solid things done right in this game. For example if you play the game with normal or low difficulty level, you will not die so easily because you can take more damage and it gives you more time to get somewhere you need to go and that’s the reason you don’t notice the glitches so easily. Then you can actually enjoy from good storytelling and few jokes on the way that made me laugh. The atmosphere is really good and the sand dunes feel real and graphics really do bring the place alive (unless there is a glitch). You can sometimes feel like you were really a part of that world, which is very rare and welcome thing in today’s games.
In all honesty I really tried to like this game and enjoy it more, but I just can’t believe that this game is so bad (FUBAR) when you decide to play it on harder difficulty level like FUBAR, it will get you really mad because the dumb luck factor in many levels that have nothing to do with how good or poorly you are doing at that time.
Also keep in mind that the game feels like a console port, there are controller issues, drawing distance issues, texture bugs appear if you look far away enemy with sniper scope, invisible walls, character won’t respond and once during one level I found a soldier that wouldn’t die even when he was missing one arm and a leg and was holding invisible gun in his hand. White phosphorus, hand grenades, sticky grenades, machine gun and 9mm pistol emptied in the head from short distance did nothing to him… Well I guess he’s the Superman’s lost cousin or something. The glitch list goes on and on, but the absolutely worst thing is the broken checkpoint system. Be ready to rage after you die and spawn to checkpoint and then realize that the primary gun you held has changed to something completely different and then you also find out that the ammo boxes near you might be empty, so no extra ammo for that random weapon that you have now. Also keep in mind that if you kill horde of soldiers the bodies do not disappear, the guns and ammo do. So collect them fast if you want to have some bullets to use on next assault.
If you want to play a good game, do not buy this. But if you do want to enjoy from very good storytelling, do buy this. I think the story would have worked better as a movie or a book rather than a game but that’s just my opinion of the matter. However I can’t deny the fact that the story element in this game is done so well that I have to give the game 7 out of 10 because the story here saves so much more than the gameplay manages to destroy. To keep things in perspective, a casual player might even enjoy the gameplay because he won’t be able to notice the same problems that I noticed while unlocking every possible achievement on Steam version of this game. In the end I managed to spend over 32 hours on single player mode so I’m pretty sure I noticed many things that others would have missed by playing the game only once on normal difficulty setting.  In future the developers might want to test more of the gameplay on higher difficulty levels before releasing the game, because some of us do like a really challenging game that does function accordingly. If the gameplay was better and these glitches had been polished out I would have given 10 out of 10 easily, but in this state 7 out of 10 is the most I can give and I’m being lenient over here.

Dontnod's Life Is Strange was one of the most surprisingly good video games I've played in recent years. This prequel is made by a different company, but it stays truthful to the original game and delivers a great back story.
PROS
+ Character development is strong again, especially with protagonist Chloe, who starts out as an angry, self-centred teenager but matures more over the course of the story. Most other original characters are fleshed out more, and newer ones are generally well-developed also.
+ Rachel - Chloe's new best friend - is a fantastic deuteragonist with excellent voice-acting, though she is criminally underused in Ep. 3.
+ Character animations and lip-synching are vastly improved, in comparison to the original game. Visually, the game is stunning.
+ The narrative is generally strong and rather more focussed compared to the first game.
+ We have yet another beautiful soundtrack to listen to. Daughter recorded most of the music and retain some of the indie-folk vibe from the original game, but bands such as Wolf Alice also provide more Chloe-appropriate rock.
+ All three main episodes are of a decent length. Each episode should take around 2-and-a-half hours if you really want to explore the game thoroughly.
+ Much like with the first game, there are plenty of hard-hitting (and sometimes even unsettling) moments covering difficult subjects.
+ Decisions (both minor and major) seem to have more of an impact on how the story develops. Again, there is one story-defining choice to make at the end. Both endings seem perfectly logical to me, and choosing which one to go for will definitely be the hardest decision you make in this franchise.
CONS
- Though Deck Nine certainly did their best to stay faithful to Dontnod's original story, there were still a lot of anachronisms and inconsistencies that slipped through the net.
- Speaking of inconsistencies, Chloe writes graffiti with either her right hand or her left hand, with no obvious preference. However, when another character reveals to her that they are ambidextrous, Chloe does not disclose her two-handedness. Maybe I'm being a bit picky there...
- The 'Backtalk' conversation options designed to help Chloe get her own way provided a promising mechanic, but in truth, it's probably harder to screw things up than 'win'. If made harder and more prevalent, I would have been more satisfied.
- I felt my decisions regarding Chloe and stepdad David made little difference, and that their 'tempestuous' relationship seemed rather flat.
- Three chapters is not a lot for an episodic video game. Yes, we will get a special episode featuring young Max in 2018, but this game is all too brief in comparison to Life Is Strange.
- Further to that, a lot of questions are left unanswered. I know Deck Nine don't want to fill in all the blanks for us, but as this is supposed to be our last venture into Arcadia Bay, I would have liked more closure.
In summary, Before The Storm retains the flawed charm of the original Life Is Strange, and is arguably a better game in many aspects. Would I recommend it? "HELLA YES!"

The game has the same problems most prequels do - how much choice and character development can you really have when the main characters and the world around them are dead set for a fixed destination?
And the answer is: not a lot.
Don't expect Before the Storm to blow your mind or make you cry the way Life is Strange did.
Why do I still recommend this game?
Have you ever thought about a story or franchise that you really loved 'hey I wonder what an average day is like in this universe?" Before the Storm is kind of like that. If you temper your expectations and just want a nice ride in this world without questioning what you should do with your life once you finished the game, then Before the Storm will give you just that. Plus it will put you in the mood to replay LiS for the fifth time.
This game invites you to fight your instincts - at least it did that for me.
We know how messed up Chloe is in Life is Strange.
Before the Storm goes into great length to show you how many opportunities she had to straighten up, how she absolutely had a chance to get her life in order if she took the opportunities that were presented to her.
You can experience this in two ways.
The first is to try to take those opportunities in an ultimately pointless attempt to fix her life. This way you can shake your head at the tragedy that is unfolding before your eyes and you can truly feel how stuck she is in her current situation. This will give you a feeling of powerlessness and hopelessness.  You will feel the frustration, sadness and the desperation that comes with knowing what the right thing to do would be, and still ending up in the wrong place, because no matter how hard you try, Chloe is stuck in a self-sabotaging mindset. If you want to be very meta about it, and not blame it on prequel limitations, you can say that it's some sort of depression simulator where you are the quiet little voice in Chloe's mind that knows what would be right thing to do, but every time you say something, you ultimately get silenced. I'm sure all of us have experienced that to some degree, so perhaps in the best case scenario, Before the Storm can open your eyes about the dangers of being stuck in a certain state of mind, and the importance to think things through and to seriously consider the advice people give you.
But, understandably, this might frustrate and disappoint a lot of players, so there is a second option.
You can do the 'wrong' thing willingly. You can flip people off, you can act stupid and you can make bad choices not because you want to exhaust all the options provided to you in order to get the full gameplay experience, but because that's what Chloe is like, and all you can do is enjoy her descent into nihilism.
Forget about the consequences and just enjoy the fun and freedom of not giving a crap and rebelling against everyone and everything for the sake of rebellion and nihilism.
If you read all of that then kudos, you deserve a steam achievement.
TL;DR
It's a tame ride, but you'll enjoy it if you liked LiS.
Ooooh and that very last scene at the end of Episode 3?
It might be a cheap shot, but it gave me goosebumps and brought back all the memories.

I used to play the Deer Hunter games years ago, so I figured that I would give this a try. My pc setup is an AMD Ryzen R7 1700 @3.80ghz, 16GB DDR4 at 2933mhz and a 1080ti. The graphics are amazing and the game does seem to be well optomized, I had one blue screen but I think it was not game releated. The maps are huge and lush with amazing weather affects. The wind knocks leaves from trees, this game has lots of small details, even the grass bends from the rabbits running by. There are many different animals to hunt in the USA and Germany, I have not tried the newest map. I would like a bigger selection of firearms, not that I do not like the guns that they have, I would just like a few more. With all of this being said, my only gripes with this game are that you have to buy things like an ATV and extra tents/blinds, yes I get it, the game is only $30, but I would buy new hunting areas all day, but not things like tents and an ATV. The game also seems to be lacking structure, and by this I mean it does just drop you in the woods, and you can just kill and kill and kill. I would like the addition of tags for animals and such, or a limit, that really takes away from the game just being able to kill an unlimited number of animals, theres been times that I have shot a bear, then walked over the hill...shot a deer, walked around the lake, shot 2 more deer....you get the Idea. But I suppose this appeals to the new generation that need that instant gratification...otherwise they might get bored. Overall I do like the game and the price is decent. I think it needs some polish but a job well done. I give it 7/10.

This game is a hardcore RPG Platformer that is tough as nails. I would say that about 70% of the challenge is fair, but there is a 30% of pure unfair torture. And what I mean by that is that the basis of the game is that each attempt is different and randomly generated, and that is mostly a good thing. But it IS possible to get a string of incredibly tough rooms or horribly handicapped children thrown at you very early on, when you don't have access to the better character upgrades that come later on. But this is less of a problem when you finally get enough money to spend on better gear/upgrades about an hour - 2 hours into the game. It might take a bit of grinding to get up to speed, but once you do build up your legacy a bit, this game is an addictive thrill that's hard to put down.
It's also a great party game to play with your friends, if you pass the controller after each death.

Although this game is great, There are still some annoying bugs. So be fair warned. Some projectiles tend to glitch through walls that aren't supposed too. Aswell as attacks not hitting.
But with those aside. The game is great. Probably my best purchase on steam yet. Ill continue to play untill I beat the game.

This is a great prequel of the original Life is Strange (LiS) but plot-wise and gameplay-wise, the original was way better. To put it simply, the story of LiS got me really hooked and the plot twists are awesome plus I really like the dark theme in it which is what LiS: Before the Storm lacks.
However, the strong points of this prequel are the following:
1) More Realistic: Since there is no more rewind or time-travelling stuff (which is also a strong point of the original game), this game felt more realistic. Making choices were really harder since you know that you cannot go back in time to change those. And since it is modeled this way, you get to be in character yourself. I really liked acting rebellious like Chloe.
2) Character Development: Having played the original version, I got to understand more some of the characters through this game like Frank, Nathan, David, and Chloe. So it is a great additive to the story that you already know if you have played the original. It was also nice to get to know Rachel who is somewhat another "mysterious" character from LiS because she was always mentioned there but we don't know anything about her.
3) Soundtrack: Just like LiS, the soundtracks of this game is awesome!
4) AMBERPRICE: SUPER GAY. SUPER NICE. NUFF SAID. Lol Seriously tho, their chemistry is awesome.
I still have a lot of questions about Rachel tho which were still not addressed in this game. I am wondering if they will still add new series of this game and I am wondering what will the story be but let's see. Really hoping to play more games like this!

This game is a hidden gem. For $30 you get an authentic hunting game, but let me remind you of some things and give you some tips.
-The ATV is a must if you get bored with just walking around(because running around like madman will spook the animals). The $4 tag for this DLC is a bit of a low blow, but I got this game for like 17 bucks with all the DLCs so I just bit the bullet that time.
-DO NOT just rely on scopes. Some scopes have weird zooms and if you use it around near point blank range, you will hit a bad spot. Press your mouse wheel to remove the scope and use the iron sight. It is definitely much more accurate than the scope. I also read on some forums that the scope bug is still around, but slightly fixed.
-As much as other people complain about the starting rifle, IMHO it is not really that bad. They say it's as weak as a BB gun lol, but it's not. These people might have been hunting an elk or a moose, which is definitely bad for using the starter .243 rifle unless you get a perfect heart shot. Ive been using the starter rifle for a while and I have downed most white tails, black tails, and coyotes in one shot. Sometimes with vital shots. The rifle is kinda underpowered, but it is absolutely accurate even at 300m(provided with the wind in your favor. Blowing against you).
-I would never shoot in the head part of the animal ever again even in point blank range. I dont know if this is a bug or not but any living thing taking a point blank bullet from any rifle should die in an instant. Ive read on the forums one guy said that the skull deflects the bullet so it is a bad spot. Now I just usually aim for the spine, which is much more exposed. Or neck shots, easier to hit even with soft point bullets, but less space to hit.
-Choose the ambush skill tree instead of the stalker tree. There is a bug that where you follow the tracks of the animal, either the animal itself or the tracks just disappear. I once followed a black tail for like 30 minutes and I was crouched and slowly moving. Using the caller and camping near trees and shadow is much more efficient and faster. But camping might not be for your tastes if you dont have the patience.

As a original Trackmania Nations patron, I bid welcome to the newest one! Trackmania 2 Stadium has brought back what we all loved! From the crazy tracks, physics and the competition; this racing game is very fun and exciting.
Pros:
+ Crazy track designs and fun physics. (More 3-dimensional than most racing games.)
+ Ranges from highly competitive to very casual. (Pick your poison.)
+ Custom tracks with the track editor. (Essentially a map editor, but with modular track "blocks".)
+ International sport. (Everywhere in the world competes.)
+ Countless tracks to race on.
+ Simple controls brings everyone into the racing.
+ Customizable music playlists.
+ Car painter (Click and drag mouse spraying on 3D object, WOW!)
Cons:
- None. Trackmania has been a favorite of mine for years, so it's only fair that I am biased.
Even if you aren't a big racing game fan, give this a shot. It has a lot of excitement and thrill to offer vs. other conventional racing games. As stated, the tracks are mostly more vertical, featuring jumps, loops, suprises, stunts, boosters, etc.

My biggest issue is the feeling that you need to grind through the game in order to get anywhere. I don't have the feeling that anything is possible on any run, instead I feel that I will only be successful after hours and hours of commitment.
I'm also not a huge fan of the unpredictable combat: because each character you play has different stats, you don't know if an enemy will take 1 or 2 hits to kill.
Spelunky on the other hand offers up the entire game everytime you play, and instead allows you to progress by learning the predictable behaviours of all the enemies you face.

Mad Max is an open world game with plenty of distractions. If you don't mind going around the map and constantly clearing side objectives then you will find plenty of enjoyment here, as that is what you will be doing most of the time. The primary missions and a few side missions are fun and well made, however there are not nearly as many of them as I'd like.
There just isn't enough story here, there are lots of collectibles which give you some sort of a background, but to me that wasn't enough. I would've liked to see Max interact with more people and for longer periods of time, not just to take a mission.
As someone who likes to clear the map of objectives I got caught up in Mad Max, but there is a point where most people will get fed up with doing this. There's just too much of doing the same thing over and over.
That being said, the core gameplay is fun. Driving your main car - the Magnum Opus - is fun, because you have access to one of the best weapons in a video game ever, the harpoon. It's just so satisfying to dismantle your enemies cars and bases. It would have been nice if its use was expanded even more. And the ground combat is also quite fun, it's a slightly watered down version of the Arkham battle system and it does its job.
I hope they make a sequel as Max is an interesting character, and I think they have a good core of a game. It just needs more variety.

Spec Ops is an interesting game. It's a Third-Person Shooter with a story that is designed to make you think about your decisions. My problem with the game is that the major decisions are out of your control. You have no say what-so-ever in the outcomes of them. The few decisions that you are given are minor and ultimately have no effect on which of the 4 endings of the game you will receive. The endings are based on which of the 4 options you choose at the very end of the game. I have a hard time feeling bad for a decision that the game chose. The "obvious" answer to some who say you do have a choice is to just not play the game. That is a poor answer to me. You would not experience the rest of the story or the game unless you watched it on YouTube, or had someone tell you what happens.
The actual combat in the game is typical TPS or FPS run-and-gun. I would recommend playing on Easy if you do decide to play the game. You do not lose or gain anything other than achievements by picking this option. I would play the game for the story and not the gameplay.
All in all, it is an interesting game, but I would never say that I had fun playing it. Get it if you are just absolutely interesting in playing. I would recommend waiting for it to be on sale for $5 or around that area, for the 5-6.5 hours that it lasts.

An action filled and incredibly addictive game, I loved playing Mad Max from start to finish. Let me try to break my experience into some aspects:
Pros:
-Combat is great. The combo/fury system makes fighting a large number of enemies more exciting, especially when facing different kinds of foes (by the way, the combat in Mad Max reminds me A LOT the combat in the Arkham series games)
-I really enjoyed how the game gets you to survey a certain area for keypoints. Unlike in other games, in Mad Max just standing on a lookout point won't award you with the location for every stuff in the map, you have to look for those things!
-Even though the game is set on a wasteland there is a large number of modifications you can apply to both the character and the car.
-The game reflects the atmosphere of one of the best movies in the Mad Max series (Mad Max 2: The Road Warrior). Throughout the game you will be aided by a companion (Hunchback) and you may even by accompanied by a dog that helps you track landmines.
-I really love side missions, therefore, I had a real good time trying every kind of possible activities available in the map.
Cons:
-Car physics are not accurate at all. At times you might just ride off a hill, the car will land on its hood and just spin back on its wheels...
-Enemies' AI are not very challenging. Although it feels good to beat hordes of foes dead, in the long run I wish they would give me a little harder time defeating them.
-The plot is not very catchy. To put it in few words, it is just plain predictable.
Overall, I give this game a 8/10. Would and will play again and recommend it to anyone who is looking for a great experience with action games!

This game is one of a great game that I will strongly recommend - but not to everyone. Indeed, it is both very similar to the basic TPS and very different from the other "common" games.
For a start, the game mechanics don't really stand out from other shooters. The cover system is quite classic, the various weapons are nothing but well-made, enemies will most likely be coming by everywhere while shooting and yelling, the different AIs are correct, although your teammates will most of the time die while running, and there are shining red barrels that will explode when shot, as well as turrets and miniguns. Multiplayer is not worth the single player, and coop consists of alternative 2-players missions. Still, there are quite some original things, such as the contextual sand that will often allow you to get rid of a bunch of angry people or some eye-candies like the trees, walls or towers that fall when shot at.
That brings us to the fact that the game also looks like a movie. Indeed, it's very linear, as the main storyline can be summed up with a map. But it's also pretty scripted, and every single detail seems to have been done with care : the crashing helos, the falling towers, the blowing glass roofs, the collapsing quicksands... and even though sometimes, the action is spoiled by the too obvious script, it still succeeds in stressing the player, who'll eventually have to choose between four pretty different endings.
But the biggest part of the game revolves around the story. It may be a little hard to get why you get shot at so much in the beginning, but except a few odd things, the struggle between morality and immorality, allies and enemies, life and death is surprisingly thorough for a videogame. Indeed, there is nothing silly, as it's not a simple confrontation between good and evil, but rather a showdown of cruelty, selfishness, and deceived ideals meant to ensure the survival of a few people - or to wipe out guilt -, even if it leads to the death of dozens of - more or less - innocent people. There is no one truly good, not even civilians, and no one truly evil, not even soldiers, and there is thus no right choice to do : whatever you do, people will die, and you only can determine who - to some extent. Indeed, you'll end up doing things totally against common sense, only because it's the only way to face the others, who are already doing crazy things : it's a shocking experience that to burn people with white phosphorus and watch them burn while speaking to a dying burnt man. The dialogues are, by the way, pretty interesting, and the characters' psychologies are really profound, as both of your two teammates will have a different position on what happened, what you've done and what to do next. The interesting part is that it's hard to tell who to follow, as no one seems to be wrong, and in the end, you'll be the main problem down there - but you won't realize it before the last few minutes.
In the end, the story can be summed up as a descent into hell of a mad soldier caught in the spiral of violence and guilt, and the whole game leads the player through sceneries of despair and desolation, all along a depressing story tainted with blood. But if that game is a masterpiece, it's also thanks to the fact that the story is complex and
hard to get, as the main character is sliding into madness - which is also hard to get to which degree until the very last moments. Thus, this game isn't suitable for everyone, as it requires to be able to use their brain while playing, so as to make choices as well as to try to understand the story so far: you simply can't play just to shoot. That game is a proof that videogame is art.
P.S. : Somehow, the game made me remember of Prayer of the Refugee, by Rise Against. Just check the lyrics :p

LIS: Before The Storm is fan service at its finest! If you enjoyed Life Is Strange, you will enjoy this game. This prequel explores the friendship of Chloe and Rachel Amber. While not quite as long or mindblowing as its predecessor, it actually adds to the original game by fleshing out the backstory of the events that lead up to the first game. As Chloe, witness the blossoming of your friendship with Rachel as the two of you unravel each other's struggles, confide in each other, and then take matters into your own hands. Fall in love with Rachel's Antics as she points out yours. Get into trouble, get out of trouble, and back in again.
As a player, you make choices that constantly toe the line between emotional outpours and holding back - breaking hearts in the process - including, potentially, your own.

While the episode doesn't open particularly well, it does a decent enough job of introducing you to everyone and getting the story rolling, this introduction allows for you to meet Rachael Amber who will play a pivotal role throughout the story and provide a reason as to why she was of so much concern to Chloe in the original life is strange.
There is a scene with Rachael and Chloe on a train which gives some good insight into her character and is the main start of the relationship between Chloe and herself. It has nice visuals and an enjoyable conversation between the two. Some good character development and dialogue choices are also stand out and this scene did enough on its own to warrant my score going higher by a full +1.
There is a lot of foreshadowing for the end of episode 1 which I noticed and thought it was done reasonably well and once again the story writers doing 100x better than the dialogue writers. I think the main reason I even gave either of these games a play-though and the sole reason I enjoy Life is Strange is the story, while it's not the best it has some enjoyable moments but looking back on it, it's nowhere near as good as I once thought. Its probably like a 5/6 out of 10.
Touching upon the writers yet again... the writing for what the characters say is still """""""Hella""""""" bad. "oh I'm so edgy" "damn stepdad always your fault" its like Chloe is so predictable, you click on a fire extinguisher and she says "I wish this had oil in it for when his car gets set on fire". It's monotonous and boring to hear it every 2 seconds. I'm not against dark and brooding characters but when it's this incessant it drives you insane.
Most other characters writing is shoddy too but hers is by far the worst. I think Rachael is the best-written character in this episode (and even her's isn't very good) and let's hope they take feedback like this into episode 2 and give Chloe at least a bit of nuance.
The voice acting isn't great either, it's serviceable and maybe that's not the actor's fault when the dialogue is so poorly written but one definitely stands out and that is Samantha. Her voice is so grating and unbearable I actually took a point off the score even though she is in the episode for a solid 5 minutes max.
Ep1 Overall: This episode has some decent story moments and even some character based ones like having the option to play a game on a bench at School which ya know actually lets us know that the character we are playing as can have some fun outside of being an edge-lord. It has kept my interest for the 2nd episode but it has so many flaws I cannot give this more than an average 4/10
I think episode 2 suffers from nearly all the same issues as the first, in fact, they are incredibly similar which I guess is to be expected but with that said there are some better parts than episode 1 too
I really felt like the voice acting got worse in this episode, Nearly every character bar a few seemed off, it was like the director didn't give them any kind of... well... Direction. It took me out of the game a lot of times and I get that the voice actors strike was affecting them so its not entirely their fault but it really wasn't something I could overlook.
I also like that not every choice of the dialogue isn't just edgy garbage, Chloe can actually speak like a real human who has different responses to different things. It's not every time but at least its there and is definitely an improvement from the last episode.
Ep2 Overall:
The story doesn't really go anywhere too unexpected but the scenes it does focus on and the choices you have to make are certainly an improvement on the 1st episode. Its just a shame a lot of good shot and lit emotional scenes are ruined once again by shoddy writing and unimpactful acting but I did appreciate the fact that Chloe isn't just "hella lit dab ♥♥♥♥♥" all the time in this episode, it gives at least some depth to her character and her relationship with Racheal is pretty well done. But this episode in general still doesn't warrant a recommendation to buy this game but if they tweak a few of the substandard parts episode 3 could just about push it above a 7 but for now, episode 2 is a 5.5
While still not the best (or even very good) thing to ever exist in any shape or form; Life Is Strange: before the storm episode 3 is probably the best from the series so far, that includes the first game as well, and I know this isn't saying much as I don't rate any of the episodes too high but it shows that they might actually be learning something.
This episode starts strong right off the bat with a pretty decent opening. It has some nice visuals and what is being discussed carries some actual weight for once. This is generally continued throughout the whole episode with much better dialogue and story steaks but I'll talk about those in a bit.
I still have a lot of gripes with some of the stupid things the characters do, however, whether this is gameplay (something along the lines of talking about "if there was only a way to screw this in" while carrying a wrench). It may be nothing to do with the gameplay and the characters just act irrationally for no good reason, although I can only recall one time where this really got to me it; It made me think out loud saying "why the ♥♥♥♥ would you do that" or something along those lines.
There is some good stuff with the characters but once again where there could have been a great scene something just had to ruin it and this time around it was some awful voice acting.
I do appreciate that the dialogue was once again improved upon and wasn't all just edgy stupid stuff, it made Chole feel like a real person for once instead of a self-insert cutout for the tumblr lords.
In previous episodes in the scenes with David, every option was some "I h8 u, bro. hope u die!" cringe like that, but now there is actually some sympathy for him. I don't know why it took this long to incorporate but at least it actually exists now.
My main issue with this episode is that, for a "choice" based game, THERE IS ONLY 1 MEANINGFUL CHOICE IN THE ENTIRE EPISODE! (and you could even say in the whole game but I wouldn't go that far) which makes everything feel just a little bit pointless however the smaller choices seem to have a bigger impact than the last game which is good I suppose but when it just concludes based on a binary 0-1 choice once again does it really matter?
Ep3 Overall:
This is probably the best Life is strange episode so far in terms of everything it gets right vs everything it doesn't, but It still isn't anything special and there are a lot of things that still get under my skin and grate on me something fierce. However, credit where its due to Deck Nine for at least putting in the effort to try and create something that isn't even formed from their own property and I hope that Dotnod takes notes from their improvement in writing/ dialogue over the 3 episodes and applies it to LIS2.

Everything from animal spawns, animal teleportation, dropped animals dissapearing, non harvestable animals, ammo issues, sights and scopes not working properly on weapons, weapons bugging out. Windward is a good game if you appreciate heavy grinds for gear and levels, intense combat, co-op and pvp. If you're not a big fan of grinding, then you might want to pass this one up. If you're looking for a game like Sid Meier's Prates!, then  be warned that while this game does have a present trade element, most of the game revolves around ship combat. Combat, trading, and exploring is about all there is to this game, which for the price is to be expected.
The combat can be a bit repetitive early on, but with a healthy dose of RPG elements, players can use talent trees and skills to spice things up. Getting a new ship is thrilling as you adapt your strategy to maximize your survivability and damage. Right now there are only ten ships, and I hope they add more.
PVP ensues as players vie for control over the procedurally-generated map with one of five factions. On a good server the give-and-take is solid, with factions rising and falling in power, gaining and losing territory. Sometimes apathy or indifference on the part of players means one motivated faction can grab a lot of land. Sometimes a rogue, high-level player griefs a low-level area out of spite, but such activity is to be expected in any multiplayer game. The community is polite and cooperative in general.
If this sounds like fun to you, and you don't mind a bit of repetition, then this is a good game for you. If you're looking for something with a little more depth, move on. But I've played over thirty hours and have no intention of stopping now.

Trackmania is known as being one of the most competitve racing games out there, and for good reason. Stadium, like any TM game, has a huge learning curve. While you can definitely hop in and have fun from the start, you won't find yourself competing at the highest level without intense determination and dedication to the game. There are lot's of little details in the game that separates the great from the good. This learning curve might drive some people away from the game, but it is incredibly rewarding when you hop into a server against some of the best drivers as you trade times back and forth, one-upping the other by only a few thousanths of a second.
There is near infinite replay value here. The game features a massive track editor where the only real limitation is your imagination. Even if you're not into creating maps yourself, there is already an incredible selection made by other players. There are different types of tracks, such as mini, tech, circuit (Nascar), dirt, and speed. Each of them requires their own special skill set to master, and each will challenge your abilities.
I would highly recommend this game, but I must give you fair warning of the steep learning curve associated with a TM title. At first, you will find yourself at the back of the pack wondering how the other guys are putting up the times they are. If you stay with it and make efforts to improve though, the game is incredibly rewarding. The single player maps do not do a good job of preparing you for how competitive the multiplayer is, but they will at least give you a way to improve. The game encourages you to try again and shave another half a second off your time. Websites such as maniaexchange allow you to download user created maps that you can play offline. If you're looking to take this game seriously, I would highly recommend doing so. Practice makes perfect may be cliche, but it was never more true.
This is an excellent title, one that you will spend endless hours on, but only if you can get past the steep learning curve.

Spec Ops is an interesting game. It's a Third-Person Shooter with a story that is designed to make you think about your decisions. My problem with the game is that the major decisions are out of your control. You have no say what-so-ever in the outcomes of them. The few decisions that you are given are minor and ultimately have no effect on which of the 4 endings of the game you will receive. The endings are based on which of the 4 options you choose at the very end of the game. I have a hard time feeling bad for a decision that the game chose. The "obvious" answer to some who say you do have a choice is to just not play the game. That is a poor answer to me. You would not experience the rest of the story or the game unless you watched it on YouTube, or had someone tell you what happens.
The actual combat in the game is typical TPS or FPS run-and-gun. I would recommend playing on Easy if you do decide to play the game. You do not lose or gain anything other than achievements by picking this option. I would play the game for the story and not the gameplay.
All in all, it is an interesting game, but I would never say that I had fun playing it. Get it if you are just absolutely interesting in playing. I would recommend waiting for it to be on sale for $5 or around that area, for the 5-6.5 hours that it lasts.

This game is one of a great game that I will strongly recommend - but not to everyone. Indeed, it is both very similar to the basic TPS and very different from the other "common" games.
For a start, the game mechanics don't really stand out from other shooters. The cover system is quite classic, the various weapons are nothing but well-made, enemies will most likely be coming by everywhere while shooting and yelling, the different AIs are correct, although your teammates will most of the time die while running, and there are shining red barrels that will explode when shot, as well as turrets and miniguns. Multiplayer is not worth the single player, and coop consists of alternative 2-players missions. Still, there are quite some original things, such as the contextual sand that will often allow you to get rid of a bunch of angry people or some eye-candies like the trees, walls or towers that fall when shot at.
That brings us to the fact that the game also looks like a movie. Indeed, it's very linear, as the main storyline can be summed up with a map. But it's also pretty scripted, and every single detail seems to have been done with care : the crashing helos, the falling towers, the blowing glass roofs, the collapsing quicksands... and even though sometimes, the action is spoiled by the too obvious script, it still succeeds in stressing the player, who'll eventually have to choose between four pretty different endings.
But the biggest part of the game revolves around the story. It may be a little hard to get why you get shot at so much in the beginning, but except a few odd things, the struggle between morality and immorality, allies and enemies, life and death is surprisingly thorough for a videogame. Indeed, there is nothing silly, as it's not a simple confrontation between good and evil, but rather a showdown of cruelty, selfishness, and deceived ideals meant to ensure the survival of a few people - or to wipe out guilt -, even if it leads to the death of dozens of - more or less - innocent people. There is no one truly good, not even civilians, and no one truly evil, not even soldiers, and there is thus no right choice to do : whatever you do, people will die, and you only can determine who - to some extent. Indeed, you'll end up doing things totally against common sense, only because it's the only way to face the others, who are already doing crazy things : it's a shocking experience that to burn people with white phosphorus and watch them burn while speaking to a dying burnt man. The dialogues are, by the way, pretty interesting, and the characters' psychologies are really profound, as both of your two teammates will have a different position on what happened, what you've done and what to do next. The interesting part is that it's hard to tell who to follow, as no one seems to be wrong, and in the end, you'll be the main problem down there - but you won't realize it before the last few minutes.
In the end, the story can be summed up as a descent into hell of a mad soldier caught in the spiral of violence and guilt, and the whole game leads the player through sceneries of despair and desolation, all along a depressing story tainted with blood. But if that game is a masterpiece, it's also thanks to the fact that the story is complex and
hard to get, as the main character is sliding into madness - which is also hard to get to which degree until the very last moments. Thus, this game isn't suitable for everyone, as it requires to be able to use their brain while playing, so as to make choices as well as to try to understand the story so far: you simply can't play just to shoot. That game is a proof that videogame is art.
P.S. : Somehow, the game made me remember of Prayer of the Refugee, by Rise Against. Just check the lyrics :p

I've flippantly referred to this game as Lesbian Teenage Rebellion Simulator 2k17, often. I mean that positively. This is a strange, wonderful, beautiful, heartbreaking game.
And it's unapologetically queer.
There's a few themes intertwined together. This is a game about the lies and fictions we tell to ourselves and others, big and small, about the ways we navigate and adapt to loss, and about coming into queerness in the midst of both. Unlike the original season of Life Is Strange, there's no cosmic magic, no superpowers, and there's a greater weight to everything for that.
It asks you to make Choices a few times, and there's rarely a clearly correct one to make. Only flawed people and consequences. Those consequences won't shake the world or save your city, but they're no less important than ones that do in other games. Humans don't have the power to reshape time, but we - all of us - have the power to utterly upend another person's life. We'll all make those choices more often than we might like to think about.
...seriously. Unrepentantly queer. This is a game that centers queer characters still not necessarily in check with their queerness, and loves them absolutely, and allows them to be flawed and fallible and human without destroying them for it. There's not much of that in games, or media in general. It's hard to express what that meant for me, personally, in words. I hope other people get the same catharsis from it. :)

Right, so...Windward. *Deep Breath* Where to start?
Ah, right. Let's get this review rolling by getting a few things out of the way from the git-go.
1) This game is billed as an adventure-sandbox title.
2) This game relies upon repetitive, simple tasks.
3) This game has some beautiful scenery and aesthetics.
Okay, with that out of the way, you're going to fall into one of two camps. Those camps are the 'I love this game!' and the 'I tried to like this game and I ended up wasting a handful of hours trying to like this game,' And that's fine. You have your tastes and your preferences. I'll be writing this review from the aspect of the latter camp, having tried to be a member of the former camp.
What Windward tries and (arguably) fails to present you with is an in-depth naval combat/economy simulation, top-down with nice graphical appeal. Where it fails is the 'in-depth' aspect with its 'bounce your ship back and forth between towns for hours' mentality, you may begin to ponder the value of your time. Unfortunately, because of this, it's not a game that I would say is fun if you want to just 'jump in for a few minutes' but instead is probably a far more playable game from the sphere of 'play a few hours at a time and save your game progress'.
Each and every faction tries to offer a special ability or focus that, after the first couple of hours, you don't even really think about anymore. And that is because each faction does the same things, with the same ships, but with one of four different color options. In the end, you may decide to restart simply because you want to play as your preferred color rather than for any 'faction specialty' reasons. In fact, one of my biggest problems with this game is that your sail embroidery is stuck as the color of your team. Frankly, that just pisses me off.
All this being said, I did play the game and I may continue to play it, and since I work a decent job the price tag isn't a deal-breaker either (especially on sale!).
But let me bring up another point, the game's aesthetics; they're pretty damn cool. I like the wind and sunlight effects. I like the way my sails creak and the mast groans and the wind buffets my ship around. That's cool stuff right there, and that little detail here and that other little detail there--that is what makes me want to play this game, and makes my little voice in the back of my head say, 'This game sure is neat--but we've been bouncing back and forth in this same square block of the map for hours now...'
Trust me. It'll happen, if you're any sort of gamer with an adult life and an adult schedule.
Interestingly enough about the 'sandbox' descriptor...is it? I mean it's got that basic random-map-generator thing right? But what does it honestly matter, when you're going to essentially be setting up some variety of chess board squares, slowly trying to build up the first block so you can move to a second block and begin again, grinding and bouncing around inside the map block of various islands/waterways in an attempt to stymie the flow of rabbit-like spawning pirate ships. (Oh god, the pirate ships...)
The game seems to aim big. It's got a lot of polish. But it's shots fall short of their target. In fact, now that I think about it...
...the game designer(s) have a lot in common with the in-game crew of my Sloop-O-War.

I purchased this game on the anticipation of Mad Max: Fury Road hype. I didn't particularly care for the movie which is basically 2 hours of♥♥♥♥♥♥waving action and 0 plot, a good movie does not make.
The good news is this game is not exactly like the movie... at first. The beginning of the game is actually very good, and pulls the player in, and sets an interesting story. Hey, you have a sidekick name Chumbucket, what's not to like?
A winner I thought I had on my hands.
The combat is reminiscent of Batman Arkham Asylum, but more in depth and varied, but in many ways you would think you are playing a similar game. There are a number of interesting changes including shivs, shotgun, and explosives. Like Arkham Asylum though the basics boil down to being surrounded by a bunch of baddies and non-stop parrying their attacks and punching them until they fall down. Sprinkle in some other actions for good measure.
Car combat is deeper than any game I've played as well allowing you a variety of ways to dispatch of rival vehicles and enemies. It's actually not usually very boring just driving around, as you will likely be attacked out of no where and can make for some adrenaline type moments. It is not uncommon to find yourself in a pickle and un-winnable situation.
You objectives revolve around looting random locations, finding sweet jumps, infiltrating strongholds and punching guys a lot, finding hot air balloons to mark objectives on your map, racing, and a few other things. These are all, fairly well done and could seemingly keep you occupied for quite a long time.
The closest game I can think of comparing this one is something like GTAV, which I thought was a pretty good game that had a good mix of missions, characters, writing, and story.
Mad Max though, after ~15 hours just start hitting the wall. You do basically the same missions over, and over, and over. There really isn't much if any of a story, you expect something to happen to no avail. The characters are bland to the point you really will not care about them. Like Fury Road, all the characters could instantly die and I would really not care.
TLDR;
The good:
+ Good beginning.
+ Solid graphics.
+ Good driving.
+ Good combat.
The bad:
- Repetitive.
- Basically no story.
- Bland crappy characters.
- No controller sensitivity settings in the menu, have to edit a file.
If you enjoy mindless everything, or just want a time waster, you will love this game. Otherwise avoid.

Spec Ops: The Line is the hidden gem of 2012. FTL would be my "hidden gem," but after the whole massive Kickstarter success thing, it was obvious FTL was going to be good in my point of view. Honestly, I used to play Call of Duty and Halo. There. I said it. However, after Black Ops 1, I quit the Call of Duty series and haven't played any of the games since MW3. Halo Reach was the Halo that I played the most, and was the only Halo game (Halo 3 and Wars were good though) that I loved and played often. However, above all of these games, Spec Ops: The Line has one of the best stories of all time. It isn't like Call of Duty how you're fighting as some American soldier running around solo armed to the teeth with weapons and murdering terrorists and in the end "saving the world." Not at all. Some people believe there are "good guys" and "bad guys," but this game is solid evidence that war is just opinions being decided to the death, sometimes costing one's sanity, social health, emotional health, and physical health. Spec Ops: The Line proves war in no way is enjoyable, cool, or humorous in any kind of way. War is horrific, and this game is enough to prove that.
The visuals are absolutely outstanding. The environments look beautiful, and the atmosphere is bright on the outside, but dark and horrific on the inside. The characters look amazing, and it's rare you can actually see the sweat of a character in the middle of combat. This game is able to do that. If I were to compare these visuals to The Last of Us, Spec Ops: The Line would win by a mile. These graphics are extremely realistic, but the only con to this is that the facial animations can look weird. For example, when Walker is talking to Lugo or Adams when it isn't a cutscene, it looks like he's gaping every time, like he's shocked at everything for some reason. During cutscenes though, Walker looks fine and doesn't gape like that when he speaks.
The gameplay is suprisingly the weak point to the game. Although this game is a shooter, Spec Ops is more for people who want a story based game, rather than a gameplay based one. The AI is suicidally bad and the difficulty spikes at times and the awful gunplay ruins it even more. My squadmates keep bumping into me and I die, one enemy shot 3 RPG rockets in a row without reloading for some reason (He had an RPG, I saw him with the weapon, I swear!) and the AI prefer running toward me like overconfident barbarians. However, the game understands the meaning of "limited" unlike other games *cough* Call of Duty *cough* *cough* and makes ammo a bit more difficult to get, so that's something few games did that aren't in the zombie survival genre.
The story is the reason Spec Ops is highly praised. Like I said before, it proves that war is a terrible thing and (quoted from Fallout 3) "never changes." Lugo, Adams, and Walker's bond with each other was strong, like they were old friends, then all of a sudden, Lugo and Adams part away from Walker, realizing that he's gone insane, but Adams is still merely following orders, while Lugo wants to make a stand. You realize that Walker is in no way a hero, but calling him a villain is illogical. The plot twist around the midst of the game was amazing and blew my mind. I'm going to do another quote, but this time from one of my favorite songs: "This ain't no place for no hero, this ain't no place for no- better man, this ain't no place for no hero, to call home." -"Short Change Hero" by The Heavy. It perfectly describes the story, mixed with the atmosphere, and how the characters develop over time in the destroyed and now insane city of Dubai. I assure you, this game has one of the finest stories in gaming. It seems like 2012 was the year for gaming, since games like this and The Walking Dead came out and wowed us with their storytelling. In the end, the story for this game is simply outstanding.
The audio is also amazing for this game. The voice actors did an amazing job with their roles, and all showed personality. They  weren't androids and were kind of like the Mass Effect characters, in a way you grow attached to them because they feel like real, breathing humans. But you still gotta hate Walker. Then, hate yourself while you're at it for doing all the harsh decisions. Name me a few other games that truly make you want to hate yourself that much. The music is similar to those found in a zombie apocalypse game, like the recent ones State of Decay and The Last of Us. It's usually a guitar backed up by a few other instruments or the guitar playing solo. It sounds beautiful and fits in perfectly. The audio in this game is some of the finest in recent gaming.
It's a bit more difficult to provide replayability to a game like this, unfortunately. However, you could go back and get all the endings. The multiplayer is pretty dead, so I haven't had any chance to try it yet. Either way, I suppose the replayability in this game is determinant.
In conclusion, Spec Ops: The Line proves war is terrifying and that it's not fun at all. However, the horrible gameplay holds it down significantly, along with a dead multiplayer and the jaw drops that happen when Walker talks while playing (Not in a cutscene) hold it back. Either way, Spec Ops: The Line is a must have for any story based game buyer. I highly recommend this gem.
