This is one of my 2017 GOTY contenders for sure. If you played season one, this is a must play. If you haven't played season one, go play it RIGHT NOW and then play this.
Life is Strange: Before the Storm is the prequel to one of the best single player games ever created. Despite being a prequel, the game is best enjoyed and has much more impact if you play season one first. The prequel makes subtle references to season one that a person unfamiliar with season one would miss, and I personally think that would take away from the experience of this game.
This game tells the story of Chloe Price three years prior to the events of season one, and is set over the course of three days. This game explains Chloe's relationship with Rachel Amber, and explains how Chloe becomes the Chloe we see in season one. If you played season one, this game will fill in much of the mystery behind Chloe's condition and Rachel Amber. That's as much as I will say about the plot.
I am pleased to say that the writing/dialogue in this game is on par, and in some cases even better than season one. The story is just as relatable, heartwrenching, and impossibly sad as the first season. While I think that the story of season one is better and had more of an impact on me, I still think the story presented here is VERY good and still evoked some of the strong emotions from the first season.
While this game does not feature any powers, Chloe does have the ability to use backtalking in order to get what she wants in many situations. This does mean that you need to be more careful when making decisions (or you can just reload to the last checkpoint, but you will have to replay the entire scene again).
The visuals have improved significantly from season one. Most noticibly, the facial animations and lip sync look FAR better when compared to season one. The graphics themselves are a direct improvement over season one, but still feature that "painted world" appearance from the first season. I will also say that this game runs much smoother than season one (at least on my PC). I experienced faster loading times and no random stutters, hitches, or crashes of any kind.
Overall, this game is a masterpiece and I HIGHLY recommend it to anyone interested in single player narrative games and people who enjoyed Life is Strange Season One.

I played Rogue Legacy a couple years back at a friend's house, and thought it was an interesting diversion.
Fast foward to this year's Winter Sale, I saw it was under three dollars, and couldn't justify
getting it.
The premise is you are an adventurer entering a mysterious castle in search of riches, and have to literally pay a toll to do so. When you die, you then get to choose a successor to attempt another run, and so on. These successors have a variety of quirks, from nearsightedness to flatulance.
Gameplay-wise, it's quite good, if abeit difficult.
There's different classes and spells that fit a number of playstyles, and different 'upgrades' that can be purchased (which range from additional cash, to new classes, to better healing), including a reduction in Charon's cost (more on that in a minute).
Additional abilities can be imparted via found armours and runes (which must be found in chests and then purchased back at the castle), which increases the build and playstyle choices even more, from a life-leeching tank, to a sneaky spelunker who specializes in getting lots of gold.
The gameplay itself is also solid. The player navigates through progressively harder dungeons for greater rewards, though even the slightest misstep can be punishing, which isn't surprising for a roguelite game.
As someone who has had a long love/hate relationship with rougelites, this is probably the fairest one I've played.
That said, be prepared for dying A LOT, as the RNG aspect of the game can spawn some brutal rooms.
All of these things were (generally) positives for me, but there were a couple major sticking points.
The 'successor' mechanic is cool, but it has a downside: you are unable to store money, and the only ways to not lose it is either buy upgrades with as much as possible, or buy the upgrade that allows you to have to forfeit less to Charon the gatekeeper.
However, the ability to not have to hand over all your cash to Charon is expensive, and I hit a rut several hours in where, even after a fairly successful run, I would not have enough money to either buy an upgrade (I had already bought the cheap upgrades) or purchase runes/equipment, and would end up having multiple runs where I literally gained nothing from them. This was very, very frustrating.
Second issue was, in spite of the randomized rooms and layouts, this gets to feel very grind-y and same-y within 10-20 hours. I can't do more than one run through at a time anymore, because it's just boring.
There is one final thing I took issue with.
After you defeat a boss, you have a small chance of finding an Obol of that boss at a shrine. Once you die and attempt to return with your successor, Charon will take the Obol and you will have access to that boss room again.
Except.
You fight a massively upgraded version of the boss, and you have to do with a
.
As in, none of your build setups or upgrades or runes or spells or armours carry into the fight, and you HAVE to use a random character you are given.
Some of the 'extra' bosses are also very luck based and unfair.
Since these are optional (though there is an unlock and some Steam achievements), I considered not mentioning them, but the design is so frustating, it's actively malicious.
tl;dr: generally good rougelite platformer marred by a lack on long-term replay value, progression hindernace, and horrifically bad design in a couple spots.

This game is amazing because, like most people have pointed out, it breaks alot of "norms" in the shooter genre. The story is amazing, and by the end of it all you genuinely feel bad for walker and for yourself for the things you have done. Alot of reviewers have said that while the story is good the gameplay leaves alot to be desired. Im not really going to argue that but i will say that the shooting mechanics get the job done. This is a 3rd person cover based shooter. There is not really much room to "revolutionize" the industry in terms of shooting mechanics here. It gets the job done and thats it.
I found the gameplay fun, and the AI, while not exactly Skynet level intelligent, DOES attempt to give you a hard time if you dont take them out quickly. They will flank you, and use grenades quite frequently (i was playing on the hardest initial difficulty, before unlocking the FUBAR difficulty). A wider choice in weaponry would have been welcome, and perhaps some sort of weapon customization options, but considering the type of game this is, weapon customization would have probably not been incredibly useful overall anyways.
What i appreciate the most though, above everything else, are the subtle changes to Walkers character and personality as the game progresses. I dont want to spoil anything, but i will say this: from the start of the game pay attention to how walker acts. From reloading, to taking out enemies, to using the teammate commands. EVERYTHING. Then notice towards the end of the game how he handles taking out enemies, how he gets impatient and screams while reloading, how progressively more brutal and unneccesarily cruel executions become.
This is definitely a game that deserves your time. It has an amazing story, amazing characters, and the gameplay is solid. I highly recommend playing this game on the hardest initial difficulty though, because on normal it can feel a tad on the easy side.

Picked up the game on a recommendation from a friend. Was always intrigued by the good visuals despite not being a hunting buff.  After a brief learning curve the game hooked me. Big thumbs up.
Pros:
- Nearly unmatched environmental visuals. More immersive world I've stepped into in a game by far.
- Massive maps with plenty of variation even within a single map
- Sound design is well done
- Relaxing, slow pace (not for everyone)
- Progression system through gear upgrades, skills and perks
- Bit of a 'story' to go with it with some minor quests etc.
- Multiplayer works nicely (shared spotting, etc.)
- Devs continue to patch it with fixes and features
Cons:
- Some the DLC perhaps should have been in the base game (ATV and Tents I'm looking at you). The total cost is still worth the value of the game for me anyway.
- Limited game to hunt (wish there was waterfowl, or things smaller than a fox)
- Some buggy behavior on the ATV at times (nowhere near gamebreaking)

Some might call this game casual, some might call it fast paced. Well the choice is yours. you can decide whether you want the challenge to be easy and the combat hard, vice versa, or at an equal level.

In summary: loads of fun, time flies, I don't want to stop playing.

I've put a few hours into this game now, I feel compelled to write a review on how good this game is.
This game requires brains, you need to have skills on planning, resource management, patience and  the ability to spot small things.
Its easily the best prison simulator you will find in the gaming world and I say so because i have played them all.
The graphics perfectly suit the type of game it is, it may not appeal to those wanting spectacular explosions and textures.
The audio isnt overbearing, done just right.
Its incredibly in-depth, each prisoner has their own biography, character sheet and traits (including their reputation in the prison. Ignoring 1 prisoners repuation can have severe consequences. You have the ability to manage every aspect of your prison.
9/10.

I enjoy good "Simulation" and "Tycoon" games: trains, farming, flying, business, etc.  ETS2 is a pleasurable cargo transportation simulator, and a decent business tycoon game if you want to tackle more than just driving your rig.
The graphics are beautiful, and the audio is well done.  Some of the routes can feel repetitive, and the traffic AI can be aggravating at times, but I bet that any long haul driver would same the same thing about real life.
If you feel that you can handle a game that doesn't involve killing everything in sight, then this is a good game to give a try.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a great Trucking Simulator improving so much over the first one, with a huge map that you can explore right away with out needing to unlock any parts (some DLC is required for the full map), jump in the cab of real world trucks from Scania, Man, IVECO and Mercedes-Benz all are fully customizable with new rims and paint jobs.
ETS2 has great graphics, animations and sound, the truck handeling is spot on, featureing controller suport for the G27 (I don't now about the new G29) and the xbox 360 wireless controler.
ETS2 is a must buy for trucking and sim fans alike. What are you waiting for jump in start your engine and head out on the open road.

Imagine your favourite platform game, your favourite funny game and the dark souls series had some sort of witty 2D lovechild. This is how i best describe this game.
This game is challenging and difficult until you figure out the pattern of enemies attacks and once you have managed to save enough money for upgrades and gear therefore the first few hours you will play you will die..... a lot. But dont despair with death as you can play as one of your heirs over half a dozen classes with different abilities and classes and 'traits'. The traits range from dwarfism to ADHD, from OCD to short sightedness, and from dyslexia to being on roids (and a few more). These traits are made hilarious through the game and really add to the game - "oh no im low on health and must search for some food - oh look a roast chicken - oh wait im scared of chicken so it somehow attacks me and i die. 10/10 would be murdered by chicken again".
There are a few generic spells and most of the enemies are what you would expect to see - knights, warlocks, zombies, bone archers and mutant flowers. Each playthrough comes with a different castle layout so you never really know what is around the corner, and this game epitomises the 'one last attempt' as you really want to progress in the game and not be killed by a spike trap for the 20th time in a row!
Overall its a great game that is perfect for the odd 20 minutes you have spare and it really emphasises that every attempt matters!

Note that this review was done from the single player experience. And as a single player experience, Windward is woefully grindy and simplistic. That's not a good combination.
There's nothing interesting to explore in Windward - the next map is a generic version of the last map. The game play is exceptionally grindy as you buy two or three goods (that's all your ship will hold for the first 10+ hours of any game), travel across the generic map to go to a different city and sell those two or three goods. You're thanking your lucky stars when you can sell both goods at the same city. And the cities take FOREVER to develop into anything remotely large, and there's no way to develop your cities beyond enduring this grind because the "quests" (all are either "kill x" or simple Fedex quests) level your cities even more slowly.
Single player combat is nothing more than sailing in a circle waiting for the next hotkey to come up - it's like the worst example of level 1 MMO combat.
So you move on from region to region, doing the exact same thing. There's no fundamental personality or purpose to the single player component. It becomes tedious very quickly and the known bug with pirate spawning rates (this is going to be fixed) only adds to that incredible annoyance. You're also pretty much on your own. You can have computer AI ships follow, but they simply fail to do so (or can't keep up), meaning that any battle you face will undoubtedly be on your own.
MP is a different game. Windward is a better game when played cooperatively - it's easier to take down other enemies, coordinate strategies and so forth. But as a single player experience, Windward loses its luster quickly. Since that's what I like to play, Windward gets both thumbs down.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a great Trucking Simulator improving so much over the first game, with a huge map to explore (some DLC is required for the full map), jump in the cab of real world trucks from Scania, MAN, IVECO, DAF and Mercedes-Benz all are fully customizable with new rims and paint jobs custom bull bars and even cabin accessories.
ETS2 has great graphics, animations and sound, the truck handling is spot on, featuring controller support for the G27, G29 (also the G920) and the Xbox 360 wireless/wired controller.
ETS2 is a must buy for trucking and sim fans alike. So what are you waiting for jump in start your engine and head out on the open road. :)

In a world where many simulator games are pretty much jokes at this point, I find peace that I have discovered this rare gem of a game. It restores my sanity to know that not all developers are out there to suck every penny out of your wallet. Euro Truck Simulator 2 is fantastic as a base game, and the DLC is really not required unless you are interested in expanding the map so you can drive in Scandanavia or Eastern Europe.
The game is pretty simple. You deliver different cargoes all over Europe to make money, buy your own truck, and expand your empire. I know, it sounds boring and terribly bland, but I assure you it's quite the opposite.
There's just something about hauling heavy cargo all over the map and praying that you don't clip that car on that turn because you'll incure that annoying 400 euro fine, not to mention that it might even damage your cargo. At that point, you can bid farewell to your already small profit. Or the adrenaline rush when you know you took that turn too hard and your trailer is moments away from tipping over, which would only result in you blocking the way and having the regular cars honk at you, as if you could do anything about it. It's relaxing (and cheaper than therapy).
There's loads (no pun intended) of options to customize your truck. There is also a really active modding community in which you can find tons of different maps, trucks, and cargoes.
I haven't found many bugs, and the developers are wonderful. They still come out with updates even though this game was released nearly 3 years ago.
It is best played with a racing wheel or gamepad, the keyboard is rather unrealistic and not nearly as much fun. The graphics are beautiful. I love watching sunrises and sunsets in this game as they are simply stunning, even if you don't have a great graphics card (like myself).
Euro Truck Simulator 2 is an amazing game. I really do recommend purchasing the DLC, despite my previous statements. It adds new cities so you can explore to your heart's desires. Also, it helps to support the devs who have been working very hard to make quality games like this.
~Krystal~

Spec Ops: The Line is an incredible game. It's also an incredibly gory, horrifying game. The story is phenomenally well done, and if you're alright with gore (not typical video-gamey "fun" gore - there's a lot of really gross realistic gore (and a lot of the worst is your character's fault) and feeling horrible about your character (Captain Walker) then I highly recommend it. But if you're particularly sensitive to... pretty much any sort of violence and gore, I'd steer clear.
All aspects of the game have been done well. The scenery looks beautiful, the guns feel powerful, and there's actually a good reason to have all of that cover (you can die REALLY easily, and I played it on normal mode). Your two AI companions (Adams and Lugo) do end up coming in handy, especially once the game gets really difficult. The gameplay itself isn't anything new (it's very Gears of War-esque), but it's enough to serve the game, and it's been put together splendidly. Basically, the story drives the game, and the gameplay includes you in the story, just as any story-driven game should do.
This game is truly proof that video games can be art in the same way movies and books have been - not just "oooh pretty" art (though games can do that and have definitely done that too (look at Journey)), but the kind of art that makes you think, poses questions, and makes commentary. It's based around Heart of Darkness, though it takes many different twists and turns, and it does manage to show the sides of one of the victims of actual war that tends to get ignored: the citizens in war-torn places. Though there isn't much direct commentary on that, it's pretty clear the way these people feel, and the game does much to show the horror of your actions.
The game is very linear, but it's alright here because it serves the story, displaying your character's descent into the heart of Dubai, ruined by great sand storms and violence - as well as his descent into the darkest places of the human heart. In this way, it's hard to say the game doesn't make you feel horribly guilty - either for yourself or for Captain Walker. It's rather clear by the linear nature of this game that Captain Walker is his own character, not you - his decisions are his decisions. However, it is you who end up carrying out his decisions - just following orders. Whether you like it or not, you are part of the story.
I highly recommend you play this game. It is not for the faint of heart, but it shows a lot of depth that video games (particularly modern war shooters) really need to get behind. This is by far the most mature game I have ever played.

Specifics:
Most maps are not worth playing, and you are forced to play them or suffer negative marks on your gaming record. DLC maps are not worth the money either. DayZ is the survival game that started it all, the original so to speak.  Other companies have made much more polished survival games in their own vision.  Less buggy, less clunky, easier to play, more exciting.  However as a player of the mod there is still the survival element in DayZ that is not found in other games, mainly the philosophy of not making things too easy, which is what keeps me waiting for the Beta or full release to at least have a decently polished finished game.  I do hope with full release they will not compromise this hardcore philosophy and of course release server files to allow hosting and modding.  Bohemia Interactive sort of missed (though not really they sold a lot of copies) an opportunity to really make a great game here.  It took them so long because they just apparently do not have the ability to create a well-polished game.  However the one great thing about them as a PC gamer is they allow heavy modding and this will redeem this game.
Basically if you are new to DayZ, its probably not worth getting this until they release a beta or full release, unless you have friends who will play and teach you.  I play all sorts of other survival-flavored games like Rust, PUBG, etc. they are all different and if you want a game that is actually difficult to survive in and unforgiving then there is no other survival game like DayZ.

I have very mixed feelings about this game. It started promising, but then turned out to be a major letdown. The last episode specifically.
This game does some things better than its predecessor, but in many ways it's worse.
THE LOOK
They've improved lip sync and some character models look more detailed than in the original LiS. However, this is very uneven. There are many low-res muddy textures, one particular male character looks very bad. Overall, many new characters look comical and unrealistic. Something's wrong with their body proportions. E.g. bouncer, the guys who attack Chloe during the concert, the main villain. I mean, the original LiS wasn't about 100% realism either, but there were no such grotesque-looking characters. And you cannot just take them seriously,
Body animations are worse than in the original game. When people are hugging, for example, it really feels like you play a game from the early 2000s or something. And in many other cases character movements just feel awkward. There were some clunky animations in the original LiS, but overall it felt much more smooth and added to immersion.
For the game that pretends to be an interactive movie these things are deal-breaking. I am not mentioning the lack of shadows, jarring close-ups on low-poly and low-res body parts and other things like this.
I even reinstalled the original game, because at first I thought I might be imagining things, No, I wasn't.
PERFORMANCE
I have a GTX970, and the game constantly stutters, suffers from frame rate drops, even on the lowest graphics settings. That's some poor optimization.
THE GAMEPLAY
I felt like this game was much more streamlined than the previous one. I guess this is mostly due to the lack of time rewind mechanics. This one felt like yet another Telltale game. Despite there are couple of more or less meaningful choices, many other choices don't really matter.
The fact that the ending is affected by the choice you make in the middle of the game is nice, but at the same time you cannot really guess that this particular choice will affect this specific thing in the end. That makes you feel somewhat betrayed. E.g. in the Witcher 3 you can clearly see how your choices affect the ending, it's more of a pattern of your choices throughout the game. But here it's just one choice, which is, you know, very random.
The talking mini-game is too easy, it definitely lack depth. Nothing compared to the conversational challenges in Deus Ex: Human Revolution, for example. Not even close. Another problem with these conversational options is that they are often not the ones that you would really like to choose. However, the biggest issue is that these conversations don't really affect anything, Do those or not, you will still progress through the game.
Oh, and you cannot restart from a specific chapter, only full episode.
THE STORY AND THE CHARACTERS
The first episode was good, except for the forced and somewhat ridiculous ending.
The second one was okay, nothing too special and no real plot twists. The acting sometimes felt wrong (e.g.

Spec Ops: The LIne is a truly thought-provoking journey.This is not so apparent at the start of the game but once you hit the mid-way point, the story gets really interesting. The voice acting is superb and I can honestly say I grew to like the characters (despite the circumstances), which made the ending really heartbreaking.  Graphics-wise, the game looks great. Gameplay mechanics are also good although I found some aspects of it a bit clunky (such as melee and vaulting being bound by default to the same button).  In my opinion, the pacing was great and there was enough variety to the chapters/scenarios so the game did not drag or feel repetitive. As a third person shooter, the game is pretty enjoyable. However, what elevates Spec Ops: The Line to greater heights is its narrative. It is one of those rare games that left me emotionally aroused at the end, not to mention dumbfounded - in a good way, of course :) I was pleasantly surprised and was not disappointed whatsoever in Spec Ops: The LIne. Highly recommended especially if you appreciate an intellectually (and emotionally) stimulating experience.

is one of those rare games with a formula that produces long-lasting, satisfying replay with relatively simple ingredients. Though its campaign is a satisfying length, its focus on co-op, loot collection, and near-infinite leveling pushes its replayability to the max. I managed to finish the main storyline and nearly all of the side missions in tens of hours of play. However, I haven't downloaded any DLC yet, and boy! is there a lot of DLC. I also haven't played through the campaign another two times; yes, this game supports two replay modes ("True Vault Hunter Mode" and "Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode") with increasingly challenging enemies and increasingly rare loot. Even further, I understand that the DLC expands the leveling capacities even higher, in addition to adding more missions and more locations.
I can confidently say that
outweighs any other game in my library for value, originality, and enjoyment. I haven't even mentioned the quality of the game's story and writing, which you might expect to be irrelevant given the strength of this game's other features, but it's excellent!

Customizable loadouts and the addition of campaign perks
Strike Force missions (Command a squadron of troops and drones defending, escorting and eliminating objectives)
Multiple endings
Play as a bad guy in the campaign for the first time!
New playlists and gamemodes (Nuketown, anyone?)
Several decent-sized maps
New Pick-10 System in Multiplayer allows more flexibility with custom loadouts
Offline (and online!) Combat Training
Create your own emblems
Zombies return! (with some new faces)
Cons:
Community hasn't changed at all since CoD4
Imbalanced weapons (though not as bad as in the previous games)
It's still the same generic gameplay as it was a decade ago (but what'd you expect?)
Though it falls short in more ways than one, it's far from unpleasant. If anything, it's a godsend compared to the more recent Ghosts.

I put 24 hours into Mad Max, and so I can't reasonably ask for a refund. I beat the game, and for quite a bit of it, I had fun.

That being said, I found this game's conclusion almost offensively bad. So here's the bottom line if you want to enjoy this game (if, for instance, you're getting it as part of a humble bundle, which will be the case for anyone getting this month's humble monthly):
-The core mechanics of driving around, using your grappling hook to rip off doors and shoot drivers, and sometimes using your shotgun to shoot fuel canisters, is actually pretty fun and generally satisfying. Later, when you have the rocket launcher, it's a bit disappointing but not bad either.
-The core mechanics of ground combat, countering with one button and punching with the other, is pretty easy but generally fine too.
-The... plot... if you might call it that... is not why anyone would reasonably play this game, and is actually so bad by the ending that I can't reasonably recommend the game despite its otherwise perfectly fine features. "Let's introduce a bunch of characters you don't care about, kill them, then immediately bring them back to life because we can't be bothered to animate a replacement character!" Stupid. STUPID.

My recommendation is to enjoy driving around fighting convoys, and don't even bother advancing the plot if you can avoid it. Quit playing when you hit gas town. Don't finish it--you'll have better memories of the game.

First, anyone considering buying this game should know that, as of the time of this writing, the game is oriented primarily towards combat. Trade, questing, and exploration are indeed present, but serve to fund the player's upgrades; you will not be playing this game as a merchant, diplomat, or explorer. That said, if you do enjoy naval combat and aren't averse to a challenge, you will enjoy this game.
The developer claims to have taken inspiration from Sid Meier's Pirates!, and anyone who has played any of the releases of Pirates! will definitely notice some of the influence. I'd personally classify the game as an improved successor; the game took everything that was fun about Pirates!, strips away the tedious things that no one liked (we're looking at you, dancing.), and improved on some things that had potential but weren't explored, such as trade. This is probably why the game is so oriented towards combat, as Pirates! was as a whole about you sailing around being a scurvy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Except now you can have giant multiple ship brawls where crap is exploding left and right and everything is on fire.
The game itself follows your regular RPG sort of formula; kill things, gain experience, upgrade skills, and search for good loot. There are four playable factions, but aren't very different aside from some minor gimmicks. The world is split up into multiple procedurally generated regions, with enemies becoming stronger the further you venture from where the playable factions start. Those four factions start with a region they control and a couple that they hold part of, and the rest of the world is infested with pirates. Unless you're playing online, your faction will be the only one to ever advance beyond where they start, and you will spend most of your time fighting pirates. Inter-faction warfare is a thing, and you can contest other factions for control of a region, but I haven't figured out the purpose as of yet. Your end goal is supposedly to help your faction take over the world, but I have no idea what actually happens if you do.
Combat is, again, the largest part of the game, but I found it to be the funnest. Fights are largely tactical affairs, usually with you sailing into range and your crew automatically firing at enemy ships with standard cannon fire while you fire off skills at the enemy. Multiple ships can enter and leave a fight, and whether you're engaged in a fight is guaged based on proximity to hostile ships and towers. The AI, which I'll address in a moment, does come to back both you and the enemy up, but only within a certain distance. In single player, this can turn skirmishes into full battles just to take a harbor, and that capacity for fluid battles is part of the appeal that combat has. The game scales rather well, so unless you sail to the lower level areas with higher level gear (and there's an option in world creation to force high level gear to get scaled for an area) or you try to rush too far ahead, you'll never too over or underpowered.
The game is not without its lackluster components though. Despite advertising diplomacy, trade, and exploration as options, they're not as prevalent as you would think. Diplomacy exists in the form of quests, which usually revolve around delivering stuff, killing something, or building new towns or defenses, and the only real benefit is gold and increasing the size of a town. Trade is a regular buy low and sell high deal. Exploration is just lifting the fog of war; there's no relics to be hunting for or anything. The AI is also a bit strange, with it usually backing me up pretty well but sometimes acting as if the pirate sloop currently taking over the nearby port isn't something it should intervene in. So far I've chalked that up to expected instability an overall effective AI. My biggest gripe is that you're thrown into the game to sink or swim; no tutorial, or even a quick brief on controls. Thankfully everything is rather simple and a guide does exist outside of the game, but a little guidance before sending me to take on every pirate in the entire ocean would be nice.
As for graphics and sound, gorgeous and fitting. The varying biomes each have their own graphics styles, and the models of the ships look great. The extra effects such as explosions or fires look nice, and they give a real feeling of weight to the carnage you're unleashing on the ocean. The graphics are a bit more artsy than realistic, but everything fits together really well. The music gives off a feeling off a nice feeling of adventure, and the sound effects are on point for everything. You will enjoy every single time a ship blows up, whether its yours or someone else's.
Overall, this is a pretty nice game for what it is. I'm not sure of the developer's plans, but hopefully it will make trade and diplomacy more important and make the AI a little smarter. It's a good mix of RPG and... Whatever Pirates! was, and it's addictingly fun at that. I recommend getting it while it's still on sale, you should be getting your money's worth.

It's time to take a trip back to Blackwell Academy, you're an alum now so you should pretty much know where everything is, right? Good, I’m sure you’ll find your way around without too much trouble. Honestly, not much has changed here at Blackwell, and that’s just the case with Life is Strange: Before the Storm. You know what you'll be getting before you dive in, and it's all the goods you remember, but it never really strays to far outside its comfort zone.
Before the Storm (BTS) is set three years prior to the events of the original game in the series, Life is Strange (LIS), and follows the exploits of Chloe Price and her BFF Rachel Amber. As with the first game, drama ensues, and the duo soon find themselves on a journey that will change their lives forever.
Here we have all of the ingredients for another great LIS game, and the things that were done well in LIS are all present; great characters, emotionally driven plot, super detailed worlds. Let's face it, LIS taught us that you never really know someone until you dig through their personal belongings. No matter how creepy that is, it's the truth, and because of it, the characters in BTS surprise us just like they did in the original game. People you normally hate become much more endearing; those you love have something to hide. Either way, BTS really captures the same feelings from the first game.
One thing it manages to miss, however, is the feeling of true decision making, and part of the blame should be placed on the protagonist, Chloe Price. Don't get me wrong, Chloe is a great character. She's hard to love at times, but she's even harder to hate, but her strong personality makes it really difficult to feel like you're actually making a difference in her world. Sure, it could just be the fact that the game is a prequel and you know what will happen in the next game so none of it seems to matter, but when it comes down to it, Chloe will be Chloe. Her strong personality and undeniable resolve makes her an awesome character, but you never truly escape from her will. In the original game, Max was also a great character, but she was more malleable than Chloe. It felt like you were growing with her, whereas with Chloe, you're just along for the ride.
Another thing that really detracts from this otherwise great game is the plot. LIS had an awesome concept, regular girl, regular school, regular life - but wait? She can travel through time? Interesting. Aside from the occasional weird dream, Chloe's story lacks the originality of Max's crazy trip through, not only adolescence, but time itself. Hear me out, I'm not saying that this game needed time travel, I'm simply stating that one of the aspects that made LIS so amazing was the outlandish, time travel driven plot. At the end of the day, between the two games, LIS has a better plot than BTS.
So what does all of this mean, should you get BTS? I'd say so, heck, I got the deluxe edition. When it all boils down, it's a great game that fills in a lot of the questions that crop up in LIS, and it has a few hair raising moments to boot. But I really don't think it makes a name for itself apart from the first game and as a result, it won't escape the shadow of the original LIS. But maybe that's not what it was designed to do, and if that's the case, maybe that's perfectly fine. Either way, you should give it a shot. Chloe can’t get in hella trouble on her own.

The one problem in the game is that it lacks some depth. It's awesome getting to meet Rachel Amber and seeing her relationship with Chloe. Also seeing all of Chloe's relationships with her parents, the school, and her friends, but the ending kind of felt shallow. The games don't connect with each other very well other than a short, implied scene at the end. It also suffers from what most Choose Your Own Adventure games do by not having choices really matter in the long run.
Despite that, I really recommend this game. It does a really good job with the story, and it makes the characters feel very alive.

To put it shortly: if you can spare the doubloons, buy it.
The game's development was geared highly towards the consoles which resulted in highly linear levels and that bothered me the most. There was so much potential to let the player explore a beautiful post-apocalyptic Dubai, but nooooooo... The second hint would be the controls for the cover-based gameplay, half of the difficulty for me came from that.
Still, even if you consider yourself to be of the PC-using master race, do buy it, since the overall image looks beautiful.
Now, the right way to play it would be starting from the highest available difficulty setting, anything lower and You'd be missing out on the frustration and probably go through the game too fast (I went through the HIGH difficulty in 7 hours), and do it in one run. Heck, the frustation might even force Your hand in some situations which come up in the course of the story which leaves me to the good part of the game.
The game has a strong emotional component which the frustation deriving from the difficulty and from battling with the controls only helpt to strengthen. The choices are tough and the plot-twists interesting, which is the selling point of the game. Also, the story doesn't have as much of the "'MURICA!" factor as other modern shooters, which was refreshing.
I'd rather not go too deep into the actual story, but in the end I was truly left asking myself:
"Do you feel like a hero yet?"

First let me say, this game was gifted to me by a friend, and I'm now cursing them for it...  while this gem of a game looks like a "cute" way to kill a couple of minutes here and there, it's so much more (evil) than that.  I started a game to give it a try and kill a couple of minutes, and my first 4 hours were behind me before I realized it!
Take the best (sailing) parts of the various pirate themed sailing games from the 80's and 90's, speed up the game play a bit, and be ready to lose yourself for a bit!  I don't know what it is about the balance they were able to achieve in this mix, but it simply works for this game.
Combat
Pretty straight forward, you get into range and your ship auto-attacks the closest enemy within the various firing arcs.  You can hire escort ships or try to bribe pirates if you have enough gold, and those extra guns can make the difference between collecting the booty, and spending the night with Davy Jones!
There are special attacks you can unlock as you gain experience, some of these increase your DPS, reduce your damage taken, or can buff your allies (including defensive structures like sentry towers!)  Each faction has it's own perks, and depending on what you enjoy, you'll probably find one of the factions that calls to you.
Later game play has you capture towns, towers, etc.. for your faction, and there is a benefit for doing so beyond it being a goal.  As you control more of the towns, you have more places to trade/quest, which also helps advance the town's level, opening new items for you to use on your ship, new ships, and even new quests.
Trading/Quests
To me, probably the most "boring" aspect of the game, and it's still not that boring at all.  You can choose to take on quests or cargo, all missions take one of your cargo (not your inventory) slots, and as you advance up the various ship lines, you'll gain/lose cargo slots based on the ship's role.
The various "world" missions have been entertaining so far, and their rewards tend to be usable/in scale for the quest line.  One complaint here, you can get random missions for specific resources (like cotton) which are not available in your current region.  It would be nice if the game allowed you keep these types of missions in inventory when you find them, but you don't know the objective until you Examine the quest.  Unfortunately, unlike the port quests, you cannot choose to not take the quest on and save it for later.
Overall
Even though I was gifted a copy of them game, knowing what I know now, I'd have bought this one.  If you enjoy the game's style/theme, and are looking for a fun game that might surprise you, you'll probably enjoy this one!
Its simple Sid Mier's Pirates camera style, yet complex and very in-depth PvP.  A very fun game and worth your money!

I don't do reviews. I had never seen a Mad Max movie before. I never got sad that a game was over because I wanted it to continue on and on. Mad Max changed all of that.
I spent 25 hours in my playthrough, completed the story, yet still have only completed 58% of the game. There is plenty of content in this game. Yet, it still took 25 hours.
I would rank this game up there just behind Red Dead Redemption for my all time list. The story is well written and presented in such a way that it often felt like I was Max inside of a moive. The graphics are phenomenal. The lighting is some of the best I have ever seen and the terrain in each region looks unbelievably real at times. The combat on foot and in vehicles is very satisfying and never felt stale despite being simple.
There is not much I can say about this game that I feel is not a pro. I wish the story was longer, but that's more because I never wanted this game to end because of how much fun I was having with it and how well the cinematics are done. It still took me 25 hours to complete and like I said previously, I kind of rushed through it on accident.
This is a game I will be playing over again. I'll attack it differently and attack more of the non-story activities/missions. I'll take my time. I'll probably go for 100%. Then I might play it over and over because it is just that good of a game. I am so glad I decided to bite on this game. I not only got to experience a sleeper hit and what I view as maybe the GOTY for 2015, but I was introduced to a character that I have become a fan of. Because of this game I have gone back and watched the older movies.
If you are on the fence for this game, GET IT. You won't regret it. The only thing that will upset you is that no sequel(even if it's just a spiritual sequel) has been announced.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a great Trucking Simulator improving so much over the first game, with a huge map to explore (some DLC is required for the full map), jump in the cab of real world trucks from Scania, MAN, IVECO, DAF and Mercedes-Benz all are fully customizable with new rims and paint jobs custom bull bars and even cabin accessories.
ETS2 has great graphics, animations and sound, the truck handling is spot on, featuring controller support for the G27, G29 (also the G920) and the Xbox 360 wireless/wired controller.
ETS2 is a must buy for trucking and sim fans alike. So what are you waiting for jump in start your engine and head out on the open road. :)

In a world where many simulator games are pretty much jokes at this point, I find peace that I have discovered this rare gem of a game. It restores my sanity to know that not all developers are out there to suck every penny out of your wallet. Euro Truck Simulator 2 is fantastic as a base game, and the DLC is really not required unless you are interested in expanding the map so you can drive in Scandanavia or Eastern Europe.
The game is pretty simple. You deliver different cargoes all over Europe to make money, buy your own truck, and expand your empire. I know, it sounds boring and terribly bland, but I assure you it's quite the opposite.
There's just something about hauling heavy cargo all over the map and praying that you don't clip that car on that turn because you'll incure that annoying 400 euro fine, not to mention that it might even damage your cargo. At that point, you can bid farewell to your already small profit. Or the adrenaline rush when you know you took that turn too hard and your trailer is moments away from tipping over, which would only result in you blocking the way and having the regular cars honk at you, as if you could do anything about it. It's relaxing (and cheaper than therapy).
There's loads (no pun intended) of options to customize your truck. There is also a really active modding community in which you can find tons of different maps, trucks, and cargoes.
I haven't found many bugs, and the developers are wonderful. They still come out with updates even though this game was released nearly 3 years ago.
It is best played with a racing wheel or gamepad, the keyboard is rather unrealistic and not nearly as much fun. The graphics are beautiful. I love watching sunrises and sunsets in this game as they are simply stunning, even if you don't have a great graphics card (like myself).
Euro Truck Simulator 2 is an amazing game. I really do recommend purchasing the DLC, despite my previous statements. It adds new cities so you can explore to your heart's desires. Also, it helps to support the devs who have been working very hard to make quality games like this.

When I first heard of Undertale, I had no interest in playing it. I thought the fanbase was massively cringeworthy and the game was probably uninteresting.
I was correct about the fanbase, but boy was I wrong about the game.
I normally play action/adventure RPG games with the occasional sprinkling of singleplayer FPS. I am not the kind of person to normally go in for conceptual hipster nonsense, and I say that because that's what I thought this game was.
In reality, it has some of the best atmosphere and writing I've seen in a game in a very long time. And above all else, it manages to be heart-rendingly (no pun indended) sad at times and actually funny at other times. Plus, the music is fantastic and the whole package has a level of care I don't often see anymore.
You are doing yourself a disservice if you don't try this game out. And I don't say that lightly.

I wish Steam had the option to give a "mixed" review, because I honestly can't say my review is either positive or negative. Out of coherence, since for past games I had the same problem with I just put in "positive", we'll go with that. I do enjoy the game.
It's pretty simple, it's super fun, and the style not only of the characters, but of pretty much all of the items and interface are mostly consistent and hella stylish. Seriously, every minor artwork for events has their suburban/slightly anime schtick. Soundtrack helps a lot with the feel too, although obviously it gets repetitive after a while.
Unfortunately, the game is plagued by some issues that cannot be ignored: first of all, having a bad ping absolutely destroys your game experience and that of the others. It's not as bad as in other games, but that's not saying much: it's pretty terrible.
Secondly, the game is very luck-based, which arguably some casual players might enjoy, but not me. Admittedly, it makes sense in the way they made it, having your chance of success or fail an action depend on your stats compared to those of your adversary, trying to simulate variation or something... still, this effectively means playing consistently doesn't yield the same result all the time, and sure, the usual argument against this is "that just means you have to adapt to new circumstances", but I personally dislike this approach. Plus, someone succeeding a low-chance Steal, turning around shooting 2pt is not exactly giving anyone time or chance to react, although obviously there are plays and "strats" that, paired with reflexes, minimize risks. So, it's bad, but not all that bad.
Secondly, the oh-so-dreaded pay2win. It's definitely there.
There's this argument going around, claiming that "even if you pay for the boosts, you gotta know how to use your character, so this isn't true", but what the people who say this are forgetting is that that effectively means if two people of roughly the same "skill level" meet, the person who payed will objectively have better stats and therefore the exact advantage they need to defeat the other person, without having achieved this via either luck or skill.
Overall, try it. It's fun. I'm not taking it seriously and I'm having a blast, but I'm not sure I'd ever want to touch the comp scene.

Windward takes from a now boring classic, Sid Meier's Pirates. Pirates lacked multiplayer and was clearly tailored for young audiences. It was a game I got bored with extremely fast. Windward brushes off the Pirate dust and makes way for a whole lot of improvements. I find the faction system in Windward extremely fun to play around with. You start to have a faction grow on you and you genuinely start to get to know the other players playing for your faction and the enemy factions. The way the game plays promotes a sense of community that is lacking in a lot of faction-based games. I played the game with a friend throughout my entire play experience. It provided a ton of laughs and some intense moments for us. The PVE challenged us. The PVP made us want revenge. Our homeland was being stolen by the Valient. We started to fight back as hard as we could, but some of their players were a far higher level than us. We picked off small ships while dodging and outrunning their behemoths. Armadas of Valient players would chase after us, but we specialized in speed, mobility, and guerrilla tactics. The game was extremely fun, but I don't think it has enough content to keep us going much longer. This could be improved if more abilities are added, more things to do when not fighting, and extension of faction systems. I'd recommend this game to anyone who wants to play a short MMO-like experience with their friends. It is definitely worth the $15 for what it provides. Make sure to join the biggest server possible instead of creating your own!

"Life is Strange: Before the Storm" is a prequel of the game "Life is Strange". Unlike the previous game, this time you'll play as Max's best friend Chloe and developing your friendship with the missing/dead girl Rachel in the previous game. This game has inherited almost all the cons from the previous game. For example, very awkward/unrealistic dialogues that make you cringe, the weird lesbian relationship between the two protagonists, and the crazy/annoying friendzone dude who has a crush on you. Other than the story, the gameplay mechanics doesn't felt as unique as the first game. Because as Chloe, you no longer have the time rewind superpower. You can still reload from the last checkpoint. But you'll have to rewatch the same dialogues from 10 minutes ago. And you CAN'T fast forward!
Despite all the cons I mentioned, I'm still giving the game a positive review. Because it still has a top notch soundtrack, and it has one major improvement over the last game. In the last game, your final choice were either sacrifice everyone to save Chloe who had been a whiny♥♥♥♥♥♥the whole time; or save everyone and sacrifice Chloe. The choice was very obvious to me, I killed Chloe without hesitation. In the new game however, for the first time I couldn't decide for a few minutes. I'm looking forward to play the bonus episode soon. I actually like Chloe a lot more after playing this game. I'd like to see the character transition in the upcoming episode.

It perfectly ties in with the first game, Life is strange is a game that has seriously changed the way I view gaming. It's not like any other story. It feels almost real. The voice acting the characters, it's all amazing.

The announcement of Life is Strange: Before the Storm had a lukewarm reception at best. Many people were puzzled as to why someone even thought the original game needed a prequel. Some were incredibly disappointed by the absence of Max, or the original VAs. Others still took a look at Deck Nine's history and were very unimpressed. Dis-impressed, even. So how come so many people, me included, are recommending this?
Well, turns out Before the Storm is actually, legitimately good (mostly)! It manages to carry over a lot of things from the original without giving you the sense that you've already been there. But, more importantly, it improves many things! Deck Nine weren't afraid of adding something of their own. The... cinematography (?) is a lot better, utilizes more angles, strives to add something to every frame. The music, while being of a pretty different genre (more indie rock than indie folk), comes from the same rule established by the first game: the music must always reflect mood and character. The rebellious young Chloe Price is super into indie rock, punk rock, and the more "hardcore" varieties of indie folk music. While the original game's spotlight shined on a French indie folk band Syd Matters, Before the Storm props up a British indie rock/indie pop band Daughter. Listening to the tracks taken from the band's standalone albums and the album "Music from Before the Storm", the player will become absolutely mesmerized and enchanted by Elena Tonra's moody yet sensual vocals and the band's incredibly powerful mix of depressing yet energetic music. And I haven't even mentioned some of the other great bands appearing on this game's soundtrack - including one where the devs themselves play!
Before the Storm isn't a purely formalist game, of course. The writing done by Zak Garriss, an ancient history and philosophy geek, rivals that of Life is Strange and, in some ways, even overpowers it. In slice-of-life fashion, Before the Storm stresses the daily, normal, and mostly cheery human interactions, as opposed to the original game's taste for the grim, paranormal, and crime-related. Zak Garriss holds the proud title of the man who turned Chloe and Rachel into favorite characters of those people who disliked, even hated them previously. Many have also noted that the dialogue of Before the Storm is a lot more human-like than that of the original game.
Not everything is perfect, however. While the technical side of Before the Storm, especially the lipsyncing, is absolutely an improvement over the original game, it is somewhat harmed by the transition to Unity - plenty of people have complained about the, shall we say, immersion immolating loading screens which accompany jarring cuts between scenes and cuts in music (all of which are "perfectly" illustrated by Episode 3). The new animations are also a mix of good and bad: some of them are really good, yet others look absolutely alien-like.
While I have praised Zak Garriss' writing, I should note that my praise was mostly limited to episodes 1 and 2. Episode 3 is packed full of things that aren't exactly great. Or good. Or even okay. Without spoiling anything, the ending is very rushed and lacking; the sequence before that ending - absolutely bizarre (and not in the good sense); the sudden metamorphosis of some characters - extremely weird; the shift from Chloe's story to something else - pretty arguable; and so on, and so on. All of these things surprised me because the first two episodes absolutely convinced me the last one will AT LEAST not faceplant. Which is kind of what happened. There's also a lot of retcons, which is weird for a team that said they adored and respected the original game.
To sum my rambling up: a very impressive start, a very impressive fall. Even though I'd say I was kind of let down by the final episode, I'd still really recommend this to anyone, be they a fan of Life is Strange or a total newcomer. While some of the issues are really glaring and Deck Nine's treatment of some themes requires criticism, I simply cannot hold all of that against a game that has such a great ability of really carrying its mood and passing it down onto you. Before the Storm was a very invigorating, enjoyable, and emotional experience, just like the original game. And I guess that's what actually matters, and not the silly retcons and whatnot. And remember: you miss 100% of the shots you don't drink!

Its a beautiful game, has some stunning scenary at times. Its really well optimized, I had minimal loading screens and even on medium settings on my lower-mid range PC it ran at a high stable FPS and still looked fantastic. The sounds and lighting are on point, the firearms sound real and the animals act as they should. It is the best hunting game out there. So why the negative review?
It's not because its a walking simulator, which for 80% of gameplay, it is. It is because they lock off important and useful items behind a points system, which would be fine.. if you didn't have to kill countless animals before you can unlock something like a blind or a lure. Trying to hunt without these means you will be doing a lot of tracking and for a very long time.
When it comes to weapons, as i said, they sound awesome, But there are very little to choose from and there are no "fun" guns, I know they are going for realism, but give me something ridiculous to play with! I want to pop squirrels with a full auto .22!
The map is huge, which should be a good thing, but unless you fork out even more cash for an ATV, which should be in the base game.. you better get used to walking several kilometers in real time to reach destinations.
The fact you must pay for ATVs and tents is very reminsient of the original games pay to win structure, The base game is already quite expensive for a non AAA title and is still loaded with bugs. Within the few hours I played, I witness my ATV randomly blow up from being parked in a weird place, to shooting a deer in the engine room, seeing it drop and then randomly getting up a few seconds later without a scratch on it.
I really, really want to like this game. It has so much potential to be a 10/10, but the fact you have to play for hours and hours just to get the items and weapons you want is really off putting. I killed about 10 deer and I only made enough money to buy the cheapest shotgun, which have bird shot and slugs locked off until you kill a whole bunch of things with buckshot.. Its going for arcadey gameplay in a sim game and it just doesn't work in a game like this. It turned into a chore real quick.
If you have world of warcraft levels of free time, the patience of a crocodile and don't care about the occasional glitch, Then i'd recommend it. But for your average joe who just wants to put on a game and have the freedom to go hunt some animals they way they want, when they want to, then i'd say stay clear.

When I first heard of Undertale, I had no interest in playing it. I thought the fanbase was massively cringeworthy and the game was probably uninteresting.
I was correct about the fanbase, but boy was I wrong about the game.
I normally play action/adventure RPG games with the occasional sprinkling of singleplayer FPS. I am not the kind of person to normally go in for conceptual hipster nonsense, and I say that because that's what I thought this game was.
In reality, it has some of the best atmosphere and writing I've seen in a game in a very long time. And above all else, it manages to be heart-rendingly (no pun indended) sad at times and actually funny at other times. Plus, the music is fantastic and the whole package has a level of care I don't often see anymore.
You are doing yourself a disservice if you don't try this game out. And I don't say that lightly.

Gameplay: 6 for the actual fun of it, but I'll give it a 7 just because of how inventive the mercy system is. This is an RPG you can play without killing anything.

Prison architect is a video game that exists. You can play this video game, if you wish. In this video game, you design, build and run a prison. Or rather, you design, command workers to build and shout at workers for not building a prison. But once you do finish your prison, and you artfully engineer the doorways such that your peons aren't being caught in them, there's a fun game here.
Managing a prison is actually quite interesting; there's a lot to manage and a lot to watch, but you can't watch too closely, or your prisoners might get sad that you're trying to ensure they don't escape. And then they'll try to escape, and be caught. But then they'll stab your guards with forks and OD on various narcotics your dogs couldn't sniff out. You retaliate by ordering a mass searching of cells and prisoners. One prisoner was hiding a box of fudge sent by his Grandma. Naturally, he is sent to solitary confinement and your guards go back to work happy and full of fudge.
But the fifteen other prisoners who were needlessly searched will decide that enough is enough. The next day, the ring leader takes his veggie burger with 75% vegetarian ingredients and 25% chef's spit, and throws it at a guard. The burger had a shuriken in it. The guard dies. You tighten the security, and hire a man with a shotgun to walk around the prison. And then you hire another one, because snipers work in pairs and you're a smart architect. But now the prisoners are sad and suppressed and are no longer enjoying their stay in prison. So you fire a shotgun guard. As the fired guard is leaving, an opportunitistic prisoner seizes his gun and fires it at the other shotgun guard, killing his face off, before putting on the guard's face and proceeding to saunter out of the prison undetected. Your prison has had an escapee; say goodbye to any profits this quarter.
And now you're losing money and need to lay some more guards off. So you do. And then more guards are stabbed with forks, by the prisoners they are guarding. And the cycle continues.

>Ingredients
One 15 1/2-ounce can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 medium onion, chopped
4 cloves garlic, minced
1 teaspoon ground coriander
1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
2/3 to 1 cup chicken broth, homemade or low-sodium canned
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
>Directions
Reserve about a third of the beans. Mash the rest of the beans in a medium bowl with a large fork. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion, and cook until lightly browned, about 4 minutes. Add the garlic and continue to cook, stirring, until lightly browned. Add the spices and cook until fragrant about 1 minute.
Add the mashed beans and half the broth; cook, stirring frequently, until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes. Add the reserved beans and the enough of the remaining broth to loosen up the beans. Simmer until the beans are thick but not pasty, about 2 minutes more. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in the fresh coriander, if desired, and serve.

This game has a funny story to it. First let me start with, I like this game. It gives and keeps trying to give the most realistic zombie survival sim experience. The game has bugs, and has been in development for a while, a very long while. If anyone looks at their development updates they would understand why.
This game provides probably the most realistic zombie survival experience:
-Bleeding, broken bones, freezing, and overheating are not the only things that nature/bullets can hit you with.
-Zombies, people, and animals provide for an immersive and sometimes heart racing experience.
- Gun/melee fights can feel a little clunky, but are very satisfying in my opinion. (they will be overhauling the combat system soon)
-This game is better with friends, BUT more intense when playing alone.
-This game is in early access, so DON'T buy if you are expecting a finished game without bugs, which some people expect (stupid right)
Now to my favorite part:
This game is being bashed for having a super long early access cycle, that I do understand, but while it does have a long early access you should understand the players asked for it. In fact, the game was not intended to release when it did (Dec 16, 2013). Due to the insane amount of begging by fans it inevitably released. (that’s when I bought the game 5mins after it came out) They warned us that the game was "FAR" from being finished, but we still plead for it. In fact, the developers were not happy with their game at launch, so they started from scratch mid-alpha, by redoing the game's engine, which, if you don’t know usually takes years to perfect. Now players are upset with what they have gotten themselves into, That’s unbelievable!!!
Before you buy the game, you are told that you are joining their testing and are expected to submit bugs to:
. Which I never did, but I also never B****ed about the bugs I never tried reporting.
I find it funny how the game has people with over 1k game time giving it negative reviews. You would think that they would follow the developers and see how much they’re putting into the game.  Some of them are really justified with their negative review though.
All in all, the game provides a realistic zombie survival experience like no other, with bugs of course. And I get really triggered when people bring up a long development cycle as an excuse to give it a negative review when they asked for it :^).
